Town Planning Inst. of Britain, 1913-1914, and mem. of coun., 1914-1919; mem. bd. of gov't., American City Planning Inst., 1915-1918; chmn., Town Planning Inst. of Canada, 1919.

Publications:—"Land Question in Scotland," 1897; "Garden Cities and Agriculture," 1903; "Housing in Town and Country," 1906; "Town Planning in Greater London," 1914; "State, City and Town Planning," 1916; "Rural Planning and Development," 1917; "Community Planning in Wartime," 1918; "Planning and Development in Oregon," 1919, and numerous papers to scientific societies.

ADAMSON, SIR JOHN ERNEST, KT, B.A.C. (1924), C.M.G. (1923).—B. 1867; ed. in London; Litt.D., M.A., London Univ.; principal, Normal Coll., Pretoria, 1902; dir. of educn., Transvaal, 1908; M.L.C. Transvaal; mem. of coun. of Cape University; dir. of educn., Transvaal Prov.; ret.

ADDISON, D'ARCY WENTWORTH, M.V.O., I.S.O.—Ent. Tasmanian pub. serv. 1st Dec., 1867; clk. of exec. coun., 1903; sec. to premier since 1909; ch. electoral offr., 1914; mag., 1918; admstr. of charitable grants, 1914-19; sec. for neglected children's dept., 1914-19; state organiser, visit of H.R.H. Prince of Wales, 1920; under sec. for Tasmania.

ADDISON, JOSEPH BARTLETT, M.B.E. (1918), M.R.O.S., L.R.C.P.—Ed. at St. Mary's Hosp., London; asst. med. offr., Seychelles, 1907; chief med. offr., 1908; ag. priv. sec. and clk. to exec. coun. from May to Nov., 1912; mem., legis. and exec. couns., 1918; prin. civ. med. offr., Hong Kong, Feb., 1924.

ADELAIDE, BISHOP OF, RIGHT REV. ARTHUR NUTTER THOMAS, D.D., Cantab.—B. 1869; rector of Guisborough, Yorks., 1901-1906; bishop of Adelaide since 1906.

ADERS, WALTER MANFIELD.—B. 1881; ed. Dulwich Coll. and Univ. Coll., London; Marburg Univ., Prussia, Ph.D. (science honours)
1902; engaged on research work, Marine Biological Assoc., Plymouth, 1903; asst. to pathologist, Egyptian govt. hosp., Cairo, and curator of pathological museum, 1905; res. off. of rinderpest serum station, Abassia, Cairo, 1906; priv. asst. and scientific sec. to dir. of quarantine bd., Alexandria, 1907; called to El Tor for research work re cause of dysentery amongst pilgrims; research work with Prof. Viguerie Algiers (marine biology); research work, Welcome Laboratory, Khartoum, 1909; London Sch. of Trop. Med., 1910; research work, Zanzibar, since 1911; read. thanks of S. of S. for foreign affairs and the Order of the Brilliant Star of Zanzibar, 2nd cls., for services rendered, 1912; asst. postal censor, 1914-1916; ch. censor, 1916-1918; lent to milly. authorities for work in Dar-es-Salaam and Kilwa, 1917; economic biologist, 1st June, 1917; at request of gov. of Tanganyika Territory proceeded to Dar-es-Salaam to advise on anti-malarial work, 1921; author of numerous papers and reports on scientific subjects.

AGAR, ARTHUR KIRWAN.—B. 1877; ed. at Brighton Coll., called to the bar, Grays Inn, May, 1919; temp. lieut. R.A.S.C., Oct., 1915; ag.-capt. R.A.S.C., Aug., 1916; staff capt., W.O., Feb., Dec., 1919; dist. mag., dep. judge, ct. of summary juris., coroner, regnr. of sup. ct., escheator gen., provost marshal, regnr. gen., regnr. of titles and legal adviser to gov't of Montserrat, 1st Oct., 1920; dist. commnr., Belize, Br. Hond., Nov., 1923; ag.-atty-gen., 6th Dec., 1923.

AGEBEBI, DENTI.—Asst. warder, Lagos prison, 1885; 4th clk., treas., 1886; examg. offr., customs, 3rd Aug., 1893; paymr., Ibadan detchmt., Hausa Force, 15th May, 1897; in conjunction, postmtr. and clk. to res., Ibadan, 14th Dec., 1901, to Mar., 1903; audit clk., June, 1903.

AHEARNE, CHRISTOPHER DOMINIC.—B. 1886; ed. Christian Schls., Cork, and Trinity Coll., Dublin, scholar 1907; senr. moderator, B.A., 1909; cadet, S. Stitltns., 1910; India, studying Tamil 1911; asst. supt., Indian immigrants, Selangor 1912; 1st asst. contrlr. of labr., Penang, 1913; dep. contrlr. of labr., Klang, 1914; dep. regnr., sup. ct., Penang, 1916; dist. offr., Balik Pulau, 1916; asst. supt., govt. monopolies, Spore, 1917; asst. regnr., impts. and expts. (war dept.), 1918; offr., ics, iv., Jan., 1919; asst. adviser to gov't of Johore, Batu Pahat, 1919-21.

AIKINS, SIR JAMES A. M., KNT. BACH. (1914), K.C.—B. 1861; ed. Upper Canada Coll., Univ. of Toronto; graduated in arts; called to the bar, Ontario, 1878; Manitoba 1879; Q.C., 1884; counsel for the C.P.R. Co. at Winnipeg, 1881-1911; pres. Canadian Bar Assoc., 1914-1916; lieut.-gov., Manitoba, 1917; re-apptd. for a second term, 1921.

AINSWORTH, THOMAS WILLIAM.—B. 1861; ed. Leeds Gram. Schl. and St. John's Coll., Oxford; B.A., 1913; M.A., 1918; cadet, Hong Kong civ. ser., Nov., 1914; passed cadet, June, 1917; ag. sec., sanitary bd., 1917; seconded for mil. serv., 1917; ag. dep. regnr. and appraiser, sup. ct., 1919; 2nd dist. asst. to sec. for Chinese affairs, 1919; sec. to the industrial employment of children commn. in addn., 1921; J.P., 1922; 2nd pol. mag. and 3rd asst. sec. for Chinese affrs., 1922; asst. col. treas. and asst. assessor of rates, 1923.

AITKEN, JOHN, B.A., L.L.B. (1906).—B.1885; ed. Giggleswick Coll. and Christ's Coll., Camb.; barrister-at-law, Inner Temple, 1909; asst. dist. offr., S. Nigeria, 1913; station mag., Nigeria, 1915; crown counsel, Gold Coast, 3rd Nov., 1920; ag. solr.-gen., Dec., 1920 to Apr., 1921, July to Sept. and Oct. to Nov., 1921, and June to July, 1922; ag. puisme judge, Sept. to Oct., 1921, and from July to Sept., 1922.

AKBAR, MAAS THAJOON.—B. 1880; ag. crown comm., Ceylon, Aug., 1907; crown comm., June, 1908; ag. 2nd admn. dist. judge, Colombo, and as solr.-gen. on several occasions; solr.-gen., Oct., 1924.

AKITOYÈ, DANIEL.—B. 1866; ed. at Lagos Gram. Schl.; copyist to Queen's Advocate, Lagos, Aug., 1886; was fourteen years regiar. of instruments affecting land; dep. regiar. of births, deaths, marriages, and aliens, Jan., 1896; ag. regiar. at intervals; clk. to commnr. of lands (now dir. of surveys), Apr., 1901.

ALBURY, G. A.—B. 1865; entd. Bahamas civ. serv., 1898; Out Island commnr. (1st div.), 1909; ssnl. inspnr., pro tem., Jan., 1919; ag. stip. and circuit mag. for various periods from 1919-1923; ag. stip. and circuit mag. in 1923 and 1924.

ALBURY, JOSEPH JOHNSON.—B. 1881; Out Island commnr. (4th div.), Bahamas, 1910; 3rd. div. commnr., Jan., 1918.

ALBURY, STANLEY VICTOR STRATHMERE.—B. 1873; tidewaiter, Bahamas, 1901; clk., post office, 1907; Out Island commnr. (3rd div.), 1911; (2nd div.), 1912; supt. of hospital, 1917.

ALBURY, WILTON GRANT.—B. 1877; public school teacher, Bahamas, 1896; resigned, 1906; re-apptd., 1909; head-master, boys' central school, 1914; inspnr. of schools, 1915.

ALCOCK, WILLIAM D. E.—B. 1892; ed. King Edward's schl., Birmingham, and Birmingham Univ.; B.A., 1913 (1st class, two distinctions); cadet, Fiji, Jan., 1915; dist. commnr., Savusavu, Kadavu, Colo East, Lautoka and Bua, Nov., 1915 to Jan., 1920; qual. in law, Oct., 1917; asst. polit. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Apr., 1920.

ALEXANDER, CHARLES SHULDHAM, M.A., Cantab.—B. 1877; cadet, F.M.S., 1900; ag. collr., land rev., Matang, Feb., 1901 to Jan., 1902; ag. asst. dist. treas., Kuala Lumpur, Apr., 1902; ag. dist. treas., Telok Anson, June, 1904; ag. dist. treas., Batu Gajah, Sept., 1905 to Nov., 1906; ag. state treas., Perak, Feb., 1908; ag. asst. treas., F.M.S., Apr.-Oct., 1912 and June, 1913; ag. treas., F.M.S., June-Oct., 1914 and Nov., 1914; finan. commnr. and aud. gen., Johore, Oct., 1914; finan. commnr. and aud. gen., Johore, Jan., 1919; ag. finan. adviser, F.M.S. in addn., Jan.-Aug., 1924; treas., F.M.S., Feb., 1924.

ALEXANDER, EDWARD BRUCE.—B. 1872; ed. Forest Schl., and Trin. Coll., Oxford (B.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Dec., 1896; offl. asst. to govt. agt., S. Prov., Aug., 1897; pol. mag., Panadure, Aug., 1899; asst. govt. agt., Matale, Dec., 1900; Kegalle, Oct., 1903; seconded addl. supl. of pol., Cent. Prov., May, 1906; supl. of pol., S. Prov., July, 1906; ag. inspnr.-gen. of pol., Mar.-Nov., 1907, and Dec., 1908 to Jan., 1909; supl. of pol., Cent. Prov., Nov., 1907; asst. govt. agt., Puttalam, June, 1910; ag. govt. agt., Sabaragamuwa, Aug., 1911; chmn., mun. coun. and mayor of Colombo, Apl., 1913; on military duty Sept., 1914; govt. agt., Prov. of Sabaragamuwa, Apl., 1919; ag. contr. rev. and ag. food contr., Mar., 1920; addl. contr. of rev., Sept., 1921; ag. prin. collr. of cust., Oct., 1921; govt. agt., W. Prov., Nov., 1921; ag. contr., rev., Nov., 1922 to Feb., 1923; addl. contr., rev., Feb. to May, 1923; ag. contr., rev., May to Aug., 1923; contr., rev., 21st Aug., 1923.
ALEXANDER, Gilchrist Gibb.—Ed. at Glasgow Acad. and Glasgow Univ.; M.A., with 1st cl. hons. in mental philosophy, 1893; Eglington Fellowship; gold medal as most distinguished graduate in arts of year; called to the bar, Middle Temple, 1896; practiced in London, 1907; chief pol. mag., Fiji, Mar., 1907; ag. atty.-gen., and mem. exec. and legis. couns., Fiji, June, 1907, to May, 1908, June to Aug., 1908, Aug., 1910, to Feb., 1911, and from Oct., 1912, to Sept., 1913; seconded for serv. with W. Pacific High Comsnr., on special mission to Peru, Oct., 1908, to Apl., 1909, and to Tonga, July-Aug., 1911; ag. British judge of joint court, New Hebrides Condominium, Feb. to Oct., 1912; chmn. of comsnr. to enquire into shipping conditions of colony, 1913-1914; ag. chief just., Fiji, and chief judcl. comsnr., W. Pacific, Sept., 1913 to Jan., 1915; on mil. service, July, 1917; special comsnr. to deal with land disputes in Brit. Solomon Is., 17th Oct., 1919; senr. puisne judge, Tanganyika Territory, Aug., 1920; ag. ch. just., Feb. to Nov., 1921 and Nov., 1923 to July, 1924.

ALEXANDER, John Edward—Asst. land ranger, E.A.P., Oct., 1912; lands offr., Nyassaland, 21st July, 1922.

ALLAN, Kenneth Bruce, M.B., B.S. (Durham), Certif. London Schl. of Trop. Med., and Coll. of Med., Durham Univ.—Ed. Denstone Coll., Staffs.; med. offr., W.A.M.S. Gold Coast, May, 1911; temp. lieut., R.A.M.C., 1916-17; transf'd as capt. on gen. list and attd. 1st K.A.R., Nyassaland Field Force, July, 1917 to Jan., 1919; med. offr., W.A.M.S., Gambia, Mar., 1923.

ALLAN, Peter, M.B., Ch.B., D.P.H., Edin. M.D. (1920).—Res. med. offr., Royal Victoria Hosp. for consumption, Edinburgh, 1911-12; clin. asst., med. out-patient dept., Royal Infirmary, Edinburgh, 1912; asst. tuberculosis offr., boroughs of Paddington and Kensington, 1912-13; 1st med. supt., Romsey Hill Sanatorium, Birmingham, 1913-1920; capt., R.A.M.C., 1917-18; med. inspr., dept. of pub. health, Union of South Africa, 1920; med. supt., tuberculosis sanatorium, Helsport, C.P., 1923; author of "An investigation into the increased mortality from pulmonary tuberculosis, 1914-1920."

ALLARD, Jules.—B. 1859; ed. Nicolet Coll., Quebec; lawyer; elec. to legis. assem., Quebec, 1897, 1900, 1904; apptd. to legis. coun. and min. of pub. wks., Quebec, 1905; min. of agric., 1907; min. of lands and forests, 1909, 1917; re-elec. to legis. assem. at bye-election 1910 and g.e., 1912; re-called to legis. coun., 1916; prothonotory of the superior ct., Montreal, 1919.

ALLARDYCE, Sir W. L., K.C.M.G. (1916), C.M.G. (1902), Knt. of Grace of the Order of St. John of Jerusalem (1916).—B. 1861; clk. and interp., Provincial Dept., Fiji, 1879; transf'd to Rotumah, 1882; stip. mag., July, 1882; asst. native comsnr. and stip. mag. and inspr. of native taxes, Kadavu, Jan., 1890; mem. exec. coun., Nov., 1893; native lands comsnr. and mem. legis. coun., 1894; native comsnr., 1896; asst. col. sec. and receiv.-gen., Dec., 1896; deputy gov., 14-20 Feb., 1901; adminstr. govt., 18th July, 1901, to 9th Sept., 1902; col. sec. and receiv.-gen., 18th July, 1902; gov., Falkland Is., 1904; gov., Bahamas, 28th Dec., 1914; assumed govt. 15th June, 1915; gov., Tasmania, 1920; editor of native newspaper "Na Mata," 1890-99; author of a digest of Native Regulations, 1877-1900; attended first Fed. Conf. on Education, 1907; gov., Newfoundland, 1st Sept., 1922; assumed govt., 1st Dec., 1922.

ALLDER, WM. Howell.—B. 1873; 5th clk., C.S.O., Barbados, 1892; 4th do., 1896; 3rd do., 1900; 2nd cls. clk., P.O., 1904; ch. clk., do., 1908; ch. clk., audit off., 1913; acted on several occasions as clk. of the exec. coun. and comttee., as acctnt. in P.O., and as auditor-gen.; sec. Barbados quarantine comsn., 1903; to West Indian quarantine conf., 1904, and to confer. on trade relations between West Indies and Canada, 1910; sec., Barbados civ. serv. comsn., 1920.

ALLEN, F.T.—Enlisted as trooper in Rhodesian field force, 1900, and served in S. African war; invalided home 1901; obtained comsnr. as 2nd lieut. in 5th Batt. Royal Irish Rifles, Dec., 1901, and returned to S. Africa until end of war; passed Hythe musketry and machine gun course, 1903; military course of instruction, 1906; captain, May, 1906; dist. supt. of police, Uganda, July, 1907; cadet course, Royal Irish Constabulary, 1907; supt. of police, Uganda, 1911.

ALLEN, H.—Tempy. asst. dist. commr., E.A.P., Apl., 1919; ast. treas., Uganda, Aug., 1920.

ALLEN, H. T.—B. 1879; apptd., after compt. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser., and assigned to the C.O. Mar., 1898; conf. clk., Dec., 1907; also clk. to concessions and finance comttee., Sept., 1910 to June, 1916; promoted, under order-in-council of 1910, 2nd cls. clk., C.O., 16th June, 1916; ast. sec. to trade relations comttee., Aug., 1917; sec., Dependencies of Falkland Islands comttee., Jan., 1918; sec., raw materials board, Dec., 1918; ast. priv. sec. to sec. of state (Lord Milner), 1st Jan., 1920; prin., 1st Apr., 1920.

ALLEN, Hon. Sir James, K.C.B. (1917), M.A., Camb.—B. 1865; entd. New Zealand Parlmt., 1887; lieut.-col. in command Otago Division, New Zealand Garrison Artillery, 1902; min. of defenc., 1912; min. of finance, min. of stamp duties and min. of educn., 1912-15; min. of finance and min. of external affairs, 1919-20; high commr. in England, 1920.

ALLEN, Leonard Gilbert.—B. 1901; entered C.O., 1917; apptd., after exam., ast. clk., 2nd Apr., 1919; cler. offr., 1st Jan., 1920.

ALLEN, Lucien Arthur.—B. 1888; ed. Merchant Taylors' Schl. and St. John's Coll., Cambridge; B.A., 1910; cadet, F.M.S., Dec., 1912; ag. ast. dist. offr., Batang Padang, Dec., 1913; ag. 2nd ast. dist. offr., Tapah, Feb., 1915; ag. sec. to res., Negri Sembilan, Apr., 1915 to Sept., 1918; passed cadet, June, 1915; ast. dist. offr., Kuantan, Sept., 1918 to Aug., 1919; ast. dist. offr., Lower Perak, June, 1920; Brit. res., Brunei, Mar., 1921; ast. dist. offr., Ipoh, Jan., 1924; ag. ch. ast. dist. offr., Kinta, Mar., 1924.

ALLEN, Percy Tothill.—B. 1878; ed. at Highgate Schl., Christ's Coll., Camb., (boas. class. tripoe, 1899); cadet, F.M.S., Nov., 1903; ag. 2nd ast. prot. of Chinese, Penang, Sept., 1906; ag. ast. dist. offr., Matang, June, 1906; ag. dist. offr. Christmas Is., Nov., 1907 and Nov., 1908; ag. ast. prot. of Chinese and supt. of prisons, Penang, Feb., 1909; ag. 2nd ast. dist. offr., Tapah, Apr., 1909; ag. mag., Seremban, Apr., 1912; ag. ast. prot. of Chinese and musk comsnr., Penang, Oct., 1913; ag. ast. prot. of Chinese, Singapore, Jan. and May, 1917; ag. prot. of Chinese, Singapore, Feb., 1917; ag. insp. of prisons, S.S. in add., Jan., 1918; ag. rev. and Sel., N. S. and Pahang, April, 1919; ag. prot. of Chinese, Selangor and Negri Sembilan, June,
1919; ag. dist. offr., Ulu Selangor, Sept., 1919; ag. state treas., Selangor and ast. treas., F.M.S., Mar., 1920; ag. sec. for Chinese affairs, S.S. and temp. off. mem., leg. coun., S.S., May, 1920; ag. regis., titles, Perak and supt., convict estab., Taiping, Sept., 1922; ag. dist. offr., Larut, in add., May, 1923; ag. chmn., many, bd., Kuala Lumpur, Dec., 1923.

ALLEYNE, JAMES DOUGLAS, M.D. (Tuft's Univ., U.S.A.)—Ag. pol. med. offr., dist. A., Barbados and visiting physician, leper asylum, 1917; ast. port health offr., 1919; ag. supt., lunatic asylum, 1919; port health offr., 1921; ex officio mem., quarantine board.

ALLIES, E. J.—B. 1891; apptd. ast. clk., Scottish Educn. Dept., 1910; apptd. after compet. exam. clk. of the 2nd divn. of the civ. serv. to National Insurance Audit Dept., 1913; on mily. serv., 1917-19; assigned to the C.O., Aug., 1919; cler. offr., higher grade, 1st Apr., 1922.

ALUWIHARE, RICHARD.—B. 1895; on mily. serv., Oct., 1915; cadet, Ceylon, Oct., 1920; attd. to Jaffna kach., Oct., 1920; office ast., dir. of agr., Feb., 1922; ag. pol. mag., Dandaganamuwa, Oct., 1923; pol. mag., Pt. Pedro, Nov., 1923.

AMERY, Lieut.-Col., L.C.M.S.—B. 1873; ed. at Harrow and Balliol Coll., Oxford; late Fellow of All Souls, Oxford; Ouseley Scholar of Imp. Inst. in Turkish; called to the bar, Inner Temple, 1902; on editorial staff of The Times, 1899-1909; served during the war in Flanders, Salonika, and the Near East; on the staff of the Imp. War Coun. at Versailles, and as ast. sec. to the War Cabinet and Imp. Cabinet to Jan., 1919; under-sec. of state for the colonies, 14th Jan., 1919; acted as sec. of state during Lord Milner's absence in Egypt, Nov., 1919 to Mar., 1920; First Lord of the Admiralty, Oct., 1922; S. of S. for the Cols., 7th Nov., 1924; capt. 14th 1st Bham Batt., Royal Warwickshire Regt., 1914; lieut.-col. on general staff, 1917; M.P. (U) for S. Birmingham, May, 1911; ditto Sparkbrook div., Deo., 1918; edited "The Times History of the South African War"; author of "Problem of the Army," 1903; "Fundamental Fallacies of Free Trade," 1906; "The Great Question" (with J. M. Robertson, M.P.), 1909; "Union and Strength," 1912.

AMPHTHILL, 2nd BARON, creat. 1881, OLIVER ARTHUR VILLIERS RUSSELL.—Son of the 1st Baron; born 1869; succeeded his father, 1884; G.C.S.I. (1904), G.C.I.E., 1900. Ed. at Eton and New Coll., Oxon. Rowed in the Oxford eight, 1889-91; pres. of the Oxford Union, 1891; B.A., 1891; M.A., 1900; ast. priv. sec. to Mr. Chamberlain, Sec. of State for Cols., June, 1895; priv. sec., June, 1897; one of the British delegates to the Internat. Sugar Conference, Brussels, May and June, 1898; lieut. Roy. 1st Devon Yeomny Cavalry; capt. 3rd batt. Bedfordshire Regt.; J.P.; past grand master, Freemason's grand lodge of England and prov. grand master of Freemasons, Bedfordshire; governor of Madras, Oct., 1900-1905; ag. Viceroy of India in 1904.

ANDERSON, C. E.—Ast. polit. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 1st Nov., 1916; A.P.O., cadet, 25th Aug., 1920; confirmed in appt. as A.P.O., 1st Jan., 1921.

ANDERSON, CHARLES OSBORNE.—B. 1868; 2nd. clk. and letter carrier, P.O., Bahamas, 1888; chief clk., 1890; ag. res. just., Inagua, 1896; ag. warehouse keeper and examg. offr., 1906; ag. postmtr., 1907, 1909, 1910; ag. aud. of pub. accts., 1910; postmtr., 1913; mem. H. of A.; M.L.C., 10th Jan., 1924.

ANDERSON, E. L. B.—Ast. dist. comsrr., E.A.P., Oct., 1919.

ANDERSON, GEORGE BARTLET.—B. 1880; ed. Gordon's Coll., Aberdeen; clk., acct.-genl.'s dept., G.P.O., London, 1896; clk., war office, Jan., 1900; 2nd cls. clk., G.P.O., Johannesburg, Dec., 1909; transf. to ext. and legis. councils dept.; 2nd cls. clk., June, 1903; 1st cls. clk., July, 1905; acct.'s clk. and cashier, Transvaal agt.-general's office, London, Oct., 1907; acct. acct., Apl., 1908; clk., P.W.D., Nyassaland, June, 1909; chief clk., secretariat, Apl., 1914; ag. ast. chief sec., Aug., 1916; on re-organisation of secretariat apptd. 2nd ast. sec., Aug., 1919; ag. 1st ast. sec., Aug., 1919; ag. ch. sec., June to Nov., 1920; admin. offr., 1st grade, July, 1922; ag. 1st ast. sec. Mar. to Nov., 1922.

ANDESON, HON. GEORGE JAMES.—B. 1860; ed. Lawrence Gram. Sch.; mem., N.Z. parl., since 1908; chmn. labour bills comtee., five years; chmn., library comtee., eight years; min. of internal affairs, 1920-21; min. of lab., 1921; min. of mines, 1921; min. of marine, 1922.

ANDERSON, MAXWELL HENDRY.—C.B.E. (mil.) (1919); O.B.E. (1918); K.C., Aug., 1919; capt., R.N. (ret.); entered Royal Navy, 1893; ret. at own request, 1912; reed. thanks of Adm'y. for valuable series of magnetic observations carried out in the Pacific Ocean; instructor, R.N. Coll., Portsmouth, 1908-10; called to the bar, Middle Temple, 1909; younger brother of Trinity House, 1910; rejoined Navy on outbreak of war; employed on special services; reed. thanks of Adm'y. for services rendered to naval prize fund and at courts martial; specially promoted capt., Apl., 1919; govt. mem., central (unemployed) body for London, 1913 to 1919; atty-gen., Gibraltar, 9th May, 1919; ag. chief just., and col. sec. on several occasions.

ANDERSON, ROBERT MOWBRAY.—Entd. govt. printing dept., St. Vincent, 6th Feb., 1886; chief govt. printer, July, 1894; steward, col. hosp., Aug., 1901; mem. of comtee. to inquire into admtn. of poor relief, Aug., 1904; clk. to regis., sup. ct., and regis. of B., M. and D. for dist. I., Nov., 1904; tempy. ast. landing waiter for spec. excise duties, Nov., 1904; edited first "Illustrated Handbook of St. Vincent," 1907.

ANDERSON, R. T. H.—Ast.-supt. of police, E.A.P., 1911.

ANDERSON, THOMAS EDWARD.—B. 1877; excise offr., B. Honduras, Dec., 1902; 2nd grade customs and excise offr., July, 1905; ag. 1st grade customs and excise offr., from April, 1904; confirmed March, 1906, rlyw. acctnt., 1st Aug., 1909; on completion of rlyw. construction reverted to substantive appt., 7th Sept., 1910; ag. chief clk., etc., treasy. and customs dept., 20th May to 7th Sept., 1911.

ANDERSON, THOMAS JOHN, M.A., B.Sc., (Hons. Edin.) F.Z.S., F.S.E.—Entomologist, agric. dept., Kenya, May, 1908.

ANDRE, WILFRID JOSEPH.—B. 1890; called to the bar, Gray's Inn, 1912; mag., St. Andrew, &c., Trinidad, Nov., 1923.

ANDREW, ROBERT CHARLES.—Ed. Liverpool Inst., Harper-Adams Agric. Coll., Newport, and Liverpool Univ.; B.Sc. (agric., London); National Diploma in agric.; mem. (by exam.) of Surv'r's Instit. ; lecturer under the East Sussex county council, 1905 to 1910; foreign experience, 1911; ast. supt. of agric., N. Nigeria, 24th April, 1912.

ANGLIN, HON. FRANCIS ALEXANDER.—B. 1866; ed. St. Mary's Coll., Montreal, and Univ. of Ottawa; called to the bar, 1888; K.C. 1902;
apptd. sen. puisane judge, exchequer div., high ct. of just., Ontario, 1904; puisane judge, supreme ct. of Canada, 1909; ch. just., sup. ct., Canada, 1924; dep. of gov.-gen.

ANNETTS, HERBERT HENRY.—B. 1888; Ed. Magdalen Coll. sch., Oxford, and Worcester Coll., Oxford; B.A., 1910; ass't master, preparatory schl., Repton, 1910-1911; served in Oxfordshire educ. comte's office, and inspr. of evening schla., Oxfordshire county council, 1911-1912; apptd. junr. supt., educ. dept., Northern Nigeria, 12th Sept., 1912; senr. supt., 1st Jan., 1913; ag. dir. educ., 4th Apr., 1920; senr. supt., 1st Jan., 1919; dep. dir., 1st Jan., 1920; ag. dir., 1920 and 1922.

ANSON, MAJOR-GENERAL SIR ARCHIBALD EDWARD HARBORD, R.A., C.M.G. (1876), K.C.M.G. (1882).—B. 1826; entered the royal mil. acad., Woolwich, 1841; presented with sword for exemplary conduct; 2nd lieut., R.A., June, 1844; 1st lieut., 1st Apr., 1846; 2nd capt., 9th July, 1852; 1st capt., 1st Sept., 1855; brevet major, 21st July, 1864; lieut.-col., 12th May, 1866; brevet col., 12th May, 1874; col., 23rd Dec., 1875; ret. with the hon. rank of maj.-gen., 26th August, 1879; served at the siege of Sebastopol in 1855; Crimean medal and clasp, 5th class Medjidie, and Turkish medal; inspr.-gen. of pol., Mauritius, Sept., 1868; was employed in 1862 as the responsible mem. of the Br. mission to the court of Radama II. of Madagascar, on the occasion of his coronation; lieut.-gov. of Prince of Wales Is., Feb., 1867; admstd. govt. Str. Stltmts. 1871, 1877, and 1879; conducted the successful military operations for repelling the invasion of the state of Sungei Ujong, 1875-76 (medal and clasp); ret. 1882; J.P. for Sussex.

ANTHONY, EDWIN AUGUSTUS.—Olk., ch. mag's office, Tembuland and Transkei, 2nd May, 1894; clk. and dep. audr. of rev., atty-gen's office, 28th Mar., 1897; examr. of accts., July 1897; ag. ch. olk., pol. branch, 1st Mar. to 30th Apr., 1902; ag. bookkeeper, guardian's fund, master's office, from 16th Jan., 1903; ag. 1st olk., Simons Town, 6th to 29th Sept., 1904; olk., civ. comanr., Cape, 30th Sept., 1904; ch. paymr.'s office, treas'y., 1st July, 1908; regar. of friendly societies and treas'y. rep., Cape Town, Sept., 1918; civ. comanr., Cape, Mar., 1921.

ANTHONY, PHILIP ARNOLD, C.M.G. (1918), M.I.C.E.—B. 1873; ed. at Mill Hill Schl.; served in engineering dept., G.W. Rly., 1894-1910; gen. man. and chief engnr., F.M.S. Rly., 1910; services lent to ministry of munitions, May, 1915 to Nov., 1916, resumed duty in F.M.S., Feb., 1917; services lent temporarily to govt. of South Aust., Apr., 1918; resumed duty in F.M.S., Jan., 1919.

ANTROBUS, MAURICE E., B.A.—B. 1896; ed. Winchester, and Trinity Coll., Cambridge; math. exhib., Trinity Coll., Dec., 1913; 2nd lieut., 6th King's Royal Rifle Corps, Aug., 1914; lieut., June, 1915; capt., Jan., 1917; served in Flanders, Salonica and France, 1915-19; 2nd cls. math. tripes, pt. I., 1919; 2nd cls. hist. tripes., pt. II., 1920; B.A., 1920; temp. 2nd cls. elk., C.O., Aug., 1920; apptd. under reconstruction scheme, asst. prin., 7th Feb., 1921.

ANTROBUS, SIR REGINALD L., K.C.M.G. (1911), C.B. (1898).—B. 1863; ed. at Winchester and at New Coll., Oxford; scholar of New Coll., 1872; 1st class in classical moda., 1874; 2nd class in final classical school, 1876; B.A., 1876; apptd., after an open compet. exam., to be a elk. in the C.O., May 3rd, 1877; asst. priv. sec. to the Earl of Kimberley, 5th Dec., 1880, to Dec., 1882; priv. sec. to the Earl of Derby, 16th Dec., 1882, to 24th June, 1885; to Col. the Right Hon. F. A. Stanley, M.P. (afterwards Earl of Derby), 24th June, 1885, to 6th Feb., 1886; and to Earl Granville, 6th Feb. to 3rd Aug., 1886; adminstr. the govt. of St. Helena, 5th Nov., 1889, to 8th June, 1890; priv. sec. to Mr. Meade, 1st Feb., 1892, and to Mr. S. Burton, M.P., 17th Aug., 1892; sen. elk., Jan., 1894; prine. elk., 1896; ass't under-sea. of state, Oct., 1898; crown agent for the colo., 1909; retired, 1918.

APPLEGATE, F. W.—B. 1887; ed. Bath Coll. and Queen's Coll., Cambridge; B.A., 1911; ass't dist. comanr., Gold Coast, Apr., 1916; junr. ass't col. sec., 13th May to 30th Sept., 1916; travelling comanr., Nasawam, 1st Oct., 1915 to 31st May 1916, and from 12th Apr., 1917; ass't dist. comanr., Kwahu, 1919.

ARCHER, GEOFFREY FRANCIS, K.C.M.G. (1929), C.M.G. (1913).—Ass't colnr., East Africa Prot., 1st Dec., 1902; attached secretariat, June, 1902; Mar., 1903; dist. comanr., 1st Apr., 1907; spe. serv., Northern Frontier, East Africa, 1909; eff. in-charge, May to Dec., 1911; awarded Cuthbert Peak Grantby the R.G.S., 1918, for survey of E. Africa connecting Major Gwynn's Abyssinian triangulation with the triangulation of K. Afr.; transferred to Somaliland Prot., June, 1912; admin. govt., July to Oct., 1912, and from June to Oct., 1913; dep. comanr., 31st Mar., 1913; comanr. and comdr.-in-chief, Somaliland Prot., 15th May, 1914; assumed govt., 22nd May, 1914; present at operations against the Dervishes at Shimbere, Feb., 1915 (African General Service Medal and clasp); member of British Mission on occasion of coronation of the Empress Zauditu of Abyssinia, Feb., 1917 (Star of Ethiopia, 1st class); govt., Somaliland Prot., 4th Nov., 1919; directed operations against the Mullah, 1920, resulting in complete destruction of Dervish power in Somaliland; govt. and comdr.-in-chief, Uganda Prot., 6th Sept., 1922; govt., Sudan, 1924.

ARCHER, NORMAN E.—B. 1892; ed. R.N. Colls., Osborne and Dartmouth; midshipman in Mediterranean and Home Fleets, 1909-12; sub-lieut. (six 1st cls. certfs.), Sept., 1912; lieut., June, 1913; H.M.S. Warrior in Mediterranean and Grand Fleets, 1912-15; qualified, specialist course, as torpedo lieut., 1915; served with Russian Navy in Black Sea, &c., 1915-17 (Order of St. Stanislas, 3rd cls.); passed exam. as Russo-interpreter, 1918; intell. divn. adm'y., H.M.S. Lowestoft in Adriatic, minelaying squadron, Grand Fleet, and H.M.S. Malaya, 1917-20; app'd under reconstruction scheme asst. prin., min. of lab., Sept., 1920; temp. attd. to C.O. as ass't prin., Dec., 1921.

ARCHER, W. J.—Supt., govt. printing offce., Cyprus, 27th May, 1902.

ARCHIBALD, EDGAR S., B.A., B.S.A.—B. 1886; read. prmr. educn. at Yarmouth pub. schl. and Yarmouth acad.; grad. Acadia Univ., 1906; also grad. from the Nova Scotia hort. schl. in the same year, and from Nova Scotia agric. coll. in 1906; read. deg. of Bach. of Scien. Agric. from the Ontario agric. coll., 1908; inst. of agric. and experimt. at the Nova Scotia agric. coll., 1908; prof. of agric. and farm supt. of the same coll. in 1910; entd. the serv. of the Fed. Dept. of Agric. in June, 1912, as Dominion animal husbandman at the Cent. Expmtl. Farm, Ottawa; ag. dir. of Expmtl. Farms, 1918-19; dir., June, 1919.

ARCHIBALD, GEORGE.—B. 1869; ass't Trinidad civ. ser., Jan., 1892; cashier, Trinidad govt. rly., 1894; acctnt., 1906.
ARCHIBALD, MUNGO TENNENT, M.C.—B. 1886; ed. Glasgow (M.A.), and Pemb. Coll., Oxford; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Nov., 1909; off. ast. to gov't. ast. N. Prov., May, 1910; ditto, Batticaloa, May, 1911; pol. mag., Kurnegala, May, 1912; ast. land settm. offr., Jan., 1913; special comm'r in connection with riots, June, 1915; ast. land settm. offr., Aug., 1915; on military duty, 1916; ast. land settm. offr., Aug., 1919; ast. gov't. ast., Puttalam, Dec., 1922; dist. judge, Nuwara Eliya, Apr., 1923; ast. dist. offr., July, 1923; ast. dist. offr., June, 1924.

ARMBRISTER, PERCY W. D.—B. 1862; ag. reg'lar., prothonotary, and clk. of Crown, Bahamas, 1884; ag. ch. clk., col. sec.'s dept., 1886; clk., pol. ct., Nassau, 1887; J.P., 1890; res. mag. and collr. of rev., Abaco, 1890; Eleuthera, 1894, Harbour Is., 1895, Inagua, 1896; ag. stip. and circuit mag., Bahamas, and judge of ct. of com. pleas, 1896 and 1897; reg'lar. of ct., prothonotary, and clk. of Crown, Jan., 1897; Out Island comm'r, 1909; recvr.-gen. and treas., 1916; ag. col. sec. for various periods between 1919 and 1924; ag. dep. gov. and seni. mem. of exec. coun. from 9th to 11th Mar., 1923; ag. dep. gov. from 25th to 28th Feb., 1924.

ARMITAGE, CAPT. CECIL HAMILTON, C.M.G. (1911) D.S.O. (1901).—Ast. inspr., G. Coast constab., 1894; served in Ashanti exp'd., 1895-6 (star); Northern Territories (Neutral Zone), 1897 (medal and clasp); inspr., 1898; priv. sec. to gov. of G. Coast and clk. of leg. and exec. couns., 1899-1900; Ashanti campaign, 1900 (ag. res. during siege of Coomassie, D.S.O., medal and clasp); trav. comm'r., 1901; comm'r. of S. Province of Ashanti, July, 1901; comdt. of Ashanti Mines volunteers with rank of maj., Nov., 1905; ag. chief comm'r of Ashanti, Oct., 1901, to end of year Apr. to Oct., 1906, Dec., 1907, June, 1908, and from June to Dec., 1909: chief comm'r. of Northern Territories, 28th Jan., 1910; gov., Gambia, 20th Nov., 1920; assumed gov't., 3rd Jan., 1921.

ARMSTRONG J. R.—B. 1881; clk., defence dept., Union of S. Africa, Nov., 1913; clk. High Comm'r's office, S. Africa, Jan., 1915; apptd. to Swaziland estab., Jan., 1919; ag. conf. clk. to gov-gen. on various occasions from 1916-1919; ast. sec. (in S. Africa) to Lord Cave's comm. on S. Rhodesia, 1919.

ARMSTRONG, ROBERT.—B. 1879; ed. Friends' Sch., Great Ayton, Yorks and Durham Univ.; diploma in agric., Armstrong Coll., Newcastle-upon-Tyne, in Univ. of Durham; lecturer, schl. of agric., Egyptian gov't., 1905-1910; lecturer and organiser in agric. for the Hampshire County Council; ast. dir. of agric., Zanzibar, 6th Feb., 1913; ag. dir. of agric., 28th Oct., 1915 to 13th Aug., 1916; ag. chief supply offr., 16th Sept. to 16th Nov., 1918, and 30th Mar., 1919; ag. admstr.-gen., 10th Nov., 1919 to 22nd Jan., 1920; ag. dir. agr., 30th Mar., 1919 to 13th Jan., 1920, and 30th Nov., 1923 to 10th May, 1924; ag. dir. of agr. and ch. supply offr., 7th Feb. to 16th Nov., 1923.

ARNOLD, 1ST BARON (creat. 1924), Rt. HON. SYDNEY ARNOLD, P.C.—B. 1878; was parly. priv. sec. to the pres. of the bd. of educn. and to the finan. sec. to the treas., 1914; lib. M.P. for Holmfirth and later for Penistone, 1912-21; parly. under sec. for the coln., Jan., 1924 to 7th Nov., 1924.

ARTHUR, JAMES STARTIN WILLS.—B. 1881; ed. at Marlborough Coll. and Balliol Coll., Oxford; B.A. (1904); cadet, S. Stiltna, Jan., 1905; ag. 2nd ast. prot. of Chinese, Penang, Sept., 1907; ag. ast. treas., Singapore, June, 1909; 2nd ast. prot. of Chinese, Penang, July, 1910; attached to col. audit office, Feb.-Mar., 1911; ag. 2nd ast. prot. of Chinese, Singapore, July, 1911; ag. dist. offr., Christmas Is., Aug., 1911; ag. 3rd mag., Singapore, May, 1912; ag. ast. P.M.G., Penang, Sept., 1912; ag. ast. prot. of Chinese, Singapore, Mar., 1915; offr. cls. IV, May, 1916; seconded as ast. adviser, Kodah, May, 1916; ag. temp. as adviser in addn., Feb.-Mar., 1917; offr., cls. III, Jan., 1919; offr., cls. II., Dec., 1921.

ARUMUGUM, JOSEPH NALLIAN.—B. 1896; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Dec., 1921; attd. Anuradhapura kach., Dec., 1921; ag. pol. mag., W. Prov., May, 1924.

ASHTON, DANIEL ASPINALL.—B. 1869; ed. at Manchester gram. schl. and Owens Coll.; M.B., B.Ch., Victoria Univ.; civ. surg., S. African war, 1901-1902 (medal and three clasps); col. med. offr., S. Nigeria, Jan., 1903; served in Cross River expdn., 1904 (medal and clasp); med. offr. at Abe and Obubura.

ASHTON, HUGH.—B. 1878; served in S. African War; sub-inspr., Basutoland Mounted Pol., 1908; inspr., 1914; served in European War with native labour contingent; ast. comm'r., Basutoland, 1923.

ASHWORTH, HENRY TWEDDALE, M.M.—B. 1836; apptd., after compet. exam., clk., G.P.O., 1902; on mil'y. serv., Oct., 1914 to May, 1919; served in Gallipoli, Egypt (Canal Defences) and France; passed supplementary clks. exam., Jan., 1921; services loaned to C.O., 1st May, 1922; apptd. cler. offr. and assigned to the C.O., 1st Sept., 1922.

ASPINALI, ALGERNON EDWARD., C.M.G. (1918)—B. 1871; ed. at Eton and Magdalen Coll., Oxford; B.A., 1894; called to the bar, Inner Temple, 1897; sec., West India Comtese since 1908 and of the Impl. Coll. of Trop. Agr. since 1921; hon. treas. of W. Indian Club; mem. of comte. on Col. blue-books and blue-book repts., 1917; mem., W. Indian shipping comte., 1919; hon. sec., Trop. Agr. Coll. comte., 1920; hon. sec., W. Indian Contingent comte., 1916-21; mem., W. Indian currency comte., 1923.

ASSER, LIEUT.-GEN. SIR JOSEPH JOHN, K.C.B. (1924), K.C.M.G. (1918), K.C.V.O. (1917), C.B. (1915), and many foreign decorations.—B. 1867; served with Nile expdn., 1897-9; in command of Kordofan expdn., Soudan, 1910; A.G., Egyptian Army, 1907-16; served in European War, 1914-19; base comm'dt., 1914-16; lieut.-gen., 1919; gen. offr. comm'dg. Br. troops, France and Flanders, 1919-20; gov. of Bermuda, 4th May, 1922; assumed gov't., 9th Aug., 1922.

ASTON, ARTHUR VINCENT.—B. 1896; ed. King's Sch., Chester, and Queen's Coll., Oxford (open maths. scholar); R.F.A., 1915-18, M.C., 1917; apptd., cadet, M.C.S., 1919; ag. ast. to seni. dist. offr., Prov. Wellesley, June, 1920;
ag. dist. offr., Nebong Tebal, Sept., 1920; ag. harbmr., Malacca, Mar., 1922; ag. collr., income tax, Malacca, Apr., 1922.

ATHAWES, EDWARD JOHN SPOFFORTH, B.A.—Ed. King's Sch., Canterbury and Corpus Christi Coll., Cambridge; called to the bar, Gray's Inn, 1899; dist. comsnr., Corozal, Br. Honduras, Aug., 1914; ditto, Belize, Nov., 1919; ag. atty.-gen., May to Nov., 1919, Jan. to May, 1921 and from July, 1921; ag. ch. jnt., May to July, 1921; res. mag., Jamaica, Oct., 1923.

ATHILL, SAMUEL LAUCHLAND, JUNR.—B.1885; ent. civ. serv., Leeward Is., Sept., 1901; clk. to atty.-gen., Leeward Is., Aug., 1906; sec. to legal affairs inquiry comsnr., Montserrat, 1911; ag. regiar., Montserrat circuit, Feb.-Mar., 1915; deputy coroner, dists. "A" and "B," Antigua, 6th Oct., 1917.

ATHLONE, FIRST EARL OF (created 1917), ALEXANDER CAMBRIDGE, G.C.B. (1911), G.C.V.O. (1904), C.M.G. (1917), D.S.O. (1900).—Served in Matabele campaign, 1896-7; S. African war, 1899-1900; European war, 1914-18; maj., 2nd Life Gds., 1911-19; brevet-col., 1919; G.S.O., 1st grade, 1915; ret. with hon. rank of brig.-gen., 1919; personal A.D.C. to the King from 1919; gov. gen. and commdr.-in-chief, Union of S. Africa, 1923; Grand Cordon of Order of Leopold of Belgium, Croix de Guerre (Belgium); G.O. Leg. Hon. and Croix de Guerre (France); Knt. of Justice of St. John of Jerusalem.

ATKINSON, HON. LLWELYN, B.A., LL.B.—B. 1867; ed. Church Grammar Sch., Launceston, Tas. and Melbourne Univ.; called to the bar, 1893; el. mem. of H. of R., Commonwealth of Australia for Wilmot (Tas.), Dec., 1906; vice-pres. of exec. coun., C. of A., 1923.

ATTERBURY, H. W.—B. 1903; apptd. after compet. exam., cler. offr., C.O., 14th Oct., 1921.

ATTERBURY, JOHN LUCAS.—B. 1877; admitted a solicitor, June, 1899; served in S. African war, 10th Regt. Imperial Yeomanry (Royal Bucks Hussars), Jan., 1900 to June, 1901, medal and four clasps; dist. comsnr., Gold Coast, 19th Dec., 1908; ag. prov. comsnr., Cent. Prov., May-July, 1911; ag. prov. comsnr., Western Prov., Nov.-Dec., 1912; ag. prov. comsnr., Cent. Prov., July, 1915, to May, 1916; ag. prov. comsnr., Western Prov., Nov., 1917, to May, 1918; ag. comsnr., Cent. Prov., Mar. to Dec., 1919; ag. prov. comsnr., Cent. Prov., July-Dec., 1920; dep. prov. comsnr., 1st Jan., 1920; ag. prov. comsnr., Jan.-June, 1921; prov. comsnr., 2nd Aug., 1921; ag. sec. for native affrs., 27th Oct., 1923 to 28th Feb., 1924.

AUBER, STEVEN JEREMIE.—B. 1858; temporary outdoor offr. customs, S. Leone, June, 1878; tide waiter, Aug., 1879; landing waiter, Sept., 1880; sen. ag. measuring survr. of shipping, Aug., 1882; clk. of customs, Gambia, 1883; ch. clk. and cashier, 1892; measuring survr. of shipping, Nov., 1902; clk. to navigation and pilotage bd., June, 1904; offr. in charge of cust. dept., 18th Sept. to 14th Nov., 1906.

AUCHINLECK, GILBERT GRAHAME.—B.Sc. (McGill), F.C.S., B. 1884; ed. West Indies and McGill Univ., Canada; 1st cls. hons. in chemistry and botany, McGill Univ.; govt. laboratory, Leeward Is., 1902-04; McGill Univ., 1904-08; science and 2nd mast., St. Kitts-Nevis gram. schl., 1908-09; supt. of agric., Grenada, 1909-14; ast. dir. of agric. and chemist, Mauritius, 1914; ag. dir. of agric. and regiar., C.C. societies, Dec., 1916 to May, 1917; nominated M.L.C., Mauritius, Jan.-May, 1917; reported on Is. of Rodrigues to the Mauritius govt., 1919; Mauritius del. to Im. Entom. Confoc. in London, 1920; divnl. agric. offr., Ceylon, 1920; seconded to Seychelles to report on the possibilities of agric. development, 1921; has served in defence forces of Antigua, St. Kitts and Mauritius; author of papers on land settl. and various trop. agric. subjects.

AUCKLAND, BISHOP OF, RIGHT REV. ALFRED WALTER AVERILL, D.D.—Ed. St. John's Coll., Oxford (2nd cls. Th. sch.), 1887; M.A., 1897; Ely Coll., 1888; deacon, 1888; priest, 1894; Lon.; formerly curate of St. George's, Hanover Square, 1888-91; Holy Trinity, Dalston, Middlesex, 1891-94; vicar of St. Michael's, Christchurch, N. Zealand, 1894-1909; chaplain of Christchurch Cathedral, 1892-1909; archdeacon of Akaroa, 1903-1909; Bishop of Waiapu, 1910-1913; Bishop of Auckland, 1913.

AUDEN, FRANCIS THOMAS.—B. 1869; ed. Shrewsbury; M.D., Edinburgh Univ., 1906; M.B. and C.M., 1891; formerly res. med. offr., Albany general hosp., Grahamstown, Car Colony; dist. surg., Rustenburg, Transvaal civil surg., S. African field force, 1900-1914 (medal and clasp); dist. comsnr. and govt. med. offr., Caicos Islands, Dec., 1914; govt. med. offr., Turks Is., Oct., 1916; mem. legis. bd., Sept., 1916.

AUDETTE, HON. LOUIS ARTHUR, B.A., LL.B., K.C.—B. 1856; apptd. regar. of exchequer et. of Canada, 1887; ast. judge, exchequer ct., 1912; puisne judge, 1919.

AUSTIN, JAMES.—B. 1867; apptd. to home civ. serv. in cust. dept., 1886; bd. of educa., 1891-1896; clk., educ. offr., Natal, 1st Jan., 1897; 2nd cls. clk., audit dept., 1st Aug., 1900; re-transferred to educn. dept., 1st June, 1901; examg. offr. and statistical clk., 1st July, 1902; ag. acctg. offr., 8th Aug. to 30th Sept., 1903; acctnt. and statistical offr., 1st Jan., 1904; ag. sec., 10th May to 9th Aug., 1907; prov. acctnt., Natal, 1913.

AYLESWORTH, HON. SIR ALLEN BRISTOL, K.C.M.G. (1911), K.C., B.A. (1874), M.A. (1875).—B. 1854; educ. at Newburgh high school and Toronto univ.; Prince of Wales prizeman; bencher of law soc. of Upper Canada; called to bar, Q.C. (Ontario); one of H.M.'s comsners. for settlmt. of Alaska bound., 1903; elected to the H. of C. for North York, 1904; postm-r-gen. of Canada, 1905; min. of just., 1906; British ag. internat. fisheries arbitr., at the Hague, 1910; resigned portfolio and retired, 1911; mem. privy coun. of Canada; called to the Senate, 1923.

AYTON, A. L.—B. 1878; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. 2nd div. civ. ser. and assigned to science and art dept., Mar., 1899; to C.O. July, 1899; clk. in charge of accts., Western Pacific high coman., Dec., 1913; ag. sec., W.P.H.C., 29th Mar., 1915; returned to C.O. as staff clk. in acctn. dept., 29th Jan., 1920; ag. ast. prin., 16th Aug., 1920.

BABER, EDWARD ALFRED.—B. 1888; copyist, survey dept., B. Honduras, 1906; apprentice, ditto, 1906; passed exam. in theory of land surveying; 2nd cls. clk., Aug., 1910; ag. 1st cls. clk., 1911; 1st cls. clk., col. sec.'s dept., Nov., 1913; clk., roads and rivers bd., 1914; ag. ch. clk. and clk. of coun., 1914-15; ag. inspr. of schls. and clk. to bd. of educn., Nov., 1915; senr. clk., col. sec.'s dept., Feb., 1917; ag. ch. clk., etc., for various periods, 1917-21; ag. ast. col. sec.,
Nov., 1921; ag. priv. sec. to Sir Eyre Hutson, May-Aug., 1922; ch. clk., Apr., 1921; astl. col., June, 1923.

BACKWELL, H. F.—B. 1884; ed. at Charterhouse (jun. and sen. scholarships), and at King's Coll., Camb., exhibr.; astl. mast., Portsmouth gram. schl., 1907-8; astl. res., N. Nigeria, 19th Dec., 1908.

BADDELEY, FRANK MORRISH.—B.A., Magdalene Coll., Cambridge, 21st wrangler, Math. tripos, 1896; cadet F.M.S., 1897; passed final exam. in cantonese, Dec., 1900; called to the bar, Inner Temple, Jan., 1913; ag. astl. dist. offr., Kuala Kubu, May, 1901; ditto, Serendah, Nov., 1901; recd. thanks of govt. in connection with Ulu Selangor riots, Feb., 1902; revenue auditor, Pahang, Jan., 1904; ag. dist. offr., Telebu Jan., 1905; ag. dist. astl. prot. of chinese, Singapore, Aug., 1905; ag. dist. offr., Xmas Is., Oct., 1906; ag. offr. assignee, Singapore, Apl., 1907; apptd. a currency commnr., May, 1907; dist. offr., Kuantan, June, 1908; supt. govt. monopolies dept., S. Stltmsts., Sept., 1909; P.M.G., S. Stltmsts., Feb., 1916; food controller, Oct., 1920; under-sec., S. Stltmsts., July, 1921; ag. col. sec., S. Stltmsts., Apr., 1922.

BAGSHAWE, ARTHUR WILLIAM GARRARD.—C.M.G. (1915), B.A., M.B., B.C., D.P.H., Camb., M.R.C.S., Eng., L.R.C.P., Lond.; ed. at Marlborough Coll. and Caius Coll., Camb., served in resident hosp. appts., 1896-1899; med. offr., Uganda Prot., Oct., 1900; served as med. offr. on Lango expdttn., 1901; served with Anglo-German bdnry. comm., 1902-4; employed in sleeping sickness extended investigations in Uganda, Apr., 1906, to May, 1907; director of sleeping sickness bureau, 1908.

BAILEY, EDWARD LISLE.—B. 1886; extra clk. col. sec.'s off., Barbado, Mar., 1904; 4th clk. treasy., Mar., 1908; ag. 3rd clk. on several occasions.

BAILEY, EDWARD SHEPPARD.—B. 1857; 2nd clk. col. treas. Barbados, 1880; ch. clk. 1892; sec. to emigrn. commn., 1893; ag. col. treas., 1894 and on other occasion; clk. to plantation commrs., July, 1903; man. of agric. bank, 1907.

BAILEY, JOHN F.—Dir. of botanic gardens Adelaide, S. Australia, 1917; formerly dir. of Brisbane gardens.

BAILWARD, A. N.—Astl. dist. commnr., Kenya, Jan., 1920.

BAIN, NORMAN KERR, B.A. Cantab.—Cadet S. Stltmsts., Jan., 1907; ag. dist. offr., Malacca, Sept., 1907; ag. astl. to res., Malacca, July, 1910; offr. of ds. V., 31st Mar., 1911; ag. dist. offr., Kuala Langat, 29th Mar., 1914; ag. astl. to res. and harbmr., Malacca, Mar., 1918; ag. agent, food controller in addition, 1919; ag. dist. offr., Port Dickson, Negri-Sembilan, Jan., 1921; ag. 2nd mag., Kinta, July, 1921; mag., Ipoh, Aug., 1921; ch. astl. dist. offr., Kinta, Aug., 1922.

BAKER, ALAN CUSTANCE.—B.A., Oxon.; cadet, S. Stltmsts., Dec., 1908; attchd. to land office, Malacca, Jan., 1909; ag. dist. offr., Alor Gajah, 1912; ag. dep. regist., sup. ct., Singapore, Apr. and Sept., 1912; ag. dist. offr., B. Pulau, 1913; joined offr. cadet batt., July, 1916; demob. June, 1919; officiating astl. supl., monopolies, Penang, June, 1919; officiating astl. offl. assignee and dep. regist., sup. ct., Penang, Aug., 1919; ag. 2nd mag., Aug., 1919; capt., Penang volunteers, Nov., 1919; supermy. offr., cls. III, Oct., 1920; ag. astl. offr. assignee, Penang, Nov., 1920; ag. 2nd mag., Penang, Jan., 1921.

BAKER, ERNEST LAIDLAW.—B. 1880; ed. Australia; clk., col. sec.'s office, Fiji, 1901; shorthand writer, legis. coun., 1906; sec., Albert Park Bd.
