KERSHAW, HENRY VALDRE.—Capt., 19th Batt., London Regt., adjutant Nairobi defence force; served as lieut. in 2nd Middlesex Regt. in African War, 1899-1902 (Queen's medal and clasp); asst. traffic supt., Jamaica govt. rlyw., Apl., 1906; travelling auditor, Lagos rlyw., Apl., 1908; ag. chief acctnt., Sierra Leone govt. rlyw., Mar., 1909; asst. acctnt., Lagos rlyw., June, 1909 to Dec., 1910; asst. chief acctnt., Uganda rlyw., 23rd Oct., 1912 to 31st Mar., 1915; deputy chief acctnt., Uganda rlyw., 1st Apl., 1915.

KETTLE, JAMES DAVID, B.So. (Lond.), F.I.C., F.C.S.—B. 1879; asst. govt. analyst, Trinidad, 1922.

KEYTE, CHARLES ROBERT, Mem. I.R.E.—B. 1883; offr. in charge, wireless station, Georgetown, B. Guiana, 1909; senr. engr., with rank of sub-lieut., naval wireless station, Demerara, May, 1915; engr.-operator in charge, wireless station, Ocean Is., Aug., 1915; ag. conf. clk., res. commr.'s office, Gilbert and Ellice Is., June, 1918, to Feb., 1919; a dep. commr. for the W. Pacifico, Feb., 1919; offr. in charge at govt. headqu. during absence of res. commr., May to Nov., 1919; dir., posts and telegraphs, Somaliland, Nov., 1920; ag. D.P.W., Apr., to Oct., 1924.

KIDD, CAPT. W. R., M.C., B.A. (Oxon).—Asst. dist. commr., Kenya, Feb., 1920.

KILBY, WALTER WHEATLEY.—B. 1890; ed. Reading Schl. and St. John's Coll., Oxford; White scholar, 1908-12; 2nd cls. class. mods.; 3rd cls. lit. hum.; asst. dist. commr., Gold Coast, 29th Apl., 1914; ag. dist. commr., Oct., 1914, to June, 1915, and from Nov., 1915, to Dec., 1916.

KILPIN, SIR ERNEST FULLER, K.C.M.G. (1910), C.M.G. (1901).—B. 1854; clk. and shorthand writer, col. sec.'s office, Cape, June, 1876; priv. sec. to Hon. J. Gordon Sprigg, premier and col. sec., Feb., 1878, to June, 1890; clk. assist. of the house of assem., June, 1880; clk., 16th July, 1897; has served as sec. on the following Cape govt. comms.: Dorthcia, 1877; war expenditure, 1881; Liesbeek municipality, 1883; diamond laws, 1887; liquor laws, 1889; lighthouses, 1890; fisheries, 1892; scab., 1893; defence, 1896; and acted as priv. sec. to premier, the Hon. Sir T. C. Scanlan, Feb. and Mar., 1883; sec. to the Anglo-German coman. on Angra Pequena and W. Coast claims, 1886; author of parly. agents' manual, Cape, 1902, 2nd edtn., 1906; of S. African Union and private bill legislation, 1908, and editor of civil service list, 1886-1910; prepared standing rules and orders for the legis. coun., Rhodesia, 1898; has frequently been consulted on parly. procedure in South Africa; at the invitation of the O.R.C. govt., assisted in the inauguration of parly. institutions there in Dec., 1907; was examiner for shorthand under civ. ser. comms., 1889-1910; is a J.P. for the Cape Province; chief sec., S. African National Convention, 1908-1909; retired, 1910.

KILPIN, RALPH.—B. 1887; ed. Diocesan Coll., Rondebosch, S. Africa; clk. of papers, Cape H. of A., 1906; clk. of papers, Union H. of A., 1910; 2nd clk.-asst., 1917; clk.-asst., 1920; admitted sworn translator (Eng. and Dutch), sup. ct., of S. Africa, 1912; assessor apptd. by admtr., Cape exec. comtes, elections and elec. of senators since 1910; on active serv., E. Africa, 1916-17; author of "The Old Cape House."

KIMBELL, ALFRED HENRY.—B. 1878; ed. at Otago Boys' High Schl., N.Z.; entd. N.Z. pub. serv., 1895; held various positions in P.W.D., including land purchase offr.; under-sec. of mines, 1920.

KINDER, F. T.—Asst. engr., Singapore rlyw., Mar., 1900; asst. supt. of wks., S. Stilimta., Mar., 1903; ag. supt. of wks. and surveys, Malacca, Mar., 1908; asst. supt. of wks., Penang, Apr., 1909; asst. engr., Jan., 1910;...
exec. engr., prov. Wellesley, Jan., 1910; exec. engr., supernmy., Penang, Jan., 1912; ag. exec. engr., Malacca, June, 1913; exec. engr., supernmy., Penang, Mar., 1915; ag. exec. engr., Singapore, July, 1919; exec. engr., grade II., Aug., 1919; ag. exec. engr., grade I., Malacca, 28th Jan., 1920, and 3rd Mar., 1920; ag. dep. col. engr., Penang, 20th Feb., 1920, and 26th Mar., 1921; ag. exec. engr., P.W.D., Singapore, 14th Feb., 1921.

KINDERSLEY, WILLIAM LORING.—B. 1868; ed. Marlborough Schl. and Exeter Coll., Oxford (B.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., 1893; priv. sec. to lieut.-govr., Sept., 1893; off. asst. to govt. agt., Uva Prov., Oct., 1895; addl. pol. mag., Matara, Dec., 1895; pol. mag., Kandy, May, 1897; dist. judge, Kalutara, Apr., 1903; asst. govt. agt., Trincomalee, Sept., 1894; Chilaw, Nov., 1905; Puttalam, Apr., 1906; Matara, Mar., 1907; govt. agt., N.C. KING, CLEMENT HAMPDEN.—B. 1876; ed. Queen's Coll., B. Guiana; ag. 6th cls., elk., police dept., B. KING, GEORGE HOWARD.—Ag. elk., treasy., St. Kitts, 1894; ag. rev. offr., Nevis, 1895; elk., P.O., St. Kitts, 1896; ag. elk. regis.'s office, Nevis, 1897; rev. offr., Nevis, Jan., 1898; govt. offr., St. Kitts, 1899; rev. offr., Nevis, June, 1906; 1st elk., P.O., and sub-inspr. of schls., St. Kitts, 1906; ag. postmr., St. Kitts, 1914; postmr., May, 1915.

KING, HOWARD THOMPSON MCKENZIE.—Clerical asst., comary dept., B. Guiana, 1st July, 1882; ag. ast. comary., June, 1884 and Sept., 1885; confirmed as ast. comary., 5th July, 1887; dist. comary., 1st Dec., 1890; comanr. of N.W. dist., and stip. mag., 9th July, 1907.

KING, HON. JAMES H., M.D.—B. 1873; ed. St. Mary's Coll., Montreal, and Laval Univ.; private tutor; called to the bar 1886; K.C., 1899; special law offr., Quebec, 1891; dep. atty.-gen., Quebec, 1905; mem. of commr. for revision of code of civil proceed., 1893-97; commr. for revision of statutes of Quebec, 1909-10; published "Traité théorique et pratique du droit criminel"; "Manuel du juge de paix"; "Annotated Criminal Code."

LANE, CHARLTON ADELBERG GUSTAVUS.—B. 1890; ed. Winchester and Univ. Coll., Oxford; B.A. (Hons.), 1911; astt. dist. commr., E.A.P., 1913; ag. dist. commr., 1918; attd. secretariat, 1918; ag. senr. astt. sec., 1919; senr. astt. sec., 1920; dist. commr., Zanzibar, 1923.

LANG, HON. SIR FREDERIC WILLIAM, KT. BACH. (1916).—B. 1852; mem. of H. of R., New Zealand, 1893-1905, and since 1906; chmn. of commt., 2nd Aug., 1912, to 26th June, 1913; speaker from 26th June, 1913 to 1922; M.L.C., 1924.

LANGE, ANDRE PHILIPPE, M.R.C.S., Eng.—B. 1863; entd. med. serv., Trinidad, 21st Jan., 1890; dist. med. offr., 15th July, 1915.

LANGHAM-CARTER, W.—Ed. at Bradfield Coll., Berks.; cadet, S. Sitilima., 1890; passed final exam. in Malay, Dec., 1892; ag. dist. offr., Malacca, Jan., 1896; dist. offr., prov. Wellesley,
April, 1897; continued to act at Malacca; ag. collr. of ld. rev. and regir. of deeds, Singapore, Dec., 1898; inspr. prisons, S.S., Jan. to May, 1901; asst. P.M.G., Penang, Dec., 1901; 2nd magis., Sing., Aug., 1902; ag. collr. of land rev., and regir. of deeds, Sing., Sept., 1902; apptd. to cls. III, B, Jan., 1903; 2nd mag., Sing., Jan., 1905, but cont. to act as collr. of land rev.; ag. sen. dist. offr., Prov. Wellesley, April, 1907; senr. dist. offr., Prov. Wellesley, April, 1911; British adviser, Kelantan, Dec., 1912; ag. dist. judge and 1st mag., Singapore, May, 1916; offr., cls. I., Oct., 1919; ag. res. councillor, Malacca, 15th Mar., 1922.

LANGLEY, EDWARD RALPH.—B. 1889; ed. Cheltenham Coll. and Caius Coll., Cambridge; B.A. (Cantab.); war service, E. Africa 1917-18; passed lower stand. exam. in Temne; asst. dist. commnr., Sierra Leone, 29th Apr., 1914; ag. asst. col. sec. in 1916 and 1918; ag. senr. asst. col. sec. May to Oct., 1919; dist. commnr., 21st Aug., 1922.

LANGSTON, STEPHEN HORATIO.—B. 1877; ed. Westminster Schl. and Keble Coll., Oxon. H.A.; cadet, F.M.S., Nov., 1900; ag. asst. dist. offr., Kuala Selangor, Jan., 1902; passed cadet, May, 1903; ag. asst. dist. offr., Kuala Kubu, Dec., 1903; ag. asst. dist. offr., Serendah, May, 1904; ag. asst. dist. treas., K. Lumpur, Dec., 1904; ag. dist. treas., Seremban, Mar., 1905; 2nd asst. dist. offr., Tapah, June, 1905; ag. dist. treas., Raub, Aug., 1905, and July, 1906; offr., cls. V, Jan., 1906; ag. asst. dist. offr., Raub, Mar., 1906; ag. asst. collr. of land rev., Seremban, Aug., 1906-Feb., 1908; ag. asst. dist. offr., Ipoh, May, 1909; ag. 2nd asst. dist. offr., K. Kangar, Jan., 1910; ag. dist. offr., K. Langat, June, 1911; offr., cls. IV, Jan., 1912; dist. offr., coast, Neg. Semb., Apr., 1912-Apr., 1913; dist. offr., Tampin, Apr., 1914; censor, Penang, S. S., June, 1916; ag. 2nd mag., Penang, Oct., 1916; asst. dist. judge, Penang, Oct., 1916; ag. asst. regir. of imports and exports in addn., Aug., 1917; offr., cls. III, Jan., 1918; offr., cls. II, Jan., 1919; dist. offr., Batang Padang, Aug., 1920; mag., K. Lumpur, Sept., 1920; ag. collr. of land rev., K. Lumpur, Dec., 1920; ag. temp. as 2nd mag., K. Lumpur, in addn., May, 1921; mag., K. Lumpur, June, 1921; ag. collr., land rev., K. Lumpur, Sept., 1921; on sp. duty as town planning adminstr., Apr., 1922; valuer-gen., Jan., 1923.

LANKTREE, CHARLES JOSEPH DANE.—B. 1896; on mil. serv., Sept. 1914; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., October, 1921; addt., Colombo Kachcheri, Nov., 1921; ag. office asst. to govt. agt., Prov. of Sabaragamuwa, Oct., 1922; office asst. to govt. agt., Cent. Prov., Mar., 1924.

LANSDOWN, CHARLES WILLIAM HENRY, B.A., LL.B.—Clk., C.G.R., Mar., 1889; clk., C.S.O., Capetown, Oct., 1893; atty.-gen.'s off., Nov., 1894; mag.'s clk., Aliwal N., Feb., 1896; pte. sec. to atty.-gen., Aug., 1898; ag. chf. clk. to sol.-gen., Grahamstown, May, 1901; ag. asst. mag., Port Elizabeth, Sept., 1901; ch. clk. and pte. sec. to atty.-gen., Oct., 1901; addnl. legal adviser, July, 1907; prof. asst., atty.-gen.'s off., Capetown, Apr., 1912; law adviser, dep. of justice, Union of S. Africa, Aug., 1918.

LANSDOWNE, 5TH MARQUIS OF (Gt. Brit., creat. 1784), K.G., P.C., G.C.M.G. (1884), G.C.S.I., G.C.I.E.; Rt. Hon. Henry Charles Keith Fitz Maurice, eldest son of the 4th Marquis.—B. 1845; succeeded his father in 1866; was under-secr. for war from Apr., 1872, to Feb., 1874, and under-secr. India Office, May to Aug., 1880; gov.-gen. of Canada, 1883; viceroy of India, Nov., 1888; sec. of state for war, 1886-1900; sec. of state foreign affairs, 1900-1905; chancellor of Order of St. Michael and St. George, 1917.

LAPOINTE, HON. EMERSON.—B. 1876; Rimouski Coll. and Laval Univ., Quebec (LL.B.); advoc., K.C., Quebec, 1908; cl. br. for Kamouraska to H.C., 12th Feb., 1904; sec.-g.a., 1904, 1908, 1911 and 1917; ed. byc., Quebec E., 27th Oct., 1919; re-elec., g.e., 12 min. of marine and fisheries in King slzn., 29th Dec., 1921; del. to League of Nat. assem., 1922; min. of just. and atty.-gen., 1922.

LAROCHELLE, MICHEL GAULTIER, B.A., LL.D.—B. 1868; ed. at Nicolet Coll. and Laval Univ.; priv. sec. to Sir Wilfrid Laurier, 1886-90; barr.-at-law, 1891; recorder of St. Hilaire, Montreal, 1896; mem. of civ. aer. coman., 1908.

LASCELLES, SIR ALFRED GEORGE & BACH.—(1913), B.A.—Univ. Coll., 2nd class med. hist.; b. 1857; called to bar, Inner Temple, 1885; acted on several occasions as pres. of dist. ct., Cyprus; puisne judge; pres. of dist. ct., Paphos, 1892; Larnaca, 1893; ag. puisne judge, June, 1896; Queen's advoc., Feb., 1896; pres. dist. ct., Nassau, 1896; Queen's advoc., 1898; atty.-gen. of Ceylon, 1902; ag. ch. just., Mar., 1906; atty.-gen., 1906; chief just., May, 1911; retired, 1914.

LASSALLER, CHARLES FRANCIS, M.D., M.B.C.M. (Hons.), Edin., D.P.H., Oxf., B. 1871; ed. Univ. of Edinburgh; postgrad. work at London schl. of trop. med., 1921; Polyclinic, London, 1902; Univ. Coll., Lond., 1902; Lister inst. of Preventive Medicine, mem. of B.M.A.; mem. of coun. of med. of Trinidad and Tobago; apptd. govt. med. of Trinidad, 3rd Nov., 1894; port health and med. inspr. of immigrants, Trinidad, 1st Jan., 1895; asst. med. offr., inspr. of health, 7th Dec., 1895; has acted as asst. M.O.H., res. surg. at main hosp., and also as D.M.O. at Cedros, Nassau, St. Joseph, Arima, Chaguaramas and Town; author of "Notes of lectures on midwifery for Midwives," and contributions to med. journals.

LAST, JOSEPH SPURRIER.—B. 1897; ag. serv., Egypt and Palestine, 1915-1917; ag. commnr., Zanzibar, 3rd Dec., 1919.

LATCHFORD, HON. FRANCIS ROBERT, K.C.—B. 1856; ed. Ottawa Univ.; called to bar, 1886; K.C., 1898; elec. to Ontario, 1899; re-elec., 1902; min. of pub. wks., Ont., 1899; atty.-gen., 1904-5; judge, chancery div. high ct. of just., Ontario, 1906; ch. just. divnl. ct., sup. ct., 1923.

LATREILLE, HERBERT ROWLAND.—B. 1878; clk., asst., col. sec.'s office, Jamaica, Jan., 1901; asst., June, 1905; 2nd cls. clk., Oct., 1916; cls. clk., Apr., 1917; ag. sen. clk., 1918 to June, 1919; sen. asst. treas., Tangany Territory, June, 1919; ag. dep. treas., Dec., 1920 to Mar., 1922, Dec., 1922 to Sept., 1923 and Mar. to Oct., 1924.

LAUDER, JOHN ILES.—2nd clk., regir. prov. marshal's offr., Dominica, Jan., 1904; ag. asst. mast., Dominica gram. schl., May to 4th Aug., 1905; gov't. offr., treas., Sept., 1905; clk. to commnr. and clk. of exec. Montserrat, Oct., 1906; educnal. offr., Aug., 1907; deputy coroner, Dist. "I," Mar., 1911; mem. of road bd., Apr., 1911; ag. cert. botanic station, 20th Jan. to 13th Feb., 1912; J.P., Mar., 1912; ag. mag., Dist. "I," 1912.
LAW, JOHN CRAWFORD.—Ed. at the Royal Mil. Coll., Kingston, Canada; comsnr. in 10th Regt., Royal Grenadiers of Toronto, Oct., 1897; seconded for serv. with the 3rd (S.S.) batt., Royal Canadian Regt., for Impl. garrison duty, Halifax, N.S., 1st May, 1902; capt., 3rd Sept., 1902; returned to 10th Regt. as capt.; seconded for serv. as asst. collr., E. Africa Prot., 15th July, 1904.

LAW, Y. P., B.A. (Cantab).—B. 1888; asst. mast., educn. dept., Hong Kong, 1915; ag. inspr. of vernac. schls., 1915 and 1917; mem., bd. of examra., 1919-22; inspr., vernac. schls., 1920 and 1921; hon. sec., bd. of educn., in addn., 1920-22; inspr., vernac. schls., New Territories, 1922.

LAWLEY, HON. SIR ARTHUR, G.C.S.I. (1911); G.C.I.E. (1906); K.C.M.G. (1901).—B. 1860; sec. to adminstr., S. Rhodesia, May, 1896; dep.-administr., Matabeleland, Nov., 1896; administrator., Matabeleland, Dec., 1898; ag. administrator., Mashonaland, July, 1899; gov. of W. Aust., Jan., 1901; lt.-gov., Transvaal, 16th Aug., 1902; ag. gov. of Transvaal and O.R.C. and high comsnr., 1903; chmn. of ex. coun., pres. of leg. coun., mem. I.C.C.; gov. of Madras, 1905.

LAWRENCE, A. S.—Capt., reserve of officers; major, Middlesex Hussars; served with I.Y. in S. Africa, 1900-1902 (Queen’s medal with 3 clasps, King’s medal with 2 clasps, ment. in desps.); served with 6th Batt., K.A.R., Somaliland, 1905-1911 (African General Serv. medal with clasp “Somaliland 1908-1910,” ment. in desps.); asst. res., N. Nigeria, 1st Feb., 1911; comdt., Somaliland camel corps constaby., 13th Oct., 1913.

LAWRENCE, MAJOR ERNEST HARRY THORNE, O.B.E. (1919).—Capt., reserve of offrs., 4th Batt. Connaught Rangers; served in S. Africa with 20th Batt. I.Y., 1900-1901; 2nd lieut., 5th Batt. Connaught Rangers, Oct., 1901; seconded to remount dept. and served in United States and S. Africa, 1902 (Queen’s medal and four clasps); passed promotion to capt., 1903; schl. of musketry, Hythe (distinguished), 1904; A.S.C. transport course, Aldershot, 1904; army physical training, Aldershot, 1905; instr. of musketry, 5th Connaught Rangers, 1906; instr. of signalling, Aldershot, 1906; army veterinary course, Aldershot, 1906; passed for maj., 1906; mil. schl. of instr., Chelsea, 1903 and 1907 (special); dist. supt. of pol., Uganda, June, 1907; R.I.C. course, 1909; ag. comsnr. of pol. and prisons, Uganda, Mar. to Sept., 1910, Sept., 1911 to Jan., 1912, and from Mar.-Sept., 1914; asst. comsnr. of pol. and prisons, 1st Apr., 1911; offr. in ch., defence measures, Uganda, on outbreak of War with Germany with temp. rank of major; provost marshal, Uganda, Aug., 1914; comdt., Uganda Vol. Res., Aug., 1914; comdt., Uganda Pol. Service Batt., Dec., 1914; served in G.E. Africa till 15th Jan., 1917 (ment. in desps.); major, res. of offrs., Jan., 1917; ag. comsnr. of pol. and prisons, Uganda, Sept., 1917 to Oct., 1918, and from Apr.-July, 1921; mem., Uganda Development Coman., 1921; comsnr. of pol. and prisons, 12th May, 1922.

LAWRENCE, JOHN DUNCAN.—Ed. at Clepington schl., Dundee, and civ. serv. coll., Aberdeen; prelim. in arts (higher mathematics and German), Aberdeen Univ.; govt. trav. schl. master, Falkland Is., Sept., 1896, to Jan., 1902; 2nd asst. insp. of schls., B. Guiana, Oct., 1903.

LAWRENCE, W. C.—B. 1870; apptd., after exam., 3rd cls. messenger, C.O., 16th Apr., 1904; 2nd cls. messenger, 23rd May, 1907.
LAWSON, Hon. H. S. W.—B. 1875; M.L.A. for Castlemaine, Victoria, 1899; has sat continuously in State Parlmt. since 1899; comsrr. of crown lands and survey, Dec., 1913 to Nov., 1915; afterwards atty.-gen., solr. gen. and min. of public instrm., premier and atty.-gen. since 21st Mar., 1918; premier and min. of agr., 1920-24.

LAWSON, R. A.—Asst. traffic man., Uganda rly., Apr., 1919.

LEA, F.—B. 1876; apptd., after exam., 3rd cls. messngr., C.O., 23rd July, 1907; 2nd cls. messngr., 30th Jan., 1912; on military service from 19th Apr., 1918, to 9th Feb., 1919.

LEA, WALTER ALBERT, A.M.I.C.E.—B. 1833; ed. at Carpenters' Company's Coll. and West Ham Tech. Inst.; employed by Messrs. Perry & Co., Ltd., Contractors, Bow, 1900 to 1914; dist. engrnr., Br. Guiana, 3rd Dec., 1914; seconded to sea defence work, Feb., 1916.

LEACH, FRANK, M.C., B.A. (Oxon).—B. 1898; on mily. serv., July, 1917; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., May, 1921; stdt. to the secretariat, June, 1921; office asst. to astt. gov't. agt., Hambantota, Nov., 1922; ag. astt. stimt. offr., Oct., 1923.

LEACH, JOHN VINCENT, M.B.E. (1924).—Ed. Stonyhurst Coll., England; admitted solr. sup. ct., Jamaica, 1881; res. mag., 1888; has frequently been specially apptd. to conduct important inquiries and to report thereon.

LEADBETTER, SIDNEY.—B. 1902; apptd. after compet. exam., cler. offr., C.O., 4th May, 1920.

LEAVITT, CLYDE.—B. 1878; ed., High Schl., Bellaire, Mich., Univ. of Mich. (B.A., 1901; M.Sc. For., 1904); ent. U.S. forest serv., as student asst., 1903; apptd. forest asst., 1904, with successive appts. as ch. of boundaries, asth. ch., office of organization, ch., office of organization, dist. forester, and astt. forester; ch. forester, comsrr. of conservn. and bd. of rly. comsrrs., Canada, 1912; ch. fire inspr., bd. of rly. comsrrs., 1921; mem., soc. of American Foresters; successively, pres. and sec., Can. Soc. of Forest Engrns.

LECHMERE-GUPPY, GARETH EVERARD.—B. 1874; entd. civ. ser., Trinidad, 20th May, 1895; seconded for special serv. to water authority and sewerage bd., 1904-1905; ag. inspr. of immigr., in 1903, 1910, 1912 to 1913; statistical clk. and librnr., colonial secretariat, Trinidad, 15th July, 1915; sec. to income tax comttee., estimates comttee., tenders comttee., and civ. serv. comttee.; J.P. for the col. and Tobago; dep. sub-intendant crown lands, Dec., 1920.

LECHMERE-GUPPY, P. (Jnr.).—Supernumerary clk., audit off., Trinidad, 1889; 4th clk., sub-treas., San Fernando, 1st Jan., 1892; landing waiter, customs, 1st May, 1894; clk., col. treas., 1st Mar., 1898; acted as warden, Tacarigua, in 1902, 1904 and 1905; sub-recvr., postmaster, collr. of cust. and harbr. mast., Tobago, 16th Oct., 1917; collected fresh-water fishes of Trinidad for British Museum.

LECLEZIO, Sir Henry L., K.C.M.G. (1915); C.M.G. (1897).—Elected mem. of coun. of govt. for dist. of Moka, Mauritius.

LEDEBOER, CLAUD MARIUS.—Served in S. African Constab., 1901-7; Bech. Prot. police, from 1907; sub-inspr.; Bech. Prot. police, 1st Apr., 1914; astt. res. mag.; passed Cape civ. serv. lower law exam. and 2nd grade Sechuan exam.; ag. res. mag., 1921; res. mag., 1921.

LEE, H. N., O.B.E. (Mily.) 1918.—Ed. Portsmouth Grammar schl. and King's Coll., London, 1906-11; articles, Inst. of Chartered Acctnts., London; col. audit dept., 1913; astt. audr., E.A.P., Jan., 1914; R.A. Expedy. Force, 1914-19 (ment. in despr.); senr. astt. audr., Kenya, 1919.

LEE, Hon. Sir W. H., K.C.M.G. (1922), Bach. (1920).—M.H.A., Tasmania; premier, sec., and min. for educn., 1916-22.

LEES, HENRY BABBY, M.C., M.I.C.E., M. and Cy. E., F.S.I.—B. 1880; dist. engnr., P.W.D., Ceylon, 1905; ag. prov. engnr., Prov., 1908; extra astt. dir. of pub. wks., 2nd astt. dir., pub. wks., 1912; ag. astt. & pub. wks., 1913 and 1920; on active serv. R.E.'s in France, Belgium, Italy, and with army of occupation on the Rhine, 1915-19; mem., R.E., M.C., Legion d'Honneur, Croix de Guerier, twice ment. in despr.; comsrr. of water supply and drainage, 1920; chmn., cent. rev., 1920; dir., pub. wks. and mem., advisory x Palestine, 1923.

LEEE, CHARLES WILLIAM.—Astt. astt. comsrr., S. Nigeria, Sept., 1906; trans. treasry. dept., 1907; acted as supervsr. customs, 1906, and as junior astt. sec. n. served as finan. offr., Cameroons Expedy., 1916; dep. treas., 1921; ag. treas., May to 1921 and June to Dec., 1923.

LEEE, CAPT. ERNEST BENJAMIN.—3rd B. Yorks Regt., res. of offr.; served in S. African War, 1900-1901 (Queen's medal clasps); subaltern in G. Coast Regt., 2nd B. 1905; capt., 9th Jan., 1908; priv. sec. and adj. to gov'r. of G. Coast, Nov., 1910, to Feb., trav. comsrr., Gambia, 6th Nov., 1911; served with Cameroons Expedy. Force, 1915-16.

LEK-WARNER, W. H.—B. 1880; ed., Rugby and Univ. Coll., Oxford (scholar), 1st class, mods., 1901; 2nd cls. lit. hum., 1903; barrister-at-law, 1912; cadet, F.M.S. ser., 1903; passed cadet, 1905; ag. astt. dist. Batu Gajah, Jan., 1907; ag. 2nd astt. astt. gen., and priv. sec. to res. gen., May, 1908; priv., 1910; bonus exam. in Tamil, 1910; ag. Brunei, 1910-11; temporary 2nd cls. dist. Feb.-Oct., 1912; resumed in Brunei, 1913; sec. to high comsrr., Malay States, and ag. to O.A.G., S. Stiltsm., July-Sept., 1914; priv. sec. to gov., Sept., 1914; A.D.C., Oct., 1914; also ag. sec. to high comsrr., Malay States, Jan., 1916; astt. to res., Malacca, Nov., 1916; seconded under F.O. vice-consul, Sabang, Jan.-Mar., 1917; ag. vice-consul, via, Apr. to July, 1917; seconded for mil. intell. dept., W.O., Sept., 1917; temp. 2nd lieut., Feb., 1918; seconded under F.O., Mar., 1918; temp. hony. capt., sp. list, 1918; supernumy. offr., cls. III., Jan., 1919; agent, food contrlr., Penang, Aug., 1919; food contrlr., Jan., 1920; supernumy. offr., Nov., 1920; astt. for sp. duty, col. secret., Singapore, 10th Jan., 1922.

LEFEBVRE, PHILIP LLEWELLIN.—B. 1875; at Victoria Coll., Jersey, and Brighton Coll., Sch. clk., G.P.O., Cape Town, Feb., 1896; clk., gen.'s off., Feb., 1896; clk. to res. mag., Grey, Feb., 1896; clk. to res. mag., East Lancs., Sept., 1898; clk., sol. gen.'s off., Grahamstown, Apr., 1899; clk., astt. gen.'s off. (treason tr.), Cape Town, Sept., 1900; B.A., Cape Univ.; clk. to astt.-gen., O.R.C., June, 1901; sec. law dept., Oct., 1904; ag. clk. to legis. com., July, 1906; relieving mag., 1912; mag., T. Nchu, May, 1917; joint editor of law J. O.R.C., 1900-1906.

LEFFLER, WILLIAM FREDERICK.—Clk. stb. broh. of treas., Feb., 1881; clk. res. mag.,
ARNARVON, June, 1883; master's off., Kimberley, 1886; ag. clk. to esp. ct., Dec., 1886; deeds l., Cape Town, Sept., 1887; chf. clk., high sheriff, July, 1894; chf. clk., insolvent and law anchor, master's off., July, 1897; ag. clk., deeds off., July, 1899; chf. clk. and ast. regis. deeds, Cape Town, June, 1901; ag. regis., Dec., 1918; ag. regis. of deeds, Cape Town, Oct. to Dec., 1919; regis. deeds, Transvaal Prov., Apr., 1922; mprlr., "Law of transfer duty"; editor, Foster's Deeds Office Practice," and "Legal Forms."

LEFROY, Hon. Sir Henry B., K.C.M.G., C.M.G. (1903).—Elected M.L.A., Western Australia, 1892; re-elected, 1894 and 1897; min. education, May, 1897; min. of mines, May, 1898; gen. for W. Australia in London, 1901; signed, 1904; min. for lands and agric., July, 1916; premier, 1917; resigned, Apr., 1919.

LEGAT, Charles Edward.—B.S.; joined rest dept., Cape Colony, May, 1898; ast. to pt., George, Apr., 1899; ast., Concordia Station, Jan., 1901; dist. forest off., Hanover, Aug., 1901; transfd. to Transvaal govt. as forestry ast., Apr., 1902; conservator of rests, Transvaal, Oct., 1904; 1st grade conservator, Transvaal, Apr., 1912; chief conservator forests, Union of S. Africa, 31st May, 1913.

LEGGE, Charles Arthur Lionel.—B. 1879; clerical ast., B. Guiana, May, 1897; 6th class ft., cust., June, 1899; 5th class clk., pol. dep., Dec., 1900; lieut., B. G. Artillery, 1901; attached to No. 32 Coy. R.G.A., Portmouth, July, 1904; cert. in depression range finding, July, 1904; Hythe musk. cert., Aug., 1904; sub-instr. of pol. and excise, Grenada, Oct., 1904; promoted capt., B. Guiana Artillery, seconded, Dec., 1904; mem. local health authority, St. Andrew's parish, Grenada, Jan., 1905; ag. ch. of pol., Grenada, from June, 1907.

LEGGE, Cyril Henry Ethelwood.—B. 1883; joined B. Guiana civ. serv., 22nd June, 1901; k. in surg. gens. office, cent. bd. of health, stomas and asty.-gens. office; commissary, 24th July, 1906; ag. stip. mag., 29th Mar., 1914 to 1st Dec., 1916; stip. mag. 2nd grade, 1st Dec., 1916; stip. mag., 1st grade, 29th Mar., 1921; passed final bar exams., 1912; called to the bar, Inns Inn, 28th July, 1922; passed gov't. India exam.

LEIGH-CLARE, Harry James Leigh.—B. 1891; on mil'y. serv., Jan., 1915; cadet, Ceylon, 'eb., 1920; attd. to Colombo Kaschcheri, Mar., 1920; attd. to office of food contrl., Apr., 1920; g. office ast. to govt. agt., S. Prov., Mar., 1921; office ast. to govt. agt., Cent. Prov., Apr. and ext., 1922; ag. ast. govt. agt., Kandy, May, 1922; ditto to govt. agt. Cent. Prov., Apr., 1922; g. ast. govt. agt., Kandy, Mar. to Sept., 1922; idnl. landing waiter, cust., Colombo, Oct., 1924.

LEMBERGER, Maurice.—B. 1900; apptd. after compet. exam., ast. clk., 23rd Apr., 1918; on mil'y. serv., 26th Aug., 1918 to 27th Feb., 1920; apptd. cler. offr., 1st Jan., 1920; trans. to 'O. stores dept., Mar., 1920; trans. to C.O., 1st sept., 1923.

LE MESSURIER, Henry Wm., C.M.G. (1916).—B. 1848; J.P., Newfoundland, 1879; M.H.A., 1885 to 1890; 3rd landing waiter and ast. tide irrvr. of cust., Newfild., 1894 to 1897; ast. collr. nd sec. to bl. of rep., 1897; dep. min. of cust., with title of ast. collr., 1898; superintended organisation of cust. dept., and planned and inaugurated cust. service in connection with Reid Newfild. Co.'s steamer and rly. system, 1898; corrpdnt., C.I.R., B. of T., 1905; served as commissariat clk. under ast. commissaries prior to removal of the Imperial troops.

LEMIEUX, Hon. Rodolphe, K.C., LL.D.—B. 1866; ed. Nicolet Coll. and Laval Univ., R.C.L. (1891), LL.D. (1896); called to the bar, 1891; prof. of law, Laval Univ., 1896-1906; Q.C., Quebec, 1898; K.C. by Dom. Govt., 1904; elec. to H. of C., 1896; re-elec. 1900, 1904, 1908, 1911, 1917 and 1921; solr. gen. of Canada, 1904; postm. gen. and min. of labour, 1906; Knight of Legion of Honour, France, 1906; envoy of Canadian govt. to Japan in connection with Japanese immigr., 1907; deleg. of Canadian govt. to the opening of first parlmt. of Union of S. Africa, 1910; min. of marine and fisheries, 1911; resigned portfolio on defeat of Laurier govt., Oct., 1911; speaker of House of Commons, 1922.

LENNOX, Hon. Haughton I. S.—B. 1850; ed. pub. and gram. schls., Barrie, Ontario; called to the bar, 1877; K.C., 1908; practised at the bar for many years at Barrie; elec. to H. of C., Canada, 1900; re-elec., 1904, 1908 and 1911; judge of high ct., Ontario, 1912.

LENTON, Henry John.—Cape teleg. serv., 1st Sept., 1898; clk., staff branch, 21st Jan., 1902; 1st cls. clk., ditto, 1st Apr., 1912; senr. clk., ch. clk.'s office, 1st Apr., 1918; prin. clk. (lower grade), ditto, 18th Dec., 1919; 2nd grade, ch. clk., 1st Apr., 1921; ast. sec., 1st Nov., 1923.

LEONARD, Hugh Goodwin Runsell, M.A. (Edin.)—B. 1880; cadet, F.M.S., 1903; passed cadet, 1906; ag. ast. dist. treas., Kuala Lumpur, 1906; ag. dist. treas., Raub, Apr., 1906; ag. 2nd ast. sec. to res. gen. and priv. sec. to res.-gen., Aug., 1906; ag. ast. supt. of imigrts., Nov., 1906; ag. harbmr., Port Swettenham, in addn., Aug.-Oct., 1907; bonus exam. in Malay, 1908; ag. emigr. agt. in India, Mar., 1909-Mar., 1912; ag. dep. contr. of lab., Feb., 1913; bonus exam. in Telugu, 1913; ag. 2nd mag., Kuala Lumpur, Apr.-Aug., 1915; ag. dep. contr. of lab., Sept., 1915-Aug., 1919 and June, 1920; offg. ast. treas., F.M.S. and state treas., Selangor, Nov., 1921; chmn., European unemployment comtee., in addn., Apr., 1922; on sp. duty, Aug., 1924.

LESLIE, Allan Wallace.—Ag. clk., Estcourt magistracy, Natal, 1889; 3rd cls. clk., Newcastle, Jan., 1890; clk. of ct. and Zulu interp. (2nd cls.), Alexandra, May, 1891; 1st cls. clk., Jan., 1898; transfd. to Newcastle, Jan., 1899; mag., Ndwandwe, July, 1900; Krantzkop, Apr., 1904; Richmond, Oct., 1906; mag. for col. of Natal, Oct., 1906; ast. under-se., Dec., 1907; ag. principal under-se., Apr. to Nov., 1909; ag. under-se. for justice, Union of S. Africa, Jan., 1911; chief clk., dept. of justice, 1st Apr., 1912; mag., Dundee, Nov., 1915; mag., Durban, May, 1920; judge. native high ct., 1st Oct., 1920.

LESLIE, Major George Arthur James, R.E.—B. 1867; ed. at Dulwich and King William's Colls.; entd. royal mil. acad., 1885; 2nd lieut., R.E., Mar., 1887; two years' practical training at Chatham; one year's training for submarine mining at Chatham and Portsmouth; employed in India on submarine defences at Rangoon and Karachi, 1891-1894; special employment at Aden, 1895; mil. works services in Baluchistan, 1896-1899; survey offr., Tirah campaign, 1897 (ment. in desps., medal and two clasps); brevet majority, May, 1908; regimental majority, Oct., 1905; special service, Chitral campaign, 1900-1902; with corps of 3rd sappers and miners, Kirkee, 1903-1908; acted as mil. sec. to G.O.C., Southern army, India, 1907;
services lent to Gold Coast Colony for construction of trunk road in Ashanti, 1st Nov., 1908.

LETHEM, G. J.—B. 1886; ed. at Mill Hill, Schl., Middlesex, and Edin. and Grenoble Univ.; M.A. and LL.B. (with distinction) Edin.; mem. of Lincoln's Inn; asst. res., N. Nigeria, 22nd Mar., 1911.

LEVESON-GOWER, JOHN.—Subaltern, 3rd K.A.R., 8th May, 1903; asst. coll., E. Africa Prot., 22nd May, 1906.

LE VIEUX, LÉON.—Asst. survr., pub. wks. dep., Seychelles, 24th May, 1902; inspr. pol. and supt. prisons, July, 1905; supt. of pub. wks., excise inspr. and chrmn. of local bd. of health, central dist., June, 1918.

LEWIS, ALFRED DALE, B.A. (Cape), M.A. (Cantab.), M.Inst.C.E.—B. 1881; P.W.D., India, 1905-07; circle engnr., irrig. dept., Cape and Union of S. Africa, 1907-15; on mily. serv. as major, R.E., in France, Egypt, Mesopotamia, 1915-19; ag. dir. of irrig., 1920; dir. of irrigation, 1921; author of "Irrigation in America."

LEWIS, ARTHUR KENNEDY.—Ed. at Wesleyan high schl. and C.M.S. grammar schl., S. Leone; med. dresser attached to Anglo-French boundary coman., Dec., 1891, to Apr., 1892 (recd. thanks of gov't.); clk. to D.C.; clk. of ct. of requests; registr. of births and deaths, W. dist., 1893 to 1895; 3rd clk. regisr.-gen.'s dept., 1895 to 1897; 2nd clk., atty.-gen.'s off., 1898; travelled with and clk. to atty.-gen. during trial of insurgents by Judge G. A. Bonner, 1898; transport clk., N.A. dept., 1899; ditto P. W. D., Jan., 1900, to July, 1901; offr. in charge of transport on gov't.'s tours, 1899-1901; regian. offr., G.P.O., Freetown, Aug., 1901, to Jan., 1903; asst. postmr., Gambia, Feb., 1903.

LEWIS, FREDERICK JAMES.—Tempy. draughtsman, survr.-gen.'s office, Natal, Mar., 1892; draughtsman, July, 1896; draughtsman and computer, Sept., 1898; ag. examnr. of diagrams, Jan., 1908; examnr. of diagrams, Jan., 1909; professional asst., survr.-gen.'s office, Natal Prov., Apr., 1912; survr.-gen., Natal Prov., 1st Oct., 1915.

LEWIS, L. H.—B. 1885; clk., acot.'s office, G.P.O., O.R.C., 1903; clk., sec.'s office, P.O., Union of S. Africa, 1914; seconded to admistr., S.W. Africa Prot., 1915-17; 1st grade clk., treasy., S. Africa, 1917; senr. clk., 1919; prin. clk., 1921; sec., prov. finances coman., 1922-23; sec., educn. admistr. coman., 1923.

LEWIS, HON. SIR NEIL ELLIOTT, K.C.M.G. (1902), C.M.G. (1901), B.A.—B. 1858; atty.-gen. in Dobson-Hervy ministry, Tasmania, 1892-4; premier and atty.-gen. in Lewis ministry, 1900; joined 1st Commonwealth ministry as min. without portfolio, Jan., 1901; again premier of Tasmania, 1909-1912; treasur., and min. for mines, Apl., 1916.

LEWIS, SIR WALTER LLEWELLYN, KT. BACH. (1904), M.A.—B. 1849; gold medallist, Queen's Univ. (Ireland), 1869 and 1871; called to the bar, Mid. Tem., Jan., 1876; South Wales and Chester circuits; stip. justice, Trinidad, Jan., 1885; chmn. of coman. on agricultural contracts; chmn. of directors, public service widows' and orphans' fund, 1890-1900; puisne judge, 1893; ch. justice, British Honduras, 1900; coronation medal, 1902; ret., 1906.

LEYH, STANLEY GEORGE HOARE, O.B.E. (Mily.)—B. 1893; ed. East Ham Tech. Coll., A.S.C. (T.F.), 1908-12; Royal Navy, 1913-20; staff of comdr.-in-chief, Grand Fleet, 1914; admity. war staff (allied naval coun.), 1915; staff, comdr.-in-chief, China station, 1919; "1914-15 Star," Brit. War Med., Victory Med. librarian, col. sec.'s office, Singapore, 4th to 1920; ag. office asst., ditto, 15th Mar., 1921; asst., col. sec.'s office, Singapore, 1st to 1922.

LIDDARD, M.—B. 1875; ed. at Heath End Schl., Kent, and St. Charles Coll., Lond., served under Royal Niger Co., 1895-1899; cls. res., N. Nigeria, 20th Jan., 1910.

LIESCHING, PERCIVAL.—B. 1885; Bedford Schl., and Brasenose Coll., Oxon. (scholar); lit. hum. (D.) 1920; pvt., 1st H.A.C., 1914; 2nd lieut., Rifle Brig., Feb., 1918; lieut., June, 1915; capt., Tank Corps, 1918; served in France, 1914, 1917-18; Edin., 1916; ment. in despe., 1918; appd. to reconstruction scheme, asst. prin., C.O., 9th July, 1920; joint sec., col. survey comittee, sec., comittee on priv. enterprise in trop. Afr., 1920.

LIGHT, JOSEPH.—B. 1898; cadet, Celest. serv., Nov., 1921; attd., Galle Kachcheri, Feb., 1922; ditto, Galles Kachcheri, Feb., 1922; office asst. to ast. govt. agt., Kegalla, Aug., 1922.

LILLEY, CYRIL CHARLES.—B. 1889; Cheltenham Coll. and Sandhurst; capt., Worcestershire Regt.; ast. dist. coman., Gold (ad.), 25th Aug., 1920.

LINCOLNSHIRE, 1ST MARQUESS OF (G.C.)

CHARLES ROBERT WYNNE-CARRINGTON, BART. (or. 1895), VISCOUNT WYNNE (U.K.), BARON CARRINGTON (Great Britain, 17th and Ireland, 1796), P.C. (1881), K.G. (or. 1895), G.C.M.G. (1885).—B. 1843; ed. at Eton and Col., Camb., B.A. 1863; late capt. Roy. Irish Guards, lieut.-col. 3rd batt. Oxford Leg. Infantry; capt. Queen's Body Guard, 1880; lord gov. of N. S. Wales, 1885-90; lord chamberlain, 1892-95; pres. bd. of agric., 1906; lord pres. 1911; joint hered. lord great chamberlain, England.

LINDSAY, JAMES.—Ed. Edin. Univ. Li. Ch.B., 1906; late res. physician, royal sanatorium for consumption; late clin. med. Royal Victoria Dispensary for Consumption; diseases of the chest, Edin.; joined W.A.M., Apl., 1910.

LINDSAY, K. G.—Ast. dist. coman., Kent, June, 1921.

LINDSELL, HAROLD OFFLEY.—B. 1881; at Bradfield Coll. (exhibitioner) and All Souls Coll., Oxford, B.A. (Litt. Hum.), 1907; res., N. Nigeria, 10th Apl., 1909.

LINDSELL, ROGER EDWARD.—B. 1885; at Uppingham schl. (scholar) and King's (Cambr.) (scholar); class. tripods, part I, cl. cadet, Hong Kong, 1909; passed cadet, 1911; 2nd ast. regisr.-gen., 1911; J.P., 1912; pass. law exam., 1913; ag. 1st astt. to sec. for Chinese affairs, 1913; ag. 2nd ditto, 1913; 3rd dist., continued to act as 2nd ditto, 1914; ag. sec. mag., 1915; ag. chief astt. to sec. for Chinese affairs, 1915 to 1916; ag. astt. P.G., 1916; ch. astt. to sec. for Chinese affairs, 1916; ast. asupt., imports and exports dept., 1916; ag. dep. regisr., sup. ct., 1918; ag. 2nd pol. mag., 1919, 1921, 1922 and 1923; ag. 1st pol. mag., 1921 and 1924; ag. P.M.G., 1923.

LINEHAN, WILLIAM.—B. 1892; ed. Christian Brother's Coll. and Univ. Coll., Cork (schol. and exhib.), 1910-13; B.A. (1st clas., 1913); post grad. scholarship, 1913-14; M.A., hona., clas., 1916; cadet, F.M.S., 1916;
LLOYD, T. I. K.—B. 1896; ed. Rossall SchL and Caius Coll., Cambridge (schol., 1914); cadet, Royal Mil. Acad., 1915; 2nd lieut., R.E., 1916; served in Egypt and Palestine, ment. in despatches, 1917; apptd. under re-construction scheme, asst. prin., miny., of health, July, 1920; temp. attached to C.O. as asst. prin., Dec., 1921.

LLOYD, WILLIAM BUTLER.—B. 1880; ed. Shrewsbury, and Christ Church, Oxford; M.A.; called to the bar, 1905; dist. and stip. mag., Mauritius, 1913; mag., Rodriguez, 1916; mag. for occupied territories of German East Africa, 1919; mag., Tanganyika Territory, 21st Nov., 1919; pol. mag., S. Leone, 6th June, 1922; dep. judge, sup. ct., 3rd July to 1st Aug., 1922.

LLOYD, HON. SIR WM. FREDERICK, K.C.M.G. (1919).—B. 1884; ed. Owen's Coll., Manchester and Durham Coll. of Science, Newcastle-on-Tyne; bachelor of law, London Univ., 1894; D.C.L., Victoria Univ., Toronto, 1901; vice-principal, Bishop Field Coll., St. John's, Newfild., 1891; editor, "Evening Telegram," 1904; M.H.A., Trinity dist., 1904; leader of the opposition, H. of A., 1916; with Sir Edward (now Lord) Morris formed a National Govt., becoming attorney-general, 1917; ag. prime minister, 1917; prime minister, 1918.

LLOYD-BLOOD, CAPT. L.I.N., M.C., B.A., Barrister-at-law.—Dep. regiar., sup. ot., Kenya, Oct., 1920; regiar., July, 1921; asst. atty.-gen., Nyasaland, 16th Aug., 1924.

LOBB, REGINALD POPHAM, C.M.G. (1914), B.A., F.R.G.S.—Ed. at Clifton and Christ's Coll., Camb.; mod. and medieval languages tripes, 1896; priv. sec. to Sir F. Lugard, high commr. of N. Nigeria, Oct., 1900; transf'd to polit. dept. as asst. res., Nupe Prov., Oct., 1901; 3rd cls. res., Zaria, May, 1902; ag. res., Zaria, Jan., 1903; 2nd cls. res., Muri Prov., Oct., 1903; Kano-Sokoto campaign (medal and clasp), 1903, and minor operations; 1903-6; ag. 2nd cls. clk., C.O., 1st Jan., 1906; mem. of African trop. ser. comte., 1907-8; col. sec. and regiar.-gen., Bermuda, 8th Aug., 1908; chmn., gen. bd. of health, bd. of pub. wks., and bd. of pilotage comsrs.; recd. thanks of S. of S. for memo. on tuberculosis, 1912; adminstr. and col. sec., St. Vincent, 8th June, 1915; ag. adminstr., St. Lucia, 23rd Mar., 1917, to 16th Dec., 1918; dormant coman. to administer govt. of Windward Is., dated 21st May, 1917; recvd. thanks of U.S. Govt., 1918, for services to U.S. Navy Dept.; senr. del. from Windward Is. at inter-col. educn., confee., Trinidad, 1921; chmn., Windward Is. med. comte., 1922; col. sec., B. Guiana, 23rd Nov., 1922; ag. gov., B. Guiana, Dec., 1922 to Apr., 1923; chmn., currency comsrs. and harb. bd.; chmn., rly. coman., 1925.

LOCKHART, CHARLES RAMSDALE.—B. 1892; mil. serv., Aug., 1914 to Mar., 1919 (Gallipoli, Egypt, and with K.A.R. in E. Africa); twice ment. in despatches; asst. treas., Tanganyika Territory, Mar., 1919; ag. senr. asst. treas., May, 1921; senr. asst. treas., 1st Apr., 1923.

LOCKHART, SIR JAMES HALDANE STEWART, K.C.M.G. (1908); C.M.G. (1898); F.R.G.S., M.R.A.S.; LL.D. (Hong Kong Univ.), 1868; Edin. Univ.; Greek medallist, etc.; apptd. after compet. exam., to a Hong Kong cadetship, 1878; attached to the C.O. for one year, 1879; passed cadet, 1882; supt. opium revenue, Mar., 1883; asst. col. sec. and asst. auditor-gen., Aug., 1883; ag. regiar. gen., 1884 and 1885; regiar.-gen., 1887, and M.L.C., 1889; mem. exec. coun., 1891; chairm. bd. of examiners in
Chinese, 1891; ditto governg. body Queen's Coll., dep. regiwr., sup. et. in prize, 27th Nov., 1914; 1894; ag. col. sec., Apl., 1894; col. sec. and regiwr.-gen., Mar., 1895; special commr. to report on the extension of the bdry. of H. Kong, 1898; representative of Gt. Br. to delimitate bdry., for both of which reed. thanks of S. of S., 1899; rector of coll., medicine for China, 1898-1902; commr. of Weihaiwei, 20th Jan., 1902; assumed govt., 3rd May, 1902; ret., 1920.

LOCKHART, KENNETH SPENCER.—B. 1890; copyist, admstr.'s office, Dominica, 1908; 2nd clk., regiwr.'s office, 1910; 2nd rev. offr. and harmbr., Nevis, 1913; ag. acctnt., treasy., 1917; is also sec. to quarantine bd., and clk. to cent. bd. of health; govt. trade agt. to enquire into and report upon conditions affecting W.I. labourers at Santo Domingo, Nov., 1918; rev. offr., St. Kitts, May, 1920; ag. audlt. clk., Sept., 1920; 2nd clk., treas. dept., 23rd July, 1921; capt., St. Kitts-Nevis Defence Force; ag. 1st clk., treasy., May-Sept., 1922; audit clk., St. Kitts-Nevis, 1st June, 1922; income tax commr., 1924.

LOOKYER, NICHOLAS COLSTON, C.B.E., I.S.O. (1906).—B. 1886; entd. treasy., N.S. Wales, 1888; collr. of cust. and first commr. of taxation, N.S.W., 1896; compt-r.-gen. of custs., C. of A., 1911; mem. Inter-State commr., July, 1913.

LOGAN, EWEN REGINALD.—Ed. at Charterhouse and Exeter Coll., B.A., 1891; M.A., 1897; student, Inner Temp., Jan., 1894; called to bar, Nov. 1899; joined Middlx. and N. London sess. and cent. crim. ct., 1900; serv. in Boer war as 2nd lieut., 65th squad., I.Y., 1901; Queen's medal and four clasps; mines dept., Transvaal govt., Aug., 1901, to Apr., 1902; asst. res. mag., Transvaal, May, 1902, to May, 1904; mag. E. Africa Prot., 4th Aug., 1905; chief just., Seychelles, 1914; admst. govt. from 23rd July, 1916 to 26th Mar., 1917 and from 13th May to 7th Oct., 1917; drafted in conjunction with Alfred Gellé, Esq., barrister-at-law, code of civil procedure for Seychelles; reed. thanks of sec. of state; puisne judge, G. Coast, 9th June, 1920, with seniority from 28th Mar., 1920.

LOGAN, WILLIAM MARSTON.—B. 1889; ed. Bristol and Brasenose Coll., Oxford (Hulme exhibr., Bridgeman prizeman, B.A.); asst. dist. commr., East Africa Prot., Mar., 1913; sec. cent. comte., of supplies, 1914-15; hon. lieut., unattached list, 1915-17; ag. dist. commr., 1918 and Dec. to July, 1921; ag. senr. asst. sec., to Nov., 1920 and July, 1921.

LOGGIE, THOMAS GEORGE JOHNSTON, I.S.O. (1917).—B. 1854; ed. Presbyterian Acad., Chatham, New Brunswick; dep. survr. gen., New Brunswick, 1908; lieut.-col. in the active Militia; now dep. min. of lands and mines.

LOGGIN, GEORGE NICHOLAS, M. Inst. C.E.—B. 1882; pupil and asst. engrnr. with Messrs. Topham, Jones and Railton, admv. contractors, Gibraltar Dockyard, 1900-07; dist. engrnr., P.W.D., Ceylon, 1908; ag. 2nd asst. and ag. asst., D.P.W. for periods aggregating 4½ years between 1913 and 1919; sent to Madras Presidency to study and rept. on tech. details, excise control, 1913; reed. thanks of govt. for sp. rept. on mechan. systems of water filtration, 1915; sec., ministry of munitions local priority authority and asst. milly. censor, in addn., 1917-18; asst., D.P.W., Ceylon, 1921; dir. pub. wks., Uganda Prot., Apr., 1922; chmn., economic comte., rly. extensions, Uganda, 1923-24; dep. D.P.W., Nigeria, 1924.

LOGIE, HON. WILLIAM ALEXANDER, C.M.G. (1918).—B. 1866; ed. Queen's Univ., King's College, Canada; B.A. (cl. l.st. hons. in classics), M.A., 1888; LL.B., 1892; barrister, Canada, 1890; bencher, Upper Canada, 1911; ensign, Vol. Militia, 1883, and is maj.-gen. commr., Div., Toronto; puisne judge of high ct., Ontario, and a judge of Appellate div., 1918.

LOLTGEN, W. G.—B. 1894; on milly. ser., 18th May, 1916 to 18th Feb., 1920; temp. O.S.O., Mar. 1920 to 27th June, 1922; agt. after compet. exam., cler. offr., O.S.O., June, 1922.

LONDON, GEORGE ERNEST.—B. 1889; ed. Warwick, and Downing Coll., Camb. (scholarship in nat. sci. tripoms, 1910; hist. tripoms, 1911; cadet, F.M.S., 1911; offr., cl. V., 1914; dist. offr., Dindings, 1916; on active serv., 1919; lieut., Glouc. Regt.; offr., cl. IV., 1919; to res., Pahang, 1920; offr., cl. III., Nov., 1921; ag. state treas., Perak, July, 1924; ag. sec. res., Perak, Aug., 1924.

LONG, ARTHUR TILNEY, C.B.E. (1918).—B. 1871; served in S. African War (medal and clasp); entered Transvaal service, 1900; col. customs, Lourenço Marques, 1902; ag. sec. customs, Transvaal, 1906-6; agent of Transvaal govt. at Lourenço Marques, 1906; agent of Union of S. Africa at Lourenço Marques, also British vice-consul since 1908; ag. commr., 1909 and 1911; ag. British consul-general, Mombasa, 1917 to Apr., 1918, Sept., 1922 to May, 1925; from Oct., 1923 to Mar., 1924.

LONSDALE, CAPT. PHILIP.—Ed. at Sandhurst; commr. in regular forces, 18th June, 1893; served on the N.W. Frontier (Tirah), 1893-94; with Ashanti Field Force, 1900 (medal and clasp, "Kumasii"); ag. commr., Northern Territories, G. Coast, 1906; commr., schl. of signalling, Dublin, 1906; res., N. Nigeria, Mar., 1906; 3rd cl. ass., Oct., 1908.

LORAM, CHARLES TEMPLEMAN.—B. 1879; L.L.B.; asst. mast., Pietermaritzburg Coll., 1896; asst. mast., Pietermaritzburg Coll., 1896; seconded, 31st May, 1901; asst. inspr. of schls., 15th Feb., 1906; asst. inspr. of schls. in July, 1906; inspr. of schools, 1910; chief nat. educn., 1st May, 1918.

LORD, GERALD FRANCIS.—Clk., P.M.C., dept., Natal, 1901; inspr. of educn., Transvaal, 1901-2; civil serv. examn., Natal, 1902; agt. lands and works dept., and rlys. and harb. dept., 1903; senr. clk., 1906; prin. clk., 1907; ag. sec., rlys. and harb. dept., in 1908 and 1909; prin. clk., admstr.'s dept., Natal Prov., 1910; chf. clk., 1st Feb., 1918.

LORD, Lieut.-Col. J. E. C., C.M.G., D.S.O., V.D.—Ent. Tasmanian civ. ser., 1886; commanded 49th Batt. Tas. A.I.F. in European W., from 10th Feb., 1915 to 4th Aug., 1919; commands 12th Inf. Brig., Australian Mil. Force A.D.C. to the gov.-gen.; commr. of police, Tasmania.

LORNE, J., M.A., B.Sc. Edin.—Cadet, S.S.S., Nov., 1899; passed final exam. in Malay, Apr., 1901; ag. head of Malay Coll., Malacca, May, 1901; ag. asst. regiwr., sup. ct., and mag. and sheriff, Malacca, Apr., 1903; ag. dist. offr., Penang, Jan., 1904; ag. dist. offr., Dindings, Jan., 1908; ag. temp. 3rd mag., Penang, Jun., 1910; ag. dep. regiwr., sup. ct., Penang, May, 1910; offr., cl. IV., May, 1911; ag. collr., inspr. rev. reg. of deeds, Singapore, Aug., 1911; offr., cl. III., Feb., 1916; asst. dist. judge (civil).
COLONIAL OFFICE LIST.

addition, Jan.–Feb., 1917; July–Aug., 1920; Nov.–Dec., 1920; supernumy. offr., cls. II, 1919; offr. mem., leg. comm., May, 1920 to eb., 1921; ag. collr., land rev., and regnr. of sds., Singapore, 2nd Nov., 1921; ag. under sec., Sttlmts., 28th Apr., 1922.

LOUDOUN, WILSON ANDERSON.—B. 1874; pub. schls., Chatham, New Brunswick; ass't udr.gen., 1902; audr.-gen. of New Brunswick, 1907; now comptroller-general.

LOUGHEED, HON. SIR JAS. ALEXANDER, C.M.G. (1916); K.C.—B. 1854; ed. public schools, Toronto; studied law there; member of bar of the N.W. territories since 1883; summoned to Senate of Canada, 1889; Q.C., Canada, 1889; leader of the Conservative party in the senate, 1906-1907; mem. of the Privy Coun. for Canada and minister without portfolio in Mr. order's cabinet, Oct., 1911; and in National ov't., Oct., 1917; gov't. leader in the Senate, 1907-21; min. of soldiers civil re-establishment, 1918; min. of interior, July, 1920; resig. portfolio in defeat of admn't. in g.e., Dec. 1921.

LOUW, JACOBUS STEPHANUS.—Ch. clk.; deeds office, Transvaal, Apr., 1902; ass't regnr., deeds, etc., 1912; ass't regnr., deeds, Cape Prov., ept., 1918; ass't regnr., deeds, Windhoek, Oct., 1919; regnr., deeds, Windhoek, May, 1920; regnr., deeds, O.F.S., Apr., 1922.

LOVETT, HERBERT J.—A.C.A.; ed. at Loughborough coll.; chartered acctnt., England and Wales, 1900; ass't acctnt., G.P.O., Ceylon, 1901; reg. acctnt. on several occasions; on military duty, Sept., 1914; acctnt., G.P.O., Oct., 1916.

LOW, ALFRED MOORE.—Ed. at Aldenham; pen scholarship at Pemb. Coll., Camb., 1890; B.A. ass't tripes, 1883; prof. of classics, Codrington Coll., Barbados, 1896; 3rd master, Queen's Coll., Trinidad, June, 1897; 2nd master, July, 1914; prin., July, 1920.

LOW, ROBERT ALLAN, M.A., Cantab.—B. 1873; ed. Aldenham and Selwyn Coll.; served in S. African Field Force, 1900-1901; ass't mast., Queen's Royal Coll., Trinidad, 1901; censor, 1917; headmaster European schl., Nairobi, E. Africa Prot., 1918.

LOW, HON. THOMAS ANDREW.—B. 1871; ed. ub. and high schls., Pembroke, Ont.; pres. and ir. of several large corporations; past-warden of Kennewick county; ed. to H.C., g.e. 1908 and 1911; signed, 1912; re-el., 1921; min. without portfolio in King admn't., 29th Dec., 1921; min. of trade and commerce, 1923.

LOWE, ALEXANDER FRANCIS, C.M.G. (1924).—B. 1862; ed. Nelson Coll., New Zealand, and at private schl., England; filled various positions as offr. of New Zealand parl'mt., 1885-1915; clk. f H. of R., 1915; clk. of parl't. and clk. of legis. jun., 1919.

LOWINGER, VICTOR ALEXANDER.—B. 1879; l. at Pietermaritzburg and S.A. Coll., Cape own; Royal Observatory, Cape of Good Hope, 1895-1904; licensed surv., Cape, 1901, Transvaal, 1902; sec. confere. of surveyors-gen., S. Africa, 1904; geodetic surv., Transvaal and O.F.S., 1904-15; trig. surv., F.M.S., 1906; supr. trig. surveys, 1913; ag. ast. surv.-gen., 1918-19; ag. ast. surv.-gen., F.M.S. and S. Sttlmts., in addition, July, 1921 to Feb., 1922; ag. survr.-gen., F.M.S. ad S. Sttlmts., May, 1922; survr.-gen., July, 1922.

LUCAS, SIR CHARLES PRESTWOOD, K.C.B., K.C.M.G. (1907), C.B. (1901), B.A.—B. 1858; ed. at Winchester Coll., and Balliol Coll., Oxford; open exhibitioner; 1st cls. in mods., 1873; and 1st class in final classical schools, June, 1876; Chancellor's prize for Latin essay, 1877; called to the bar by the Soc. of Lincoln's Inn, Easter, 1885; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. in the office of the sec. of state for the colo., Apr., 1877; priv. sec. to Sir R. Herbert, Dec., 1881; Sir R. Granville, Feb., 1886, and again to Sir R. Herbert, Aug., 1886; also chairman of comte. of emigrants' information officer till 31st Dec., 1896; 1st class clk., Feb., 1892; prin. clk., Sept., 1896; ast. under-sec. of state, June, 1897; head of the Dominions division, 1907, in which capacity he visited Australia and N. Zealand, 1909; regnr. of the Order of St. Michael and St. George, 1909-1911; retired, 1911; author of "Historical Geography of the British Colonies," "The Canadian War of 1812," "A History of Canada, 1763-1812," "Greater Rome and Greater Britain," etc.

LUCAS, HON. SIR EDWARD, KT. BACH. (1921).—M.L.C., S. Australia 1910-1918; agt. gen. for S. Australia in London, 1918-24.

LUCETTE, EDWARD HENRY, B.A. (Oxon.), M.C.—B. 1896; on mily. serv., Apr., 1915; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., May, 1921; att'd. to Anuradhapura Kach., June, 1921; att'd. Trincomalee Kachcheri, Mar., 1922; att'd. col. sec.'s office, Nov., 1922; pvt. sec. and ag. A.D.C. to the gov., July, 1924.

LUCIE-SMITH, SIR ALFRED VAN W., KT. BACH. (1911).—Ed. at Rugby; solr., Br. Guiana, 1877; called to bar, Mid. Temp., 1881; ag. solr.-gen., Br. Guiana, 1882 to 1887; pres. dist. ct., Famagusta, Cyprus, 1887; Limassol, 1892; ag. Queen's advoc., 1893; ag. judge, cons. ct., Constantinople, 1896; res. mag., Kingston, Jamaica, Nov., 1896; puisne judge, B.G., Jan., 1898; ag. ch. just., 1900-01; one of the compilers of the "Rules of Court." 1900: ch. just., Trinidad and Tobago, 1908; pres. W. Indian ct. of appeal, 31st May, 1920; ret., 1924.

LUCIE-SMITH, JOHN ALFRED, O.B.E., V.D.—B. 1888; ed. Stonyhurst Coll.; col. sec.'s office, Br. Guiana, 1905-06; called to bar, Middle Temple, 1910; advoc. and solr., S. Sttlmts., 1910-14; on mily. serv., 1914; twice ment. in desps.; ag. pres., dist. ct., Trinidad, 1920; ast. mag., Port of Spain, 1920-23; pres., dist. ct., Cyprus, 1924.

LUCIE-SMITH, JOHN DUDLEY.—B. 1886; ed. Berkhamstead schl.; entd. civ. serv. of Jamaica, 1909; 2nd ols. clk., 1914; 1st cls. clk., 1920; sec., Westmoreland hurricane relief comm., 1912; sec. foot and mouth disease comm., 1922; ag. priv. sec. to gov. of Jamaica (Sir Sydney Olivier) 1912; priv. sec. and A.D.C. to gov. of Jamaica (Sir Leslie Probyn), 1920-23; war serv., R.F.A., France and Flanders) 1916-18; A.D.C. to C.R.A., 68th Div., 1918; W. O. staff, 1919; edr. of "The School Garden in Jamaica" and "Elementary Hygiene."

LUDDINGTON, NORMAN JOHN, M. Sc., Durham Univ.—B. 1888; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., 17th Nov., 1911; attached to the Jaffna Kachcheri, Dec., 1911; ag. pol. mag., Trincomalee, July, 1912; ag. office ast. to gov't. ast., E. Prov., Mar., 1913; ag. office ast., Kurunegala Kachcheri, Aug., 1913; ag. ast. gov't. ast., Puttalam and Chilaw, Apr., 1914; resumed duties as office ast. to gov't. ast., N. W. Prov., May, 1914; pol. mag., Negombo, May, 1915; Panadura, June, 1915; Negombo, Aug., 1915; Galle, Apr., 1916; Colombo, July, 1921; ast. comnt., excise, July, 1923.

LUGARD, RT. HON. SIR FREDERICK JOHN DRAITLY, P.C. (1920), G.C.M.G. (1911), K.C.M.G. (1901), C.B. (1895), D.S.O. (1887).—B. 1868; ed.
Rossall and Sandhurst; 1st coman., 9th foot, May, 1878; captain, Aug., 1895; major, Aug., 1896; lieut.-col., July, 1899; col., July, 1905; temp. brig.-gen., 1900-07; to India, Sept., 1878; active service, Afghanistan, Sept., 1879, to Sept., 1880; medal; Sudan, Feb. to Nov., 1880; medal, clasp, "Tofrek" Khedive's Star, despatches; Burmah, Oct., 1886, to Aug., 1887; mentioned in despatches, D.S.O. and medal. To Africa, Feb., 1888; commanding expdn. against slave traders; very severely wounded. To East Africa, Nov., 1889, to Oct., 1892; exploration of Sabakhi; adminstd. Uganda; went to Borgu in comd. expdn., July, 1894, and made treaties on behalf of Royal Niger Company, returned, Apr., 1895, Feb., 1896, led expedition across Kalahari for Brd Charterland Co.; apptd. comsmr. and comdt., West African frontier force, Aug., 1897; high comsmr. for Northern Nigeria, 29th Dec., 1899; resigned Sept., 1906; gov. of Hong Kong, 1st May, 1907; gov., N. and S. Nigeria, 26th Mar., 1912; gov.-gen., Nigeria, 1st Dec., 1913; assumed govt., 1st Jan., 1914; retired, 1919.

LUKE, HARRY CHARLES Knight of Grace of the Order of St. John of Jerusalem.—B. 1884; ed. at Eton and Trinity Coll., Oxford; 2nd cls. med., hist., B.A., 1906; M.A., 1910; B. Litt., 1919; priv. sec. to the govrs. of Sierra Leone (Sir L. Probyn, K.C.M.G.), 1908, and A.D.C., 1909; ag. aast. col. sec., Sierra Leone, Mar. to July, 1909; priv. sec. to the govrs. of Barbados, Feb., 1911; attached to C.O., May to July, 1911 (Coronation medal); priv. sec. to the high comsmr. of Cyprus (Sir H. Goold-Adams, G.C.M.G.), and clk. of exec. coun., Oct., 1911; asst. sec. to govt., Cyprus, 1912; ag. comsmr., Paphos, 1917; comsmr., Famagusta, 1918; sec., Cyprus defence comttee, 4th Aug., 1914; served in H.M.S. Doris on Syrian Coast, 1914-1915; political offr., on staffs of Admirals Wemyss and Christian and govt. sec., Mudros, Feb., 1915, to June, 1916; (lieut.-comdr., and ag. comdr., R.N.V.R.); recd. thanks of admry.; Italian med. for mily. valour; political offr. to Admiral Sir J. de Robeck, Constantinople and Black Sea, Aug., 1919; ag. Br. ch. comsmr. in Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan, Apr. to Sept., 1920; asst. gov. of Jerusalem, Oct., 1920; mem. of comsmrs. on the orthodox patriarchate of Jerusalem, and on the Jaffa disturbances, 1921; col. sec., Sierra Leone, May, 1924; adminstd. govt., June to Oct., 1924; passed in Turkish and modern Greek (hons.); author of "A Bibliography of Sierra Leone," 1910 and 1925; "Cyprus under the Turks," 1921; joint editor, "Handbook of Cyprus," 1913 and 1920; "Handbook of Palestine," 1922.

LUKE, SIR JOHN PEARCE KT. BACH. (1921), C.M.G. (1917), M.P., A.M.I.M.E., J.P.—Ed. Penzance, Cornwall, and privately Wellington, N.Z.; M.P., 1908-11, and since 1917; Mayor of Wellington, 1913-21; el. life mem., N.Z. Returned Soldiers' Association, and holds Medaille de la Reconnaissance Française (3rd cls.) for war services.

LUKIN, MAJ.-GEN. SIR HENRY TIMSON, K.C.B. (1918); C.B. (1916); D.S.O. (1900); C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1860; ed. Merchant Taylor's schl.; served S. African War, 1879; Zulu campaign; attd. to cavalry brigade in advance on Ulundi; present at battle (severely wounded, medal with clasp); operations in Basutoland, 1881 (medal and clasp); field adjutant Bechuanaland Field Force, Langeberg campaign, 1896-97 (despatches several times); lieut.-col., 1900; commanded artillery, Wepener siege, 1900; for some time commanded column of mounted troops, Cape Col.; commanded 1st Colonial div., Cape Col., 1901 (despatches thrice, Queen's medal four clasps, King's medal, two clasps, D.S.O.; col. comdg. Cape Mounted Rifmn., 1903-12; comdt.-gen. Cape colonial forces, 1904-12; ingm.-gen., permanent force, Union of S. Africa, 1912; served European War, 1915-18 (Order of the Nik. 3rd class); ret., 26th Jan., 1919; mem., comm. of defence, Union of S. Africa, 1924.

LUKIN, LIONEL OSCAR.—B. 1868; puimie jude (central), supreme ct., Queensland, Dec., 1910.

LUMB, T. F.—Medical offr., E.A.P., May, 1909.

LUMLEY, JAMES MADY.—B. 1878; ed. Ren. Gram. Schl., Newcastle-on-Tyne; served R.H.A. 1895-1901; S. African war, 1899-1902; wounded; Queen's medal, four clasps; King's medal, two clasps; S. African constab., 1901-08; pub. law and just. of the peace, Heidelberg, Transvaal, 1904-08; asst. supt. of pol., E.A.P., 1909; served in E. Africa, 1914-17; King's pol. medal, 1919; asst. pol., Kenya, 1919; ag. asst. comsmr., Keny. pol., on various occasions, 1920-24.

LUNNON, GEORGE JOSEPH.—B. 1902; apptd. after compet. exam., cler. offr., C.O., 4th May, 1920.

LUSCOMBE, LAURENCE GEORGE.—B. 1889; ed. Heles schl., Exeter; served in S. Africa war, 1901-02; clk., Swaziland adminstr., Sept., 1902; asst. acctnt., Dec., 1909; acctnt., Apr., 1910; finan. secy., 1918.

LYALL-GRANT, R. W., M.A. (Aberdeen), L.L.B. (Edin.).—Vans Dunlop schol. in law, Edin. Univ.; called to Scottish bar, 1903; practised till 1909; atty.-gen., Nyassaland, Apr., 1909; ag. judge, high ct., Sept., 1909 to June, 1910, and from Aug., 1912 to May, 1913; judge of high ct., Aug., 1914, and mem., H.B.M. Ct. of Appeal for Eastern Africa; chmn., native rising coms., 1915; chmn. of claims bd. for Nyassaland, under Br. prots. defence O. in C., 1916-19; judge adv. to Nyassaland-Rhodesia Field Force, 1917-18; atty.-gen., Kenya, July, 1920; mem., exc. and leg. councils.

LYDDEKER, C. J.—Asst. dist. comm., E.A.P., Aug., 1914.

LYNCH, FRANCIS CHRISTOPHER CHISHOLM.—B. 1884; ed. at pub. schls., priv. tuition, McGill Univ.; assoc., Eng. Inst., Canada; assoc. mem. Town Planning Inst. of Canada; gen. engnr., 1902-06; apptd. to interior dep., 1906; asst. supt., rly. lands br., 1911; asst. nat. resources intell. br., dept. of int. Can., Dec., 1911.

LYNDE, WALTER MICHIGELLS, F.S.I. (Eng.).—B. 1883; ed. Cranleigh Schl.; quantity surv., P.W.D., K.A.P., 1910; in charge sp. wt. Kabete, 1918; contracts offr., P.W.D., Kenya, 1923.

LYON, WILLIAM ROY.—B. 1889; ed. at Mountjoy Schl., Dublin; 2nd lieut., 6th batt. City of London Regt. (T.F.), Feb., 1909; Hythe certif., musketry and mach. gun, 1910; lieut., 1910; asst. dist. comsmr., Sierra Leone, Nov., 1912; ag. dist. comsmr. for various periods, 1914-16; capt., 1914; major, 1916; served with Nigeria Carrier Corps in E. Africa, 1917; attcd., 4th batt., Nigeria Regt., as O.C. details, Lagos, 1st Apr., 1918 to 20th May, 1918; dist. comsmr., 2nd cl., 29th Nov., 1917; passed lower standard native language (Tenne).

MAARTENSZ, LEWIS MATTHEW.—B. 1876; barrister-at-Law, Middle Temple; addtnl. crown counsel, Ceylon, Apr., 1903; crown counsel, July, 1906; addtnl. dist. judge, Kandy, Oct., 1910.
COLONIAL OFFICE LIST

Litto, Colombo, Apl., 1911; ag. dist. judge, Colombo, Apr.-Oct., 1916, Apr.-Dec., 1920, Mar.-Nov., 1923 and from June, 1924.

MAASDORP, HON. SIR ANDRIES FERDINAND BROEKENSTROM, KT. BACH (1904).—B.A., Lond., 1869; barrister-at-law, Inn. Temp., Nov., 1871; mem. of the house of assem., Cape Colony, 1874 to 1878; solr.-gen., Cape Colony, Aug., 1878 to May, 1897; mem. of special (treason) court, Cape Colony, Oct., 1900, to June, 1902; ch. just. of the L.R.C., June, 1902; ret., Jan., 1920.

McCALLISTER, RONALD.—B. 1875; ed. privately; asst. res., N. Nigeria, 4th Feb., 1905; present at Satiri rising, Sokoto, in Feb., 1906 (medal and clasp); 3rd cls. res., 21st Sep., 1908.

McARTHUR, JAMES JOSEPH.—B. 1856; asst. sttltm. surveys in Manitoba, 1872-3; prov. land surv., 1878; Dom. land surv., 1879; engaged until 1886 in sttltm. meridian and base line surveys in N.W. Territories, and expln. of N. Saskatchewan and Brazeau riva.; photo-topographic survey of the Rocky Mts., 1887-92; photo-topographic surveys along the coast of S.E. Alaska, prelimin. sttltm. of boundary dispute, 1893; mapped region from Portland Canal to Mt. St. Elias; conducted explor. expeds. through the Yukon country, 1897-9; on staff of high joint comm., Washington, D.C., as topograph. expert and geographer, 1899; engrnr. to boundary comm., ptd., to lay down provisional boundary at head of Lynn Canal, 1900; in conjunction with U.S. engrnr., recovered the boundary line between British Columbia and the State of Washington, 1901; tdhd. to staff of Br. agt. before Alaskan boundary tribunal at F.O., as geographer, 1903; engrnr. to Br. comm., and in charge of final demarcation, 1904-11; int. internat. boundary comm., 1909; has conducted extensive topographical surveys throughout Canada; H.M. comm., to determine, in connection with a U.S. comm., the boundaries between Canada and the U.S., according to existing treaties, 1916; pres., Assoc. of Dom. Land Survrs., 1917; chmn., Ottawa centre, Roy. Astron. Soc. of Can.; fellow, Roy. Astron. Soc. f Can., 1918; mem., Engng. Inst. of Can.

MACARTHUR, WM. HENRY, M.R.C.V.S.—B. 1863; govt. vet. surgeon, Penang, S. Stiltns., 21st May, 1892; app't placed on fixed establishment, st. Jan., 1897.

MACALAY, JOHN DAVIDSON.—Extra clk., ol. sec.'s office, S. Leone, 1874; in customs, 1875; ide waiter, 1877; landing waiter, 1879; clk. of customs, 1883.

McCALL, Lieut.-Col., FREDERICK JOHNSON, I.C., M.R.C.V.S.—Veterinary offr., E.A.P., Ian., 1910; served in Great War, Oct., 1914 to June, 1918; M.C., 1917; 1914-15 Star, British War med., twice ment. in despatches; major, A.D.V.S., nd divn., E. Africa Force, 14th May, 1916; A.D.V.S., G.H.Q., E.A. Force, 8th Aug., 1917; h. vety. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 26th Feb., 1919.

MACCALL, THOMAS VERNON.—B. 1884; ed. 'ickery's schl., Portsmouth, and Edin. Univ.; joined London Metro. Police, 6th Feb., 1905; served in C.I.D., New Scotland Yard; resig. 27th Feb., 1911; served in B. of T. labour exchanges, June, 1911, to Mar., 1914; asst. supt. of police, Honduras, 12th Apr., 1914; J.P., 23rd Apr., 1914; ag. dist. comm., Orange Walk, July-Aug., 1914; visiting justice of dist. prisons, 1914-19; deputy atty.-gen., Corosol sessions, supreme ct., 1914; ag. dist. comm., Orange Walk 'eb. Mar., 1915; commr. of supreme ct., Ist Apr., 1915; 2nd lieut., B. H. Volra., 7th Dec., 1915, attached to Corosol; lieut., Jan., 1917; served in Cayo Exped. Force, on Guatemalan frontier, Apr. to July, 1916; capt., B.H.T.F., 5th May, 1917; deputy atty.-gen., Corosol sessions, supreme ct., Dec., 1918; ag. dist. comm., Corosol, from 13th Nov., 1918.

McCALLAN, E.A.—Ck. post office, Bermuda, 1903; clk. works dept., 1904; rev. offr., 1907; agric. ast., 1913; dir. of agric., Bermuda, 1920.

McCARTER, HARRY BERTRAM ADAIR.—B. 1883; entd. civil serv., Cape Colony, 1899; served in S. African war in Fingoland native levies, 1901-02; served in law dept., Transvaal civil serv., 1902 to 1907; clk., Swaziland adminstr., June, 1907; clk. and dep. ast. comm., Apr., 1911; passed Cape Univ. civ. ser. lower law exam., 1911.

McCAETHY, LESLIE ERNEST VIVIAN, B.A.—B. 1885; ed. Keble Coll., Oxford; 2nd cls. honours final jurisprudence; barrister-at-law, Gray's Inn, 1911; apptd. crown counsel, Gold Coast, 21st Sept., 1921; ag. solr.-gen., July to Sept., 1922.

McCarthy, Roft. Henry, C.M.G. (1906).—and class clk., impl. customs, Belfast, Feb., 1875; served at Cork and Plymouth; selected for special service with survrs.-gen., and in connection with reorganisation of customs statistical dept., 1893; 2nd offr., Folkestone, 1894; col. of customs, Trinidad, Dec., 1895; mem. legis. coun., 1898; one of the representatives of Trinidad at commercial conferences at Washington and Ottawa, 1900; apptd. to exec. coun., 1903; del. for Trinidad at W. Indian quarantine confere., 1904; mem. West Indian central quarantine authority, 1907; ret. on pension, 1908; visited Malta to inquire into working of customs dept., 1908, and re-organised dept. in course of subsequent visits, 1909-10; apptd. gov't. dir. of Trinidad Dock and Engineering Co., 1908; technical adviser to roy. comm. on trade relations between Canada and W. Indies, 1909-10.

McCAY, Major-Gen. Sir Jar. Whiteside, K.C.M.G. (1918), C.B. (1915); C.B.E., M.A., LL.M., V.D.—B. 1864; M.L.A., Victoria, Nov., 1895, and Oct., 1897, to Dec., 1899; min. of pub. instrn. and commr. of trade and cust., Dec., 1899, to Jan., 1900; mem. of Commonwealth parl., Mar., 1901, and Dec., 1903; min. for defence, ditto, Aug., 1904, to June, 1905; served in European War, 1914-18.

McClellan, John William Tyndale, C.M.G. (1919).—Ed. at Malvern Coll. and Royal Agric. Coll.; ast. dist. offr., E. Africa Prot., 4th Oct., 1896; Africa gen. serv. medal 1896-6; Africa gen. serv. medal, Jubaland, 1898; col., R.A.P., 5th July, 1900; prov. commr., 1910.

McClelland, Francis Alexander Stewart.—B. 1874; ed. St. John's College, Cambridge; cadet, F.M.S., Nov., 1896; ast. res., Brunei, 1906; ag. audr. gen., F.M.S., 1912; audr. gen., S.S., 1919; ag. treas., F.M.S., mem. of fed. coun., Sept., 1920; ag. Br. res., Pahang, Nov., 1921-Sept., 1922; ag. Br. res., Perak, Apr., Sept., 1923.

McClintock, Samuel Alexander.—M.B., Ch. B. Edin., D.P.H., R.C.P. and S. Edin., R.F.P. and S. Glasgow, D.T.M. and H. Edin., certif. trop. diseases, Edin., M.D. Edin.; ed. Foyle Coll., Londonderry, Royal Univ. of Ireland, Univ. of Edin., King's Coll. Univ. of London and London schl. of trop. med.; house surg., general hosp., Sepoy Lines, Singapore, Aug., 1906; res. med. offr., St. John's Island quarantine statn. and ast. port health offr., S. Stiltns., Dec., 1903;
dep. port health offr., Singapore, Jan., 1906; res. med. offr., dist. hosp., Penang, June, 1906; dep. health offr., Penang, Aug., 1906; state surg. and health offr., Puket, West Siam, Mar., 1907; prin. med. offr., West Siam, Mar., 1908; med. offr., G. Coast, Apr., 1909; med. offr., Papua, Jan., 1911; pathologist, bacteriologist, etc., W. Australia, Feb., 1912; med. offr., dept. of pub. health, New South Wales, June, 1913; prin. med. offr. and chief health offr., Tasmania; chief-inspr. of factories and offr. adminstr. wages boards and industrial affairs, Tasmania, Sep., 1913; federal chief quarantine offr., Tasmania, Oct., 1913.

McCLoughin, Robert James.—B. 1881; ed. privately; St. Thomas's Hosp., Lond., 1888-1902; lieut.; 3rd King's Own Scottish Borderers, 1902-1905; lieut., Beds. regt., 1906; seconded to W.A.F.F., 1909-1910; priv. sec. and A.D.C. to gov., Gold Coast, 1911.

McClure, Andrew.—B.A. Oxon., Assoc. M. Inst. C.E., M. Inst. Water E.; ed. at Dover Coli. and Wadham Coll., Oxford; served in S. African war (King's medal with 4 clasps) 1900-1901; Derwent Valley water scheme, England, 1901-1905; ast. engr. on new water supply for Port Elizabeth, S. Africa, 1903-1905; diploma of R.G.S. in surveying and astronomy, 1906; ast. dir. pub. wks., Uganda Prot., 12th May, 1906; D.P.W., Zanzibar, 28th Nov., 1919; 3rd cls., Order of the Brilliant Star, Zanzibar.

McClure, Herbert Reginald.—Ed. at Eastman's Royal Naval Acad. and H.M.S. "Britannia"; China medal 1900, relief of Pekin clasp; ast. collr., E. Africa Prot., 5th Apr., 1906; polit. offr. with Sokot Punitive Force (ment. in desps.), and Mandi Field Force (ment. in desps.), A.G.S. Med.; dist. comsrr., 1910; res. comsrr., Gilbert and Ellice Is. Colony, Nov., 1921.

McColl, Duncan P., B.A.—B. 1864; ed. pub. schls., Elgin Co., Ontario, St. Thomas High Schl. and Toronto Univ.; principal, Union Schl., Calgary, Alberta, 1892 to 1897; inspr. of schls., Alberta, 1897 to 1902; principal, normal schl., N.W.T., 1902 to 1905; dep. min. of educn., Saskatchewan, 1905; now supt. of educn.

McCormick, Francis Harpur, B.A.—B. 1891; ed. St. Columba's Coll. and Dublin Univ.; supt., educn. dept., N. Prov., Nigeria, 7th Sept., 1921.

McCoy, W. T.—Director of educn., S. Australia, 1919.

McCrae, John, Ph.D., F.I.C., M.S.P.A., F. Chem. Soc., Priestly Schol., Kbrhard prize-man—Ast. chem., dept. of agr., Pretoria, 1903; ag. govt. chemist, col. sec.'s office, 1906; appt. confirmed, 1907; dept. of int., 1912; govt. analyst, 1917; examr., physics and chemv., Transvaal Pharmacy Bd., 1916; examr., chemv., Univ. of S. Africa, 1920; transf'd. to dept. of agr., 1st Apr., 1923.

Macrae, Lachlan, M.A. (Aberdeen), M.A. (Cantab.).—B. 1886; dir. of educn., Ceylon, Jan., 1922.

McRea, Hon. Charles, K.C.—B. 1877; ed. high schls., Queen's Univ., Kingston and Osgoode Hall, Toronto; barrister; el. to Ont. legis., 1914; re-el., 1919 and 1923; min. of mines in Ferguson admstrn., 1923.

Macdonald, Hon. Charles.—B. 1861; pres. of Austn. Lab. Fedrn., 1890-1892; M.L.A., Queensland, 1893-1901; returned to first H. of R., C. of A., 1901, and re-elected 1903 and 1906; chrmn. of comtees, H. of R., 1907; speaker, July, 1910, to June, 1913, and from 1914 to 1916.

Macdonald, Hon. Daniel Alexander—B. 1858; ed. privately and at gram. schl., coll. and Prince of Wales coll., P.E.I.; admits to bar, P.E.I., 1883; Manitoba bar, 1885; practised law in Manitoba; judge, ct. of King's Bench, Manitoba, 1906.

Macdonald, Hon. Edward Mortimer, K.C., LL.D.—B. 1855; ed. Pictou Acad. and Dalhousie Coll., N.S.; barrister; mem. of N. legis., 1897-1904; H. of C., 1904-17; re-el. to H. of C., 1921; min. of national defence in Ken. admstrn., 1923.

McDonald, Ernest Eldred.—B. 1870; ed. Sydenham Coll., Kent; supernum. clk., ed. office, Br. Honduras, 1887; clk. to atty.-gen., Feb., 1888; clk., col. engrnr.'s dept., Sept., 1888; 2nd clk., col. sec.'s office, June, 1892; ag. dist. comsrr. and pres. bd. of health, The Cayo, Apr., 1895; dist. vaccinator and pres. bd. of heal., Stann Creek, Mar., 1896; ch. clk., col. sec.'s office, Cyprus, Apr., 1897; ag. ast. sec., 1897-8; mun. comsrr., 1898; sec., Central Mejia-Iida, 1898; ag. ast. sec., 1899 and 1900; ag. comsrr., Kyrena, 1902 and 1907; coroner, 1902; mun. comsrr., Kyrena, 1902; pres., Kyrena hosp. comte., 1902; ag. comsrr., Famagusta, 1904; pres., mun. coman., Famagusta, 1904; pres., Famagusta hosp. bd., and ag. ast. sec., 1904; comsrr., Kyrena, 1912; mem., leg. com., July, 1922.

McDonald, K. H. E.—Ast. supt., pol. & Honduras, July, 1919; ag. supt., pol., July, 1919 to July, 1920; supt., Belize fire brig., Oct., 1920; on mily. service in Egypt, Mesopotamia, India, 1915-19 (ment. in desp.); Merit Cross Medal, 1918.

Macdonald, Hon. Hector Y.—B. 1871; ed., common schls. of Nova Scotia, and Univ. of St. Francis Xavier's Coll., Antigonish, N.S. (A.B. 1900); studied law in the law schl. of Dalhousie Univ.; called to bar of N.S. 1895; practised in Sydney, NS., removed to Regina, 1906; called to bar of Sask., 4th May, 1906; as clk. in atty.-gen.'s dept.; city solr., Regina, K.C., 1913; justice, ct. of King's Bench, Sask., 2nd Mar., 1918.

Macdonald, Hugh.—M.B., C.M. Univ. Edin., 1893; F.R.G.S., ast. col. surgeon, Lagos, 24th Apr., 1896; on activeserv. in Lagos Hinterland, 1896 (medal); ag. M.O.H. for town of Lagos, May to Aug., 1901; provincial med. offr., Fiji, 1st Dec., 1901; stip. mag. of Fiji, 24th Apr., 1902; res. comsrr. and prov. med. offr., Rotuma, 23rd Apr., 1902; dist. comsrr. and dist. med. offr., Rotuma, 12th Aug., 1916.

Macdonald, Hon. James Alexander—B. 1858; ed. coll. inst., Stratford, Ont.; called to Ontario bar, 1889; Brit. Columbia bar, 1897; K.C., 1905; bencher, Brit. Columbia Law Soc., 1906-7; elec. to legis. Brit. Columbia, 1903 re-elec. 1907; leader of the opposition, 1903-1909; ch. just., ct. of appeal, Brit. Columbia, 1909.

McDonald, John, D.F.C., B.Sc. (honors), Mycologist, agrl. dept., Kenya, Sept., 1920.

Macdonald, John William.—B. 1883; ed., Timaru Main and High Schls., N.Z.; barrister, dept. of justice, N.Z., 1900; ast. solr., p. trust. office, 1906; solr., 1909; ast. pub. trust., 1917; pub. trustee, 1920.

McDonald, O. J.—B. 1859; Out Island comsrr. (4th div.), Bahamas, 1909; 3rd div., 1914.
MACDONALD, W. G. MACLEOD.—Imp. post office, 1899; transf'd, to combined post and tel. erv. of E. Africa and Uganda, 1908; dep. postmtr., 1910; ch. clk. and storekeeper, 1913; postmtr., 1913; in charge radio teles., Lake Victoria area, 1914; 1st cls. postmtr., 1918; asst. postmtr.-en., 1922.

MCDONALD, W. M., M.R.C.S. (England), R.C.P. (London).—B. 1870; ed. Liverpool coll. and St. Bart.'s Hosp., London; house physician, St. Bart.'s, 1896; ag. med. offr., Montserrat, 1897; litto, Antigua, 1899; med. offr., Montserrat, 901; med. offr., burgher refugee camp, Klipspruit, Transvaal, 1902; med. offr., Antigua, 904; med. offr., St. Kitts, 1905; J.P., St. Kitts, 1906; med. supt., hosp., etc., St. Johns, 913; med. offr. of health, St. Johns, 1914; surgeon-lieut., Antigua defence force, 1914.

MCDONNELL, MICHAEL FRANCIS JOSEPH.—B. 1882; ed. St. Paul's Schol. and St. John's Coll., Lambeth (scholar), B.A., 1904; pres., Cambridge Union, 1904; called to the bar, Inner Temple, May, 1906; asst. dist. comsrr., Gold Coast, Jan., 911; pol. mag. and inspr. of schls., Gambia, Apr., 1913; legal adviser, Gambia, July, 1918; olnr.-gen., Sierra Leone, Aug., 1918; atty.-gen., Apr., 1920; ag. ch. just., circuit judge and judge of ct. of appeal on various occasions, 1919-23.

MCDOUGALL, ARCH.—B. 1889; ed. West of Scot. Tech. Coll., Glasgow; civ. engr., P. and W. Anderson, rly. contractors, 1906-11; asst. engr., Caledonian Rly., 1911-12; M.I.E.S., 1914; engr., way and works dept., Demerara Rly. Co., Br. Guiana, 1912-21; engr., way and works dept., col. transport dept., 1922.

McELDERRY, SAMUEL BURNSIDE BOYD.—B. 1885; ed. at Campbell Coll., Belfast, and Trin. Coll., Dublin; math. schlr., B.A., sen. mod. n. maths., sen. mod. in exp. science; cadet, Hong Kong, 1909; ag. asst. dist. offr., northern list, New Territories, 1911; ag. deputy regar., supreme ct., 1912; J.P., 1912; ag. 1st asst. sec. or Chinese affairs, 1913; ag. deputy regar., supreme ct., 1913; ag. asst. dist. offr., Southern Dist., New Territories, 1913; apptd. as an offr. of 3rd grade, 1915; temporarily in C.O. 1915-1917, and 1919; released for mil. serv., 1918; ag. ch. asst. sec. for Chinese affairs, 1919 to 1920; attached, col. secs. office, 1920; ag. asst. col. sec. nd clk. of couns., Nov., 1920 to 1921; addt. to secretariat, League of Nations, opium section, 1922; represented Br. Eastern Cols. on opium question at internat. red cross confce., Bangkok, 1922; asst. col. sec. and clk. of couns., 1924.

McELWAINE, PERCY ALEXANDER, B.A. (Hons.), LL.B. (1907).—Ed., Campbell Coll., Belfast and Trinity Coll., Dublin; called to Irish bar (King's Inn) 1908; Alberta bar, 1913; temp. lieut., Royal Irish Rifles, B.E.F., 1916-19; stip. nag. and coroner, 2nd and 3rd dists., St. Lucia, 1920; crown counsel, Kenya, Apr., 1923.

McFALL, JOHN LYND.—B. 1888; educ. Coleraine Acad. Inst. and Queen's Coll., Galway; B.A., Royal Univ. of Ireland, 1909; cadet, Straits Stltmrs., Nov., 1910; passed final exam. in Chinese, Aug., 1913; ag. dist. offr., Christmas s., Aug., 1913 to July, 1915; ag. asst. prot. of Chinese, Singapore, May to Dec., 1916; ditto, Melangor and Negri Sembilan, Jan., 1917; ag. st. asst. sup't. Chandu monopoly, Negri Sembilan, Feb. to July, 1917; ag. prot., chinese, Penang (Iv., F.M.S.), Aug., 1920; addt. to cust. dep., F.M.S., Aug., 1922; supernvy. offr., ics. III., Nov., 1922; dep. pub. prosecutor, Perak, Apr., 1923; g. dep. pub. pros., F.M.S., Apr., 1924.

MACFARLANE, JOHN ALEXANDER, M.D., C.M. (Edin.).—B. 1871; entered med. serv., Trinidad, 25th Jan., 1895; dist. med. offr., 1st Aug., 1915.

MACFARLANE, NEIL MORRISON.—B. 1886; med. offr., Basutoland 1894; dep. prin. med. offr., Apr.; 1920; supt., leper stltm., 1920; served in European War; prin. med. offr., 1923.

MACFEAT, P. D.—Exec. engr., P.W.D., E.A.P., Oct., 1913.

MACGILLIVRAY, JOHN WALKER, F.S.I.—B. 1884; 4th asst., trig. survey, Trinidad, 1901; 3rd asst., 1903; 2nd asst., 1904; 1st asst., 1906; qual. by exam. for diploma or sworn land survr., 1906; survr., Trinidad rly. extensions, 1909; survr., roads and traces, P.W.D., 1912; topographical asst., survey dept., 1917; crown survr., 1920.

MACGREGOR, ALEXANDER JOHN, B.A. (Cape).—B. 1864; ed., Oriel Coll., Oxford; 1st cls. hons., mod. hist.; called to the bar (Inner Temple), 1889; admitted to Cape sup. ot. bar, 1882; puisne judge, Eastern dist. local divn., Grahamstown, 1st Aug., 1913; puisne judge, O.F.S. prov. divn., 15th July, 1915.

MACGREGOR, D. S.—Fellow of soc. of acnts. and auditors; ch. audit clk., Leewards, Apr., 1895; and federal acnt., Jan., 1896; ag. treas., St. Kitts-Nevis, Dec., 1896; ag. aud.-gen. and mem. of Leewards and Antigua leg. couns. and Antigua exec. coun., Sept., 1897, to Jan., 1898; on special mission to investigate and adjust acnts. of Trinidad, Dec., 1899, to May, 1900; auditor, British Honduras, June, 1900; ag. reg.-gen. and reg. of sup. ct. on five occasions in 1904-5; ag. dist. comsrr. of Belize, Mar.-Apr., 1905; aud.-gen., Mauritius, 11th Oct., 1905; chmn., widows' and orphans' fund, May, 1906; col. auditor, Ceylon, 8th Apr., 1909; treas., Nigeria, 27th May, 1914; is also chmn. of P.O.G. fund, currency offr., and public custodian.

MACGREGOR, ERNEST S.—B. 1867; pub. schl. teacher, Bahamas, 1890; Out Island comsrr. (4th div.) and teacher, 1917.

MACGREGOR, GREGOR.—Ed., George Watson's Coll., Edin. and Edin. Univ.; solr., 1907; asst. res., N. Nigeria, 22nd Nov., 1911.

MACGREGOR, SIR JAMES COMYN, KT. BACH. (1923), C.M.G. (1920).—2nd lieut. 7th battn. K.R.R., 1881; lieut., 1881; sub.-inspr. Basuto land mtd. pol., 1884; asst. comsrr., 1893; govt. sec. and master, Bech. Prot., Nov., 1912; ag. res. comsrr., May to Sept., 1913; special comsrr., Ngamiland, 1914; res. comsrr., Bech. Prot., 15th Dec., 1917; ret., 11th Nov., 1923.

MACGREGOR, JOHN GRANT, M.B., B.Ch. (Aberdeen).—Med. offr., S. Stltmrs., Feb., 1908.

MACGREGOR, HON. WILLIAM CUNNINGHAM, K.C. (1914).—B. 1862; ed. George Watson's Coll., Edinburgh, Edinburgh Univ., and Otago Univ. (N.Z.); gold medallist, N.Z. Law Soc'y., 1883; solr.-gen., N.Z., July, 1920; judge, sup. ct., N.Z., 1923.

MCHARDY, W.—Asst. local auditor, E.A.P., 1909; asst. traffic man., Uganda rly., 1914; deputy traffic man., 1917.

MACHTIG, E.G.S., M.B.E. (1918).—B. 1889; educ. at St. Paul's and Trin. Coll., Cambridge (scholar) also at the Sorbonne, Paris; 1st cls. 2nd div., class tripes, Pt. I., 1911; B.A. (Cantab), 1911; apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd cls. clk., C.O., 15th Oct., 1912; ag. 1st cls. clk., 1st Nov., 1917; prin., 1st Apr., 1920.

MOINNES, WILLIAM, B.A., LL.D., F.R.S.C., F.G.S.A.—B. 1858; ed. Collge Schol., Fredericton,
and Univ. of New Bruns.; joined staff of geol. surv. as ast. geologist and explorer 1st Jan., 1882; geologist, 1892; directing geologist, 1915; dir. Victoria Memorial Mus., and editor-in-ch., dept. of mines, 1919; fellow, Geol. Soc. of America, 1889; fellow, Royal Soc. of Canada, 1912; pres., sec. IV., 1920; has published numerous repts. on geological subjects.

MACINTYRE, DUNCAN CHARLES, O.B.E. (1919), M.B.E. (1918).—Capt. R.N.R. (retired); harbour master, Penang, Sept., 1903; special service outside colony, Jan., 1904; res. naval offr., Penang (in addition), June, 1916; comdr. Coast Defence Vols. (in addition), May, 1917; promoted Capt. R.N.R. (retired) 11th Nov., 1918; received thanks of Admiralty for services as res. naval offr., Penang.

MACIVER, AGNES R., M.A. hon.—B. 1889; ed., Geo. Watson's Ladies' Coll., Edinburgh. High Schl., Weimar, Germany, Normal Schl., Melun, France, Edinburgh Univ. (1st cls. hon., mod. lang.), 1914; educn., dipl., Edinburgh Univ., 1915; lady supervisor, Malay girls' schls., S.S. and F.M.S., 1918; Malay certif., Schl. of Oriental Studies, 1919; passed 2nd standard, Malay, 1920.

McJANNET, WILLIAM J.—Ed., Irvine Royal Acad. and Technical Coll., Glasgow; ast. engr., Uganda Rly., Mar., 1913.
