MACKAY, ALEXANDER HOWARD, B.A., B.Sc., LL.D., F.R.S.C.—B. 1848; ed. at Picton Academy, Prov. Normal Coll., and Dalhousie Univ., Halifax, 1873; principal Annapolis Roy., 1873, Picton, 1873-1889, and Halifax, 1889-1891, academies; lectr. in biology, Dalhousie Univ., 1889-1910; pres., teachers' assoc. of Nova Scotia, 1874-1876, of Canada, 1898, of N. Scotia inst. of science, 1900, 1901, and 1902, of summer schl. of science, Atlantic provs., 1887 and 1888, of Victoria schl. of art and design, of biological sect. of roy. soc. of Canada; vice-pres. of religious educn. assoc. (America); mem. of geographic bd. of Canada, of marine bd. biological laboratories of Canada, of American and British assoc. for advancement of science, etc.; gov. of Dalhousie univ., of Halifax ladies' coll., etc.; memb. of exec., Strathcona trust for Canada; editor of Dalhousie Gazette, 1870-1873, Educational Review, 1887-1891; Journal of Education, 1891 to date; supt. of educn. for prov. of N. Scotia, since 1891; representative of N. Scotia at Imperial Education Conference, 1911 and 1923.

MACKAY, GEORGE, M.A. (Hons.), Aberdeen, 1902.—B. 1880; ast. master, Victoria schl., Seychelles, 23rd Aug., 1903; ag. headmaster, ditto, and ag. inspr. of schls., Nov., 1903; headmaster, Victoria schl., and inspr. of schls., Dec., 1904; ag. auditor and mem. of couns., June-Aug., 1909; principal, King's Coll., 1911; chrmn., bd. of directors, Carnegie public library, Feb., 1912; chief inspr. of schls., Mauritius, Apr., 1914; supt. of schls., Fiji, Dec., 1916; sec., bd. of educn., Jan., 1917; capt. and comdg. offr., Fiji schl. and defence cadet corps, Mar., 1918; resig. coman., Apr., 1919; dir., educn., Trinidad and Tobago, Apr., 1922.

MCKEAG, CAPT. V. M.—Ast. dist. comanr., Kenya, May, 1920.

MCKEAN, LIEUT.-COL. ALEXANDER CHALMERS, C.M.G. (1891).—B. 1852; cornet, Inniskilling Dragoons, Oct., 1871; A.D.C., Bengal, 1880; served in Transvaal war, 1881; staff offr., Zululand war (Khowe column), 1883; D.A.A. and Q.M.G., S. Africa, 1884; ag. D.A.A.G., Natal, 1886; surv. to Zululand and New Republic boundary comanr., 1886; ast. comanr., Zululand, 1887; comanr. of Basuto levies in Zulu disturbances, 1888; was honourably mentioned and made brevet lieut.-col. for services; ast. mil. sec. gov., Malta, 1889.

MCKENNY, J. D.—Ast. dist. comanr., E.A.I., Jan., 1917.

MCKENNY, CHARLES WILLIAM—B. 1888; B.A., Trin. Coll., Dubl., 1907; M.D., B.A.O., Trin. Coll., Dubl., L.M. (Rotunda), B.F., H. S. and H. F., Meath hosp. and Co. Den. Infirmary; graduate of Coombe midwifery hosp., diploma of London S.T.M.; fellow of Tr. Soc.; med. offr., Hong Kong, 1912; in charge Tungwa hosp., Victoria Gaol (1912 to 1917), infectious disease hosp.; supt., civil hospital lunatic asylum, 1917; ag. P.C.M.O., 1919; mem. of comm. to enquire into child labour; lecturer in clinical medicine, Univ. of HKong; mem. and lecturer to St. John's Aux. ans. comte.; lecturer in sanitary science to Inst.; mem. Brit. Med. Assoc.; surg.-lieut., HKong Volr. Corps; ag. prin. civ. med. 1923.

MACKENZIE, CAPT. ANGUS DURHAM, K.C.—B. 1883; ed. Aberdeen and Edinburgh Univ.; 2nd cls. supervisor, cust., Dec., 1913; sewn for mily. serv. with Seaforth Highlanders, June; staff capt., W.A.F.F., 1917; ag. intelligence offr., Gold Coast, from Nov., 1917 to Oct., contr., enemy property, offr. in charge, resp. and cust., Togoland, July, 1920; rep. of dep'ts. in final handing over of Louis and portion of Togoland ceded to the French, Oct., 1920; colnr. of cust., Jan., 1921; ag. compt., cust., Aug., 1922; contr., enemy property, Gold Coast and Br. Togoland, 15th Oct., 1921; 11th May, 1923 and from 16th Aug., 1924; pr. colnr., cust., 1st Feb., 1924; ag. dep. comt., 16th to 19th Aug., 1924 and from 30th Aug., 1924.

MCKENZIE, HON. DANIEL DUNCA.—B. 1868; ed. pub. schl. and Sydney acad.; barmayor of N. Sydney, N.S., for five consec. years; judge, county et dist. No. 7, N.S.; el. to leg. ass., N.S., 1900 and 1901; el. 1904; re-el., g.e., 1908, 1911, 1917 and 1921; leader of opposition in H.C. after the death of Wilfred Laurier until end of 2nd sess., 1919; gen. in King admtn., 29th Dec., 1921; sup. ct., Nova Scotia, 1923.

MACKENZIE, H. A.—B. 1881; ed. Edinb. Acad. and Fettes Coll., Edinburgh; clk. exec. agts. office, 24th Apr., 1901; ast. treas., (pro Prot.), 20th June, 1907; treas., offr., Kampala, 1st Oct., 1907 to Feb., 1909, and Oct., 1910; ast. dist. comanr., 2nd July, 1911; ast. dist. comanr., Entebbe, Aug., 1911 to 1913, and May, 1914 to May, 1915; ag. reg. of docs. and adminar.-gen., Aug., 1912; dist. mag., Entebbe, for various pers., 1912-15; ast. dist. comanr., Kampala, Nov., 1913 to May, 1914; second in command, armed levies (afterwards Baganda Rifles), 1914 to May, 1915; senr. ast. dist. comanr., Kampala, 28th May, 1915 to 8th Nov., 1916; dist. comanr., Bunyoro, Nov., 1917 to May, 1918; dist. comanr., Bunyoro, 1st July, 1918 to 21st Aug., 1919.

MACKENZIE, HON. SIR THOMAS, G.C.M.G. (1920).—B. 1854; ent. N.Z. parl., 1887; min. industries and commerce and min. of agr., N.Z., 1910; prime min. and min. of lands, 1912; comanr. in London, 1912-20; mem. of commit. of ex-service men within the Empire, M.L.C., 1921.
McKEOWN, HON. HARRISON ANDREW, B.A., L.B., K.C., D.C.L.—B. 1861; ed. at Fredericton coll., schl., and Mt. Allison univ.; called to the bar, New Brunswick, 1885; elec. to legis., N.B., 1890; s-elec., 1893, 1903, and 1908; solr.-gen., 1903; ty-gen., 1908; judge of sup. ct., N.B., 1909; chief just., King's Bench, 1916; chmn., bd. of ly. comsrs., 1924.

McKERRON, PATRICK ALEXANDER BRUCE—L. 1896; ed. Fettes Coll., Edin.; 2nd lieut. Gordon Highrs., 1914; capt., 1916; trans. A.R.O., 1917; capt., 20th Punjab, 1918; emb., Feb., 1919; cadet, S.S., Feb., 1920; tds., treas., Singapore; ag. ast. asupt. govt. monopolies, Singapore, Sept., 1921; passed final exam. in Malay, June, 1921.

MACKIE, GEORGE DOUGLAS, O.B.E. (1923)—g. 2nd clk., govt. office, St. Vincent, Dec., 1890, to Apr., 1891; 2nd clk. and cashier, treasy., pl., 1891, to May, 1892, and from Jan., 1897 to Oct., 1898; clk., crown lands and survey office, fay to Dec., 1892; audit clk., Jan., 1893, to dec., 1896; 2nd clk. and acctnt., treasy., Trinidad, Nov., 1898; ch. clk., Jan., 1903; ch. ub-collr. and revenue offr., treasy., St. Lucia, an., 1911; ag. treas. on several occasions in 1911 to 1915; treas., Nov., 1915.

MCKINLEY, JOHN, B.A.—Served with I.Y. in African campaign, 1900-1; acctnt., and statistician, educ. dept., O.R.C., 1st July, 1902; provincial acctnt., O.F.S. prov., 15th Aug., 1910.

MCKINNEY, E. H.—B. 1877; ent. Bahamas iv. ser., 1898; Out Island comsrr. (2nd div.), 909; comsrr. (1st div.), 1912.

MACKNINSON, HON. D.—Attorney-gen. and min. of rlyws., Victoria, Dec., 1913; dir.-gen. of recruiting, Commonwealth of Australia, during the European war; comsrr. for C. of A. to J.S.A., 1923.

MACKNINSON, WILLIAM LUNAN, M.A. (Aberdeen), 1911.—B. 1888; astt. auditor, G. Coast, 23rd Nov., 1912; ag. senr. astt. auditor, 23rd May, 1917 to 6th Jan., 1918, and from 18th Mar. to 8th Oct., 1919; ag. astt. treas. (in addition to own duties), 23rd May to 10th Sept., 1919; g. senr. astt. auditor, 19th Oct., 1919.

MCLAREN, HUGH, A.M.I.M.E.—European instructor, tech. schl., Accra, G. Coast, 5th June, 1909; astt. mast., training institution, Accra, st July, 1910; ag. principal, ditto, on several occasions.

MCLAREN, JOHN SUTHERLAND, M.A. (hons.).—B. 1900; ed. Edinburgh Univ.; cadet, Hong Kong, 1923.

MACLEAN, ADRIAN JOHN.—Ed. at Selwyn coll., Camb., B.A., 1895; M.A., 1901; astt. collr., E. Africa Prot., 14th May, 1901; collr., st April, 1905; recorder of titles, 1911; senr. comsrr., Kenya, May, 1920.

MACLEAN, ANGUS A., K.C., B.C.L.—B. 1854; d. Prince of Wales Coll., Charlottetown and Harvard law schl.; barrister; Q.C. (Dominion), 394; law clk.; Prince Edward Is. legislature for 9 years; pres. law soc., P.E.I., 1904; M.L.A., P.E.I., 1888-1900; unsucc. cand. for H. of Canada, at bye-elecs., 1902 and 1904; elected at e., 1911; comptroller of the Royal North West mounted Pol., Oct., 1917; financial contr., 9th eb., 1920.

MACLEAN, F. H.—B. 1889; apptd. after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div., and assigned to bd. educn., May, 1908; transf'd to C.O., Dec., 1911; on military serv., from 26th Apr., 1917, to 3rd Feb., 1919; cler.offr., higher grade, 24th Jan., 1922.

MACLEAN, G., M.B., Ch.B. (Glas.).—Temp. lieut., R.A.M.C., Mar., 1918 to Mar., 1919; temp. capt., Mar., 1919 to June, 1920; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 1st Apr., 1921.

MACLEAN, HON. JOHN D., M.D.—B. 1875; ed. pub. schls., Prince of Wales Coll., and normal schl., P.E.I.; schl.-teacher for some time; removed to British Columbia, 1893, where engaged in teaching until 1900; graduated in medicine, McGill Univ., 1906; returned to B. Columbia, taking up practice in Greenwood; mayor of Greenwood for two years; elec. to legis. assem., 1916; prov. sec. and min. of educn. in Brewster cabinet, B. Columbia, 1916; min. of finance, educn. and industries in Oliver cabinet, 1924.

MACLEAN, JOHN DOUGLAS.—B. 1865; ent. civ. ser., Canada, 1876, as 3rd cl. clk.; promoted to junr. 2nd cl., 1878; senr. 2nd cl., 1883; 1st ols., 1887; ch. clk. and sec. of the dept. of Indian affairs, 1897; astt. dep. asupt. gen. and sec., 1908.

MACLEAN, SIMON JAMES, M.A., LL.B., Ph.D.—B. 1871; comsrr. of the Canadian govt. to report on rly. rate grievances, 1901; advr. to comm., of govt. to draft Railway Act, 1903; prof'r. of polit. econ., Toronto Univ., 1906-1908; apptd. a mem. of rly. comsrr., Canada, 1908; re-apptd., 8th Nov., 1918; astt. chief comsrr., 6th Aug., 1919.

MACLENNAN, FINLAY MALCOLM.—B. 1887; ed., Tarbutt Public Schl.; Sault Ste. Marie, Ont., High Schl.; astt. serv. of dept. of rlys. and canals, Can., as officeman, Sault Ste. Marie Canal, Sept., 1910; transferred, Port Nelson on Hudson Bay terminals work, as junr. engr., 1912; astt. audr., dept., rlys. and canals, Ottawa, 1st Apr., 1915; audr., 1917; ch. audr., 1918; astt. comprtr., 1920.

MELEOD, HON. ALEXANDER DONALD, M.P.—B. 1872; ed. privately; mem. N.Z. parl. since 1919; min. of lands, 1924.

MELEOD, HON. SIR EZZIKIEL, KT. BACH (1917), B.C.L. (Harv.), LL.D. (New Brunswick univ.).—B. 1840; ed. at high schl., King's co., New Brunswick; called to the bar, 1868; Q.C., 1882; atty.-gen. of N.B., 1882-1883; mem. of senate of Univ. of N.B., since 1869; elec. to H. of C., Canada, 1891; judge, sup. ct. of N.B., and judge of N.B. v. a. dist., 1896; chief just., N.B., 1914-1917.

MCLoughlin, A. P.—Entd. civ. serv., O.R.C., 23rd Mch., 1900; ag. distributor of stamps, Transvaal, 21st Aug., 1900; distributor of stamps, 1901; ch. clk., treasy., 1st July, 1903; ch. clk., dept. of finance, Union of S. Africa, 1910; under sec. for finance, Union of S. Africa, 1st Aug., 1912; comsrr. for inland rev., Oct., 1916.

MACLURKIN, ALFRED ROBERT.—M.B., Ch.B. Glasg., D.P.H., R.C.P. and S. Edin., R.F.P. and S. Glasg., D.T.M. Liverpool; ed. Allan Glen's, Glasgow, Univ. of Glasg., Univ. of Liverpool Schl. of Trop. Med.; R.M.O. Grey's Hosp., Pietermaritzburg, Natal, 1901; dist. surg., Nqutu, Zululand, 1902; A.M.O. Metrop. Asylm. Bd., 1906; astt. educ. med. offr., Surrey C.C., 1908; govt. med. offr., Cook and N. Islda., 1911; astt. educ. med. offr., Derbyshire C.C., 1914; govt. med. offr., Fiji, 1915; ag. med. supt., leper asylum, Makogai, 1916; dist. comsrr., dist. med. offr. and M.O.H., Bua Prov., 1917.

MOAHON, CECIL.—Knt. S. Rhodesia civ. serv., Nov., 1909; served S. African rebellion and German S.W. African campaign, 1914-15; served E. Africa campaign with 1st Rhodesian Regt., 1915-18; capt. and adjt., 8th S. African Inf. Regt.; "1914-15" Star and M.C.; astt. polit. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 6th Mar., 1918.
McMILLAN, Sir Daniel Hunter, K.C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1846; ed. Canada; served with Canadian Volunteers on Niagara frontier, 1864; during Fenian raid, 1866; Red River exped., 1870; N.W. rebellion (medal), 1885; mem. for Winnipeg in Manitoba legislature, 1880; mem. of Manitoba govt., 1889; lt.-gov. of Manitoba, 6th Sept., 1900; re-apptd. for second term, 1906; retired, 1911.

McMILLAN, L. B.—B. 1873; ed. pub. schls., Charlottetown, Prince Edward Is.; messenger, P.E.I. Is. govt., 1890; clk., 1893; sec. for pub. wk., P.E.I. Is., 1900.

McMILLAN, Hon. Sir Robert Furse, Kt. Bath. (1916).—Queen's scholar, Westminster school; scholar, Trin. Hall, Camb.; senior in law tripods, 1879; holder of law studentship at Trin. Hall; Inns of Court studentship and Inner Temple common law scholarship; called to the bar, 1881; joined western circuit and Devon and Exeter sessions; puisne judge, W. Australia, 1903; ch. justice, Dec., 1913.

McMURRAY, Hon. Edward James, B.A., LL.B.—B. 1878; ed. Manitoba Univ. and Man. Law Schl.; barrister; el. to H. of C., Can., 1921; solr.-gen. in King adminstr., 1923.

McNAB, Hon. Archibald P.—B. 1864; ed. pub. and high schls., Vankleek Hill; elec. to prov. legis., Sask., 14th Aug., 1908; min. of mun. affairs, 10th Dec., 1908; re-elec. by acclamation at bye-elec., 24th Dec., 1908, and g.e., 1912, 1917, and 1921; min. of pub. wks., 1913.

MACNAUGHTEN, Leslie Hay.—Ed. at Wellington Coll., and Truro Survey and Mining Coll.; asst. engnr., P.W.D., E. Africa Prot., 15th May, 1905; exec. engnr., Oct., 1913.

MACNAUGHTEN, T. C., C.M.G. (1923), C.B.E. (1918).—B. 1872; ed. Charterhouse and Oxford; scholar of Hertford Coll., 1892; 1st class classical moda., 1894; B.A., 1896; apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd class clk., Local Govt. Bd., Feb., 1896; 2nd class clk., C.O., Sept., 1896; priv. sec. to Earl of Selborne, Dec., 1899, to Earl of Onslow, Nov., 1900, to Duke of Marlborough, July, 1903; 1st cl. clk., 24th Mar., 1904; principal clk., 6th July, 1917; chmn. E.I.O., Oct., 1912; mem. of comte. for sttlmt. of ex-service men within the Empire, 1917; vice-chmn., Oversea Sttlmt. Comte., 1919.

McNAUGHTON, J. G.—M.B., Ch.M. (hons.), 1893; M.D., 1896; M.R.C.P.S., 1901; ed. at Edin. and Paris Univ.; formerly physician at Ancoats hosp., Manchester, and asst. physician, consumption hosp., Manchester; also asst. physician, Crossly sanatorium for consumption; med. offr., Ellioe Is., 1915; ag. sen. med. offr., Gilbert and Ellioe Is., Jan., 1916; sen. med. offr., Apr., 1916; sen. med. offr., Samoa, May, 1919; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Apr., 1920.

MONULTY, Thos. Sydney.—B. 1870; ed. at Marist Coll., Sydney; clk., acct. branch, wks. dept., Perth, W. Australia, 1896; clk. corres. clk., ditto, 1897; mem. mun. coun., Claremont, 1901-3; under-sec. for goldfields water supply admin., 1903; under-sec. for agric. and industries, 1909.

MOGWAN, Islay.—3rd clk., col. sec.'s off., Fiji, Sept., 1892; stip. mag., asst. to native comsnr., and tax inspr., Lau, May, 1896; stip. mag. and tax inspr., Navus, and comsnr. for Namasi, Feb., 1900; stip. mag., Lomaiviti and Tailevu; comsnr. and tax inspr., Lomaiviti; offr. in charge, Levuka gool, Jan., 1904; inspr.-gen. of constab. and prisons, and sheriff, 15th Sept., 1909; M.L.C., 1909; seconded as ag. H.B.M.'s consul and agent, Tonga, Apr., 1911, to Mar., 1911; nat. comsnr., Oct., 1913; offr. comdg. loc. forces, and lieut.-col., defence forces of Fiji, Aug., 1914; mentioned by Army Council services in 1914 in connection with defense of Fiji; British agt. and consul., Tonga, June, 1917; also judl. comsnr. and dep. comsnr., Tonga, Jan., 1917; ag. col. sec., 24th May, 1921; gov't. sec., Aug., 1921.

MACPHAIL, John Addison.—Ck., P.W.D., Transvaal, 1902; ch. clk. to govt. archt., Jan., 1904; ch. clk., P.W.D., Transvaal, Mar., 1904; under-sec. for pub. wks., Union of S. Afr., Apr., 1920; ag. sec. for pub. wks., Sept., 1921.

MACPHERSON, Barbara.—Ed. Dunn-H.G. Schi. and Skerry's Coll., Edinburgh; apptd. after compet. exam. typist, Lond. serv., 1912; transf. to C.O., May, 1918; shorthandwriter, Aug., 1918; cler. offr., Jan., 1920.

MACPHERSON, John Stuart.—B. 1878; ed. Watson's Coll. and Edin. Univ. (M.A., 1898); 2nd lieut. A. & S. Highlanders, Jan., 1915; France, Apr., 1916-Jan., 1919; cadet, F.M., Mar., 1921; ag. 4th asst. sec. to govt., F.M., Aug., 1921; passed cadet, July, 1922; ag. dist. offr., Kuala Selangor, Aug., 1922; 2nd lieut. M.V.I., May, 1923; ag.-dist. offr., Raub, May, 1923.

McPHILLIPS, Hon. Albert Edward.—B. 1861; ed. St. Boniface and Manitoba Coll.; barrister; K.C., 1900; elected to leg. assn., B.C., 1898; atty.-gen., 1903; subsequently pr. of coun.; judge, st. of appeal, B.C., 1913; mem. N.W. rebellion under Gen. Middleton, 1885.

McQUADE, J. H.—Imp. cust., 1913; cnst. Kenya, July, 1920.

MACQUARIE, Edmund Jeffrey.—B. 1878; ed. Queen's Coll., B. Guiana and Calm (at Cambridge); B.A., L.B., 1906; called to bar, Inner Temp., 1906; ag. stip. mag. B. Guiana, June to Nov., 1906, and July, 1907-Mar., 1914; dormant comsnr. as stip. mag. apptd. J.P. and comsnr. of oaths, Dec., 1915; asst. dist. comsnr., Gold Coast, 1915; sen. counsel, crown, 1916; ag. chief regiar., Apr.-May, 1917; ag. sen. crown counsel, 1917; ag. pol. mag., Nov., 1917 to April, 1918; ag. solr.-gen., Apr.-Dec., 1919; ag. ch. regiar., Apr. to Oct., 1919; solr.-gen., Tanganyika Territory, 22nd Sept., 1919; ag. atty.-gen., 5th Nov., 1923 to 8th Sept., 1924.

MACRAE, Donald Mackenzie, M.B., Ch. Glasgow Univ. (1896); M.D. (1920); F.R.G.S.; Surg. capt., Bechuanaland Prot. pol., 1903; maj. major, 1915; prin. med. offr., 1917; J.P., 1917.

MACRAE, Duncan Mackenzie, M.B., Ch. Glasgow (1896); M.B., Ch. B. (1900); M.D. (1921); Med. offr., Bechuanaland Prot., 1919.

MACRAE, Lauchlan, M.A. (Aberdeen), M.C. (Cantab.), B. 1886; dir. of educn., Ceylon, July, 1922.

McROBERTS, Capt. B. A.K.—Natal mem.; pol., 1903-08; Natal rebellion, 1906; Umr operations, 1907; inspr., veterinary pol., R.A., 1909; asst. inspr., pol., Mar., 1910; asst. sept., Sept., 1911; capt., Gordon Highlanders, Aug., 1915; France, 1916; called to bar, MacTemple, Jan., 1917; attld., Highland Light Inf., Mesopotamia, Mar., 1917; seconded, polit. dist. dist. mag. and dep. mily. gov., Basraah, 1917; mily. mission to Siberian gov't., 1919; aspt., Kenya Colony, May, 1920; mag., Zanzibar Prot., Jan., 1921; ag. asst. judge, Mar.-Oct., 1922; May to Dec., 1924.

MOVILLY, R. W., M.V.O. (1920).—Gen. mlt. of New Zealand rlys. since 1919.
McWHAE, HON. SIR JOHN, KT. BACH.—B. 1858; ed. Dumfries Acad., Scotland; I.L.C. for Melbourne Prov., 1909; min. for pub. ks. in Bowser govt., 1918; hon. min. in Lawson distmst. and hon. ag. min. of health in charge of organisation dealing with influenza epidemic, pr., 1919; six years chmn. stock exchange, Melbourne; dir. of several companies; now agt.-en. for Victoria in London; ret., 1924.

MACWILLIAM, DONALD KINTON.—2nd clk., easy., St. Kitts, 1894; rev. offr. and quarantine ffr., Apr., 1894; rev. offr. and harb. mast., 1906; 1st rev. offr. and harb. mast., 1st Apr., 1915; mem., poor law bd., Mar., 1918; mem., quarantine d., St. Kitts, 3rd May, 1921.

MAGENNS, WILLIAM BABINGTON.—B. 1869; i. pub. schl., Uitenhage; clk. mag.'s office ort Elizabeth, 1888; ast. mag., Uitenhage, 1892; Willowmore, 1893; ast. mag., Uitenhage, 1894; Willowmore, 1895; Beaufort West, 1896; Vryburg, 1897; somerset East, 1899; dep. commdt., several places during Anglo-Boer War and dep. admstr., martial lw.; mag., Aberdeen, 1902; Namakwa land, J.O.S.; commnr., relief distress, N.W. Districts asylum, 1909; inspgr. mag. and inspr. prisons, 1912; sen. mag., East London, 1920; sp. grade mag., Kimberley, and regis. of deeds, 1923.

MAGILL, GEORGE SANDS.—B. 1835; pol. probationer, F.M.S., Nov., 1904; passed final exam., Chinese, 1907; Malay, 1908; ast. comsrr., Oct., 1908; ag. comsrr., pol., Johore, 1917; ag. ep. comsrr., pol., Perak, 1919; dep. comsrr., ol. and dist. supdt., prisons, Negri Sembilan, Jan., 1920.

MAGRATH, CHARLES ALEXANDER.—B. 1860; i. priv. tutvion; irrig. and development work in S. Alberta from 1878; mem. for Lethbridge in T.W.T. assm. for several years, and finally mem. f prov. cabinet; el. to H.C., Can., 1908, for Medicine Hat; defeated, 1911; fuel contr., Can., 1917-20; chmn., International Joint Coman., Jan. seot., 1921.

MAHABIR, F.—B. 1888; ast. med. supt., unatic asylum, Trinidad, 7th Apr., 1915.

MAHAFFY, ROBERT PENTLAND.—B. 1871; d. Marlborough (foundation schol.) and King's coll., Cambridge (open schol., 1st cls. in hist. ripos.; Whewell schol., Prince Consort's prize-man; Wors' travelling schol.) editor, Calendar of State Papers, 1896-1914; called to bar, Inner temple, 1901; author, "Law relating to Motor cars" (1910, 1912, 1922), "Life of the Emperor Francis Joseph" (1908, 1914), several vols. of Calendar of State Papers; temp. capt., Devon regt., 1914; severely wounded, 1st July, 1916; p. serv., Sudan, 1917-19; ast. legal adviser, Thineline High Coman., 1919-20; legal adviser o gov. of Malta, 6th June, 1921, and to H.M. forces at Malta, 2nd Nov., 1921.

MAIN, T. W.—Supt., pub. gardens, Selangor, Jan., 1906; supt. of govt. plantations, Perak, ept., 1906; ast. curator, botanic gardens, Singapore, Mar., 1908.

MAINGOT, ARTHUR.—B. 1862; entd. civ. rv., Trinidad, 15th Nov., 1879; goodsupt., govt. y., 1st Apr., 1894; traffic man., 1st Jan., 1922.

MAINGOT, ELLIOT FRANCIS.—B. 1891; ed. shaw Coll., Durham; served articles of clerkship in London and qualified as solr., 1914; crown lr., admstr. gen. and offl. receiver, Trinidad, Dec., 1922.

MAITLAND, ANDREW GIBB.—B. 1864; ed. his educn. as a geologist and civil engnr.; Yorkshire Coll. of Science, Leeds; ast. govt. geologist, Queensland, 1888; his official duties taking him as far afield as Br. N. Guinea; govt. geol. of W. Australia, 1896; has written several works on the geology, features, and mineral resources of Queensland, British New Guinea, and W. Australia.

MAJOR, SIR CHARLES, KT. BACH.—(1911).—Called to the Bar (Mid. Temp.), June, 1887; mem. of Leeward Is. bar, Sept., 1887; chancellor of the diocese of Antigua, Oct., 1889; nominated mem. of legia. coun., Antigua, 1895 to 1899 nominated mem. of gen. legis. coun., Leewards, Nov., 1896, and pres. of same, Dec., 1896 to 1899; mem. fed. ex. couns., Leewards, Mar., 1897, to June, 1901; vice-pres. legis. coun., Antigua, May, 1897; ag. sol.-gen. and atty.-gen., Leewards, 1897, 1898, 1899; capt. commanding Antigua volunteer defence force on its establishment, 1897; J.P., 1897; ag. 2nd puisane judge, Leewards, June, 1899; atty.-gen. of Grenada, 1901; ch. just. of Fiji, and chief judicial comanr. of Western Pacific, 1902; adminstr. govt., Mar.-Oct., 1904, and in 1908, 1910, and 1912; chief just. B. Guiana, 1914.

MALAN, HON. CHARL WYNAND.—B. 1883; ed. Victoria College, Stellenbosch; mem. for Humansdorp, Union H. of A. since 1915; min. of rly. and harbrs. in Hertzog cabinet, 30th June, 1924.

MALAN, HON. D. F., M.A., D.D.—M.L.A., Calvinia Divn., Union of S. Africa; min. of int., pub. health and eduon., 30th June, 1924.

MALAN, RT. HON. FRANCOIS STEPHANUS, P.C. (1920).—B. 1871; ed. in S. Africa and Camb.; B.A. Science, Cape univ.; LL.B., Camb.; advocate of sup. ct., Cape Colony, 1895; M.L.A. for Malmesbury, 1900; re-elected, Feb., 1904; min. of agric., Cape Colony, 1908; min. of eduon., Union of South Africa, 1910; attended Imp. conf., 1911; min. of mines, industries and eduon., 1912; min. for agr., 1920; min. of mines and industries, 1921-24; defeated, gen. elec., 1924.

MALCOLM, HARCOURT GLADSTONE, O.B.E. (1918); K.C. (1910).—Priv. sec. to Sir Henry Jackson when adminstr. of Bahamas, 1892, 1893, 1895; ditto to Sir W. F. Haynes-Smith, gov. of Bahamas, 1895; called to the bar, Lincoln's Inn, June, 1899; ditto, Bahamas, July, 1899; mem. of H. of A., Bahamas, 1900; deputy-speaker, 1901; re-elected, 1904 and 1911; ag. atty.-gen., Aug. to Nov., 1905; Sept., 1906 to Feb., 1907; July to Nov., 1910; Apr. to Dec., 1911; May to July, and Aug. to Nov., 1913; ag. chief just., 1913; speaker, H. of A., 1913; re-elected speaker, 1919; thanked by S. of S. for assistance to atty.-gen. in drafting bills; thanked by legis. for obtaining copies of early records; Bahamas del. to Canada-W. Indies confco. at Ottawa, May to June, 1920; Bahamas rep. during visit of Prince of Wales, and partly tercentenary celebrations at Bermuda, Oct., 1920.

MALONE, DENIS KEEN.—B. 1903; ed. Cooper's Company Schl.; cler. offr., C.O., 29th Mar., 1921.

MANGAN, WILLIAM EDWARD.—Served in Bechuanaland Prot. pol., 1910-14; clk., 1914; ag. ast. res. mag., 1921; passed 2nd grade Secwana exam., 1917; ag. res. mag., 1922.

MANGIN, THORLIF RATTRAY ORDE.—B. 1896; ed. Marlborough Coll.; sub lieut., R.N.V.R. and attd. to Royal Naval Dvn., 1915; qualified, gunnery course, H.M.S. Excellent, 1916; apptd., to H.M.S. Repulse and served with Grand Fleet, 1916-1919; ast. dist. comsrr., Gold Coast, 1919.
MANNERS, GEORGE ROBERT.—B. 1884; asst. dist. commr., G. Coast, 22nd Mar., 1911; dist. commr., 19th Feb., 1916.

MANNING, RICHARD JOSEPH.—B. 1883; ed. Clongowes Wood Coll. and Univ. Coll., Dublin; sub-inspr. of police, B. Guiana, Oct., 1909; dist. inspr., Sept., 1912; ag. stip. mag., W. Coast, Demarara, June, 1919; called to the bar, Gray's Inn, June, 1920; mag., Tanganyika Territory, 9th Sept., 1920; higher certif. in Hindi, Mar., 1916; compiler, "Br. Guiana Police Manual," Dec., 1918.

MANNING, BRIG.-GEN. SIR WM. HENRY, G.C.M.G. (1921); K.C.M.G. (1904); K.B.E. (1918); C.B. (1903).—B. 1863; ed. at Camb. and Roy. Mil. Coll., Sandhurst; lieut., 2nd batt., S. Wales Bord., 24th Foot, 1886; capt., 1897; brevet-major, 1898; brevet-lieut.-col., 1899; brevet-col., 1904; joined Indian army, 1888; 51st Sikhs, frontier force, 1891; 2nd Burmese war (wounded, medal and clasp); Samana and Hazara expedns., N.W. frontier of India, 1891 (clasp); C. Africa, 1893-4 (medal); C. Africa and Rhodesia, 1894-98 (clasp); Somaliland campaign (medal and 2 clasps); dep. commr. and cons.-gen. for B.C. Africa, 1897; acted as commr. and cons.-gen., Dec., 1897 to Dec., 1898, and also from July, 1900 to Apr., 1901; raised and commd. C. Africa regt.; commd. Somaliland field force, 1902-1903; commd. 1st brig., Somaliland field force, 1903-4; inspr.-gen., K.A.R., 1901; ag. gov. of Nyassaland Prot., 1907; gov., Nyassaland Prot., 7th Jan., 1910; gov., Nyassaland Prot., 5th Nov., 1910; gov., Jamaica, Jan., 1913; gov., Ceylon, 31st May, 1918; assumed govt., 11th Sept., 1918; recd. Coronation Medal, 1911.

MANSFIELD, CAPTAIN EDWARD THORNTON.—B. 1878; entered Gray's Inn, 1898; lieut., E. Lancashire Regt., 1901; served in S. African war (medal, four clasps); 2nd cls. supervisor of cust., G. Coast, 9th Dec., 1909; ag. adjutant, G. Coast Rly. and Mines Volunteers, 26th Nov., 1910 to 20th Feb., 1911; asst. dist. commr., Apr., 1913; seconded for serv. with Field Force Togoland, May, 1915 to Apr., 1916; dist. polit. offr., Misahobe, Togoland, June, 1918 to 30th Sept., 1920; dist. commr., 29th Apr., 1919; dist. polit. offr., Ho. Oct., 1920.

MARCH, HARRY THOMAS.—B. 1881; ed. King's Coll., London; 2nd divn. clk., post office, 1900-07; acctnt., post office, Nigeria, 20th Apr., 1907 to 31st Jan., 1912; postmr.-gen., Sierra Leone, 1st Feb., 1912.

MARCHANT, W. S.—Asst. dist. commr., E. Africa Prot., Dec., 1918.

MARCEL, HON. CHARLES, LL.D., Ottawa Univ.—B. 1860; elec. to H. of C. of Canada for Bonaventure, 1900; dep. speaker of H. of C., 1905-1908; re-elec. at gen. elec., 1908, 1911, 1917, and 1921; speaker of the H. of C., 1909; mem. of P.C. for Canada, 1911.

MARKMAN, ARTHUR THEODORE.—B. 1876; ed. Marlborough High Schl., N.Z.; ent. N.Z. post and tel. dept., 1890; prin. clk., staff divn., 1907; supt. of staff, 1914; ch. clk., 1916; first asst. sec., 1920; sec., 1923; is also dir. signal services, N.Z. Corps of Signals, with rank of colonel.

MARLBOROUGH, 9TH DUKE OF (created, 1702), CHARLES RICHARD JOHN SPENCER-CHURCHILL, P.C., K.G.—B. 1871; Chancellor of Primrose League, 1897 and 1898; served with yeomanry cavalry, S. Africa, 1900, and A.D.C. to Lieut.-Gen. Sir Ian Hamilton, K.C.B.; paymaster-general, 1899; under-sec. of state for the colonies, July, 1903, to Dec., 1905.

MARRIOTT, FREDERICK CLAUDE M. (Cantab.), L.C.P.—B. 1875; 4th asst. mac. Queen's Royal Coll., Trinidad, 26th May, 1914; inspr. of imigrts., 1st Oct., 1913; ag. prot. imigrts., May, 1917; man. of lab. exchange, 1919; served on wages comte. and profiteers' comte., 1920; ag. dir. educn., May, 1920; Jan., 1921 and from Dec., 1921 to Apr., 1922; asst. dir. of educn. and senr. inspr. schls., dir. of educn., Sierra Leone, May, 1923.

MARRIOTT, HAYES, C.M.G. (1924), B.A.—1873, 1st cls. math. tripoe, Cantab.—Cad. Stltmts., Nov., 1896; ag. 3rd mag., Singapore, 1897; passed fin. exam. in Malay, May, 1898; offr., Malacca, Feb., 1899; ag. 2nd mag., Feb., 1902; asst. P.M.G., Penang, Sept., 1902; 2nd mag., Penang, July, 1904; ag. offr. assm. Sing., Feb., 1905; ag. 2nd mag., Sing., May, 1905; ag. oclr. of land rev., Sing., Mar., 1906; 2nd asst. col. sec., 1st May, 1907, but continued to act. col. of land revenue, Singapore; ag. inspr. prisons, S.S., June, 1908; ag. oclr. of land rev., Penang, Mar., 1910; ag. inspr. of prisons, Settmts., July, 1910; ag. supr. of census, 1910; ag. res., oclr. and offr. in charge of treas., Malacca, May, 1911; ag. sec. to high commr., priv. sec. to gov., Jan., 1912; auditor-gen., Stltmts., Apr., 1914; ag. tempy. as treas., Stltmts., Jan., 1916 to Mar., 1917; and Feb., 1916; ag. sec. to high commr., Jan., 1917; ag. treas., S. (in addition), Jan., 1917; custodian of enemy property, Jan., 1917 to Jan., 1919; pres., subsidiary coinage commn. in admin., Sept., 1917; war services recog. by sec. of int., Apr., 1918; mem. of comm. to enquire into affairs of a Malay State, Aug., 1918; mem. of public service salaries commn., Nov., 1918; mem. gen. Dec., 1918; ag. sec. to high commr., Feb. 1918 to Feb., 1920; gen. adviser, Johor, Feb., 1919; ag. oclr. sec., S. Stltmts., Aug., 1919; Feb., 1920; pres., Trades Coman., S. Stltmts., F.M.S., Aug., 1921.

MARRES, ROBERT, M.A. (Oxon.), C.I.E.—1884; prin., Ceylon Univ. Coll., Sept., 1892.

MARSH, EDWARD HOWARD, C.B., C.I.E., M.V.O.—B. 1872; ed. at Westminster and Cambridge; scholar, Trin. Coll., 1891; 1st cls. class. tripoe, 1893; sen. chancellor's medal for class 1895; 1st cls. with distinction classical tripoe II., and B.A., 1895; M.A., 1897; appd. to compt. exam., 2nd cls. clk., C.O., Sept. 29th, 1900; asst. priv. sec. to Mr. Chamberlain, July, 1900; Mr. Lyttelton, Oct., 1903; 1st cls. clk., 1st Apr., 1905; priv. sec. to Mr. Winston Churchill, U.S. of S. for the Colonies, Jan., 1907; accompanied Mr. Churchill on his visit to E. Africa and Uganda, 1907-8; priv. sec. to Mr. Churchill, Pres. of B. of T., 1908; priv. sec. to Mr. Churchill as Home Sec., 1910; priv. sec. to Churchill as first Lord of the Admiralty, 1915; priv. sec. to Mr. Churchill as Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster, June to Nov., 1915; priv. sec. to Mr. Asquith, first lord of treas., Nov., 1916; returned to C.O. as 1st cls. clk., Dec., 1916; priv. sec. to Mr. Churchill as min. of munitions, July, 1917; priv. sec. to Mr. Churchill as sec. of state for war, Jan., 1919, as sec. of state for the Colonies, Feb., 1921 and as chancellor exchequer, 7th Nov., 1924; priv. sec. to the Duke of Devonshire, Oct., 1922; priv. sec. to Mr. J.F. Thomas, 23rd Jan., 1924.

MARSHALL, CLAUDE H., M.R.C.S., L.R.C.P.—Med. offr., Uganda Prot., Apl., 1908; fam. relief duty, May-Aug., 1908; sleeping sickness work at Kyetume and Sesse camps, Sept., 1908.
July, 1909; med. offr., Toro and Mbarara, sept., 1909, to May, 1910; med. offr., Anglo-German-Belgian Boundary Coman., Jan., 1911, to sept., 1912.

MARSHALL, EDWARD FOSTER, B.A. (Oxon).—1888; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Dec., 1912; attached to Kurunegala Kachcheri, Jan., 1913; adulla Kach., Mar., 1913; ag. officer-assst., Badulla ach., Oct., 1913; ag. office assst. to govt. agt., C.C. Prov., July, 1914; ditto, cent. prov., Aug., 1915; pol. mag., Matale, May, 1917; asst. govt. rt., Mullaitivu, Sept., 1918; pol. mag., Gampola, May, 1920; asst. govt. agt., Galle, Sept., 1923; pol. mag., Matale, Dec., 1923.

MARSHALL, FRANCIS.—B. Sc., Leeds Univ., 1888; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., 17th Nov., 1911; attached to Galle Kachcheri, Dec., 1911; attached to Kandy Kach., May, 1912; ag. pol. mag., visawella, Feb., 1913; comsnr. of requests and ol. mag., Matale, Sept., 1913; addtl. pol. mag. nd addtl. munici. mag., Colombo, Jan., 1915; fice assst. to prin. collr. of cust. and second nding survr., Apr., 1915; ag. sec., Colombo port coman., in addn. to his own duties, May, 1915; pol. mag., Galle, Mar., 1916; pol. mag., rincomalee, Nov., 1916; office assst. to govt. rt., Uva, Jan., 1917; ag. sec., Colombo port oman., Mar., 1919; ag. addtnl. landing survr., olombo cust., June, 1919; sec. to food con-roller, July, 1919; addtl. asst. contr. of rev. in idn., Jan., 1920; dist. judge, N. Eliya, May, 1921; asst. contr. of rev., Oct., 1921; custodian, enemy property, Feb., 1922; addtl. asst. dir., idn., in addn., May, 1923 to Dec., 1923; ag. est. col. treas. in addn., Jan. to Sept., 1924; idn. asst. contr., rev., in addn., Oct., 1924.

MARSHALL, CAPT. REGINALD CHARLES, I.A. (Oxon.), Diploma of Forestry.—B. 1893; chbr. Queen's Coll., Oxford, 1911; hons. mods. naths., 2nd cla., hon., 1912; 2nd lieut. Worc. regt., Aug., 1914; Gallipoli, 1915 (wounded); seopotamis, 1916 (wounded); lieut., 9th Batt. 7orc. Regt., France, 1917-18 (wounded and prisoner); capt., 1st Batt. Worc. Regt., B.A. (Oxon.), 1919; diploma of forestry (with distinc- tion—placed head of the list), 1920; M.A., 1920; forestry coman., 1920-22; instr., forestry schl., forest of Dean; asst. comsnr., national savings comtee., 1922; dep. conservator, forests, Trinidad nd Tobago, 1923; conservator, forests, Trinidad nd Tobago, 1923; mem., bd. of agr., Trinidad nd Tobago, 1923.

MARSTON, S.—Treasy. asst., Kenya, Jan., 1917; senr. asst. treas., June, 1923.

MARTIN, HON. ARCHER.—B. 1865; called to the bar, 1887; apptd. counsel for Dom. gov't. nd representative of minis. of just. in Vancouver island, 1896; spec. com. to investigate affairs of B.C. crown timber lands agency, 1897; puisne judge of sup. ct. of B.C., 1898; deputy judge in admiralty for B.C., 1899; spec. coman. to settle inf. MARTIN, HENRY—Sub-inspr., Bechuanaland Prot., Polloe, 1896; ag. asst. res. mag., Serowe, 1906-07; inspr., Beoh. Prot. pol., 1909.

MARTIN, HORACE, O.B.E. Milly. (1919).—B. 1864; entd. C.A. office, 2nd Feb., 1881; asst. head of shipping dept., 1883; head of appts. dept., 1900; lent to War Office for service with inland waterways and docks section, R.E.; dep. asst. dir. (temp. capt.), Dec., 1916; major, Aug., 1917; lieut.-col. and asst. dir., Jan., 1919; demob., 31st July, 1919; chmn. overseas panel for employment of ex-service men, miny. of labour, 1920.

MARTIN, HON. J. E.—B. 1859; ed. pub. schl. Waterloo, P.Q., and McGill Univ.; B.C.L., and gold med., 1883; called to the bar of Prov. of Queb., 1884; K.C., 1908; batonnier of bar, Que., 1913-14; puisne judge, ct. of King's Bench, prov. of Que., Sept., 1918; mem. of faculty of law of McGill Univ., and lecturer on company law; ag. ch. just., superior ct., Quebec, 1922.

MARTIN, LEWIS VERNON.—B. 1902; entd. C.O., 10th Sept., 1917; apptd. after compet. exam., cler. offr., C.O., 17th Mar., 1920.

MARTIN, S. B.—Ed. Wesleyan Mission Schl., G. Coast; 6th class offr., customs, G. Coast, Sept., 1890; cik. to dir. of telegraphs and storekeeper, Aug., 1891; cik. and acntt., July, 1893.

MARTIN, WILLIAM WHITTLE, M.B., Ch.B. (Vict.), D.P.H. (Durham).—B. 1887; med. offr., cls. IV., S. Stiltna, 7th Mar., 1913; assumed duties as med. offr., general hosp., Penang, 4th Apr., 1913; med. offr., quarantine station, Penang, 1st Feb., 1914; asst. port health offr., Singapore, 22nd June, 1914; health offr., Malacca, Dec., 1917; senr. health offr., Penang, Mar., 1919; ag. ch. health offr., Dec., 1919; health offr., rural area, Jan., 1920; senr. health offr., Penang, Mar., 1920; govt. health offr., Penang, 4th Jan., 1921.

MARTINDALE, LEONARD.—B. 1884; ed. Tonbridge and Uppingham; on milly. serv., 1916-19; temp. cik., C.O., Apr., 1920 to June, 1922; apptd. cler. offr., C.O., 21st June, 1922.

MARTINS, G. N.—Ed. C.M.S. Grammar Schl., Lagos; messenger, audit, and P.O., 1889; customs, outdoor offr., 1890 to 1893 (during which time attached to revenue office); ag. cik., P.O., 1893; 4th cik. of customs, 1893; 3rd cik. and statistician, Mar., 1894; transf'd. to the revenue dept., 1900; deputy for cashier and ch. cik. on various occasions; 2nd cls. cik., customs, 1901; chief examining offr. of cust., Lagos, 1st Mar., 1906.

MARWICK, ALLAN GRAHAM.—B. 1877; served in Natal civ. serv., 1895 to 1899; served Anglo-Boer war, 1899-1901; sub. native comsnr., Mbabane, Swaziland, Jan., 1903 to Mar., 1907;
MASON, GERALD BOVELL.—Ed. Harrison Coll., Barbados; matric., London Univ., 1890; joined London hosp., 1890; passed prelim. scientific, 1892; M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), 1896, certif., London Schi. of Trop. Med., 1909; jun. astt. med. offr., St. Marylebone infirmary, 1896; clin. astt., aurial and ophthalmic depts., London hosp., 1897; house physician, Brompton hosp., 1898; ag. med. offr., Three Counties asylum, 1899; civ. surg. in charge, Station hosp., Woking, 1902; med. offr., No. 4 dist., Antigua, 1903; ag. comsnr., Virgin Is., 1904; surg.-lieut., Antigua def. force, 1904; mag. and med. offr., Anguilla and dep. judge of sup. ct., Leeward Is., Jan., 1905 to Sept., 1906; med. offr., No. 6 dist., Nevis, 1906; med. offr., dist. “D”, and mag., dist. “F”, Dominica, 1907; med. offr., St. Vincent, 1909-12; med. offr. in charge of troops, Cambridge, 1916-19; diploma, public health, Univ. of Cambridge, 1917; founder and hon. sec., West India Red Cross Soct., 1921-1924; dir., med. and health dept., Bermuda, Aug., 1924.

MASON, H.—Accts. clk., 1st grade, E.A.P., May, 1912; astt. ch. acctsnt., Uganda Rly., Nov., 1915; dep. ch. acctsnt., Tanganyika Territory rly., 10th Sept., 1920.

MASSAM, J. A.—Astt. dist. comsnr., F.A.P., Sept., 1919.

MASSETT, JAMES DAVID ARTHUR.—B. 1885; ed. privately and Harrison Coll., Barbados; post office dept., Barbados, Mar., 1904 to Apr., 1906; H.M. cust., May, 1906; sworn weigher and gauger, 1908; sub. contr. of cust., Springlands, 1910-16; seconded for serv. in occupied territory, German E. Africa, 25th Nov., 1916; confirmed as supervisor of cust., Tanganyika Territory, 1st Oct., 1919; ag. astt. comptlr., cust., 18th Feb. to 25th June, 1923 and from 18th Oct., 1923; ag. comptlr., cust., 26th June to 17th Oct., 1923.

MASSEY, T. H.—Med. offr., E.A.P., Jan., 1913.

MASSEY, RIGHT HON. WM. FERGUSON, P.C. (1913).—B. 1856; entd. New Zealand parlmt., 1894; prime min. since 1912; min. of lab., 1912-20; lands, 1912-18; agr., 1912-15; industries and commerce, 1912-20; mines, 1920-21; rlys., 1919-22; finance and stamp duties, since 1920; represented N.Z. on Imp. War Cabinet and at Imp. War Confcoas., 1917 and 1918; Paris Peace Confcoa., 1919; Imp. Confcoas., 1921 and 1923.

MASTEN, HON. CORNELIUS ARTHUR.—B. 1857, Quebec; educ. parish dist. schl. La Colle; La Colle Academy; Victoria Univ. Coburg, Ont. (graduated with hons., May, 1879); mathematical master, high schl., Orillia, Ont., 1879, 1880; entered law soc. of Upper Canada, Oct., 1880; called to the bar, 1883; K.C. (Ont.), and bencher of the law soc. of Upper Canada, 1908; comsnr. to enquire into the Insurance situation in Ont. with a view to improvements in the law; pres., Alumni Assoc. of Toronto Univ.; chmn., exec. comtee. of the speaker’s patriotic league; author of “Masten Company Law in Canada”; justice of the sup. ct. of Ontario, Nov., 1915.

MASTERTON-SMITH, SIR JAMES EDWARD, K.C.B. (1919), C.B. (1915).—B. 1878; ed. Harrow (schol.) and Hertford Coll., Oxford (schol.); ent. home civ. serv. (cl. I.), admity., 1901; priv. sec. to 2nd ast lord, 1904-8; priv. sec. to perm. sec., 1908-10; priv. sec. to successive 1st lords of admity., 1910-17; astt. sec., min. of munition., Sept., 1917 to Jan., 1919; astt. sec. (addit. W.O. and Air Mins.), 1919-20; joint perm. sec. miny. of labour, 1920; perm. under-secr. of state for the colonies, 30th Aug., 1921; sec. to Order of St. Michael and St. George; mem. of the offl. side of the National Whitley Coun.; Offr. the Belgian Order of the Crown.

MATHER, NORMAN FREDERICK HUGH.—1890; ed. Merchant Taylor’s Schi. and Hertford Coll., Oxford (schol.); cadet, F.M.S., Nov., 1897; served in Rifle Brig., Dec., 1915-Sept., 1919; sec. to res., Selangor, Nov., 1919; astt. dist. of Klang, Mar., 1921; astt. dist. offr., Larut, in 1922; regar., war serv. land grant scheme, Sttlmts., Feb., 1922; ag. dist. offr., Larut, in 1922; astt. dist. offr., Larut, Sept., 1922; sec. res., Pahang, Dec., 1923.

MATHERS, FREDERICK FRANCIS, K.C.L.—B. 1871; ed. schls. in Halifax, Nova Scotia, Dalhousie law schl. and Harvard law schl.; adls. to the bar, 1892; dep. prov. sec. and clk. of ex. coun., N.S., 1902; also regar. of joint sea companies, 1909; now deputy atty.-gen.

MATHERS, HON. THOS. GRAHAM.—R.I.P. ed. pub. and high schls., Lucknow and Kanadine, Ontario, and privately; editor, Mama “Liberal,” 1883; called to the bar, Mancha, 1889; min. of just., Manitoba, 1896-1906; judge, ct. of King’s Bench, 1906; ch. of King’s Bench, 1910.

MATHESON, CAPT. C. L. T., M.C.—On missioned in Royal Engineers, 1909; astt. dist. surv., G. Coast, 1914; Togoland campaign, 1915; Cameroonos, 1914-16; France with Field R.E., 1916-17; W.O., 1918; dep. dir. topographic surveys, G. Coast, 1920.

MATHEWS, ALBAN FRANK, F.S.A.—Corporated Accountant.—B. 1891; astt. aud. external audit dept., S. Stltmts., and F.L. 23rd Aug., 1919; ag. senr. astt. audr., lith., 1920 to 31st Dec., 1921, 7th Sept., 1922; w. June, 1923 and from 2nd July, 1923; astt. aud. office, Singapore, 1st July to 6th Sept., 1922.

MATHEWS, C. B.—Asst. dist. comsnr., Kenya, Feb., 1921.

MATHEWS, H. F.—Ed. Oxford High Schl. and Jesus Coll., Oxford; open math. exam., 1908; 2nd cls. hons., math. mods., 1907; 3rd cls. hons., physics finals, 1909; certif. in ethn. anthropology, Oxford Univ., 1912; ord. teacher, bd. of educn., 1910; astt. res. Nigeria, Aug., 1910.

MATHISON, HON. JOHN ALEXANDER, K.C.B. 1863; ed. Harrington Gram. Schi., Prize Wales’ Coll., Taught Schi., Desable Gram. Schi., P.E.I., read law with McLean and Macdonald; called to the P.E.I. bar, 1893; K.C., 1905; ed. legislature for King’s country, 1900; reld. in 1908 and 1912; leader of the opposition, 1911 premier and atty.-gen., 2nd Dec., 1911; ch. jur. P.E.I., 13th June, 1917.

MATTEL CHARLES, L.R.C.P. (Edin.), L.R.C.S. (Edin.), L.M., L.F.P.S.G., D.P.H.—Capt. Australian army medical corps, reserve of offr.; offr., N.S. Wales, 1891; ditto, W. Australia, 1897; gov’t med. offr., quarantine med. offr., mag., chmn. of quarter sess., chmn. of local med. W. Australia, 1899; med. offr., Imperial Manxian cont.; S. African war, 1901 (medal as Cape Colon. clasp); sec. for permits, East Lochn, S. Africa, 1902; med. offr. in charge of new constructions, C.S.A.R., 1903; med. offr. of hospital Malta, 1907.
MATTHEWS, CHARLES EDWARD.—B. 1872; d. privately; joined N.Z. treasury dept., 1889; justice dept., 1895; priv. sec. to various ministers, 1896-1910; chief clk., police dept., 1910; chief clk., justice dept., 1913; dep. inspr., prisons, 1912; inspr., 1914; contr.-gen., 1919; under-sec. of justice and contr.-gen. of prisons, 1922.

MATTHEWS, ERNEST LEWIS, K.C., C.M.G. (1914).—Called to the bar, Inner Temple; law adviser to Transvaal govt., June, 1902; law adviser to govt. of Union of S. Africa, 31st May, 1910.

MATTHEWS, SIR JOHN BROMHEAD, K.T. (1911).—B. 1864; barrister-at-law, Inner Temple, 1890, N.E. circuit; ag. solr.-gen., S. Settlimts., Oct., 1902, to May, 1903; M.L.C., S. Settlimts., 1901 and 1904; pres. of Moslem charities comm., S. Settlimts., 1903; atty.-gen., Bahamas, 1907; M.L.C., Bahamas, 1907-1909; S.C., Bahamas, 1909; atty.-gen., S. Settlimts., 1909; ch. just., Bahamas, Jan., 1910; resig., 1911.

MATTHEWS, JOHN CHARLES MELVIN, C.I.E.—B. 1874; ed. Portsmouth Grammar Schl. and King's Coll., London; ast. elec. engnr., Kuala Lumpur, F.M.S., 1904; engr. in, 1906; 2nd lieut. and lieut. M.S.V.R. (C.A.F.L.S. Medal), 1915-20; ag. ch. elec. inspr., addn., 1914-16; sec., elec. bd., in addn., 1921; elec. engr., F.M.S., 1923.

MATTHEWS, MARMADUKE HUMPHREY.—Ed. Keltenham Coll. and Pembroke Coll., Cambridge; probationer, col. audit dept., Feb., 1914; ast. aud. r., Nigeria, Apr., 1914; temp. lieut., Nigeria regt., 1914-15; aud. r., Brit. Honduras, Sept., 1920.

MAVROGORDATO, ARTHUR STEPHEN.—B. 1846; ed. at Oakham Schl., Rutland; clk., pol. headqrs., Cyprus, Nov., 1903; inspr. of mil. pol., Cyprus, May, 1905; in charge of pol. detachment, Kenya, 1907-1909; gov. of prison and dep. coroner; passed govt. exams. in modern Greek and Turkish; in command of Papho dist. on several occasions; detailed for special duty in Famagusta dist. in connection with Limassol riots, July-June, 1912; ast. comanr. of police, Sierra Leone, June, 1913; J.P. and dep. coroner, 1913; comanr. of police, also sheriff, prison visiting magistrate, and govt. nominee on city coun. of Freetown, and performing duties of marshal of the Admiralty prize ct., May to Nov., 1915; sec., 1916, to May, 1917, Feb. to Apr., 1918, and from Aug. to Dec., 1918; ag. harbmr. and retaining offr. under mil. authorities, May, 1916, May, 1917, and May, 1918, to Mar., 1919; ag. st. comanr. in headqrs. dist., S. Leone, Feb., 1919; dep. inspr.-gen., police and prisons, alestein, Dec., 1922.

MAXWELL, CHARLETON NEVILLE.—B. 1872; Ed. Elizabeth Coll., Guernsey, Bedford Schl., and Keltenham Coll.; S. African War, 1900-01; queen's med., 5 clasps); land office, Selangor, 1900-91; Sarawak serv., 1891-93; priv. sec. to ag. v., S.S., 1893; jun. offr., Selangor, 1st Feb., 1904; transport offr., Pahang Exped. Force, June, 1904; ag. dist. offr., Ulu Selangor, Dec., 1896; st. audr., 10th Apr., 1897; 2nd mag., Kuala Impur, 1st Jan., 1899; ag. 1st mag., K. Lumpur, 1st May, 1899; ag. dist. offr., Kuala Pilah, 19th July, 1901; dist. offr., Kuala Langat, 1st June, 1903; mag., Kuala Lumpur, 10th Mar., 1904; t. offr., Pekan, 1st Oct., 1906; dist. offr., ian, 17th May, 1911; dist. offr., Ulu Selangor, 1 May, 1914; Brit. agt., Trengganu, 17th July, 1914; seconded for serv. as pres., state coun., engganu, 9th Dec., 1915; chmn., assy. bd., Kinta, 13th Apr., 1917; dist. offr., Klang, 13th Sept., 1920; seconded for serv. as dir. of supplies, S.S. and F.M.S., 16th Nov., 1920; mem. and pres., rent assessment bd., Singapore, June-Oct., 1921; dist. offr., Klang, Oct., 1921; ag. comanr., trade and cust., F.M.S., Sept., 1922; comanr., trade and cust., F.M.S., July, 1921.

MAXWELL, SIR FREDERIC MACKENZIE, KT. BACH. (1911).—Called to the bar, Linne's Inn, 1884; 1st cl. studentship, Inns of Ct., 1882; 1st cl. scholarship (Equity), Linne's Inn, 1884; M.A. (Oxon.), 1891; 1st cl. jurisprudence, 1885; ag. atty.-gen., Br. Hond., Feb. to Dec., 1890, and May to July, 1896; atty.-gen., Br. Hond., July, 1896; K.C., Br. Hond., Apr., 1906; ag. chief just., Br. Hond., 21st June to 29th Dec., 1899, Mar. to Oct., 1902, Apr. to Nov., 1904, and Apr., 1906, to Jan., 1907; chief just., Br. Hond., Jan., 1907; ch. just., Leeward Is., 1912; lieut. commdg. mounted section of Br. Hond. vol. force, Feb., 1905; attended schl. of mounted infantry at Bulford Camp, and recd. certif. of qualification to command a company of M.I., Sept., 1905; qualified at schl. of musk., Hythe, Dec., 1905; capt., Br. Hond. vol. force, Jan., 1906; major, commdg. ditto, Apr., 1906; ret. from vola., Sept., 1908, with permission to retain rank and wear uniform of the force; chancellor of the diocese of Br. Hond., and Cent. America, 1896-1907; revised the Federal Acts of the Leeward Is., from 1871 to 1888.

MAXWELL, COL. GEOFFREY ARCHIBALD PRENTICE, D.S.O., M.V.O., M.C., Officer Ordre de Leopold, Officer Legion d'Honneur, Belgian Croix de Guerre, French Croix de Guerre.—B. 1888; R.M.A., Woolwich, 1902; R.E., 1904; Nigeria Barokano rly., 1908-11; survey, E.A.P., 1912-14; European War, 1914-18 (ment. seven times in desps.); inter-allied comm. of control, rly., occupied territory, 1919; communications sec., sup. economic coun., 1919-20; gen. man., Tanganyika rly., 1920.

MAXWELL, GERALD VERNER.—B. 1877; ed. Bedford Gram. Schl. (exhibitioner) and Peterhouse, Camb. (scholar); cadet, Fiji, Apr., 1893; ag. regist.-genl. and regist. of titles, Dec., 1898; stip. mag., Dec., 1900; ast. native comanr., Jan., 1904; native lands comanr., Jan., 1906; ag. ast. col. sec. and ag. ast. rec.-gen., Oct., 1909; ag. rec.-gen., Dec., 1909, to Nov., 1910; chmn., native lands comanr., 1912; ag. sec. for native affairs (conjoint), 21st Mar., 1917; temporarily M.L.C., May, 1917; ch. native comanr., Kenya Colony, May, 1921; mem. exec. and legis. councils.

MAXWELL, JAMES CRAWFORD, C.M.G. (1911).—Ed. Dundee High Schl. and Edin. Univ.; M.A., 1889; M.B.C.M., 1893; M.D., 1896; ast. col. surg., S. Leone, 1897-1900; dist. comanr., S. Leone, 1900; 1st cl. comanr., Southern Provinces, Nigeria, Feb., 1914; ag. gov., Sierra Leone, 9th Sept., 1921 to 3rd May, 1922; col. sec., Gold Coast, 4th Oct., 1922; W. African Medal and Clasp, 1898-99.

MAXWELL, JOHN, C.M.G. (1921).—B. 1875; ed. at Dumfries and Glasgow; passed final exam. in law, Apr., 1899; ast. dist. comanr., G. Coast, 21st Mar., 1902; travelling comanr., 28th Jan., 1905; prov. comanr., 18th Mar., 1907; has acted as solr.-genl., atty.-genl. and sec. for native affairs; sec. for native affrs., Dec., 1922.

MAXWELL, MALCOLM THOMAS, M.A., M.C.—B. 1888; ed. Westminster and Trinity Coll., Cambridge (exhib.) ; B.A. (hons.), 1911; M.A., 1918; priv. sec. to Sir Bickham Escott, 1913-15; cadet, Fiji, 1915; on active service,
1915-19; 2nd lieut., R.F.A., Aug., 1915; M.C., 1917; resumed duty, Fiji, Sept., 1918; dist. comsnr., Aug., 1920.

MAXWELL, THOMAS DOVETON.—B. 1873; ed. Tiverton, Blundell scholar, Balliol Coll., Oxford, 1892; B.A. (honours, jurisprudence), 1896; called to the bar (Gray's Inn), 1903; asst. dist. comsnr., So. Nigeria, 1902; ag. dist. comsnr., Degema, 1903; ditto, Calabar, Mar., 1904; polit. and transport offr., Ibibio patrol, Nov.-Dec., 1904 (W. African medal); ag. asst. sec., Calabar, Jan., 1906; ag. pol. mag., Calabar, Apr., 1906; comsnr. of lands, S. Nigeria, 9th Aug., 1906; crown solr., S. Nigeria, 1st Sept., 1908; pol. mag., June, 1910; legal adviser, 1st Jan., 1914; tempo. lieut., Nigeria regt., Nov., 1914; intell. offr., Cross River column, Kamerun Exped. Force, Nov., 1914, to June, 1915; 2nd puisne judge, E.A.P., Apr., 1917; 1st puisne judge, 13th Oct., 1917; ag. chief just., E.A.P., 4th Aug., 1919 to 17th Nov., 1920 and from 14th May, 1923 to 23rd June, 1924.

MAXWELL, SIR WM. GEORGE, K.B.E. (1924). C.M.G. (1915); Royal Humane Society's medal (1882).—B. 1871; ed. at Clifton Coll.; barrister-at-law, Inner Temp.; jun. offr., Perak, F.M.S., 15th Mar., 1891; asst. mag., Kinta, 26th Apr., 1892; ag. collr. and mag., Kuantan, Pahang, 16th Aug., 1896; ag. supt. of Ulu Pahang, 9th Aug., 1896; regis. of cts., Kinta, Perak, 1st Feb., 1899; ag. asst. sec. to gov't., Perak, 6th Feb., 1900; ag. collr. of land rev., Larut, regis. of titles, Perak, North, and warden of mines, Perak, North, 8th Mar., 1901; ag. sen. mag., Selangor and Negri Sembilan, 1st Jan., 1903; ag. sen. mag., Perak, 1st Aug., 1903; ag. sec. to res., Perak, 6th Apr., 1904; ag. comsnr. of the ct. of requests, Singapore, 3rd Nov., 1904; dist. offr., Dindings, 3rd Aug., 1905; dep. pub. prosecutor, Singapore, 1906; sol.-gen., S. Settmts., 22nd Aug., 1906; ag. atty.-gen., S. Settmts., Mar., 1908; British adviser to gov't. of Kedah, July, 1909; ag. col. sec., S. Stltmts., 1914; ag. sec. to high comsnr., Malay States and Brunei, 1915; ag. col. sec., S. Stltmts., 3rd Jan., 1916; ag. British resident, Perak, Dec., 1916 to May, 1917; ag. sec. to high comsnr., Malay States and Brunei, June, 1917; vice-chmn., food control comtes., S.S. and F.M.S.; vice-chmn., shipping control comte., S.S.; pres., rubber comm., 1918; pres., Singapore housing comm.; pres., Singapore centenary comte.; general adviser to gov't., Johore, June, 1918; ag. col. sec., S. Stltmts., Dec., 1918; ag. British res., Perak, Sept., 1919; Br. res., Perak, Dec., 1919; ch. sec. to gov't., F.M.S., Sept., 1920; publications, "Perak Land Laws (past and present)," "The Laws of Perak, 1877-1903"; "The Laws of the S. Stltmts., 1827-1907," "In Malay Forests."

MAXWELL, W. R.—Asst. engrn., P.W.D., E. Africa Prot., Oct., 1918.

MAXWELL-LYTE, LIEUT. JOHN.—B. 1875; F.R.G.S., F.R.H.S.; ed. at Radley and Merton Coll., Oxford; reserve of offrs. (late Northumberland Fusiliers); asst. horticulturist, dept. of agric., Transvaal, 1st Feb., 1902, to May, 1907; asst. res., N. Nigeria, Nov., 1907; cantonment mag., Mar., 1911.

MAY, A. W. J., M.B.E. (1922)—B. 1862; entered col. office after exam., May, 1882; asst. clk., May, 1892; asst. to supervisor of copying, Mar., 1900; supervisor of copying, 1st Oct., 1911.

MAY, ALMER WILLIAM, C.M.G. (1924), B.A., M.D., B.Ch., B.A.O., D.P.H. (Dublin), L.M.—B. 1874; ed. at Lismore Coll., Waterford and Trinity Coll., Dublin; served as civ. surg., S. A. Field Force, S. A. War; med. offr., N. W. Rhodesia, Jan., 1907; bacteriologist to Transvaal, Aug., 1907; prin. med. offr., N.W.R., July, 1908; prin. med. offr., N.R., 1909; maj. major, N.R.R., Feb., 1915; served in France as physician in charge of conduct of wound infect. with rank of major, R.A.M.C., Feb.-Dec., 1915; major, N.R.M.C., Oct., 1917; hon. major, Aug., 1919; mem., exec. and leg. couns.; J.P.

MAY, CHAS. GALL.—B. 1870; apptd. asst. eng. of works, Straits Settlements, May, 1889; ag. eng. of works and surveys, Malacca, June, 1890; Sept., 1901, and Oct., 1902, to Apr., 1903; ag. eng. of works and surveys, Sing., July, 1903; ag. col. engrn. and survr.-gen., Penang, Nov., 1904; Feb., 1905; ag. supt., wks. and survey, Malacca, May to Dec., 1906; ag. dep. col. engrn. and survr.-gen., Penang, Jan., 1907 to Apr., 1908; from July, 1908; confirmed, Dec., 1909; ag. engrn. and survr.-gen., May, 1911; dep. engrn., Penang, Mar., 1915; ag. col. engrn. and survr.-gen., Feb., 1919; dep. col. engrn., Feb., Dec., 1919.

MAY, DONALD RAYNES MACPARLANE.—Sec. clk., G.P.O., Jamaica, 1898; transferred to H.M. Customs, 1902; collr.-gen.'s office, 1904; superint. of customs, G. Coast, 1907; 1st cls. superint. 1914; seconded to British Zone of Togoland, offr.-in-charge of treasy. and customs, 1914; controller of enemy property 1916; controller, 1917; senr. collr. of cust., 1st Jan., 1921.

MAY, GEORGE HERBERT.—B. 1873; ag. asst. in regir.'s off., Br. Guiana, Nov., 1888; adm. gen.'s off., on staff, June, 1892; pol. dep. in 1893; 2nd lieut., Br. Guiana militia, Sept., 1897; obtained certif. for drill and musketry for schls. of instruc., Chelsea Bks., Lon. and fired ret. from mil. as lieut., and apptd. sub-instr., Br. Guiana pol., May, 1897; adjt. and instr. of local forces, Fiji, with rank of capt. (on 1898; supt. of pol., ag. sheriff, 12th Dec., 1898; dep. comm., constab., 24th Apr., 1901; commanded volunteers; comm., armed constab., supt. of pol., ag. sheriff, 24th June, 1902; L.C. to Sir Henry M. Jackson, K.C.M.G., gov't. of Trin., 4th Nov., 1902; inspr. of constab., Trin., 1905; hon. local A.D.C. to Sir G. Le Huez, G.C.M.G., June, 1909; supt., fire brigade, Trin., 1910; sen. inspr., Sept., 1912; ag. dep. inspr., Oct., 1912, to Sept., 1913, and Oct. to Nov., 1913; supt. of police, Singapore, Nov., 1913; inspr.-gen. of constab., Trinidad, 1916.

MAYALL, ROBERT PERCIVAL WALDENS, M.A.—B. 1876; ed. Sidney Sussex Coll., Camb., 1900; M.A., 1908; asst. mast., Clifton Hosp., Eastbourne, 1900; headmaster, English School, Cyprus, 1902; headmaster educn. dept., Coast, Feb., 1907; senior inspr. of schls., Coast, 1912; ag. dir. of educn. on several occasions.

MAYBIN, JOHN ALEXANDER.—B. 1889; M.A. (Edin.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Jan., 1899; attached to the Badulla Kachcheri, Jan., 1899; ag. office asst. to gov't. agt., July, 1914, and Jul., 1915; addtl. dist. judge and pol. mag., Badulla; in addition to his own duties, June, 1915; ag. mag., Panadura, Mar., 1916; on milly. ass. to chmn., mun. coun., Colombo, Mar., 1917; ag. pol. mag., Kandy, July, 1919; 2nd ass. to chmn., mun. coun., Colombo, Mar., 1919; finan. asst., Colombo Municipality, Nov., 1919; addnl. asst. col. sec., Jan., 1922; land surveyor, Colombo cust., Mar., 1923; 3rd asst. col. sec., Feb., 1924.

MAYLE, NORMAN LESLIE.—B. 1899; asst. clk., after compet. exam., asst. clk., C.O., Oct., 19

MAYNARD, PERCY.—B. 1903; apptd. after compet. exam., cler. offr., C.O., 15th Oct., 1920.

MEADE, CHARLES RICHARD.—Copyist, treas. and post office dept., Montserrat, 1st Oct., 1907; th clk., 1st Apr., 1912; 4th clk., 23rd Nov., 1912; has acted as 3rd clk. and 1st clk.; gov't offr., Sandy Point, St. Kitts-Nevis, Nov., 1915; clk., treas., Virgin Is., May, 1917; clk., exec. council.

MEADLEY, F. W.—B. 1873; clk., G.P.O., Transvaal, 1902; distributor of stamps, 1903; ast. sec., investment bd., 1908; sec., pub. debt. comm., 1918.

MEDWAY, F. W.—Imp. serv. (acct.-gen.'s dept., G.P.O.), 1901-2; clk., G.P.O., Bloemfontein, 5th Nov., 1902; clk., treas., O.F.S., 15th May, 1908; senr. clk., treas., Union of S. Africa, pr., 1912; senr. clk., inland rev. dept., 15th Dec., 1916; prin. clk., 1st Apr., 1917.

MEEK, A. I., L.R.C.P., L.R.C.S., D.P.H. (Edin.), L.R.F.P. & S. ( Glas.)—R.A.M.C., Aug., 1918 to May, 1920; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 5th May, 1922.

MEEEK, CHARLES KINGSLEY, F.R.G.S., F.R. nth. Inst.—B. 1885; ed. Bedford Gram. Schl. and Oxford (Brasenose Coll. exhib. and prize man); astt. res., N. Nigeria, July, 1912.

MEGARRY, THOMAS, B.A.—B. 1898; ed. Trinity Coll., Dublin; cadet, Hong Kong, Nov., 1922.

MEGSON, JOHN.—B. 1895; apptd. after compet. exam. clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. serv.; temporarily assigned to Board of Agric., July, 1914; Home Office, Aug., 1914; on military service, June, 1915 to Mar., 1919; Home Office, Mar.-Apr., 1919; assigned to C.O., Apr., 1919; cler. offr., higher grade, 9th Jan., 1923.

MEHLISS, JOHN MAX, M.D. (1893)—Med. apt., Rietfontein hosp. and chronic sick home, June, 1900.

MEIGHEN, Rt. Hon. ARTHUR P.C. (1920) —C.—B. 1876; ed. St. Mary's Coll. Inst. and Toronto Univ. (B.A. 1896); barrister; K.C. (dominion), 1914; elec. to H. of C., Canada, 1908; elec., 1911; solr.-gen. Canada, June, 1913; elec. by acclamation, July, 1913, and at gen. elec., 1917; mem. of the Cabinet, without portfolio, Oct., 1915; sec. of state, Aug., 1917; min. of the interior, Oct., 1917; prime min. of Canada, 10th July, 1920; represented Canada at mp. Conf., 1921; resigned on defeat of his ort. at g. e., Dec., 1921; re-elec. to H. of C. for renville, Ont., at bye-el., 26th Jan., 1922; leader of opposition in H. of C.

MELANESIA, Bishop of, RIGHT REV. CECH OR WOOD, M.A., D.D.—Late scholar and exhibitioner, St. Peter's Coll., Camb.; B.A. (2nd class, tripod), 1896; M.A., 1901; D.D., Camb., 1912; deacon, 1897; priest, 1898; curate of Kent, 1997-99; St. Marylebone, 1899-1902; St. Andrew's, Bethnal Green, 1902-1906; consecrated, 17th July, 1912.

MELBOURNE, CHARLES ALEX. DICK.—Ed. ivately and Trin. Hall, Camb.; called to bar, Inner Temple, 1891; admitted to practice in Brisbane, Queensland, 1892; and in Hong Kong, 1895; apptd. 1st clk., magistracy, Hong Kong, 1900; J.P., 1900; ag. astt. supt., Victoria gaol, 1903 and 1904; ag. astt. land offr., 1905; commr. oaths, 1905; ag. 2nd pol. mag., 1905 to 1907; ag. dep. regir. and appraiser, 1907; ag. 2nd pol. mag., 1907; ag. astt. supt., Victoria gaol, 1908 to 1909; ag. dep. regir. and appraiser, 1908 to 1909; dep. regir. and appraiser, 1909; ag. 2nd pol. mag. from 1911 to 1913 and in 1914; ag. judge of the full court, 1914; ag. regir., on several occasions; ag. 2nd pol. mag., 1916-1917, 1918-1919 and in 1923; ag. puisne judge, 1919.

MELLAND, FRANK HULME.—B. 1879; ed. at Shrewsbury and Merton Coll., Oxford (B.A.); probationer, N. E. Rhodesia, 4th July, 1901; astt. native commr., 1st Oct., 1901; native commr., 12th Sept., 1903; astt. mag., 31st Oct., 1906; has acted as mag. on various occasions between Dec., 1912 and Oct., 1917; mag., 31st Oct., 1917; J.P.

MEILISH, HON. HUMPHREY.—B. 1862; ed. Mount Mellick Schl., Prince of Wales Coll., Charlottetown, 1876-79 (holder of Govt. scholarship for County of Queen's P.E.I., 1876-78; medallist, classics and maths., 1879); Dalhousie Univ. (B.A., 1882, LL.B.); matriculant, Univ. of Lond., hons. div., 1883; called to N.S. bar, 1890; K.C., 1904; practised law, 1891-1918; pres., N.S. Barristers' Soc., 1912-13; agt., Canadian min. of just. in N.S., 1903-04; judge, sup. ct., N.S., 11th Feb., 1918, also surrogate, and dep. local judge in adm'y., for N.S. dist., 1920; local judge in adm'y., 1921.

MELVILL, MAJ.-GEN. CHARLES WILLIAM, C.B. (1919), C.M.G. (1918), D.S.O. (1916).—B. 1878; ed. Wellington Coll. (Eng.) and R. Mily. Coll., Sandhurst; 2nd lieut., S. Lancs. Regt., 1897; capt., 1902; resig., 1907; N. Z. Staff Corps, 1911; major, 1915; lieut.-col., 1916; in command, 1st Infy. Brig., N. Z. Exped. Force, with rank of brig.-gen., 1917; G.O.C., N.Z. Exped. Force, London, 1919; maj.-gen. in commd., N.Z. Mily. forces, 1924; war serv., Sept.-Nov., 1914 with S. Lancs. Regt. (wounded), and with N.Z. Exped. Force, 1915-18; offr. of Order of Crown (Belgium), Croix de Guerre (Belgium); four times ment. in despatches.

MELVILLE, SIR GEORGE, K.C.M.G. (1900), C.M.G. (1894).—B. 1842; late lieut., Kent Artil. militia; ed. Edinburgh Acad.; clk. in the solr.'s dept., inland rev., after compet. exam., June, 1862; afterwards in the legacy and succession duty dept.; ch. clk., treas., S. Leone, Nov., 1874; acted as col. treas., Dec., 1874, to Feb., 1876, during which period also acted as col. sec., July to Sept., 1875; acted also as collr. of customs and col. surrv., and held comm. as dep.-coroner and J.P.; 1st clk., govt. sec.'s office, Br. Guiana, 1877; astt. gov't. sec., 1879; acted as govt. sec., 1881, 1882, 1887, and 1888, and also as audr.-gen.; col. sec. audr.-gen., and regir.-gen. Br. Honduras, 1889; admstr. of govt., 1890 and 1891; admstr. of govt. of Falklands, 1893; col. sec., Bahamas, 1894; admstr. govt., 1894 and 1896; col. sec., Leewards, 1896; admstr. govt. under dormant commission, 1896, 1896, 1897, 1899, 1900; admstr. and col. sec., Saint Lucia, Sept., 1902; ret., 1906.

MELVILLE, THOMAS ALEXANDER.—B. 1880; apptd. after open compet. exam. for home civ. ser., to G.P.O., Dec., 1885, and served in different depts.; supt. of mails, G.P.O., Singapore, Oct., 1905; ag. supt., money order branch and savings bank, Singapore, in 1911 and 1912; ag. astt. postmr.-gen., Singapore, Apr. to June and Aug. to Oct., 1912; ag. supt. of mails, Penang, Oct., 1913; supt., money order branch and savings bank, but ag. acctnt., G.P.O., Singapore, Jan., 1915; acctnt., post and telegraph dept., F.M.S., 1st July, 1917, but continued
as ag. acctnt., Singapore; ag. astt. P.M.G., Penang, 5th Feb., 1918; assumed duties as acctnt., post and tel. dept., F.M.S., May, 1920; ag. dir. of posts and tels., F.M.S., Apr.-Dec., 1921 and Oct., 1923; acct., posts and tels., F.M.S., Apr., 1923.

MENENDEZ, Sir M. Raymond, K.T. Bach. (1906).—Ed. Emman. Coll., Camb.; LL.B., Camb., 1890; barrister-at-law, Inner Temp.; ag. stip. and circuit mag., etc., and judge of com. pleas, Bahamas, 1892-4; dist. commr., Lagos, Aug., 1894; ag. Queen's advocate, Lagos, Dec., 1896, to Aug., 1897; ch. judicial offr., Niger Coast Protectorate, Aug., 1897; puisne judge, S. Nigeria, 1st Jan., 1899; ag. ch. just. on several occasions; read. thanks of gov., for spec. services in reorganising native courts of prot., Jan., 1903; ch. just., N. Nigeria, 1905.

MENSAH, Alfred, I.S.O. (1907).—Extra clk., cust. and treasy. depts., G. Coast, 18th May, 1874; 3rd clk., 1st Dec., 1874; 2nd clk., 1st July, 1876; clk. and warehouse keeper, 13th Mar., 1878; sub-collr. of cust., Winnebah, 15th Oct., 1880; Cape Coast, 1st May, 1882; Winnebah, 16th Nov., 1882; transf. to Appam as sen. sub-collr. and examg. offr. for Winnebah dist., 12th Oct., 1883; Cape Coast, 22nd Feb., 1886; offr.-in-charge of treasy., Cape Coast, 5th May to 11th June, 1904, and 11th July, 1904, to 15th Jan., 1906; sub-astt. treas., G. Coast, 16th Jan., 1906; transf. to Kumase, 1907 and 1908.

MENTZ, Hon. Hendrik.—B. 1877; formerly M.L.A., Transvaal; M.L.A. for Zoutpansberg till 1924; min. of lands, Union of S. Africa, 1916; and ag. min. of defence, 1918; min. of defence, 1920-24.

MERCER, Sir William Hespworth, K.C.M.G. (1914), C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1855; open scholar and Hody exhib., Wadham Coll., Oxford; 2nd cl. classical mods.; 2nd cl. final classical schl.; 2nd cl. clk. in the C.O. after open compet., 30th June, 1879; awarded 1st prize in common law offered by council of legal education, 1883, and a pupil scholarship of 100 guineas, in real property law, by the soc. of the Inner Temple, 1886; called to the bar, 1886; sec. to the Earl of Jersey, when ag. as Br. delegate at col. confee., Ottawa, 1894; on special mission to Hawaii with Mr. (afterwards Sir) Sandford Fleming, Sept. to Nov., 1894, negotiating for lease of landing station of proposed Pacific cable; astt. priv. sec. to Lord Ripon, Apr., 1895; to Mr. Chamberlain, June, 1895; 1st class clk., May, 1896; sec. to Pacific cable comtee., 1896; prin. clk., Oct., 1896; sec. to Pacific cable comtee., 1899; crown agt. for the cols., June, 1900; mem. of Pacific cable bd., 1901; dep. chmn. of ditto, 1907; apptd. dir. of scholars sent to England from certain crown cols., 1902; mem. of West African currency board, 1912; joint editor of C.O. List since 1898; ret. from post of C.A., 31st Nov., 1921; chmn. of W. African currency bd., E. African currency bd. and Pacific cable bd.

MERCIER, Guy Henry Vifont.—2nd clk., regiar. and provost-marshal's office, Antigua, 1896; 4th clk., col. sec.'s office, 1897; clk. to regiar. and provost-marshal, Nevis, 1898; dep. coroner, Nevis, 1901; rev. offr., Nevis, 1901; clk., British vice-consulate, Chinde, Apr., 1905; astt. agent, Nyasaland govt., Chinde, July, 1906; vice-consul, Chinde (unpaid), Dec., 1910; acted as agt., Nyasaland govt. and consul on several occasions; apptd. agent, Feb., 1918; served as capt. in Nyasaland Field Force, July, 1917 to 28th Feb., 1919; retains rank of capt.; ag. ch. transport offr., Apr., 1923; admin. offr., 1st grade, 17th Dec., 1923.

MEREDITH, Hon. Richard Martin.—I. 1847; judge of high ct., Ontario, chancery div., 1890; ct. of appeal, 1905; chief just. of a common pleas, 1912.

MEREWETHER, Sir Edward Marsden, K.C.M.G. (1916); K.C.V.O. (1907); C.V.O. (1905); C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1868; ed. Harrow; cadet, S.S., Oct., 1880; passed final exam. in Malay, May, 1882; ag. collr. of land rev., Singapore, and J.S.S., May, 1883; confirmed, Jan., 1883; Val. interp. with H.M.S. "Pegasus" to Tenom; connection with the "Niseru" case, June, 1884; ag. mag. and offr. in charge treasy., Malacca, 1st dist. offr., Dindinga, 1886; ag. 2nd mag., Penang, 1888; ag. 1st mag., Penang, 1888; 2nd astt. sec., June, 1890; supt. of census, 1911; ag. ass. sec., Aug., 1891; collr. of land rev., and in chap. of treasy., Malacca, July, 1892; ag. rea. on Malacca, Sept. to Dec., 1893; inspr. of priza S.S., 1893; astt. col. sec. and clk. of comm., 1897; ag. res. coun., Malacca, May, 1897, to June, 1898, and Sept., 1900; ag. col. treasur., S.S., 1900; ag. res. coun., Malacca, Sept., 1901; ag. rea., Selangor, Oct., 1901; confirmed, Dec., 1901; lieut.-gov. and ch. sec. to gov't., Malta, Aug., 1902; gov., Sierra Leone, 1911; gov., Leeward Isl., 7th Jan., 1916.

MERRICK, Capt. F. S.—Joined 3rd Bat. Innis. Fus., 1906; Natal police, 1897-1902; lieu. 29th I.Y., Moh., 1902; served in S. African war (2 medals); dist. supt. of pol., N. Nigeria, 1903; ag. astt. commr. of pol., July-Aug., 1904; ag. staff offr., Aug.-Dec., 1905; 1st cls. dist. supt. of pol., Apl., 1908; deputy I.G. of pol., Dec., 1910; ag. I.G., Apl.-Oct., 1911.

MERRICK, John Edward Simpson.—I. 1888; ed. Winchester and Univ. Coll., Oxfor; B.A., 1911; astt. dist. commr., Uganda Prov., 1912; 3rd astt. sec., 1913; 2nd astt. sec., 1914; senr. astt. sec., E. Africa Prov., Nov., 1919.

MERRIMAN, The Right Hon. John Lionel P.C. (1909), M.L.A.—Commr. of pub. wks. and crown lands, C. of Good Hope, 1875-8; for several years represented the electoral div. Eldred recht in the Cape legis. assm.; again commr. of crown lands and pub. wks., 1881 to 1894; treas.-gen., 1890-3; mem. of Jameson raid comm., 1891; treas.-gen. in the Schreiner ministry, 1898-1900; mem. for Victoria West, since 1904; prem. and prime min., 1908; mem. of Imple. Conf. on naval and mil. defence, 1909; mem. of S. African national convention and of delegations to England in connection with S. Africa Bd., 1909; mem. for Stellenbosch, 1915-24.

MESSER, Chas. McIlvaine, O.B.E. (1915); B. 1874; ed. Merchant Taylors' schl., Emmanuel Coll., Camb.; exhibitioner, 1893; scholar, 1893; 16th wrangler math. tripos, 1896; B.A., 1896; M.A., 1905; cadet, Hong Kong, 1897; ag. astt. col. sec. and clk. of comm., 1898; ag. land offr., New Territory, 1899; pal. and J.P. for New Territories, 1899; J.P., 1900; ag. col. treasur., 1901; passed cadet, 1902; regiar.-gen., 1902; astt. land offr., N.T., 1903; mem. of land ct., 1903-4; pol.-mag., N.T., addition, 1905; ag. postm.-gen., 1907; mem. of sanitary dept. and pres. of sanitary bd., 1908; postm.-gen., 1908; ag. col. treasur., 1909-11; capt. supt. of police, supt. of Vict. gaol and supt. of fire brigade, 1913; offr., M.I.D., 1913; colonial treasur., 1918; custodian of crown property, 1919; estate duty commnr., 1924.

METCALFE, Charles Campbell, M.C.—I. 1880; ed. Elizabeth Coll., Guernsey; clk., W. 1901; clk., treas., Nyasaland, 1911; K.A.
914-22; ag. chief transport offr., Nyassaland, Jan., 1922 to Feb., 1923; ch. transport offr., 8th Feb., 1923.

METHUEN, FIELD-MARSHAL THE RIGHT HON. SIR ARTHUR, G.C.B., G.C.M.G. (1919), G.C.V.O.—B. 1845; entered the Army, 1864; served in Ashanti expdn., 1873-74; mil. attache at Berlin, 1878-81; served with expeditionary force in Egypt, 1882; ended special services in Bechuanaland expdn.; 1884-85; served on the staff in S. Africa, 1888-90; ient.-gen. comdg. a div., S. Africa, 1899-1902; mem. of Royal Patriotic Fund Corporation, 1905-7; F.O.C., S. Africa, 1908; gov. of Natal in 1910; ov. Malta, 27th Jan., 1915; assumed gov't. 14th Feb., 1915; retired, 1919.

METZGEN, MONRAD SIGFRID.—B. 1893; emp. clk. to keeper of prisons, B. Bond, Mar., 1910; transfd. to treas. dept., Aug., 1910; temp. ast. keeper of King's warehouses, Sept., 1910; 2nd grade cust. and excise offr., Aug., 1911; 2nd rade ditto, Jan., 1918; 2nd lieut., B. Bond, Territorial Force, June, 1918; internal rev. offr., Jan., 1920; seconded to income tax dept., June, 1921; priv. offr., income tax, Aug., 1922; offr. of ast., Nov., 1922; sec. to select comtee. to acquire into cost of living to civ. servants, Mar., 1923.

MEWBURN, MAJOR-GENERAL S. C., C.M.G. (1917).—B. 1863; called to the bar, 1885; K.C., 1910; dir.-gen., Canadian Defence Force, 1917; sec. to H. of C., gen. elec., 1917; min. of militia and National gov't., Canada, 1917-19; mem., privy coun. for Canada; re-el. to H. of C., g.e., Dec., 1921.

MEWS, ARTHUR, C.M.G. (1918).—Acomt., gov. telegraphs, Newfndl., 1893; clk. to fincl. sec., 1894; fincl. clk., col. sec.'s office, 1896; dep. col. sec., 1898; regis. of joint stock companies, 1899; P., 1913; censor of telegraphs, cables and wires stations, 1914; mem., St. John's defence comte., 1915; dep. press censor, 1915.

MICALEFF, SIR RICHARD, K.C.M.G. (1906), M.G. (1902).—B. 1846; entd. the Malta rv., Nov., 1863; clk. in office of charitable institutions, Dec., 1864; clk., sanitary office and sec. to the med. bd., Jan., 1881; dep. cr.-gen., dep. comptroller of charitable instit., and dep. comsry., Monte di Pietà, Gozo, Apr., 1884; ast. sec. to gov't. for Gozo, Sept., 1885; mp'troller of charitable instit., with seat in un. of govt., Nov., 1886, and a seat in the exec. un., Mar., 1888; ret., 1911.

MICHELIN, WILLIAM PLUNKETT.—B. 1872; mister-at-law, Middle Temple; entd. col. serv., 1890; judicial dept. Jamaica 1891-1906; dist. mantr., G. Coast, Mar., 1906; ag. chief regis. and sheriff 1909; acted as solr.-gen. on several occasions during 1908-1911; pol. mag., Coomassie, sb., 1911; ag. circuit judge, Sierra Leone, Jan.-pl., 1913; pol. mag. and coroner, Gibraltar, Jan., 1913; acted as atty.-gen. on several occasions during the years 1913-1919; 2nd puisne dge, Leeward Islands, Nov., 1919; 1st puisne dge, Aug., 1920; ag. ch. just., Nov., 1920 to ar., 1921 and from Dec., 1922 to Mar., 1923; spared revd. edn. of statutes of St. Kitts and vis., 1922; puisne judge, Gold Coast, July, 1923.

MIDDLETON, J. J. I.—Transvaal audit office, May, 1901; clk., treasy., Nov., 1901; acctnt., assy., 1st Dec., 1902; acctnt., treasy., Union S. Africa, 1910; sec. to pub. debt. comsrs., 11; under sec. for finance, 1918.

MIDDLETON, SIR JOHN, K.B.E. (1924), M.G. (1916).—B. 1870; ed. Sedbergh and Univ. Edin.; M.A.; ast. dist. comsry., S. Nigeria, 1901; ag. dist. comsry., Warri, 1901; ast. sec., 1902; sen. ast. sec., 1904; officiated as sec. to govt. and divisional comsry., 1904-5; dist. comsry., 2nd grade, 1906; ag. ch. ast. col. sec. and ast. prov. comsry., 1906-7; senr. ast. col. sec., 1907; ast. col. sec., Mauritius, 1908; ag. col. sec., 1908-9; 10-11-12-13; col. sec., 1913; admstd. govt., 1914, 1916 and 1919; gov., Falkland Is., 1920.

MIDDLETON, SIR JOHN PAGE, KT. BACH. (1912), B.A.—Ed. Uppingham and Trin. Hall, Camb.; called to the bar, Mid. Term., June, 1874, Norfolk and S.E. circuits; ag. Queen's advoc., G. Coast, Jan., 1882; pres. of dist.ct., Limasol, Cyprus, Sept., 1882; puisne judge, sup. ct., 1892; ag. ch. just., June and July, 1893; ag. judge of consular ct., Constantinople, May to July, 1894; ag. ch. just., May to Oct., 1895; received thanks of S. of S. Foreign Affairs in connection with Ottoman Dominions (Courts) O. in C., 1895; puisne judge, Ceylon, 1902; ret. 1912.

MIDDLETON, HON. WM. EDWARD.—B. 1860; ed. Toronto Coll. Inst. and Toronto Univ.; admitted solr., 1884; called to the bar, 1885; K.C., 1908; judge of high ct., Ontario, 1910.

MIFSUD, HON. PROFESSOR CARMELO, M.D.—B. 1862; matric., Malta Univ., 1876; grad. in medicine, 1883; res. ast. med. offr., cent. hosp., 1883-84; physician, cent. hosp., Sept., 1885; prof. of medicine, Malta Univ., Feb., 1903; elec. to rep. graduates in senate, Oct., 1921; min. for pub. health, Feb., 1923; attended confce. on leprosy at Strasbourg as del. of govt. of Malta, July, 1923.

MIFSUD, EDWARD R.—B. 1875; clk., Malta civ. serv. after compet. exam., 1892; clk., audit office, 1892; secretariat, 1901; ch. clk., lieut. gov't. office, 1913; dep. ast. sec. to govt. and clk. of couns., 1920; clk. of exec., nominated and privy couns. and private sec. to gov., Oct., 1921.

MIFSUD, HON. U. P., LL.D. (1910), B. Litt. (1906).—B. 1880; matric., Malta Univ., 1903; called to bar, 1911; el. to rep. first dist. in Maltese parlmt., Oct., 1921; min. of industry and commerce, 28th Oct., 1921.

MIGEOD, FREDERICK WILLIAM HUGH, F.R. Anth. Inst., F.R.G.S.—Entd. Royal Navy, 1889; ast. paymaster, 1893; resig., 1898; transport offr., W.A.F.F., Nigeria, 1st Sept., 1898 to 6th July, 1899; supervisor of customs, G. Coast, 24th Mar., 1900; ast. transport offr., Ashanti Field Force, 27th May, 1900 (Ashanti medal); head of transport dept., 21st Sept., 1901; ag. prov. comsry., 14th Feb. to 6th June, 1909; author of "The Mende Language," 1908; "The Languages of West Africa," 1911-13; "Mende Natural History Vocabulary," 1913; "Grammar of the Hausa Language," 1914; "Earliest Man," 1916.

MIGEOD, GEORGE EDWARD HENRY.—Clk., pay and acct. dept., W.A.F.F., Niger Territory, 1899; ch. clk. and cashier, treasy., Jan., 1900; subsequently ast. treasurer, N. Nigeria; collr., cust., N. Nigeria, 1st Apr., 1903.

MILES, GEORGE COOKBURN, B.A., (Oxon.)—B. 1898; on mil. serv., Mar., 1917; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., May, 1921; addl. Jaffna kach., June, 1921; pol. mag., Putalam, Aug., 1922; office ast., Galle kach., Apr., 1924.

MILES, LIEUT.-GEN. SIR HERBERT SCOTT GOULD, G.C.B. (1914); G.C.M.G. (1916); G.B.E. (1918); K.C.B.(1908); C.B. (1900); C.V.O. (1903); M.V.O. (1897).—B. 1860; entd. army, 1869; col. 1893; A.A.G., Aldershot, 1893; comdt. of staff
MILLARD, ALFRED SUTTON.—B.Sc., M.B., Ch.B. (Edin.); D.P.H., med. offr., S. Stltlnts., May, 1907; ag. sen. med. offr., Singapore, 23rd Jan. to 17th June, 1909; med. offr., grade II., F.M.S., 6th July, 1909; health offr., F.M.S., 1st Jan., 1912; temp. med. offr., Outhing, Basuto land, Sept., 1916; med. offr. of health, Cyprus, Mar., 1921.

MILLARD, THOMAS.—B. 1884; ed. King's Coll., London; paymaster, 6th K.A.R., Mar., 1908; A.G.S. medal and clasp, 1908-10; asst. treas., Somaliland Prot., June, 1910; ag. treas., June, 1910 to Feb., 1911, and from Oct., 1911 to May, 1912; asst. treas., Cyprus, 1913; on mily. serv., B.E.F., France from Sept., 1915; capt. and adjt., 20th R. Fusiliers; wounded, Apr., 1917; resumed duty, 24th Nov., 1921; ag. treas., June to Dec., 1922 and June to Nov., 1924.

MILLER, ALBERT EDWARD, M.C.—H.M. Forces, 9th Aug., 1914; serv. in Malta, Sept., 1914 to Jan., 1915, and France, 1915-19; inspr. of live-stock, Gold Coast, 20th May, 1921.

MILLER, JAMES INNES, M.A.—B. 1892; ed. Fettes Coll. and Edin. Univ. (1st cls. hona. class. and hist.); mily. serv., Gallipoli and Mesopot., 1915-19; cadet, F.M.S., Oct., 1919; dep. collr. and reg sr. of deeds, Penang, Dec., 1919; mag., May, 1920; agt., food contr., Penang, Oct., 1920; secy. to food contr., Singapore, Feb., 1921; attd. col. secy.'s office in addn., June, 1921; passed final exam., Malay, June, 1921; ag. 2nd astt. sec. B., 28th Apr., 1922; ag. astt. dist. offr., Ipoh, July, 1922.

MILLER, RICHARD ELLIOT MORGAN, B.A. (Calcutta).—B. 1875; acctnt., P.W.D. India, Nov., 1895 to June, 1899; acctnt., Uganda rly., July, 1899; asst. acctnt., Nigerian rly., Jan., 1914; acctnt., 2nd grade, Nigerian rly., July, 1915; acctnt., Nigerian rly., 1917; ch. acctnt., G. Coast rlys., Jan., 1920.

MILLER, WILLIAM.—B. 1860; survr.-gen. and civil engrnr., Bahamas, 1890; ret. on pension from office of civ. engrnr., 1st Nov., 1922, but retained appt. of survr.-gen.

MILLER, WILLIAM.—B. 1880; astt. engrnr., Aberdeen main drainage works and River Dee tunnel; astt. engrnr., burgh survr.'s office, Aberdeen; astt. mun. engrnr., Singapore; astt. resp. engrnr., Kalang river reservoir, Singapore; office astt. to dir., pub. wks., Gold Coast, 15th Feb., 1911; dir. of transport, Accra, under the defence scheme, Aug., 1914; attd. to B.E.F., Togoland, Aug., 1914; ag. dir., pub. wks., Dec., 1917 to Mar., 1918; ag. dep. dir., pub. wks., 1918 and 1921; astt. dir., pub. wks., Aug., 1919; astt. col. sec., 27th Feb., 1922.

MILLINGTON, EDWARD TURNER.—B. 1881; ed. Victoria Univ., Manchester (B.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1904; extra offr. astt. to govt. agt., N.
