MORRIS, ALFRED.—B. 1874; educn. dept., Hong Kong, head mast., Saiyingpun schl., 1905; Normal mast., Queen's Coll., 1913-14; head mast., Saiyingpun schl., 1914; tutor in English, Hong Kong Univ., 1917-19; lecturer to teacher's sem., Tech. Inst., 1917; master of method, Hong Kong Univ., 1920-24.

MORRIS, SIR DANIEL K.C.M.G. (1903), C.M.G. (3), M.A., D.Sc., D.C.L., F.L.S., F.R.H.S., I.H., C.M.Z.S.—B. 1844; ed. at Cheltenham and Roy. Schl. of Mines, London; late sen. erator and 1st gold medallist, Trin. Coll., 1876; B.A. (1876), M.A. (1880); D.Sc. (1893); dir., Roy. bot. gardens, Ceylon, 1887; special duty, "coffee leaf disease inquiry," 1879-79; recd. thanks of planters' assoc. of Ceylon, as also special commendation of govt. for honorarium of one year's salary; first dir., gardens and plantations, Jamaica, 1879; on special mission to Trinidad and Grenada to report on cultivation of cacao, 1882; reported on resources of Br. Honduras, 1882; chmn., Jamaica Soc., Amsterdam exhib., 1883; reported on resources of St. Helena, 1883; prepared report on planting enterprise in the W. Indies presented to parlmt., 1884; chmn. bd. of govt. of Inst. of Jamaica, 1884-86; comsrr. for W. Indies at the World's Exposition, New Orleans, 1885; chmn. of local comsrr. for Col. and Ind. Exhibition, 1886; asst. dir., Roy. Gardens, Kew, 1886-1898; represented govt. of India at Ratlie Conf. at Paris, 1888 and 1889; on spec. mission to W. Indies to organise botan. stations in Windward and Leeward Is., 1889-90; visited Bahamas to confer with col. govt. on agric. developments, 1896-6; scientific adviser to W. India Royal comsrr., 1896-7; presented separate report on economic resources of W. Indies; apptd. Impl. comsrr. of agric. in W. Indies, 1898-1908; on retirement services retained as adviser in tropical agric. to S. of S. for the colonies; mem. of exec. coun. of Leeward Is., pres. of seven annual agric. confs., in W. Indies, 1899-1908; on spec. mission to Sea Is., S. Carolina, to study cotton industry, 1903; successfully introduced the cultivation of Sea Is. cotton into W. Indies; visited Canada on offl. missions in 1904, 1906 and 1907; arranged for Canadian bd. of trade delegn. visit to W. Indies, 1907; organised Canadian reciprocity conf., Barbados, 1908; mem. of Roy. comn. on trade rel. between Canada and W. Indies, 1909-10; editor of W. Indian Bulletin, the quarterly scientific journal, vols. I. to IX. (1899-1908), of the Agricultural News, vols. I. to VII. (1902-1908), and other publications of the Impl. dept. of agric.; author of numerous works on pure and applied botany, and of papers and official reports relating to distrib. and cultiv. of tropical economic plants; mem. of coun. (formerly treas.) of Roy. Hort. Soc. and of Roy. Coll. Inst.; fellow of scientific and other socs. at home and abroad.

MOUBRAY, GEORGE ALEXANDER DE CHAZAL DE—B. 1888; ed. Loretto Sch., Manchester Univ. (civ. engnr.), Zurich Polytechnikum and Univ. (pure science); cadet, F.M.S., 1912; attd. to lab. dept., Apr., 1915; ag. 2nd asst. dist. offr., Tapah, Nov., 1915; ag. ass't. contr. of lab., Penang, Nov., 1919; asst. dist. offr., Tampin, Nov., 1919; ag. priv. sec. to ch. sec., Aug., 1920; ag. 2nd asst. dist. offr., Larut, 2nd asst. dist. offr., 1st asst. dist. offr., and dist. offr., Kuala Kangsar, Oct., 1921-May, 1923; ag. collr., land rev., Kuala Lumpur and registr. of titles, Selangor, May, 1923; town planning admstr. in addn., July, 1923.

MOULDER, EDWIN RICHARD DENYS.—B. 1873; ed. at Queen's Coll., B. Guiana, and Merton Coll., Oxford; Guiana scholar, 1891; 3rd cls. hist., 1895; B.A., 1896; M.A., 1898; Oxford diploma course in education, 1912; asst. mast., Lodge schl., Barbados, 1899-1901; asst. mast., Queen's Coll., B. Guiana, 1901-1914; examnr. to educn. dept., 1902-1914; ag. dir. of primary educn., May to Nov., 1914, and from July to Nov., 1918; inspr. of schl., Apr., 1914; ag. 2nd master, Queen's Coll., Oct. to Dec., 1916; ag. censor in addition to other duties, Aug. to Nov., 1917; prin., Queen's Coll., Feb., 1920.

MOULDER, HUGH ARTHUR WILLIAM.—B. 1879; ent. Fiji civ. serv., 1910; acctnt. and clk., Gilbert and Ellice Is., Dec., 1915; ag. treas., 30th July to 19th Sept., 1916 and from 25th to 28th July, 1919; seconded for sec'd, 22nd Apr., 1921; ag. astm. andr., 5th May; ag. audr., 22nd Aug., 1921 to 2nd Apr., 1923; assumed duties of substantive appt., 7th Apr., 1923.

MOUNTAIN, GEORGE ALPHONSE.—B. ed. Quebec; civ. engnr. and Dom. land surveyor, Que., 1880; Can. Atlantic Rly., 1904; ch. engnr., 1888 to 1904; ch. engrg. rly. comsnrs., Can., 1st July, 1904; past mem. of Engng. Inst. of Can.; mem. Can. Rly. Engng. Assoc., and Assoc. of Rly. Bldgs. and Bridges.

MOURITZ, GEORGE A.—Treas., Melville harbour trust, 1877; sec., 1884.

MOWAT, HON. HERBERT MACDONALD.—1863; ed. Queen's Univ. (LL.B.); barrister, 1899; formerly an offr. of 14th Regt., Kgl. and Queen's Own Rifles, Toronto; brevet Capt. Borden, 1916; el. to H.C., g.e., 1921; judge, sup. ct., Ont., 1921.

MUDIE, NORMAN DAVID.—Cadet, S. Naval Dec., 1907; sent to China to study Eng., June, 1908; ag. second astm. prot. of the Singapore, Oct., 1910; passed cadet, Jan.; offr., cls. V., June, 1911; ag. dep. rep., sup. ct., and ast. offr., assignee, Penang, July; ag. 3rd mag., Singapore, April, 1915; ag. prot. of Chinese, and ast. sup't. govt. nat. Malacca, Aug., 1917; dep. regar., sup. ct., in addition, Aug., 1917; offr., assignee, nat. estates for Malacca, Oct.-Dec., 1917; offr., Jan., 1918; supernumary offr., cls. II., No. 3 ag. sup't., govt. monopolies, Singapore, 1921; stamp and probate offr., Singap., 5 Apr., 1922.

MUIR-MACKENZIE, CAPT. K. J.—St. Paul's Sch., and Jesus Coll., Cambridge, 1907; practised until 1914; served in war, 1914-19; crown counsel, Kenya, 1915; ag. solr. gen., mem., leg. coun., and asst. Fiji, 1922; mem., exec. coun., ag. dist. oh. judl. comsnr., W. Pacific, 1922; Colombo Port comsnr., Feb., 1923.

MULHALL, JOHN ARCHIBALD.—Cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Dec., 1921; sta. Kach., Jan., 1922; ditto, Puttalam, Nov., 1922; extra office ast., Bath, Oct., 1923; office ast., ditto, Jan., 1924.

MULLENS, ERNEST THOMAS.—Frm. Lond., 1882 to 1892; clk. and shorthand legis. coun., Natal, 16th Oct., 1893; sec. of lands and works, 15th Mar., 1894; to agric., 1st Nov., 1901; mem. of lands offr., mem. of land bd., Sept., 1904.

MULLER, SAMUEL ERNEST DUNCAN.—cls. V, Ceylon civ. serv., Jan., 1921; addl. acct., gen. treas., Jan., 1921; acct. of port coman., Feb., 1923.

MULLIN, JOHN.—B. 1878; ed. East Wales; assayer, surveyor and mining engnr.; mem. of insttn. of mining and metallurgy; land; served with L. & N.W. Rly. Co., New Mining Co., Canada, B. Guiana Gold Co. Co., and Mara Mara Gold Mining Co., cert. sworn land surv., B. Guiana, 1908; cls. offr. and survr., B. Guiana, 1908; of mining dist. and J.P., 1910; 1st dept. of lands and mines, 1911; ag. cls. 1911-12, 1913-14; 1st lieut., B. Guiana forces, 1915; seconded to gort. secret. conf. clk., 1916.
MULOCK, Hon. Sir William, K.C.M.G. (1892), K.C., LL.D., M.A.—B. 1843; graduated from Toronto Univ., 1863; gold medal in modern languages; called to the Ontario bar, 1868; LL.B.; chancellor of Toronto Univ. in 1881; ass't in law, 1882 to 1905, representing N. York; maj.-gen. in Sir W. Laurier's govt., June, 1916; ch. just., exchequer div., high ct. of just., tarit., 1905; ch. just., Ontario, 1923.

FULVEY, Thomas, K.C., B.A. (Toronto).—B. 1863; fellow in physics, Univ. of Toronto, 1867-69; bar-at-law, Osgoode Hall, 1889; ass't v. sec., Ontario, 1903; under-seer of state and registrar genl. of Canada, 1909; chmn., enemy property, 1920; also held office of King's printer and contriv. of stationery, 1st June, 1920 to 15th June, 1921.

TUMFORD, William Bryant, B.A. (Cantab.), B. 1900; ed. Manchester Gram. Schi. and St. John's Coll., Cambridge; matros, trip, 1920; shipman, R.N., 1918-19; diploma of educn., London, 1923; B. of E. teachers certif., 1923; mast., educn. dept., Tanganyika Territory, 1923.

UNRO, Christopher Ralph Ellerington, B.A. (St. Andrews).—B. 1889; ed. High Schi., Glasgow and St. Andrew's Univ.; junr. ass't v. sec., Nigeria, 12th Nov., 1913; treas. ass't, 2nd Jan., 1st Jan., 1919; regraded as ass't treas., Jan., 1920; ag. senr. ass't treas., 10th Jan., 1921.

UNRO, J. S.—Ass't loco. supt., Uganda Railway, Jan., 1918.

UNRO, Thomas Ambrose Vesper.—B. 1883; bmr., Bahamas, 1st Sept., 1913; ag. marshal, navy, aide, sup. ct., 1919.

URDOCK, Hon. James.—B. 1871; removed from Canada, 1874; ent. serv. of C.P.R., 1890; now pres. of Brotherhood of Rly. Trainmen; mem. bd. of commerce of Can., 29th Sept., 1919 to 1st June, 1920, when resigned; min. of lab. in charg. admtn., 29th Dec., 1921.

UTRISON, Sir James William, Kt. Bach. (B.A.), LL.B., K.C.—B. 1872; ed. privately at Trin. Hall, Camb.; senr. classical scholar, 1st div.; 2nd cls. class. trip, 1894; ols. law trip, Part II., 1895; Latham English prize, 1896; B.A., LL.B., 1896; called to the Bar, Middle Temple, Apr., 1896; devilled practised at the Chancery Bar, 1896-1902; ass't, E.A.P., 9th Oct., 1902; town mag., Mbasa, Jan., 1904; 2nd ass't judge, H.B.M. rt for Zanzibar, Apr., 1904; sen. ass't judge, r., 1906; chief judge, Zanzibar, 20th Sept., 1906; mem. of court of appeal for Eastern Africa, 1906-1910, and from 1914 upon transfer of Zanzibar to C.O.; judge of sup. ct. of H.H. tan of Zanzibar from 1908; arbitrator in dispute between Zanzibar and E.A.P. govt., as H.H. mainland properties, 1911; read thanks 3. of S. for conversion of Applied Indian Acts into Zanzibar Decrees, 1917; judge of the Prize Court, Zanzibar, from 1914; passed govt. exam. in Hindustani, 1903, and in Swahili, 1904; miner in Swahili to the Zanzibar Govt.; attorney-gen., S. Stittm., 1919; ag. col. sec., 1920 to Mar., 1921; author of "Swahili insalations," 1911.

URPHY, Hon. Charles, B.A., M.P.—At Ottawa, 8th Dec., 1863; son of James Urphy, of Birr, King's co., Ireland, and Mary Way, of Limerick, Ireland; ed. at the Jesuit Brothers' schl., Ottawa, the Ottawa Collegiate Inst., and Ottawa Univ. (B.A.); barr.-at-law; sworn of the King's privy coun. for Canada on the 5th Oct., 1908, and apptd. S. of S. in the cabinet of the Rt. Hon. Sir Wilfrid Laurier on the 10th Oct. in the same year; elec. a mem. of the H. of C. of Canada at the general elec. of 1908 for the county of Russell, in the prov. of Ontario; re-elec., 1911, 1917 and 1921; resigned portfolio on defeat of Laurier govt., Oct., 1911; P.M.G. in King admtn., 29th Dec., 1921.

MURPHY, Hon. Denis, B.A.—B. 1870; ed. Ottawa Univ.; B.A. 1892; called to the bar, 1896; elec. to provincial legis. British Columbia, 1900; judge of sup. ct., B. Columbia, 1909.

MURPHY, J. H.—Ass't dist. comsrr. E.A.P., Oct., 1919.

MURPHY, Matthew Alexander, M.I.C.E., M.S.E., M.R.S.I.—Ed. Harrison Coll., Barbados, and Glasgow and W. of Scotland Tech. Coll.; pupil, Messrs. Kyle, Dennison and Frew, C.E., Glasgow, 1891; junior ass't engrn. (with contractors), Lanarkshire and Dumbartonshire rlyws., 1894; ass't engrn. for new works, Trinidad govt. rlyws., 1896; ass't maintenance engrn., 1898; ag. ditto, Nov., 1900, to Apr., 1901, Feb., 1904, to June, 1904; seconded for ser. on road scheme, P.W.D., Arima dist., Jan., 1903, to Feb., 1904; col. engrn., St. Lucia, 1905; provisional M.L.C., Aug., 1906; comsrr. of crown lands and charge of govt. telephones, Oct., 1905; confirmed M.L.C., Feb., 1907; on special service in Grenada for reconstruction of Gouyave jetty, June, 1907; ag. mem. of exec. coun. for various periods during 1908-10; confirmed, Mar., 1912; local priority authority (Min. of Munitions) during the war; ag. dir. of pub. wks., B. Honduras, 1919; D.P.W., 1921; M.L.C., B. Honduras; govt. dir., Belize Electric Light and Power Co.; mem., cent. bd. of health; D.P.W., Trinidad, 1924.

MURPHY, William Henry Wyndham.—B. 1874; ed. Brighton Coll., St. Edmunds, Ware. Army tutors, Versailles; served S. African War, 1899-1902; commanded M. I. Coy., 1st Leinster Regt., Queen's and King's S. A. Medals, 8 clasps, ment. in desps.; transf'd., S. A. constab.; ass't dist. comdt. and ass't res. mag., 1903; transf'd., Bech. Prot. pol., 1908; res. J.P.; Reg. Army R. of O.; served European War, France, Flanders and Rhine Army of Occupation; lieut.-col., commanded a batt., 1916-19; ag. brigadier, 1916; D.S.O., 1917; ment. in desps.; transf'd., Tanganyika Territory as dist. supt. pol., 1920; transf'd., Zanzibar, commdt. of pol. and gov. of prisons, 1924.

MURPHY, William Lindsay.—B.A., Trin. Coll., Dublin; B. 1887; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., 12th Nov., 1910; attached to the Kandy Kachcheri, 14th Dec., 1910; addtl. pol. mag., Colombo, Aug., 1911; ag. office ass't to govt. agt., Prov. of Sabaragamuwa, 31st Jan., 1912; office ass't to govt. Prov. of Uva, May, 1913; ass't land settmt. offr., July, 1913; ag. ass't govt. agt., Kandy, Feb., 1915; addtl. pol. mag. and addtl. mun. mag., Colombo, Apr., 1915; ag. ass't govt. agt., Mullaitivu, Oct., 1915; ditto, Hambantota, Nov., 1917; ditto, Matara, Oct., 1920; addnl. dist. judge, Galle, Jan., 1921; ag. ass't govt. agt., Kegalla, May, 1921; ass't govt. agt., Kandy, Sept., 1922; ass't govt. agt., Trincomalee, Apr., 1923.

MURRAY, Beverley Thomas.—B. 1874; entd. civ. serv., Trinidad, 11th Oct., 1892; statistical clk. and librarian, colonial secretariat, 1st Apr., 1907; junr. inspr. of immigrts, 19th July, 1915; warden, St. Andrew, 1921.
MURRAY, HON. SIR GEORGE JOHN ROBERT, K.C.M.G. (1917), B.A., LL.M.—B. 1963; judge of c.p. ct., S. Australia, 1912; chief just. and lieutenant-gov., 14th Apr., 1916.

MURRAY, SIR J. H. P., K.C.M.G. (1925), C.M.G. (1914).—M.A., Oxon.; ed. at Sydney grammar schl. and won Knox prize, Fairfax prize, senr. univ. prize, and John West medal; went to Brighton Coll., Germany, and Univ. Coll., London; entd. Oxford Univ. and gained foundation scholarship to Magdalen Coll., 1880; 1st cls. class. mods., 1882; Ist cls. Lit. Hum., 1884; M.A., 1885; called to the bar, Inner Temple, 1886; practised as a barrister in Australia until apptd. crown prosecutor, N.S. Wales; acted as dist. ct. judge on several occasions; commanded N.S.W. Irish Rifles, 1898; served in S. African war, 1900-1901; reed. comm. of major in Impl. army in recognition of his services, 1902; chief judicial offr. and mem. of exec. and legis. couns., Papua, Sept., 1904; ag. administrator, 8th Apr., 1907; and lieut.-gov., in addition to duties of judge, 1908.

MURRAY, JOHN PEARS.—Served in Bechuanaland mtd. police, 1885-87; actg. clk., Basutoland, 1894; sub.-inspr., Basutoland mtd. police, 1895; inspr., 1902; finan. sec., 1904; ass't commnr., 1913; govt. sec., 1918; dep. res. commnr., 1920; ag. res. commnr., June to Dec., 1923 and June to Oct., 1924.

MURRAY, ROBERT HOSWORTH.—Admstrn. offr., 1st grade, Nyasaland, 28th Feb., 1923.

MURRAY, STEPHEN SAMUEL.—B. 1887; ed. Dulwich Coll.; clk., Nyasaland Prot., Jan., 1912; ag. ch. transport offr., Jan. to Feb., 1913, and May, 1918 to Apr., 1919; ag. paymr., 1st K.A.R., June, 1913 to Apr., 1914, and Jan. to Mar., 1915; cashier in treasy., Apr. to July, 1914; ag. lands offr. and dir. of mines, May to Dec., 1919; ch. clk., secretariat, and clk. to couns., Apr., 1920; ag. 2nd asst. sec., Nov., 1920 to Mar., 1921 and from June to Dec., 1921; supt. of census, 1921; ag. 1st asst. sec., Nov. to Dec., 1922; editor, Govt. Gazette, Jan., 1923; 2nd asst. sec. and clk. of couns., 26th July, 1923; sec. govt. tender bd., Sept., 1923; author of "Handbook of Nyasaland" (1922).

MURRAY, THE HON. SIR THOS KEIR, K.C.M.G. (1901), C.M.G. (1895).—Min. of lands and wks., Natal, 1893; col. sec., Feb. to Oct., 1897; M.L.A. to 1902; census commnr., 1904.

MURRAY, WILLIAM ANSLEY, B.A., M.B., Ch.B. (Edinburgh), D.P.H. (Cape Town).—B. 1874; attd. to Dutch Reformed Ch. Mission in Brit. Cent. Africa Prot., 1901-12; co-operated with sleeping sickness commn. of the Royal Soc'y., 1911-12; capt., S. African med. corps, and was associated with Major Park-Ross in conducting the Sleeping Sickness Investigation Bureau, 1916-18; govt. pathologist, Durban, 1919; asst. health offr., Union of S. Africa, 1923; mem. statistical coun., Union of S. Africa.

MURRAY, WALTER PEARS.—Survr., 1890; asst. registry survr., deeds office, Cape Town, Nov., 1893; reg. survr., deeds office, May, 1903; reg. survr. and examr. of diagrams, Dec., 1906; professional asst., survr.-gen.'s office, Cape Town, Apr., 1912; survr.-gen., O.F.S. Prov., 4th Aug., 1916; survr.-gen., Transvaal, 10th Sept., 1922.

MURTLAND, CHARLES CAMPBELL.—B. 1884; ed. Harrogate, York and Dublin; sub.-inspr. of police, B. Guiana, 1908; dist.-inspr., 1912; ag. county inspr., 1910-1911, 1914-1916; capt., B. Guiana militia, 1915.

MUSPRATT, COLIN KNOX.—B. 1893; ed. borne and New Coll., Oxford; 2nd lieu. Hampshires 29th Aug., 1914; India, Dec.; temp. capt., 29th Aug., 1915; M.R.F., 4th Oct., 1917; capt. (subst.), 4th Oct., 1917; R.F.F., Dec., 1918; attd. Rly. Operating Co. Co., T. Caucasus, 21st Feb., 1919; demob. Oct., 1919; trans. to T.F.R., 6th Jan.; ment. in despatches, 20th Nov., 1919; B.A.O., Nov., 1919; cadet, F.M.S., Nov., 1920; press to Canton to study Chinese, July, 1921; land office, Kuala Lumpur, July, 1923; Chinese sect., Kuala Lumpur, Dec., 1923; asst. dist. offr., Gopeng and Kampar, Apr., 1924.

MYERS, HON. SIR ARTHUR MILLER, B.A., Bach. (1924).—B. 1867; ed. Wellington, N.Z.; mem., N.Z. parl., 1910-1921; min. of finance, defence and rly., 1912; min. of pol. and munitions, national min., 1915-19.

MYLNE, THOMAS.—Regist. of titles (land, 1884; clk., regist.-gen.'s office, 1885-1887; clk., 1873; 2nd deputy, 1878; prim. dep., 1879; mem. civ. ser. bd., 1890.

NAISH, RICHARD BRYANT.—B. 1881; (Oxon.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1914; attached to Galle Kach., Dec., 1914; ag. pol. mag., Galle, in addition to his own post, Apr., 1915; ag. pol. mag., Avissawella, 1916; extra office asst. to govt. agt., N. Dist., Oct., 1916; ag. office asst. to govt. agt., Prov., Dec., 1916; pol. mag., Galle, 1918; asst. contr. of estate suppliers, 1918; office asst. to govt. agt., C. Prov., Feb., 1919; asst., govt. agt., Colombo, June, 1919; Trincomalee, Aug., 1920; addnl. pol. mag., Colombo, Negombo and Avissawella, Sep., 1920; asst. finan. asst. to chmn., mun. comm., Jan., 1921; pol. mag., Pt. Pedro, Nov., 1921; dist. judge, Tangalle, May, 1922; asst. judge Batticaloa, Mar., 1923.

NANKIVELL, HOWARD.—B. 1883; sec. to secretariat, Jamaica, 1911; asst., 1912; air mech., R.F.C., 1916; 2nd lieu., 1916; lieut.-tech., R.A.F., 1917-1919; clk., 1917; 1st ditto, 1920; sec., salaried commn., 1920; sec., disturbances commn., 1920.

NANTEL, HON. WILFRID BERTHIER, L.L.D.—B. 1887; ed. at the Seminary of Therese de Blainville, Quebec; L.L.D., Univ., Montreal; called to the bar, 1897; unsuccessful cand. for H. of C., Canada, at elec. to H. of C., 1908; re-elec., 1911; mem. Privy Council for Canada and min. of educ. in Mr. Borden's cabinet, Oct., 1911; mem. of rly. comm., 1914; now dep. chmn. of NAPIER, SIR WALTER JOHN, KT., B.A., D.C.L. (Oxon.).—Barrister-at-law, Lincoln's Inn; atty.-gen., S. Stithnta., 1907-1909; mem. African lands comm., 1912.

NASH, GEORGE HUTCHISON, M.A., B. 1889; ed. Queen's Coll., Oxford; F.M.S., 16th Nov., 1912; ag. ast. inspr., schla., Perak, 12th Mar., 1914; passed exam., June, 1914; ag. dist. offr., Jelebu, Nov., 1915; offr., clv. V, 20th Dec., 1915; ag. dist. offr., Kuala Langat, 22nd Feb., 1918; supernumerary, clv. IV, 16th Nov., 1919; ag. 1st mag., Johore Bahru, and regist., sup. ct., Johore, Dec., 1920; ag. inspr., prisons, Johore, in addition to other duties, 1929; ag. mag., Johore Bahru, May, 1928.

NASH, HERBERT FREDERICK WILLIAM.—B. 1901; entered C.O., 26th Nov., 1917; after compet. exam., asst. clk. and asst. C.O., 29th Dec., 1919; cler. offr., 1920.
NATHAN, LT.-COL. SIR MATTHEW, G.C.M.G. (08), K.C.M.G. (1902), C.M.G. (1899).—B. 1862; d.R.E., 1880; capt., 1889; maj., 1898; lt.-col., 1907; served in Nile expedn., 1885; sec. col. def. tentes., 1895; adm. nat. govt. of S. Leone in 1909; gov., Gold Coast, Oct., 1900; gov., Hong Kong, 21st Sept., 1903; gov., Natal, 1st May, 1907; sec. to G.P.O., London, 1910; chmn. of inland revenue, 1911; under sec. to lord-lieut. of Ireland, 1914; permanent sec. to ministry of pensions, 1916; gov., Queensland, 1920.

NATTLE, HAROLD RUNDLE FITZ.—B. 1875; d. offr., Basutoland, 1904.

NATTLE, WILLIAM ROBERT.—B. 1871; med., Basutoland, 1896.

NAYARATNAM, SARAVANAMUTTU SAMUEL.—1894; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Dec., 1921; sec., Matare Kach., Dec., 1921; ditto, Ratnapura sch., May, 1922; extra office astt. to govt. agt., v. of Sabaragamuwa, Sept., 1923.

NAYLOR, HERBERT WILLIAM LETTS, O.B.E. (30).—B. 1873; ed. King's Schil., Canterbury, R.N. Coll., Greenwich; Admiralty presenta- sword, 1893; R.M.L.I.; entd. crown agents' corp., 1898; astt. head of gen. stores dept., 1903; head of shipping dept., 1912; head of insurance and checking dept., 1917; on loan to Office and Miny. of Munitions, 1914-19; dir. of raw materials, 1918; astt. contr. of age, 1918; head of shipping dept., 1st Jan., 1922; Chevalier de l'Ordre de la Couronne (Belgium).

NEALE, HAROLD BERNARD.—Second clk. to comsrr., Southern div., Bech. Prot., June, 1919; 2nd clk. to astt. comsrr., Northern Prot.; ed. Cape civ. ser. lower law exam., 1911; 1912; astt. res. mag., 1913; sub-instr. h. Prot. pol., 1914; astt. res. mag., 1914; listed local rank of capt.; res. mag., 1921; 3rd grade Seawana exam., 1921.

NEILL, J. H.—Med. offr., E. Africa Prot., 1919; ditto, Uganda, July, 1920.

NEILL, JAMES SCOTT, B.A., Barrister-at- —B. 1889; ed. Trinity Coll., Dublin, clas. ll., 1911; 1st sen. mod. hist. and pol. sci., 2; Victoria prizeman, Kings Inns., Dublin; Fij., 1914; clk., leg. and exec. coun., 1915; dist. comsrr., 1916; repr. sup. off., recr., 1922; ag. atty. gen. and mem. leg. coun., July, 1922 to July, 1923; prin. astl. col. sec. and agt. gen., immigr., 1924; mem., bd. examrs., Fijian language ag. editor, Indian newspaper "Rajput"; founded sp. duty under Tongan govt. and apptd. privy coun. of Tonga, Aug.-Sept., 1924.

NELSON, BISHOP OF, RIGHT REV. WILLIAM CHARLES SADLER, M.A., D.D. of London; ed. Univ. of Melbourne; B.A. (Trin.), 1894; M.A. 1896; Univ. of London, 1903; London, 1909; deanon, 1891; priest, 1892, bourne; C.F., 1896; formerly curate of amid Hill, 1891-1892; St. Paul's, Bendigo, 1892-99; incumbent of Holy Trinity, East Melbourne, 1899-1904; lecturer, St. John's Coll., bourne, 1907-1910; canon of Melbourne cathedral, 1901; examining chaplain to Bishop of Bendigo and Gippsland, 1902; vicar of Christ-ch., St. Kilda, Melbourne, 1904; lecturer, Ley College, Melbourne, 1910; consecrated bishop of Nelson, N.Z., 21st July, 1912.

NETTLETON, GERALD ENRAGHT.—Clt., res. snr.'s office, 1914; sub-instr., Bechuana land pol., 1917; sp. J.P., 1917; astt. res. ass., 1920; passed 1st grade Seawana exam., 1920; passed civ. serv. lower law exam., 1922; ag. res. mag., 1923; res. mag. and hon. inspr. Bech. Prot. pol., Apr., 1924.

NETTLETON, SIR SYDNEY CHARLES KING FARLOW, KT. BACH. (1924).—Ed. Harrow and Trin. Coll., Oxford; B.A. class hon., 1887; M.A., 1889; called to the bar, Middle Temple, 1889; went S.E. circuit and Sussex sessions; puisne judge, high ct., Uganda, 1912; ag. chief just., 1913; judge of ct. of appeal for E. Africa, 1912-14; puisne judge, sup. ct., Gold Coast, Feb., 1915; ag. chief just., S. Leone, May to Aug., 1919, and of G. Coast, June-Oct., 1921; senior puisne judge, G. Coast, Mar., 1920; ch. just., Bahamas, 30th Nov., 1922; pres., reformatory and indus. schls. comsrr., 1923; ch. just., Cyprus, Dec., 1924, author of "Some Gold Coast Judgments, 1915-17"; "The Massai Case, 1913"; "The Law Affecting a Company Prospectus"; parly. candidate, Sheffield (Attercliffe), 1909-10; South Hackney, 1910.

NEWBOLT, CAPT. A. F.—B. 1893; ed. Winchester and New Coll., Oxford; B.A.; on active serv., Oxfordshire Light Inf'y., Aug., 1914 to May, 1919; served in Flanders, wounded, Apr., 1915; capt., 1915; adjt., 1918-19; astt. priv. sec. (appts.) to S. of S., Lord Milner, May, 1919; Mr. Winston Churchill, Feb., 1921; Duke of Devonshire, Oct., 1922; Mr. J. H. Thomas, Jan., 1924; Mr. L. C. M. S. Amery, Nov., 1924.

NEWBOULT, ALEXANDER THEODORE, M.C.—B. 1896; ed. Oakham, Kingwood, and Exeter Coll., Oxford; European War, R. Naval Divn., "Hawke En." and O.C.L.I., served in Gallipoli and France, 1914-19; cadet, M.C.S., Nov., 1920; astt. sec. to rea., July, 1921; 2nd lieut., M.V.I., Aug., 1921; capt., May, 1923; astt. dist. offr., Larut, Feb., 1924; astt. dist. offr., Brusas, June, 1924.

NEWCOMBE, EDMUND LESLIE.—C.M.G. (1909).—Grad. in arts of Univ. of Dalhousie Coll.; LL.B., Univ. of Halifax; called to the bar Nova Scotia, Jan., 1883; Ontario, Dec., 1893; Q.C., Nov., 1893; reprsentive of govt. of Canada to confer with H.M.'s govt. on Canadian copyright, 1894; comsrr. for revision of statutes of Canada, 1902-06; dep. min. of just. of Canada, Mar., 1898; has represented the Dominion on various constitutional questions before the privy coun.; judge, sup. ct., Canada, 1924.

NEWDEGATE, SIR FRANCIS ALEXANDER NEWDEGATE, G.C.M.G. (1925), K.C.M.G. (1917), J.P., D.L.—B. 1862; ed. Eton and R.M.C., Sandhurst; in Coldstream Guards, 1883-85; gov. of Rugby schl.; alderman of the Warwickshire county coun.; M.P. for Nuneaton division of Warwickshire, 1892-1906; M.P. for Tamworth division of Warwickshire, 1909; gov., Tasmania, 30th Mar., 1917; gov., W. Australia, 1920; ret., 1924.

NEWITT, CAPT. A. N.—European pilot, E. Africa Prot., May, 1918.

NEWLANDS, HARRY SCOTT.—B. 1884; ed. Edin. Acad. and Edin. Univ.; writer to the signet; astt. dist. comsrr., G. Coast, 27th July, 1910; dist. comsrr., 18th May, 1914; attached to Togoland field force, 8th Aug. to 30th Sept., 1914; ag. senr. astt. col. sec., 3rd May to 1st July, 1915; priv. sec. to ag. gov., 6th May to 18th Nov., 1915; and from 3rd Mar. to 25th Apr., 1917; priv. sec. to gov., 26th Apr., 1917; sec. to offr. comdgs., Br. Forces, Togoland, Apr., 1918 to June, 1919; seconded on sp. duty to Nigeria, July to Nov., 1920.
NEWLANDS, HON. HENRY WILLIAM, K.C.—B. 1862; ed. pub. schls., Nova Scotia; called to the bar, 1883; inspr. of land titles offices, N.W.T., 1897 to 1902; legal adviser of Yukon coun., 1902 to 1904; K.C., 1903; judge of sup. ct., N.W.T., Jan., 1904; judge of sup. ct., Sask., 1907; lieut.-gov., Sask., 17th Feb., 1921.

NEWMAN, HUBERT ERNEST.—B. 1886; ed. St. John's Coll., Oxford (B.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1909; office ast. to govt. agt., Uva, Nov., 1911; pol. mag., Matale, Mar., 1913; landing survr., Colombo customs, Oct., 1913; agt. comsrr. of requests, Colombo, Feb., 1920; ast. govt. agt., Colombo, May, 1920; chmn., munic. coun., Colombo, Aug., 1924.

NEWTON, SIR FRANCIS JAMES, K.C.M.G. (1919), C.M.G. (1892), C.V.O. (1911).—B. 1857; ed. at Rugby and Univ. Coll., Oxon.; B.A., 1880; M.A., 1890; barrister, Inner Temple; lieut., 3rd batt., Hampshire regt., and extra A.D.C. to Sir H. Robinson, gov. Cape, 1881; priv. sec. to Sir Thomas Scanlen, prime minister of Cape, 1883; and to Sir H. Robinson, 1884-86; sec. to Mauritius roy. comsrr., 1886; agt. admstr. and ch. mag., Br. Bechuana land, 1888; col. sec. and rec-gen., 1889; agt. admstr. and ch. mag., 1892; res. comsrr., Bechuana land Protectorate, Dec., 1895-7; col. sec., Br. Honduras, 1898; ditto, Barbados, 1901; treas., S. Rhodesia, 1903; ret., 1919; col. sec., 1st S. Rhodesian ministry, 1st Oct., 1923; high comsrr. for S. Rhodesia in London.

NEWTON, HENRY HIBBERT.—B. 1861; entd. law dept., Victoria, 1880; joined staff of legis. assom., 1884; clk. ast., 1902; clk. of legis. assom., 1910; and clk. of parlms.

NEWTON, T. C.—Ast. res., N. Nigeria, 19th Dec., 1906.

NIBLOCK-STUART, J. H.—Treasy. ast., Kenya, Jan., 1917; senr. ast. treas., Nov., 1923.

NICHOL, WALTER CAMERON.—B. 1866; journalist, "Spectator," Hamilton, 1881; Toronto "News" and Toronto "Saturday Night"; editor, Hamilton "Herald," 1888-96; "News," London, Ont., 1896-97; editor, Vancouver "Daily Province," 1898; proprietor and editor-in-ch., 1900; lieut.-gov. of British Columbia, 1921.

NICHOLLS, HENRY ALFRED ALFORD, C.M.G. (1896), M.B. (Honours), C.M. (1873), M.D. Abdn. (1875); M.R.C.S. Eng., F.L.S. and C.M.Z.S. B. 1851; corresp. mem. N. York Acad. of Sci., Jamaica Inst., centl. agric. bd. of Trinidad and chamber of agric. of Guadeloupe; hon. mem. Roy. Agric. and Com. Soc. of Br. Guiana; Crown nominee in legis. assom. of Dominica, 1875-7; med. supt. of Dominica Yaws Hosp., 1877; surg., Roseau Infirm., 1879; med. offr., pub. instituta, 1880; chmn., poor law bd., 1885-91; local comsrr., Col. and Ind. Exhib., 1886; agt. curator, Dominica Bot. Station, May to Oct., 1890; gained prize of 100l. for best text book of tropical agriculture offered by the govt. of Jamaica, 1890; special comsrr. to inquire into prevalence of Yaws in W. Indies, 1891, for report on which (pub. as Blue Book) recd. thanks of S. of S., 1894; J.P., 1896; chmn. of the town bd. of Roseau, 1896-98; hith. offr. of Dominica, 1897; offl. mem. of legis. coun., 1898; represented Leeward Is. at W. Indian agric. confce. in Barbados, 1899, 1901 and 1902; sen. med. offr., Dominica, 1904; rep. Leeward Is. at W. Indian quarantine confce. in Barbados, 1904, and at W. Indian agric. confce. in Trinidad, 1905; chmn., permanent exhib. comttee., 1906; trustee, free library, 1910; chmn., bd. of dirs. of Victoria museum, 1910; pres. of legis. coun., Dominica, 23rd Feb., 1911; mem. exec. coun., 1914; dir. of coronation celebrations comttee., 1911; comsrr. for Dominica rubber and tropical products in London, 1914; represented Dominica at internat. congresses on trop. agric., London, 1914; represented Leeward Is. at Imperial health gress, London, 1914; mem. food prices com., 1914; chmn., roads enquiry comn., 1918; chmn. quarantine bd., 1919; admstr. govt. of Dominica Feb.-June, 1919, Oct., 1919 to May, 3 Feb., 1921, Mar.-Apr., 1922 and Mar., 1923; offl. mem. exec. coun., Leeward Is.; prin. med. offr., Dominica, 1922.

NICHOLLS, HON. SIR HERBERT, Kt. (1916).—B. 1868; LL.B., Tasmania; admstr. the bar, 1892; atty.-gen. and min. of justice, Tasmania, 1903-4; puisne judge, Tasmania, 1909; chief justice, 1914.

NICHOLLS, LUCIUS.—B. 1884; L.S.A., M.D., B.C., B.A. Cantab.; pathologist to victoria hosp. soc'y, and bacteriologist to postgrad. schl. of clinical med., 1907-8; stationed in India, 1909-12, as bacteriologist to pt. St. Lucia and surg. to Victoria hosp. in Africa, 1913-15; dir., bact. institute, Oct., 1915; ag. med. supt. lun. asylum, addition to his own duties, May, 1916 to Feb., 1917.

NICHOLS, JAMES EDWARD.—B. 1868; engrnr., Lagos rly., Feb., 1907; ast. engnr., Coast rlys. (open lines), May, 1911; charge, Togoland Mily. rly., 1916-17; charge, G. Coast rlys., Jan., 1920.

NICHOLSON, BERTRAM, C.B.E. (1921), M.C. (1917).—B. 1875; Anglo-Egyptian, 1899-1901; served six years in Natal as sub-native comsrr., Hlatikulu, Swaziland, 1902 to Mar., 1907; ast. res. mag. Hlatikulu and mem. spec. crim. ct., Dec., 1904 to Sept., 1907; ast. comsrr., Hlatikulu, 22nd May, 1907; served S.W. African campaign, 1914-15; ast. comsrr. and govt. sec., Swaziland, 1916; mem., Swaziland-Portuguese border, 1920.

NICHOLSON, WILLIAM EWART.—B. 1890; ed., Leeds Grammar Schl., and Univ. of Oxford; jun. supt., educm., Dept. Nga Sept., 1914; attached, Nigeria Regt., instr., arts and crafts, 1st Jan., 1920.

NICHOLSON, LT.-GEN. SIR W. G. (1898); C.B. (1891).—B. 1845; entr. 1868; col., 1891; served in Afghan war (ment. in despatches); Candahar Field force, 1879-80; march to Candahar (dept. major, medal with 3 clasps, bronze dewars Egyptian war, 1882 including Tel-el-Kebir, ols. Osmanieh, Khedive's star); Burma 1886-7, as A.A.G. army headquarters (brevet lieut.-col., medal with clasp); Tindall's divisionary force, 1897-8, as chief of staff (medal with 2 clasps); served in S. Africa as mil. sec. to commdr.-in-chief and transport at headqtrs., 1899-1900 (dept. promoted maj.-gen., medal with five clasps); dir.-gen. of mobilisation and mil. intell., 1901-4; gov. and commdr.-in-chief, Gibraltar.

NICKLE, HON. WILLIAM F., B.A. (1869); ed. private schls., Coll. Inst., Univ. (B.A. 1891) and Osgoode Hall; admstr. bar, 1895; K.C., 1898; alderman of Algoma Ont., 1905-09; trustee, Queen's Univ., Kingston; mem., Ont. legis., 1908-11; H. of C., re-ele. to Ont. legis., at by-el., 1922 and 1923; atty.-gen. in Ferguson admstr., 1923.

NICOLLS, EDWARD HUGH DYNELEY, (1918).—B. 1871; A.M.I.C.E., 2nd cl.
ertif. and bracketed first in All England in geom. nd perspective drawing, Camb. loc. exams., 1886; upt. of pub. wks., Cyprus, May, 1898; 1st dir. ngrnr., Dec., 1898; ag. dir. of pub. wks., Mar., 903; dir. of pub. wks., Jan., 1904; O/o., A.S.C., Cyprus; in addition to own duties, June, 1915, to Nov., 1916; O/o., R.K., from commencement of war to date of leaving Cyprus on appntn.; as ir. of pub. wks., Gold Coast, 22nd Nov., 1918; ranked local and tempy. rank of capt. from 1st July, 1916, to date of leaving Cyprus; ment. in esp.

NIGHTINGALE, Lacy Gamaliel, K.C., B.A., C.L. — Additional legal adviser, atty-gen.'s office, Capetown, Feb., 1903; crown prosecutor, Transvaal West, Apr., 1910; ag. atty-gen., Orange Free State, Dec., 1911, to Jan., 1912; crown prosecutor, Johannesburg, Aug., 1913; law adviser, July, 1914.

NIGHTINGALE, L. M.—B. 1875; ed. Wimbledon Collegiate Schl. and Soham Gram. Schl., Essex; astt. to Mr. W. H. Thomas, M.I.C.E., I.M.I.E., of Westminster, 1892 to 1901; contractors' engrnr., Bermuda harbour wks., 1901-906; 3rd cls. offr., lands and mines dept., B. Guiana, 1908; sworn land surv.; dist. engrnr., Vest Coast, Demerara, Jan., 1915.

NIHILL, J. H. B., M.A.—B. 1892; ed. Emmanuel Coll., Cambridge; barrister-at-law, Inner Temple; investigating ffr., Min. of Lab., joint industrial couns. divn., 919; priv. sec. to Sir Wm. Edge, junr., Lord of reas., 1920-21; cadet, Hong Kong, July, 1921; g. astt. to sec. for Chinese affrs., 1923.

NISBET, HUGH ADAIR.—B. 1873; ed. at Winchester Coll.; served in S. African war (Queen's medal and two clasps); pub. prosecutor, Transvaal, 1902; astt. res. mag., Transvaal, 903; pol. mag. and regiar. of supreme ct., Grenada, 1907; regiar. of supreme ct., Hong Kong, 1911.

NIXON, Hon. H. C.—B. 1890; farmer; graduate of the Ontario Agric. Coll.; elo. to legis. assembly, Ontario, Oct., 1919; prov. sec., Nov., 919; res., 1923; resigned portfolio on defeat of J.F.O., admistr., 1923.

NIXON, R., M.B., Ch.B. (L'pool), D.T.M. (L'pool), D.P.H. (L'pool),—Tempy. lieut., capt. nd major, R.A.M.C. (S.R.), 1917-19; med. offr. 'anganyika Territory, Oct., 1921.

NOAD, JOHN ELLIOTT MONOBIFF.—Ed. R. Javal Coll., Osborne and Dartmouth and Training Cruiser, H.M.S. "Cornwall"; midshipman, T.N., Aug., 1910; H.M.S. "Prince of Wales" flagship, Atlantic Fleet; resgd., 1911; Edinburgh Univ., Oct., 1911 to Aug., 1914; sub-lieut., T.N.V.R., Aug., 1914 to Nov., 1918; interned in Holland from fall of Antwerp to armistice; while in Holland passed for A.M.I.C.E., Feb., 917; astt. engrnr., P.W.D., Kenya, 6th Mar., 920; ag. exec. engrnr., 5th Apr., 1923; "1914" tar, War and Victory meds.

NOAKS, BENJAMIN.—B. 1866; ed. London nd Cambridge; M.A., 1896; principal Gill Coll., 986; high schl., Queenstown, 1896; inspr. of shls., O.F.S., 1900-08; inspr. of schls., O.R.C., July, 1909.

NOALL, W. E.—B.1880; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civil ser., and assigned to the C.O., June, 1898; promoted, ith gratuity, Jan., 1911; conf. clk., 1st Mar., 916; minor staff clk., 8th Sept., 1917; sec. to usual int. comte., 1st Jan., 1908.

NOBLE, CRAWFORD, M.B.B. (1919).—B. 1880; I. Aberdeen Univ. (dip. of agr.); astt. prin. forest offr., Cyprus, 1907; ag. prin. forest offr. and dir. of agrl. edn. on several occasions; on active serv., 1915-19; ag. inspr., fisheries, Jan. to Apr., 1921; ag. astt. island postmr., July, 1920 to Apr., 1921; ag. dir., agr., May, 1923 to Dec., 1924; dir. of agr., Jan., 1925.

NOBLE, PETER, A.M.I.C.E.—Ed. Elgin and Aberdeen, Scotland; astt. civ. engrnr., P.W.D., Cyprus, 1906; ag. dist. engrnr. in 1907 and 1909; dist. engrnr., Demerara, B. Guiana, Aug., 1910; ag. in addition as chief draughtsman, 1911, and as astt. col. civ. engrnr. in 1912; ool. engrnr. and surrv. gen., Dominica, Aug., 1912; nom. mem., Roseau Town Board, offi. mem. legis. coun. and road board; on war service as mem. commrs. of valuation (min. of munitions); reed. thanks of sec. of state for work in connection with roads of Dominica, 1916.

NOBLE, ROBERT EMILY.—Ed. Beaumont Coll.; called to the bar (Inner Temple) Nov., 1896; mag., Br. E. Africa, Feb., 1906; legal astt., Windward Is., St. Vincent, 1908; ag. atty-gen., 1910; ag. ch. just., 1912; res. mag., Jamaica, 1918-23; 1st puisne judge, Leeward Is., Nov., 1923; ag. ch. just., Leeward Is., June, 1924.

NOOTT, P. GORDON.—B. 1880; entered army (Royal Welsh Fus.), 1898; served in Boer war, 1899-00 (Queen's medal with clasp); Tugela heights, relief of Ladysmith, Cape Colony, Orange Free State and Transvaal; seconded for serv., N. Nigeria regt., Dec., 1904; served with Dakka Kerri expdn., N. Nigeria, 1908; ret. on pension, Oct., 1913; ch. warder, Belize prison, B. Honduras, May, 1914; coman. 2nd lieut., B. Honduras Terr. Force, 1914; lieut., 1916 served on Cayo expdn., B. Honduras, 1916; instructor to 2nd B. Honduras contingent, 1916; capt., 1918; supt. of prisons, Grenada, Jan., 1920.

NORMAN, HENRY.—B. 1877; ed. at Oakham and Magdalen Coll., Oxon.; cadet, F.M.S., Nov., 1899; passed cadet, Apr., 1902; ag. astt. dist. offr., Raub, Jan., 1903; astt. dist. offr., Serendah, Jan., 1904; ag. astt. dist. offr., Raub, Jan., 1904; ag. dist. offr., Raub, Apr., 1904; ag. astt. dist. offr., Raub, Sept., 1904; ag. astt. dist. offr., Matang, Oct. to Dec., 1904; ag. dist. offr., Kuala Langat, Mar. to Nov., 1905; ditto. Jan. to Mar., 1907; dist. offr., Temerloh, but cont. to act as dist. offr., Kuala Langat, May, 1907 to June, 1910; ag. astt. dist. offr., Kuala Kangsar, Dec., 1910; offr. of cls. IV., S. Stiltna., but remained in the F.M.S., Aug., 1911; ag. chmn. and sec., sanitary bd., Kinta, South, Aug., 1911; ag. ch. astt. dist. offr., Kinta, Jan., 1913 officiating as astt. dist. offr., Kampar, and chmn., sanitary bd., Batu Cajah, Copeng, and Kampar, F.M.S., June, 1913; ag. astt. to res., Malacca, Nov., 1914; lent to Kelantan govt., July, 1915; lent to Johore govt., Dec., 1917; supernmy. offr., cls. II., S. Stiltna., Jan., 1919; astt. adviser to the govt. of Kedah, Apr., 1921.

NORRIS, CAPT. ALEXANDER WOODBURN.—B. 1879; ed. in Germany, Belgium and at Bedford; oomsn. 49th Foot, 1900; seconded, Gold Coast Regt., 1901-06; R. of O., 1906; astt. dist. comsn., Gold Coast, Apr., 1911; dist. comsn., Feb., 1916; dep. prov. comsn., Apr., 1923; attd., G.C.R., Apr., 1917; ag. prov. comsn., W. Prov., G. Coast, Aug., 1923-Mar., 1924; ag. prov. comsn., W. Prov., Asante, Mar., 1924.

NORRIS, C. G.—B. 1890; ed. St. Catherine's Coll., Cambridge; B.A.; cadet, Solomon Islands, Jan., 1915.
NORRIS, J. A.—B. 1872; ed. Ballygan and Williamstown, Ireland; acc't to treas'y, Victoria, 17th Mar., 1914; audr.-gen., 1st Mar., 1919.

NORTH, ROLAND ARTHUR CHARLIE.—B. 1889; ed. Blundell's and Balliol Coll., Oxford; apptd. cadet, Hong Kong civil serv., 16th Nov., 1912; asst. cable censor, 1914; passed Cantonese, Feb., 1915; ag. 3rd asst. to sec. for Chinese affairs, 1915; in charge of pass offic, 1915; ag. 1st clk., pol. magistracy, in addition to other duties, Mar., 1916; ag. asst. dist. offr., South, 1919; passed in Japanese, 1919; ag. priv. sec. to the O.A.G., 1919 and 1921; ag. 2nd asst. col. sec. and ag. priv. sec. to gov. in addn., 1921; seconded to Samoa as asst. commr. of Chinese affrs., 1921 to 1922; studied Japanese in Japan, 1922; ag. asst. to sec. for Chinese affrs., 1923; ag. ch. asst. to sec. for Chinese affrs., 1924.

NORTHCOTE, GEOFFREY ALEXANDER STAFFORD.—Ed. at Blundell's Schl. and Balliol Coll., Oxford; B.A. (honours); and Newte and Huish exhibs.; asst. collr., E. Africa Prot., 27th May, 1904; ag. collr. and ag. dist. commnr., S. Kavirondo, 1904-06; polit. offr., Kiati Patrol, 1906; polit. offr., sleeping sickness commn., 1908-09; dist. commnr., 1909; in charge, Kikuyu Prov., 1911; ag. prov. commnr., May to Oct., 1919; ag. asst. col. sec., Oct., 1919 to July, 1920; asst. col. sec., Apr., 1921; ag. col. sec., July to Sept., 1921, Aug. to Sept., 1922 and Mar. to Sept., 1923; gov.'s dep. July to Aug., 1923; mem., legis. com., 1923.

NORTHCOTE, MAJOR LEONARD AUGUSTUS STAFFORD.—B. 1879; ed. Dulwich Coll.; 2nd lieut., Royal Fusiliers, 1900; res. of offrs., Feb., 1914; served in Gallipoli, Egypt, Salonika and Palestine, 1914-19; local commt. of pol. and asst. commr., Cyprus, 1919; passed exam. in mod. Greek; ag. commr., June to Oct., 1924.

NORTHCOTE, R. C.—Rhodesian admtn., B.S.A. pol., 1914-16; Rhodesian Native Regt., 1917-19; German E. Africa campaign (ment. in desp., mily. med.); asst. polit. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 13th Feb., 1921.

NORTHCROFT, LESLIE ARTHUR, B.A. (Can-tab).—B. 1901; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Dec., 1923; attd. to secretariat, Jan., 1924.

NORTHEY, MAJOR-GENERAL SIR EDWARD, K.C.M.G. (1918), C.B.—B. 1868; served with Hazara expdn., 1891; Miranzai expdn., 1891; Isazai expdn., 1892; in S. African war, 1899-02; and in the war of 1914-18; extra A.D.C. to H.M. the King, 1915; brig.-gen. (temp.) commdg. Nyasaland Rhodesia field force, 1915-18; lieut.-col. (brevet col.), 1915; King's R.R.C., 1911; gov. E. Africa Prot. and high commnr., Zanzibar Prot., 15th July, 1918; assumed govt., 31st Jan., 1919; ret., Aug., 1922.

NORTH-HUNT, HAROLD.—B. 1894; ed. Ipswich Schl. and St. Catherine's Coll., Camb. (exhbr.); war serv., Oct., 1914-Feb., 1920, 8th Batt. Manchester Regt., and Territorials; asst. to colonel-in-charge of R.E. Records, Chatham; capt., 1st Jan., 1918; ment. in desp., Mar., 1918; cadet, F.M.S., Mar., 1920; 2nd asst. dist. offr., Kula Kubu, July, 1920; asst. dist. offr., Rembau, Jan., 1921; passed cadet, Jan., 1922; 2nd asst. adviser, Batu Pahat, Johore, Apr., 1922; ag. asst. adviser, Kota Tinggi, Nov., 1923.

NORTON, HENRY JOHN STEPHEN.—Cler asst., Gibraltar, 1913; crane and wharf clk., 1914; treas. clk., 1914; passed compet. exam., 1917; clk.-in-charge, impta. and expts., and clk. to food contr., 1914 to 1920; dep. asst. shipping master, 1921; asst. shipping master, 1922; sec. and treas., sailors' home, 1920.

NORTON, THEODORE WALTER CECIL.—B. 1871; clk. to res. mag., Ngamakwe, Jan., 1891; asst. mag., Ngamakwe, Sept., 1892; Umtata Oct., 1899; res. mag., Tabankulu, Mar., 1902; Port St. John's, Aug., 1904; Engoobo, Jan., 1906; Butterworth, Feb., 1916; ag. res. mag., Umtata, and asst. ch. mag., Transkeian Territories, Aug., 1919; res. mag., Umtata as asst. ch. mag., Transkeian Territories, Sept., 1920; ag. ch. nat. commnr., Cape, Apr., 1923; ag. ch. nat. commnr., Cape, Apr., 1923.

NORTON-TRAILL, HENRY LIONEL (former Smith), F.R.G.S., F.S.A. (Scotland).—Capt. H.L.I.; late lieut. 36th L.Y., S. African fed. force; S. African War medal and 2 clasps; res., N. Nigeria, 1904; served as polit. offr. on expedn. against Lakai cannibals, 1905; on expedn. against Munchi tribes, 1906; 3rd cl. 1911; author of "Armourials of the County of Orkney."

NORWOOD, LEONARD ROBERT OSWALD.—B. 1896; ed. Lincoln Coll., Oxford; sup't, educ. dept., N. Provs., Nigeria, 2nd Nov., 1921.

NOSWORTHY, RICHARD.—Ed. Christ's Hosp., ent. Jamaica civ. service, 1880; held app't various dept.; 1st cls. clk., col. secretariat, 1895; sec., bd. of supervision for poor relief, 1905; supervisor of rev. and valuation commnr., 1907; ag. collr. gen. and contr., widow's and orphan fund; chmn., marine bd. on several occasions; asst. col. sec., 1918; ag. col. sec., 1921; clk., treas. and man., gov't savings bank, 1921; clk., agrl. loan bd., chmn., currency commnr., nat. civ. service guarantee assn.; sent to America to conclude purchase of Jamaica gov't rly. bond, 1912, and as mem. of banana comm., 1915; censor, 1915-19; ag. adminstr., Dominica, 1921.

NOSWORTHY, HON. WILLIAM.—B. 1867; ed. privately and at Boys High Schl., Christchurch, N.Z.; mem. of N.Z. parlmt. since 1894; whip for reform party and later sen. whip; sen. whip for Nat. govt.; min. of agric., 1919; min. of immigr., 1920.

NOVA SCOTIA, BISHOP OF, RIGHT HON. CLARENCE LAMB WORRELL, M.A., D.C.L., D.D.; B. 1863; headmaster, Gananoque schl., 1879; ditto, Brockville coll. inst., 1879; curate, Gananoque, 1881; Brockville, 1882; rector, Morrisburg, 1884; ditto, St. Mark's, Barrie, 1891; prof. of English, R.M.C., Kingston, 1891; man. chap., Bishop of Ontario, 1896; sec. deacon of Ontario, 1900; rector, St. Luke's, Kingston, 1903; consecrated Bishop of Nova Scotia, 1904; prolocutor, prov. synod of Canada, 1904; metropolitan and archbishop of Nova Scotia, 1915.

NOVAR, VISCOUNT (cr. 1921), RIGHT HON. RONALD CRAUFORD MUNBO-FERGUSON, P.C., G.C.M.G. (1914).—B. 1860; Hon. LL.D. of St. Andrew's 1910; ed. Sandhurst; late lieut., Grenadier Guards; M.P. for Ross and Cromarty, 1882-85; Leith Burghs, 1896-1914; priv. sec. to Lord Rosebery, 1886 and 1893-95; lord of the treasury, 1894; provost of Kirkcaldy, 1906-1914; vice-lieutenant of Fife; was a referee of Bills; gov. gen. C. of A., 1914-20; sec. for Scotland, Oct., 1920 to Jan., 1924.

NUGENT, GEORGE OLIVER.—2nd clk., sec. of office, Leeward Ialda, Nov., 1893; ag. clk., Dec., 1894, to June, 1895; on reorganisation of office became 3rd clk., Apr., 1897; ag. clk. and ex. co., Apr. to Dec., 1897, and Jan., 1899, to Aug., 1900; ag. clk., and clk., fed. and leg. co., and Antigua leg. co., Aug., 1900; ag. priv. sec., Dec., 1897, to Jan., 1898; Jan.,
OAKES, MONTAGUE WADDINGTON, B.A.—B. 1889; ed. Haileybury Coll., and Emmanuel Coll., Cambridge; junr. supt., dept. N. Nigeria, 3rd Dec., 1913; attd., Nigeria Regt., 1914 and 1917-18.

OBERLANDER, C. F. A., M.B., Ch.B. (Edin.).—B. 1871; ed. Victoria Coll., Stellenbosch, and Univ. of Edinburgh; major, S.A.M.C.; D.M.O., No. 1 gen. hosp., Wynberg, 1916-20; med. inspr. schls., O.F.S., July, 1920.

O'BRIEN, ANDREW, S.M.—B. 1873; indentured clk., publ. hosp., Bahamas, June, 1889; 3rd clk. gen. post off., March, 1893; clk. registrar of records dept., March, 1897; customs off., Apr., 1901; ag. res. just. and rev. offr., Ragged Is., Feb. to May, 1902; ditto, Rum Cay, June to Dec., 1902; clk., police ct., Jan., 1903; res. just., Ragged Island, July, 1903; res. just., San Salvador, July, 1906; Out Island commr. (3rd div.), 1909; 1st divn. commr., 11th Sept., 1922.

O'BRIEN, LT.-COL., SUB, C.R.M., C.M.C.G. (C.M.G.)—B. 1859; ed. Felsted, on the Continent, and Royal Military Coll. (passed out with honours); entrd. Army as 2nd lieut., 1878; lieut., 1880; capt., 1887; maj., 1897; brev.-lt.-col., 1902; 2nd in command of 1st E. Lancs. regt., 30th Oct., 1902; served in India from 1890 to 1895; retrd. on pension in order to remain under C.O., 4th Mar., 1903; served in S. African War, Jan., 1900, to end of campaign; pres. of mil. tribunal, 1900-1901; S. African War medal and 3 clasps, King's medal and 2 clasps (twice mentioned in despatches); senior dep. commr. Transvaal town pol., J.P. for the Witwatersrand, and in charge of mtd. pol., 1st May, 1901; in charge of martial law arrangements, Johannesburg and Rand, and personal asst. to commr., 1st May, 1901, to Mar., 1902; ag. commr., Transvaal town pol., and J.P. for Transvaal, 6th May to 8th Nov., 1904; deputy commr., headqrs., Transvaal town pol., Oct., 1906, to 30th June, 1908; ag. commr., Transvaal town pol., and J.P. for Transvaal, 1st Jan. to 22nd July, 1907; deputy commr., Transvaal town pol.; retired, 1908; col. sec., Gambia, 8th Jan., 1910; ag. gov., Gambia, 6th July to 10th Dec., 1910, 18th Aug. to 18th Dec., 1911, and from 17th Aug. to 25th Oct., 1912; gov., Seychelles, 7th Nov., 1912; gov., Barbados, 1st June, 1918; assumed govt., 27th Sept., 1918.

O'BYRNE, HUGH MORGAN.—Chief of customs, Somaliland Prot., 22nd Feb., 1901; registr. of shipping, 6th Mar., 1905; specially commended by S. of S. on two occasions; brought to notice of govt. for sea-transport and harbour work by Gen. Sir C. Egerton in his despatch on Somaliland campaign, 1902-4; G.A.S. medal and clasp, Somaliland, 1902-1904; recd. thanks of army council for assistance in compilation of military report on Somaliland, 1907; clasp, G.A.S. medal, Somaliland, 1908-1910.

O'CONNOR, CHARLES ANTHONY.—B. 1883; ed. Royal Coll., Mauritius; supt., Reduit gardens and plantations, forests and gardens dept., Mauritius, 5th Sept., 1904; ch. overseer, dept. of agr., 19th Aug., 1913; enlisted, 2nd Artists' Rifles, 9th Aug., 1917; recd. commr., Royal Munster Fus., 29th Sept., 1918; inspr. of plantations, Zanzibar Prot., 25th Aug., 1919; agrl. instr. and impr., co-op. credit societies, Mauritius, 22nd Jan., 1923.

O'CONNOR, HUGH JOSEPH, F.Z.S.—B. 1887; Lieut., Gambia Artillery (V.), 1910; mem. of navigation and pilotage board, Gambia, 1914; asst. commr. of police, G. Coast, Jan., 1916; ag. staff instructor, Mar., 1916, and June, 1918; ag.
commr. of police for various periods in 1917, 1921 and 1922; O.C. Togoland mil. police, and O.C. Togoland prisons, 19th Aug., 1919; capt., G. Coast Rifles, 1922; commr. of police, 12th Jan., 1923.

O'GRADY, Capt. Sir James, K.C.M.G. (1924), O.B.E. (1919), J.P.—B. 1866; mem., town coun., Bristol, 1897-99; M.P., E. Leeds, 1906; S.R. Leeds, 1913-24; with troops in various theatres of war, 1915-18; sent by govt. on sp. mission to Russia, 1917; negotiated with Russian Soviet govt. exchange of Br. prisoners of war and repatriation of Br. civilians in Russia, Nov., 1919; gov. of Tasmania, 4th Nov., 1924; assumed govt., 23rd Dec., 1924.

O'HALLORAN, GEORGE FINLEY, B.A., B.C.L.—B. 1862; graduate in arts of McGill Univ., 1883; grad. in law, 1886; called to the bar of prov. of Quebec, 1886; dep. min. of agric., and dep. commr. of patents of Canada, 1902; resigned as dep. min. of agric., 1918; now commr. of patents.

O'HARA, FRANCIS CHARLES TRENCH.—B. 1870; priv. sec. to min. of trade and commerce, Canada, 1897; 1st cls. clk., 1902; ch. clk., 1903; supt. of trade commr. serv., 1904; ch. controller of Chinese immigr., 1908-11; dep. min. of trade and commerce, 1908; mem. ships license comtee., 1916-17; war trade comtee., 1916-17; local offr. for Canada, Dominions Royal Coms. tours, 1914 and 1917; priority authority for Canada, assisting ministry of munitions, 1916-17; offr.-in-charge all industrial diamond imports under the diamond export comtee., 1915-17; mem., editorial comtee. on govt. publs., 1917; dep. commr. of patents, 1918; chmn., Canadian trade commr., 1920.

OLDFIELD, H. G.—Tempy. asst. dist. commr., E. Africa Prot., June, 1919.

OLIVER, Geo. A.—B. 1898; ent. G.P.O., Dec., 1914; apptd. asst. clk., Apr., 1916; wireless operator, R.N.V.R., Jan., 1917 to Apr., 1919; cler. offr., 1st Jan., 1920; transf. to C.O., June, 1923.

OLIVER, Hon. John.—B. 1856; went to Canada in 1870; settled in Ontario, but removed to British Columbia a few years later where he now possesses considerable land in the Fraser Valley; also engaged in contracting business; unsuccessful cand. for legss ass. in 1909 and 1912; elec. at g.e. 1916 for Dewdney; min. of agric. in Brewster cabinet, 1916; premier, B. Columbia, 1918.

OLIVIER, 1st Baron (created 1924), Rt. Hon. Sir Sydney Olivier, P.C., K.C.M.G. (1907), C.M.G. (1898), B.A.—B. 1859; ed. at Tonbridge schl.; open exhib., Corpus Christi Coll., Oxford; 2nd class classical mods., 1878; 2nd class in final classical schl., 1881; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. in the office of the S. of S. for cols., 17th Apr., 1882; honourably mentioned for Cobden prize essay, Oxford, 1883; ag. col. sec., Br. Honduras, Oct., 1890, to Apr., 1891; ag. auditor-gen., Leeward Is., Oct., 1896, to Feb., 1896; priv. sec. to the Earl of Selborne, Sept., 1896; sec. to the Roy. comsn. apptd. to inquire into condition of the W. Indies, Dec., 1896; 1st class clk., June, 1897; sent to Washington on special service in connection with W. Indian reciprocity negotiations, 1898; col. sec., Jamaica, 1900-1904; ag. gov., 1900, 1902, and 1904; returned to C.O. as a prin. clk., Oct., 1904; gov. of Jamaica, 20th Apr., 1907; assumed govt., 16th May, 1907; represented West Indian Colonies at the Coronation of H.M. King George V., 1911; perm. sec., bd. of agriculture & fisheries, 1913; mem. of comtee. for settim. ex-service men within the Empire, 1917; ast. comptroller and auditor, exchequer and admt. dept., 1917; S. of S. for India, 23rd Jan. to 1st Nov., 1924.

O'MALLEY, Sir Edward Loughlin, K.B.C. (1891).—B. 1842; ed. Trin. Coll., Cam. grad. B.A., 1864; M.A., 1866; joined the r. (Mid. Tem.), 1866; joined Norfolk circuit; gen. of Jamaica, 1876; atty.-gen., Hong kong, Nov., 1879; ch. just., S. Stltns., 1889; 1892; ch. just., Br. Guiana, 1896; judge of El sup. consular ct. for the Ottoman empire, 1896-97; ret. 1904; mem. of Mauritius royal comm.

OMAN, David James, O.B.E. (1924).—Em- master, Accra govt. schl., Gold Coast, 2nd Jan., 1902; acted frequently as inspr. of schls., 1906; inspr. of schls., 1st Jan., 1907; act. dir. of educ., on several occasions, 1907; dir. of educ. and sec. to bd. of educ., 1910-11; capt., Gold Coast Volunteers, 1914; Col. Aux. Offr.'s Decoration, Nov., 1914.

OMMANNEY, Sir Montagu Fenn, G.C.M.G. (1904), K.C.B. (1901), K.C.M.G. (1898), I.S.O. (1893), late capt. R.F. 1842; ed. at Chelt. Coll., and R.M.A., Woolwich, the Roy. Engnrs., Jan., 1864; eng. under the W.O. and admlyt., and at R.M.A. from 1867 to 1874; priv. sec. to Earl of Carnarvon, S. of S. for cols., Mar., 1874, to Jan., 1875, when he was apptd. a Crown agt. for cols.; a commr. for the col. exhib., 1887; mem. roy. comm. for Paris exhibition of 1900; permanent under-S. of S. for the colonies, 1900; ret. Jan., 1907; sec. of the Order of Michael and St. George, July, 1900; Knight of the Order, 1909.

ONGLEY, Frederick Oliver Jones, C.B., R.N., 1875; clk. Cyprus high ct. jnt. commr.'s office, 1879; ch. sec.'s, 1884; 1886; rec.-gen.'s, 1886; passed higher Turkish, 1886; transal. to high commr.'s sect. imp. bank of Persia, 1890; ch. clk., 1890; transal. Ott. land code, 1892; ass't of surv. and prin. for offr., 1892 (now asst. rec.-gen'l. and inspr.); ag. commr., Iraq, 1893; again, and loc. comdt. and commr. ag. asst. to loc. comdt., Nicosia, 1897; ag. genl., 1899; regar.-gen., Cyprus, 1902; 1910; dir., land registries, Palestine, 29th Oct., 1921.

ONRAET, R. H. de S.—Pol. probst., Stltns., Dec., 1907; passed final exam., Hokkien, July, 1910; ag. asst. sup't. of pol., Singapore, Aug., 1910; passed final exam., Malay, Aug., 1911; asst. sup't. of pol., July, 1912; ag. sup't. of pol., Singapore, Jan., 1919; asst. of pol., Singapore, Mar., 1919; ag. sup't. Malacca, Nov., 1919; ag. dir., criminal and gence, Apr., 1921.

O'RILEY, Basil Victor.—B. 1870; ed. customs dept., Port Elizabeth, 1889; ch. of Port Elizabeth, 1908; prin. clk., Cape Town, 1912; ch. clk., Cape Town, 1914; ag. ed. customs and ag. shipping master, Cape Town, 1914; ch. clk., head office, Pretoria, 1915; dep. commr. of customs and excise, Pretoria, 1916; del. to the Imp. Cust. confere., London, 1921.

ORME, G. N.—B. 1878; Ed. Cheltenham and Hertford Coll., Oxford; scholar, B.A., 1901; called to the bar, Inner Temp., 1915; cadet, Hong Kong, 1901; ast. of sanitary bd., 1904; ag. ast. regar.-gen., ag. of sanitary bd., ag. 2nd pol. mag., 1906; ag.
pt. of pol. and pol. mag. for New Territory, 1905; asst. land offr. for N.T., 1908; ag. dep. pt. of pol., 1908; asst. dist. offr. for N.T., outh., 1910; ag. dist. offr. for N.T. (North), 11; asst. dist. offr. for N.T. (North), Apr., 13; ag. 2nd pol. mag., Aug., 1913; head of nitary dept., 1913; attached to crown solicitor's ice, 1915; attached to atty.-gen.'s office, 1916; st. offr., 1917; ag. dir., educn., 1919 and 1924; 1st pol. mag., 1920; ag. offl. recr., etc., 21.

ORMSBY-GORE, HON. WILLIAM GEORGE ARTHUR.—B. 1885; ed. Eton and New Coll., Oxford (B.A.); late capt., Shropshire Yeomanry; teller, officer Arab bureau, 1916-17; asst. sec. ar Cabinet, 1917-18; asst. polit. offr., Palestine, 18; British mem., Permanent Mandates Comm., league of Nations, 1921-22; M.P., Stafford since n., 1910; accompanied C.O. mission to British est Indies, 1921-22; parly. under sec. of state for Colonies, 1st Nov., 1922 to 23rd Jan., 24 and since Nov., 1924; chmn., parly. comm., E. Africa, 1924.

ORPEN, RICH. THEODORE, B.L.—Ed. Trin., Dublin; science scholar, moderator. B.A. th honours in maths. and experimental science; called to the bar, King's Inn, Dublin, Hil. term, 98; pol. mag., S. Nigeria, 1903; ag. y.-gen., Aug., 1903 to Jan., 1904; ag. solr.-a., for various periods in 1908-10; ag. puiana judge, June to Aug., 1905; June to July, 1908 to Dec., 1909; res. mag., Jamaica, June, 10; comsnr., estate duty, offl. receiver and registrar of trade marks, 1921; ag. judge, Kingston, June, 1920 to Feb., 1921; ag. puiana judge, b. to Aug., 1921 and from Nov., 1922 to Sept., 23; judge, Kingston etc., Dec., 1921.

ORR, CHARLES WILLIAM JAMES, C.M.G. (1912).—B. 1870; ed. Bath Coll. and Woolwich Acad.; comm., Royal Artillery, Feb., 1889; capt., pte., 1899; maj., 1904; ret., Sept., 1908, served in Chitral relief force, 1895 (medal with clasp); Indian frontier, 1897 (clasp); Tirah expdn. force, 97-99 (clasp); China war, 1900-01 (medal); S. African war, 1900-02 (medal, 2 clasps); 3rd cls., N. Nigeria, Feb., 1903; 2nd cls. res., 1904; 1st cls. res., 1908; ag. sec. to adminstr., N. Nigeria, May to Sept., 1907; ch. sec., Cyprus, Feb., 1911; minstd. govt., July to Oct., 1911, and Apr. to Apr., 1913; ret. on pension on account of ill. alth., Feb., 1917; attd. W.O., Int. branch, 1918; col. sec., Gibraltar, June, 1919; ag. gov., on several occasions.

ORR, JAMES RUSSELL, O.B.E. (1924).—Director educnt., E.A.P., Moh., 1911.

ORR, HON. THOMAS, C.M.G. (1912).—3rd cls., chan. branch of exchqr. and audit dept., 11th n., 1875; examnr., 2nd sect., 16th Aug., 1885; sec., 31st Jan., 1894; 2nd cls. clk., 2nd sect., 1st June, 1901; auditor-gen., Natal, 16th Aug., 192; ret. 1910; elected to Union parlmt. as L.A. for Pietermaritzburg North; pub. debt mnsmr., 1913; min. of finance, 1918; comsnr., es. and harbours bd., 1920.

OSBORNE, MAJOR D. R.—B. 1879; ed. Prince Alfred Coll., Adelaide, S. Australia; Adelaide Univ. (mental and moral phil.) and riot's Coll., Cambridge; B.A., law; called to bar, Inner Temple, 1909; practiced at bar till 1914; joined Inns of Court O.T.C., Aug., 14; 2nd lieut. 1914; served in France with Northumberland Fus., as major and coy. commdr., 5-17; senr. offrs., schl., Aldershot, Oct.-Dec., 7; 2nd in commd., 9th Northumberland Fus., c. 1917-Apr., 1918; commmdg., 15th R. Scots until the 34th divn. was disbanded; ct. martl. offr., Nov., 1918 to May, 1920; in Ireland as A.L.O. until Apr., 1922; stip. and circuit mag., Bahamas, 25th June, 1923; ag. ch. jnst., 19th Aug. to 15th Sept., 1923 and from 29th July to 10th Nov., 1924; ag. reg.-gen. in addn. 16th June to 28th July, 1924.

OSBORNE, GEORGE HAROLD.—Ed. at Leatherhead and Pembroke Coll., Camb. (scholar); Goldsmith's exhibr.; B.A. (honours) in classics, 1898; S. African War, 1901-1902; medal and 5 clasps; asst. collr., E. Africa Prot., 14th Feb., 1906; dist. commr., 1910.

OSWELL, HENRY THEODORE WARREN.—B. 1896; ed. Dulwich Coll. and Worcester Coll., Oxford; 2nd lieut., 13th batt. Cheshire Regt., Feb., 1915; flying offr. (pilot), R.F.C., June, 1917; lieut., R.F.C., July, 1917; lieut., R.A.F., Apr., 1918; cadet, Malayan civ. serv., 1st Apr., 1920; ag. asst. contr. of lab., Klang, 1st Sept., 1920; ag. asst. dist. offr., Krian, May, 1923.

OTTLEY, Rear-Admiral Sir Charles Langdale, K.C.M.G. (1907); C.B. (1911); M.V.O. (1903).—B. 1858; Peru, 1877; Egypt, 1882; has served as naval attache to maritime cts. at Washington, Tokio, Rome, St. Petersburg, and Paris; dir. of naval intell., 1905-1907; sec. to commr. of Imp. defence, 1907; resig., 1912.

OTWAY, J. H.—Clt., treas., Grenada, 1897; 2nd audit clk., 1899; audit clk., St. Vincent, 1901; audit clk., St. Lucia, Jan., 1916; sub-collector and dist. offr., Soufriere; J.P. for the colony; cable censor, St. Vincent, 1918; chief clk., govt. office, and clk. of councils, St. Vincent, 1918; has held numerous acting appts.

OTWAY, RUPERT COLEBRIDGE, R.E., Res. of Offrs., M.I.S.E. (1924).—B. 1884; clk., P.W.D., Grenada, 1903; land offr., land stlitm. scheme, and pub. wks. offr., Carriacou, 5th Oct., 1906; ward. of the Windward dist., St. Vincent, in charge of pub. wks., 1st July, 1908; offr. in charge of inauguration of land stlitm. scheme, Union Is., St. Vincent Grenadines, 1st June, 1910 to 30th Sept., 1911; ag. ward., Leewards dist., St. Vincent, and local head of the P.W.D., St. Vincent; joined Imp. army, 1st July, 1917; lieut., Royal Engnr., 16th Dec., 1917 to 23rd Oct., 1919; inspr., wks. and roads, Montserrat, 26th Feb., 1920; mem., exec. coun., Montserrat, 2nd May, 1922; mem., leg. coun., Montserrat, Dec., 1922; ag. comsnr., 14th Aug. to 5th Sept., 1924.

OWEN, A. H., B.A. (Camb.), M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), D.T.M. and H. (Camb.), Cert. of S.T.M. (Lond.)—Med. offr., Uganda, Oct., 1912; sp. serv., (venereal diseases), Uganda, 1912; active serv., E.A. Campaign, and tempy. capt., U.M.S., Jan., 1915 to May, 1918; ment. in depts.; senr. med. offr., Uganda, Jan., 1921; ch. sanitation offr., Tanganyika Territory, 1922.

OWEN, GEORGE DOUGLAS.—B. 1887; entd. civ. ser., Trinidad, 16th Jan., 1907; 3rd clk., col.-sec.'s office, Aug., 1915; ag. 2nd and conf. clk., Oct., 1915 to May, 1916; asst. sec., local defence comm., 1914-1915; ag. sec., ditto, 1915-1916; sec. to educn. comm., June, 1914 to Nov., 1916; sec., West Indian Court of Appeal Confe., 1916; priv. sec. to Sir S. W. Knagge in 1910, 1912 and 1916; to Sir G. R. Le Hunte, 1913-1915; to Sir J. R. Chancellor, 1916, 1920 and 1921; served with H.M. Forces, 1916-19; ch. and conf. clk., col. secretariat, and clk. of legn. coun., 1st May, 1920; priv. sec. to Mr. T. A. V. Best, 1921 and to Sir S. Wilson, 1922; ag. 2nd asst. col. sec. for several periods since 1921.
OWEN, HAROLD ALBERT.—B. 1892; entd. crown agt.'s office, Dec., 1911; seconded as 3rd elk., col. sec.'s office, Antigua, July, 1916; sec. to comnr. of enquiry into condition of St. John's fire brigade, Nov., 1916; returned to crown agt.'s office, Sept., 1919.

OWEN-SMITH, GILBERT, I.S.O., (1923).—B. 1888; entd. Cape olv. serv. (customs dept.), 1888; passed civ. law exam., 1896; sec. tariff comtee., Bloemfontein customs confce., 1903; sec., Cape customs tariff comsn., 1906; customs adviser, Pietermaritzburg customs confce., 1906; ditto, Pretoria and Capetown confce., 1906; sec., commerce and industries comsn., 1910; dep. comsnr. of customs and excise, Union of S. Africa, Aug., 1914; comsnr. to enquire into prices of foodstuffs, etc., 1916; comsnr. of customs and excise, 1918; mem., advisory comtee. on control of food supplies, etc., 1918; contrlr., imports and exports, 1919; chmn., cost of living comsn., 1919-20; assessor, mem., bd. of trade and industries, July, 1921; advisory mem., Imp. Confce., 1923.

PAGE, HON. EARLE CHRISTMAS GRAFTON, M.B., Ch.M. (Syd.).—B. 1880; ed. Sydney High Schl. and Sydney Univ. (George Allen Maths. Scholarship and John Harris Scholarship for anatomy and physiology); served in European War with A.I.F. as surg. specialist to No. 3 Australian casualty clearing station, France, and No. 3 Australian gen. hosp., Egypt; mayor of S. Grafton, N.S.W., 1918; pres., N. Coast Development League, 1918; el. mem., H. of R., C. of A., for Cowper, Dec., 1919; treas., C. of A., 1923.

PAGE, GEORGE WM.—B. 1861; copyist, science and art dept., S. Kensington museum, Apr., 1881, to Dec., 1884; 2nd cl. elk. prsn. dept., Jan., 1885, to Dec., 1896; keeper of the gaol Freetown, S. Leone, Jan., 1897, to Apr., 1901; asst. dist. comsnr., S. Leone Prot., May, 1901; dist. comsnr., Oct., 1903; dist. comsnr. of Sherbro dist., Aug., 1906, and in addition dist. comsnr. of N. Sherbro dist., Mar., 1906; ag. curator of intestate estates, Nov., 1906, to Apr., 1901; is J.P. for the colony.

PAGE, CAPT. JOHN CAMPBELL.—B. 1893; ed. King's Schl., Canterbury, and Keble Coll., Oxford; B.A. (Oxon.); 2nd lieut., Buffs, Aug., 1914; on active serv. in France, 1916-19; M.C., Oct., 1916; passed progress exam. in Mendi; asst. dist. comsnr., S. Leone, 27th Aug., 1916; ag. dist. comsnr., Moyamba dist., 1922.

PAILTHORPE, WULFRED ARTHUR BOINTON, B. 1875; ed. King Edward VI Schl., Chelmsford, and Gray's Coll., Essex; serv., S. African War, 1899-1902 (Queen's med. and 6 clasps, King's med. and 2 clasps); registrn. elk., E.A.P., 1904; regir. of docs., 1910; collr. under Stamp Act, 1910; ex-officio agt. for admstr.-gen., 1911; ag. prin. regir. of docs., crown lands, etc., 1916-19; ch. controlling rev. authority, 1918; dep. regir.-zen. of titles, Kenya, 1919; prin. regir. of docs., crown lands and land titles, 1920.

PAINE, JOHN JAMES.—B. 1863; served with 19th (Princess of Wales's Own) Hussars in Egypt, and gained medal and 3 clasps and Khedive's star for Suakim and Nile expedns., 1884 and 1885; apptd. coal porter, C.O., 1st Jan., 1893; placed on estab. as office porter, 15th Apr., 1904.

PALETHORPE, RONALD FLINT.—B. 1891; ed. Hereford Schl. and Keble Coll., Oxford; asst. mast., St. George's Schl., Windsor Castle, 1913; asst. dist. comsnr., E.A.P., 5th Aug., 1914.

PALMER, ARTHUR, B.A.I., A.M.I.C.E.—B. 1881; ed. St. Columba's Coll. and Dublin Univ.; asst. engrnr., Cape govt. rly., Mar., 1903; ditto, Br. N. Borneo state rly., 1906; ditto, F.M.S. rly., Oct., 1907; engrnr., F.M.S., rly., Dec., 1912; sen. engrnr., F.M.S. rly., July, 1921; sec. to man., F.M.S. rly., Nov., 1923.

PALMER, CHAS. STUART RUSSELL, M.C.—Ed. at Roorkee Civil Eng. Coll., India; P.W.D., India, Oct., 1878, as asst. engrnr. duty in England, 1885 to 1887; asst. to ch. engrnr. and asst. sec. to ch. comsnr., cent. prov., 1889, when apptd. exec. engrnr. of Hooghly div., and in 1892 of Nagpur div.; ret. from serv., May, 1894; asst. survr., W. Aus., 1894; engrnr. in charge, roads and bridges, harbours and rivers branches, Aug., 1897; supply, 1898, and sewerage, 1900; engrnr.-gen. June, 1902; insp'tg. engrnr. for W.A. in Lond.

PALMER, HAROLD.—B. 1895; apptd. exam. elk. of the 2nd div. of the corps, apptd. to national health insurance auth., 13th Jan., 1913; on military service, 2nd Feb., 1918, to 26th Feb., 1920; assigned to O.T.U., Mar., 1920.

PALMER, HAROLD THORNBERY, M.C. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), D.T.M. (Lewes Guy's Hospital); asst. med. supt., Indo-Iran telegraph dept., Persia, and residency sur. k. 1903; med. offr., W.A.M.S., Gold Coast, Aug., 1906; tempy. capt., Cameroons stationery force, Sep., 1915.

PAMPELONE, ARMAND JOSEPH, I.Ch.B. Edin.—B. 1879; entd. med. serv., 1st Feb., 1906; dist. med. offr., 1st Aug., 1907; dist. med. offr., 1st Aug., 1907; ed. Ottawa Univ.; ent. civ. serv., Oct., 1889; sec., Canadian defence comtee., 1914; sec. to late Sir F. W. Borden, min. of militia and defence, 1904-12; sec., dept. of militia and defence from 1907; pres., bd. of enquiry, re applicants for the fenian raid volunteer list, 1912-15; pres., of pensions and claims bd., in desp. for serv. rendered in Can., 1914-16.

PARK, ALEXANDER DALLAR.—B. 1878; Waitaki Pub. Schl., Waimate High schl., privately; N.Z. pub. wks. dept., 1903-19; asst. dept., 1919; insp'tg. pub. serv. comm., 1920; sec. of marine, 1923; asst. dist. comsnr., 1923; served with N.Z. forces in Africa.

PARKER, JAMES T.—Cert. teacher, New Is.; dist. postmtr., Bethesda, 1901; schlr. boys' reformatory schl., 1903; elk. asst. keeper, P.W.D., and elk. to road bd., 1906; 1st govt. offr., Virgin Is., 1915; asst. weights and measures, Virgin Is., 1917.

PARKER, HON. SIR STEPHEN EDWARD K.C.M.G. (1914), KT. BACH (1908).—Called bar, 1868; Q.C., 1890; mem. of legislature of Australia from 1878 to 1897; col. sec., 1894; represented W. A. at the C.O. and evidence before sel. comtee. of H. of C. on the grant of self-govt. to the Colony; represented W. A. in London relative federation of Australia, 1900; justice of peace, 1901; ch. just. of W. A., 1906-1913.

PARKER, WILLIAM ALSTIN.—B. 1878; Queen's coll., B. Guiana; asstd. B. Guiana serv., 1883; qualified as notary public, 1892; admitted solr., 1897; chief clk. aconkt., adminstr.-genl.'s office, 1897; off. and pub. trustee, 1906; comsnr. of affidavits, acted at various times as crown solr., sup. adminstr.-gen., and regir. of sup. ct.; sec. comtn. of enquiry into working of regir., 1905.
PARKINSON, A. O. C., M.A. (1910), O.B.E.—
1884; ed. at Epsom and Oxford; class. deny,
adglen, 1903-7; 1st cls. mods., 1905; 1st cls. lit.,
1907; apptd. after compet. exam., 1st cls.
k., acctnt. gen.'s dept., Admiralty, Feb., 1908;
ansfd. as 2nd cls. elk., C.O., 19th Apr., 1909;
c., man. comttee, of imperial bureau of en-
mology; sec. to comttee, apptd. to investigate
relationship between wild animals and try-
nomiasis, 1913-1914; astt. priv. sec. to r.
Lewis Harcourt, 5th Oct., 1914, to Mr. Long,
Mar Law, 27th May, 1915, to Mr. Walter Long,
Dec., 1916; 1st cls. elk., 8th Dec., 1917;
military service from 16th May, 1915 to 26th
May, 1919; priv., 1st Apr., 1920; priv. sec. to
rd Milner, 1st Oct., 1920.
PARKINSON, N. F., M. Sc., A.M.E.I.C.—B.
yo; ed., Toronto Pub. and Tech. High Schla.,
Univ. of Toronto; div. engnr.; astt. to prov.
1. engnr., Toronto; enlisted in Canadian
guns, Dec., 1914; transfd. as gunner to 13th
i., Canadian Field Arty.; command in France,
g., 1916; wounded, May, 1917; invalided to
nada; returned overseas, Dec., 1917; discharged
ly, 1918; ent. dept. of soldier's civ. re-estabt.,

training, Ottawa, Nov., 1918; dir. of vocational
training, Jan., 1919; dep. min. of soldier's civ.,
re-
abt., Apr., 1920.
PARNALL, JOHN.—Solr.; astt. aud., E. Africa
1915; astt. aud. in charge, Zanzibar, Nov.,

y, 1920; regiar. and offl. assignee, H.B.M. ot.,

loc., Apr. to Oct., 1922; astt. admstr.-gen.,
ganayika Territory, 7th Sept., 1923; ag.
ntr.-gen., 18th Oct., 1923 to 3rd Jan., 1924;
ntr.-gen., offl. trustee and regiar. of docs.,
zanzibar, 31st May, 1924.
PARR, CECIL WILLIAM CHASE, C.M.G. (1923),
I.E.—Jun. offr., Perak civ. ser., 1889; dist.,
Tampin, Negri Sembilan, 1897; dist. offr.,
ng, 1904; ag. comptnr. of trade and customs,

ount offr.), 30th June to 7th Dec., 1915;
ish res., Pahang, 5th Feb., 1916; capt.,

S. Stltnts. and F.M.S. for Malay, Apr.,
major, M.V.I., 1st Feb., 1920; Br. res.,
k., 14th July, 1921; lieut. col., M.V.I.,
k., Apr., 1923.
ARR, HON. SIR CHRISTOPHER JAMES,
M.G. (1926), C.M.G. (1914).—B. 1869; ed.
Auckland Gram. Schl. and Auckland Univ. Coll.;
ister-at-law; mem., N.Z. parlmt. since 1914;
of educn. since 1920; min. of health, 1920-
min. of just., 1923.
ARRY, J. H. B. A. (Cantab.), M.R.C.S.
L.R.C.P. (Lond.)—Tempy. comptn. in
med. serv., Mar., 1915 to Mar. 1919; med.
Tanganyika Territory, Mar., 1919.
ARRY, REGINALD FRANCIS SCARLETT.—Ed.,
ohn's Schl., Leatherhead, and Lincoln Coll.
ord.; jnr. supt., educn. dept., N. Nigeria,
Jan., 1920.
ARSONS, HON. HERBERT ANGAS, LL.B.—
c. of sup. ot., S. Australia, 1921.
ARSONS, LAURANCE DUDLEY, M.B., Ch.B.
(1.).—B. 1873; res. surg. and supt., New
idence hosp., Nassau, Bahamas, Sep., 1901,
to Dec., 1904; port surg., etc., Gibraltar, Jan.,
