prin. civ. med. offr., Aug., 1922; ag. med. supt.,
gen. hosp., Colombo, Sept. to Dec., 1922.
PARTRIDGE, GEORGE JAMES, B.A. (1915),
M.A. (1921).—B. 1893; ed. Christ's Hospital
and Cambridge; open exhibr. (maths.), and
Essex County Scholar, Queens' Coll., 1912-14;
2nd cls. maths. tripes, part I., 1913, B.A.
(War), 1915; temp. comptn., 1914-18; on active
serv. in Franco and German E. Africa; 1914-15
Star; ment. in dep.; astt. polit. offr., 1st grade,
provis. admstr., German K. Africa, Dec., 1918;
priv. sec. to ag. admstr., Aug. to Dec., 1919; astt.
sec., Oct., 1919; ag. senr. astt. sec., Apr. to Dec.,
1920 and Aug., 1921 to Sept., 1923; clk. to exec.
coun., Sept., 1922 to Sept., 1923.
PASCOR, HON. THOMAS.—B. 1859; M.L.C.,
S. Australia, since May, 1900; min. of agric., S.
Australia, Dec., 1909 to June, 1910, and
from Feb., 1912 to Apr., 1915; min. of agr.,
irrigation and mines, 8th Apr., 1920; comptnr. of
pub. wks. and min. of mines and educn., 3rd
Nov., 1922; ch. sec. and min. for educn., Nov.,
1923 to Apr., 1924.
PASHLEY, EDWARD REYNOLD.—B. 1869;
storekeeper, petroleum warehouse, customs,
Bahamas, 1891; landing waiter, 1896; senr. clk.
of check staf., 1897; landing waiter and preventive
offr., 1899; attended impl. customs, London,
1900; customs offr., excise supervisor, boarding
offr., Tobago, 1901; landing waiter, customs,
Trinidad, 1902; transfd. to acntnt's branch,
treasy, 1905; 5th clk. and paymr., 1907; 4th clk.,
1912; 3rd clk., 1913; comptnr. of customs, regiar.
of shipping, J.P., Bahamas, 1914; ag. rec. gen.,
7th to 16th Feb., 1919, from 19th Sep. to 12th
Nov., 1919, and from 15th Mar. to 8th Apr., 1920;
ch. rev. inspr. Trinidad, Mar., 1921.
PASKIN, JESSE JOHN, B.A., M.C.—B. 1892-
ed., King Edwards Schl., Stourbridge and St.
John's Coll., Cambridge; 1st cls. maths. tripes,
pt. I., 1913; on milly. serv., Aug., 1914 to Mar.,
1919 (Worcestershire Regt., T.F. and Machine Gun
Corps); Croix de Guerre, 1918; transfd. to T.F.
res. with rank of major, Jan., 1920; apptd. under
reconstruction scheme, junr. higher divn. clk.,
miny. of transport, Jan., 1920; astt. prin., C.O.,
29th Mar., 1921.
PASLEY, CLAUDE BURGOYNE.—B. 1877; ed.
Clonmel Grammar Schl., Rathmines Schl.,
Dublin, R. Coll. of Surgeons, Ireland, Oct.,
1894; prizeman, materia medica, 1896; prizeman
in surgery, 1897; passed promary fellowship,
R.C.S.I., 1897; licentiate of midwifery, Rotunda
Hosp., 1898; licentiate of R. Colls., 1899; div.
surg., H.M. Forces, S. African War, 1900;
F.R.C.S.I., 1910; med. offr., Malay States med.
serv., 1912; ch. surg., F.M.S., 1921; examr. in
surgery, King Edward VII Coll. of Med., Singa-
pore, 1923; lieut., M.V.I., 1923.
PASSINGHAM, FRANK SELWOOD.—B. 1883;
ed. Goldsmiths' and Morley Colls., Lond.; hone.
medallist in typography, City and Guilds of
Lond. Inst.; govt. printer, Mauritius, Feb., 1914;
also supt., bookbinding works and stat. stores,
Apr., 1914; supt. of printing, Jamaica, Mar.,
1924.
PATERN, HENRY SIBBALD.—B. 1890; ed.
Winchester Coll. (schol.) and Magdalen Coll.,
Oxford (exhibr.), B.A., 1913; cadet, F.M.S., Nov.,
1913; ag. astt. collr. of land rev., K. Lumpur,
June, 1914; seconded for war serv., Mar., 1915;
active serv. in France and England, 1915-19; ment. in desp.; demob. with rank of major, Aug., 1919; asst. dist. offr., Kuantan, Aug., 1919; seconded as asst. adviser, Trengganu, July, 1920; supernmy. offr., cls. IV., Nov., 1920; dist. offr., Kuala Lipis, Dec., 1923.

PATSON, NICHOLAS JULIAN, B.A., K.C.—B. 1867; atty.-gen., Grenada, 1st Jan., 1912; ag. ch. just., 10th Jan., 1921; ag. col. sec., 27th Sept., 1921; admstr., Grenada, 10th Oct., 1921.

PATTERSON, JOHN, D.S.O. (1916).—B. 1878; ed. at George Watson's Coll., Edin.; Scottish Horse, S. African War; asst. treas., E. Africa Prot., 1st Apr., 1906; chief paymaster, E. Africa Pay Corps (ment. in desp., 1915), finan. adviser, Br. Salvage Coms. for E. Africa, 28th Dec., 1912; staff offr., Volunteers, 16th Feb., 1920; staff offr., war records, 1st Apr., 1921.

PATTULLO, HON. THOMAS D.—B. 1873; journalist; editor of "The Galt Reformer"; apptd. secy. to Commr. of the Yukon, 1897; resigned to enter business in Dawson; later, removed to Prince Rupert, where he took an active interest in municipal affairs, at one time holding the office of mayor; elec. to legis. ass., Brit. Columbia, g.e., 1916; min. of lands in Brit. Columbia cabinet, 1918.

PAUL, A. H. D.—Ed. at Bradfield and Bath colls.; trooper in Matabeleland mtd. pol., 1896; took part in the Jameson raid, 1896; planting in Ceylon, 1896 to 1904; trooper in Ceylon M.I.; dist. supt. of pol., N. Nigeria, 1906; asst. trea., 1st Nov., 1908; ag. supt. of agric., Aug., 1911.

PAUL, ROBERT JAMES.—B. 1888; sub-insp., constab., Trinidad, 9th Sept., 1912; 2nd lieut., Trinidad local forces, 29th June, 1913; pay and quartermaster, constab., and senr. supply and transport offr., Trinidad local forces, 21st Nov., 1914, to 9th Oct., 1916, and from 10th Apr. to 31st May, 1917; ag. inspr. of constab. and capt. local forces, 15th Aug., 1915; asst. supt., fire brigade, 24th Nov., 1914, to 14th Nov., 1916, and from 1st Feb. to 31st Mar., 1919; ag. supt., fire brigade, 15th Nov., 1915, to 30th Sep., 1916; J.P. for the colony; ag. chief of police, comdt. local forces, supt. of prison, St. Vincent, 4th Aug., 1919; J.P. for the colony; supt. of pol., Nyasaland, 11th Mar., 1923; passed govt. exams. in Chinvanja and law.

PAULIN, GEORGE.—B. 1885; ed. Canterbury Coll., Univ. of New Zealand, B.Sc., 1906; B.Eng., 1908; pupilage with govt. rlys., New Zealand, with city engr., Christchurch, and with Selwyn county engr. and engr.-in-chief, city of Dunedin drainage; engr.-survr., P.W.D., N. S. Wales, 1910; dist. engr., Fiji, 1912; res. engr., Suva harbr. wks., Fiji, 1915.

PAWAN, JAMES LENOX, M.B., Ch.B., Edin.—B. 1887; ent. med. serv., Trinidad, 1st Jan., 1913; dist. med. offr., 8th Mar., 1916.

PEACOCK, HON. SIR ALEXANDER JAMES, K.C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1861; mem. of Austn. Federal Convention, 1897-8; premier of Victoria, 1901-2; later chief sec. and min. for labour, Victoria; min. for educ. and labour, Dec., 1913; premier, treas., and min. of justice, 1914; min. for educ., forests and labour, Nov., 1920.

PEARCE, DR. ALEXANDER HUGH BLAXILL.—B. 1882; ed. George Watson's Coll., Edin. Univ. Trin. Coll., Dublin; L.R.C.F. & S., Edin.; L.R.F.P. & S., Glasgow (1904); L.M., Dublin (1906); D.P.H., Dublin Univ., 1918; spec. certif., London Sch. of Trop. Med.; F.R.I. Pub. Health; Fellow of Tropical Society; ag. R.M.O., Seamen's Hosp., Albert Dock; house st., Lincoln County Hosp.; C.C., Coombe lyng. hosp., Dublin; junr. med. offr., Montev. 1907; D.M.O., St. Kitts; res. med. st., Charitable Instit., Antigua, and health of Antigua, 1908; ag. C.G.M.O., Antigua, 1910; col. surg., Falkland Is., 1912; M.L.C. & M.E.C., Falkland Is., dormant comm. to minister govt. of Falklands; pres. tr. health, Falklands; seconded to R.A.M.C., 1918; capt., R.A.M.C.; served in France Far East; chief med. offr., Bahamas; M.L.C.; chmn., hosps. bd., Bahamas Gen. Hosp.

PEARCE, Rt. Hon. GEORGE FORSTER, K.C. (1921).—Senator for Western Australia in Commonwealth parlmt.; sec. of trades com., after 1896; pres., 1899; returned to first Commonwealth Senate, 1901; re-elected, 1906, and elect chmn. of comtees.; min. of defence, C. d. 1st Apr., 1910 to June, 1913; at. Imp. Conf., min. of defence since Sept., 1914; rep. Aust. at the Washington Disarmament Conf., min. for home and territories in Bruce ministry, 1923.

PEARCE, REV. THOS. WM., O.B.E. [LL.D.—B. 1855; Missionary of Lond. Miss. Canton, 1879-1890; Hong Kong, 1890-1902; inspr. of schools, 5th Sept., to 9th Oct., again in 1900; examiner, Queen's Coll., 1879-1898; mem. of comte., on interpretation, 1900; apptd. mem. of bd. of examiners in Chine 14th Jan., 1897; mem. of govng. body, Queen's Coll., 1906; mem. of comte., on confirmation classes, 1907.

PEARSE, ARTHUR VERNON ETTON.—B. 1878; ed. Haileybury and Clare Coll., Cambridge; service, E. Africa, 1917-18; asst. dist. succ., Sierra Leone, 18th Aug., 1914.

PEARSE, WILFRID WILLIAM.—M.B. C.M., Aberdeen, 1893; D.P.H., Aberdeen, 1894; M.B., Aberdeen, 1906; 2nd assist. med. offr., Shepherds Infirmary, 1894-96; assist. med. offr. of health, Hong Kong, 1901; J.P., 1902; ag. med. dir. of health, 1903-6, 1908 and 1918; med. dir. of health, 1915; on milly. serv., 1917 to 1918.

PEARSON, FRANCIS MEREDITH.—B. 1875; ed. Highgate Schol. and Weymouth Coll.; tax clk., Royal Comn. on Local Taxation, 1904; ent. Crown Agent's office, 2nd Dec., 1901; active service with 9th London Regt., Sept., 1914; lieut., R.A.S.C., June, 1915; capt., June, 1916; O.C., R.A.S.C., Cyprus, Nov., 1916 to Jan., 1917; O.C., R.A.S.C., Zagazig, Egypt, 1918 to Feb., 1919; asst. head, appts. dept., 26th Oct., 1917; dep. head, appts. dept., July, 1921.

PEARSON, JOSEPH, D.Sc. (Liverpool, D.S. (Manchester), F.R.S.E., F.L.S.—B. 1881; Liverpool Coll. and Univ. Coll., Liverpool B.Sc., Victoria Univ. 1st cls. hona., 1902; B.S. Liverpool, 1904; M.Sc., 1905; D.Sc., 1908; M.S. Manchester, 1920; D.S., 1922; dir., Colombo Museum, and marine biologist to Ceylon Govt., 11th Aug., 1910; offr. in charge, pearl fishers lecturer in zoology, Univ. Coll., Colombo; edit. "Spolia Zeylanica," "Bulletins of the Ceylon Fisheries," "Memoirs of the Colombo Mus." and author of numerous scientific papers on zoology and oceanography.

PEASE, J. W. K.—Asst. dist. commr., K.A.P., Apr., 1914.

PEDLOW, JOSEPH HOWARD, B.A. (N.U.)—B. 1889; ed. Queen's Coll., Galway; ed. S. Stlitms., Dec., 1912; attached Chinese Prot.
Penang, Jan., 1913; at Amoy to study Chinese Hok-kein), Sep., 1913; attached Chinese Prot., Singapore, Mar., 1916; attached treas. for custodian enemy property and war loan work, May, 1916; collr. of war tax, Singapore, in addition, Mar. to June, 1918; pol. mag., Singapore, Aug., 1919; supermny. offr., cls. PEDRAZA, R.—Ast dist. comnr., E.A.P., Aug., 1914.

PEEBLES, MAJOR H. W., D.S.O. (1917).—Joined Canadian M.I., Dec., 1899; 2nd lieut., A.S.C., Sept., 1900; lieut., Nov., 1901; S. African War, Jan., 1900, to May, 1902 (severely wounded, Queen's medal and four clasps, King's medal and two clasps); rec. of offrs., June, 1902; A.D.C. to Brig.-Gen. Sir W. H. Manning, K.C.M.G., C.B., Feb., 1903, to June, 1904; Somaliland campaign, Jan., 1903, to June, 1904 (twice men. in deep, medal and two clasps); A.D.C. and priv. sec. to Sir B. Sweet-Escott, K.C.M.G., gov'r of B. Hond., Oct., 1904; local capt., Nov., 1904; commanding, Belize L.I. volks., Dec., 1904; local major, 1905; ast. rea., N. Nigeria, Dec., 1905 to Jan., 1907; ag. priv. sec. to Sir E. B. Sweet-Escott, K.C.M.G., gov'r of Leeward I., Oct., 1907; ast. rea., N. Nigeria, Mar., 1908; 3rd class rea., N. Nigeria, Jan., 1909; resigned on account of ill-health, June, 1909; clk. and priv. sec. to administrator, Dominica, Mar., 1913; raised and commanded Dom. Defence For., Aug., 1914; served with B.E.F. in France from Oct., 1914; ment. in despatches, Jan., 1916, Jan., 1917, and May, 1917; awarded D.S.O., June, 1917; ment. in despatches, June, 1919; brevet major, June, 1919; D.A.D.O.S., 3rd Army, B.E.F., June, 1916, to Oct., 1917; D.A.D.O.S., Aldershot Command, May, 1917, to 31st May, 1919; comnr., Virgin Islands, July, 1919; comnr., Montserrat, 26th Feb., 1922; assumed govt., 4th Mar., 1922.

PEEL, W., B.A.—B. 1875; ed. Queen's Coll., Cambridge, 11th wrangler, math. tripes., 1896; adet, S. Stltlms., Oct., 1897; ag. dist. offr., Prov. Wellesley, Aug., Dec., 1898; and from Mar., 1899; passed fin. exam. in Malay, Dec., 1899; dist. offr., Prov. Wellesley, Dec., 1901; ag. 2nd ast. sol. sec., May, 1902; ag. ast. col. sec. and clk. of surns., Nov., 1902, to Jan., 1903; and in Aug., 1903; ag. ast. supt., Indian immigrts., Sing., in addition, Aug., 1903; ag. 2nd ast. col. sec., sept., 1903; ag. 2nd mag., Penang, Feb., 1906; ag. collr. of land rev., Panang, Jan., 1906; dist. offr., Tampin, F.M.S. June, 1908; ag. sec. to rea., Selangor, 22nd Oct., 1909; ag. dist. offr., Lower Perak, 21st Feb., 1910; ag. supt. of Indian immigrts., S.S. and F.M.S., 2nd May, 1910; ag. chief ast. dist. offr., Kinta, and regiar. of titles, south Perak, 21st Oct., 1910; seconded as pres., aun. comnr., Penang, 1st Jan., 1911; promoted c Class III., but remained seconded, 1st Jan., 1912; acted as res. councillor, Penang, in addtn., 'eb. to Oct., 1917; pres., mun. comnr., Singa- ore, July, 1918; offr. of Class II., F.M.S., 1st an., 1919; joint passage controller, Malaya, in addition, Feb., 1919; seconded as food contrlr., Islaya, and chmn., shipping cte., 26th May, 1919; ag. contrlr. of lab., F.M.S. and S.S., 10th Nov., 1920; chmn., European unemployment comte., in addition, Feb., 1921; contr. of lab., F.M.S. and S. Stltlms., 4th Feb., 1922; ag. Br. adviser, Kedah, 27th Apr., 1922; Br. adviser, Kedah, 4th Oct., 1922.

PEET, JAMES HERBERT.—B. 1882; clk. audit office, Bahamas, 1904; 4th clk., P.O., 1907; 2nd clk., C.S.O., 1909; 3rd clk., treasy. dept., 1910; ch. clk., P.O., 1913; ch. clk. and ast. examg. offr., customs, 1914; compt. of cust., 4th Apr., 1921; has held numerous ag. appts.

PELLETIER, PHILIPPE.—B. 1849; called to the bar, Quebec, 1875; mem. of the coun. of the bar of Montreal, and sec., 1878; a fire comnr. for city of Montreal, 1879 to 1887; unsuccessfully contested St. John's in provincial elections, 1886, and Beauharnois in Dominion elections, 1887; ch. clk., sec. of state dept., Canada, 1888; ast. under-sec. of state of Canada, 1903.

PEMBERTON, ERNEST WILFRED, J.P.—B. 1874; ent traffic dept., Cape Govt. rly., 1896; stores dept., 1899; treasy., 1903; audr.-gens. dept., 1906; inland rev. dept., 1910; ag. ree. of rev., Kimberley, 1915; recr. of rev., E. London, 1917; lieut., Cape Peninsula Regt., 1902; rec. of offrs., 1913; apptd. to Pretoria Regt. from res. and served in German S.W. Africa campaign, Sept., 1914 to Aug., 1915.

PENGILLEY, ERNEST EDGAR.—B. 1897; ed. Christ's Hosp. (exhib.) and Exeter Coll., Oxford (class. school); lieut., 23rd Batt., Royal Fusiliers, 1917-19 (wounded and prisoner of war); cadet, F.M.S., 12th Jan., 1921; ag. ast. sec. to res., Selangor, 7th Mar., 1921; passed cadet, July, 1922; addnl. mag., Kuala Lumpur in addn., Aug., 1922; sec. Selangor rubber restric. comte., in addn., Oct., 1922; passport offr. in addn., Dec., 1922; offr., cls. V., Jan., 1924; ast. dist. offr., Rembau, Jan., 1924.

PENNEFATHER, CHARLES EDWARD DE FONBLANQUE.—B. 1885; clk., Gilbert and Ellice Is. Prot., 1908; clk. of peace, 1910; sub-inspr. of constabty., Fiji, 1910; inspr., ditto, 1912; dist. comnr., 1914; ag. dist. comnr., Rewa, and gov. comnr., Naitasiri, 1914-15; ag. dist. comnr., Colo East, 1917-19; ag. ch. inspr., Fiji constabty., ag. ch. pol. mag., regiar.-gen., regiar. of sup. ct., regiar. of titles, pub. trustee, regiar. of companies, cust. of enemy property, and cur. of intestate and vacant estates, 1918; dist. comnr., 1922.

PEPPYS, WALTER EVELYN.—B. 1885; ed. at Malvern and Brasenose Coll., Oxford; B.A., 1907; M.A., 1910; cadet, F.M.S. civ. serv., 1908; ag. ast. dist. offr., Pekan, Apr., 1910; ag. ast. sec. to rea., Perak, Jan., 1911; passed cadet, June 1911; cls. V., Jan., 1912; dist. offr., Jelebu, Apr., 1913; ag. dist. offr., Kuala Langat, June, 1913; ag. mag., cent. ct., Kelantan, and state auditor, Mar., 1914; on duty with Kelantan detachmt., Malay States Guides, 15th to 31st May, 1915; dist. offr., Pasir Puteh, 1st June, 1915; ag. sup. of lands, Kelantan, and chmn., conservancy bd., Aug. to Dec., 1917; dist. offr., Pasir Puteh, Jan., 1918; offr., cls. IV., F.M.S., 1st Jan., 1918; ag. sup. of lands, Kelantan and chmn., conservancy bd. in addition, May, 1918; ag. Br. adviser Trengganu, Nov., 1919 to Jan., 1920; ag. 2nd mag., Singapore, July, 1920; offr., class III., F.M.S., Nov., 1920; federal secretariat for sp. duty, Aug., 1921; ag. comnr. lands, Trengganu, Mar., 1922; ag. ast. sec. to govt., F.M.S., Sept., 1922.

PERCEVAL, SIR WESTBY BROCK, K.C.M.G. (1894).—B. 1854; was mem. for Christchurch City in legis. assem., of N. Zealand; chmn. of comtees, in 1890; agt.-gen. for the col. in England, 1891-96;
called to bar, Mid. Tem., 1878; Roy. commr. for Chicago Exhibn., 1893; agt.-gen. for Tasmania, 1896 to 1899.

PERCY, FREDERICK WM.—B. 1857; ed. at private schl., Dublin; writer, Royal Navy, 1872; passed English civ. serv. exam., 2nd cls. clk., 1874; clk., wks. and rivws. depts., W. Australia, 1892; minister's clk., wks. dept., 1896; ag. chf. clk., Jan., 1898; statistical clk., July, 1898; ag. chf. clk., Jan. to Dec., 1902; chf. correspondence clk., Mar., 1903; ag. chf. clk. for pub. wks., 14th Nov., 1908.

PERCY, H. VANE (formerly Baumgartner).—B. 1883; ed. Bedford Grammar Schl.; clk., land settl. dept., O.R.C., 16th Oct., 1902; clk. and typist audit dept., 2nd Dec., 1902; clk., audit dept., 1st July, 1904; examr. of accts., audit dept., 1st Jan., 1908; jur. ast. treas., G. Coast, 1st Jan., 1914; ast. treas., 26th Apr., 1917.

PERDUE, CECIL GRAHAM.—B. 1891; ed. Trinity Coll., Dublin; police probationer, Hong Kong, Nov., 1912; passed in Chinese, 1915; attached to Punjab police, 1915-16; passed in Urdu, 1916; temp. 2nd lieut., Indian army reserve, 1916-19; ag. ast. supt. police, Hong Kong, 1919; ag. deputy supt. police, 1919 J.P., 1920; ast. supt. pol., 1920; ast. census offr., 1921.

PERDUE, HON. WM. EGERTON, B.A.—B. 1850; ed. Brampton high schl. and Toronto Univ.; called to the bar, Ontario, 1879; called to the bar, Manitoba, 1882; judge, ct. of King's Bench, Manitoba, 1903; judge, ct. of appeal, Manitoba, 1906; ch. just. of Manitoba, 1918.

PEREIRA, ROBERT JAMES.—B. 1869; apptd. to cls. V. Ceylon civ. serv., May, 1920; extra office ast., Colombo Kachcheri, May, 1920.

PERERA, THEODORE DUNCAN.—B. 1895; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., local divn., Aug., 1919; attchd. to Kurunegala Kach., Aug., 1919; Jaffna Kach., Dec., 1919; ag. pol. mag., Puttalam, June, 1920; pol. mag., Avissawella, July, 1921; ag. pol. mag., W. Prov., Feb., 1923; addnl. ast. commr. of stamps, July, 1923.

PERKINS, ARTHUR JAMES.—B. 1871; Diplomé de l'école Nationale d'Agriculture de Montpellier, 1890; management of farm estates, Tunisia, 1890-2; prof. of viticulture and oenology, S. Aust., 1892; sec. for agriculture, 1902-1904; prin. of agric. coll. and prof. of viticulture and oenology, 1904; dir. of agric., 1914.

PERKINS, CHARLES JAMES.—B. 1872; ed. Westbury and Melksham Grammar Schls.; dipl. in surveying, Queensland, 1896; govt. survr., Queensland, 1899-1904; survr., F.M.S., Feb., 1904; staff appt., Sept., 1904; ast. supt., 1906; supt., 1919; ag. ast. survr.-gen., F.M.S. and S.S., 1920-21; ag. survr.-gen., F.M.S. and S.S., 1920-21 and 1924; ast. survr.-gen., F.M.S. and S.S., 1922; served R. Fusiliers, Mar., 1915-Aug., 1916; B.E.F., France; M.S.V.R., 1906-16; M.V.I., 1916; capt. and 2nd in commd., Selangor Unit.; ag. offr., commdng., 1923-24.

PERKINS, LEICESTER GRANT.—B. 1890; ed. privately and Harrison Coll., Barbados; clk., post office, Barbados, Jan., 1909; 5th clk., audit office, Mar., 1911; 2nd clk., registra. office, Nov., 1913; clk. to master in chancery, May, 1914; 4th clk., savings bank, Jan., 1915; 2nd-lieut., Imperial Army, 30th Mar., 1917, served during the war in Egypt and Palestine with 2nd B.W.I. Regt.; 2nd-lieut., 1st Oct., 1918; 1st clk., Barbados savings bank, Aug., 1919; 2nd grade supvr. of customs, Nigeria, Feb., 1920.

PERKINS, PHILIP HABOLD.—B. 1891; ed. Dudley Schl.; apptd. after compet. exam., clk., G.P.O., 1907; on milly. serv., 4th Aug., 1914; 22nd Oct., 1920; commr., German prisoners' war camp, France, 1917; dep. ast. prov. marsh., 1919; capt., reserve of officers; loaned to C.O., 2nd May, 1921; apptd. cler. offr. and assigned to C.O., 1st Aug., 1921.

PERLEY, HON. SIR GEORGE HALSETT, K.C.M.G. (1915).—B. 1857; ed. Ottawa gram. schl. & Paul's schl., Concord, N.H., and Harvard Univ., B.A., 1878; elec. to H. of C., Canada (Argenteuil), 1904; re-elec., 1908 and 1911; chief conserv. whip, 1911; mem. of privy coun. for Canadian min. without portfolio in Mr. Borden's cabinet Oct., 1911; ag. high commr. in London, 1916; min. of overseas mil. forces, 1916; high commr., 1917; joint commr. and plenipotentiary of Canada to sign Peace Treaties, 1919; Canadian delegate to League of Nations Assembly, 1921; resigned as commr.-in-chief, 1922.

PERRY, SIR ALLAN, KT. BACH. (1904); M.D. (Durham); D.P.H. (Lon.); M.R.C.S. Eng.; L.R.C.P. Lond.—B.1860; prin. civ. med.offr. and insp. of hosps., Ceylon; prin. of Ceylon med. sch., 10th Dec., 1897; major R.A.M.C. (retired); mem. municipal coun., Colombo; late pres. Ceylon branch Br. med. assoc.; del. for Ceylon to Int. Nat. Leprosy Conf., Bergen, 1909; ret., 1915.

PERRY, B.C. G.—B.1886; apptd. after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. serv., assigned to C.C., 9th Apr., 1906; cler. of higher grade, 1st Apr., 1922.

PERRY, GEORGE McREDDIE, M.B., C.M. Glasgow, and St. Mary's Hosp., London, F.R.C.S.; Ast. col. surg., Lagos, Oct., 1893; ag. col. med. Feb., Mar., 1894; ag. ast. col. sec., May, 1894; med. offr. to expedn. to Idanam mountains; ast. col. surg., Aug., 1895; ag. col. surg., 1896.

PERRY-LEWIS, CAPT. GEORGE, F.R.S.—B. 1880; entd. Imp. postal serv., 1st July, 1898; transf'd. to post and telegraph dept., E. Africa, Uganda Prots., 3rd Nov., 1905; ast. P.M.G., Nigeria, 27th Apr., 1910; ag. dep. P.M.G., 1913; 1st cls. postmr., E.A.P., Nov., 1914; ast. P.M.G., Nov., 1916; ast. P.M.G., Mar., 1919; passed gov't. test in Swahili language; held 1st Africa (field) telegraph sect., Nov., 1916; capt. and offr. commdng., July, 1918; pers. gen. and man., govt. savings bank, Trinidad, Tobago, 10th Sept., 1921; senr. surtr., post & telegraphs, Nigeria, Oct., 1922.

PERRYMEN, PERCY WILBERAHM, M.R.C.S. (1919), F.R.G.S.—B. 1885; ed. Eton and Balliol Coll., Oxford; ast. dist. commr., Uganda, 1908; dist. commr., Sept., 1916; senr. ast. sec., Mar., 1920; ast., ch. sec., Uganda, June, 1921.

PERTH, ARCHBISHOP OF MOST REV. OWEN LEAVER RILEY, D.D., Cantab.—B. 1858; vicar of St. Paul's, Preston, Lancs., 1885-1896; bishop of Perth, W. Aust., 1894; created archbishop, 1914.

PETCH, TOM, B.A., B.Sc., (Lond.)—B. 1892; botanist and mycologist, Ceylon, 1906; ag. of agric. for various periods during 1914-20.

PETRIDES, PHILIP BETTER.—B. 1881; Dulwich Coll.; called to the bar, Middle Temp., 1906; joined Midland Circ. and Birmingham cent. crim. court sess., 1906; legal adviser & crown prosecutor, Seychelles, 22nd Jan., 1914; ex-officio mem. exec. and legis. conn.; ag. just., 23rd July, 1916, to 20th Mar., 1917; 1st May, 1918 to 8th Oct., 1918, and from 2nd Dec., 1918 to 11th Nov., 1919; temp. emp. C.O., Feb. to Apr., 1920; ch. just., Seychelles.
10th June, 1920; admstd. govt., 13th Mar., 1921 to Sept., 1922; atty.-gen., Nyasaland Prot., 1924.

PETRIE, GEORGE MELVIN.—Joined Bech. Prot. pol., June, 1910; treasy. clk., 1922; acct., 1924.

PHELPS, HUGH RICHARD.—Ed. Weymouth Coll. and Queen's Coll., Oxford; local auditor, Niger Coast Prot., 27th Oct., 1894; asst. auditor, E. Africa Prot., 9th Dec., 1896; local auditor, Uganda, 29th Apr., 1897; served in Uganda nativity (medal and clasp); local auditor, E. Africa and Uganda rly., 26th Dec., 1901; auditor, Hong Kong, 1st Nov., 1904; J.P., 1906; hon. auditor, Hong Kong Univ., 2nd May, 1911.

PHILIPPS, JAMES CRABRUS TRACY, Capt. r. of O., M.C. (1918), Ordre de la Couronne of Belgium (1921), B.A., B. Litt., F.R.G.S., F.R.A.I.—B. 1888; ed. Marlborough Coll., Oxford and Durham Univ., which was undergraduate representative at the Congress of Univ. of the Empire, London, 1912; editor of Durham Univ. Journal; hon. sec., D.U.B.C.; res. of the Union; lieut. Rifle Brigade, 1912; asst. dist. commr. and adml. dist. mag., Uganda, 1912; asst. intelligence offr., E. Africa Expedy. Force, from 8th Aug., 1914, attached K.A.R.; commanding 2000 armed levies and scouts, from 9th Sept., 1914 (wounded and ment. n desps.); admstd. Kifumbiro (Bukoba) area of occupied territory from 5th Sept., 1914, under martial law; polit. offr. on staff of Major-Gen. J. M. Stewart, C.B., Bukoba Expedy. Forces, from 5th June, 1915 (ment. in desps.); capttn., Kagena Command Staff, Jan., 1916; chief polit. offr., Jganda area, including Kagena mil. dist., from 7th Jan., 1916; chief intelligence offr. (G.S.O.3), staff of the Lake Command, E.A.E.F., to Tabora, from 4th Aug., 1916; Mily. Cross, 1916; in charge of polit. mission in British and Belgian areas of conquered territory, Nov., 1916, to Mar., 1917, when invalided; emp. intell. duties, W.O., June to Aug., 1917; attd. Admly. War Staff, intell. div., Aug. to Oct., 1917; employed by F.O. o Abyssinia, Jan., 1918; on special duty in Sudan, Jan., 1918; raised two companies Somalis and Abyssinians for K.A.R. in French and Abyssinian territory, Apr., 1918; ag. dist. commr., Kigezi, British Ruanda, and dist. mag. Kabale, Feb., 1919; made expedit. across Africa from E. to W. in Lake Kivu through Belgian, French and Portuguese territories; Br. commr. for Russian held Cross in Russia, 1921; Br. relief commr., Russia, 1922; mem. of Br. comttee. for Moslem refugees, Turkey, 1922; "Times" war corres., "Ibrace and Anatolia, 1922; seconded to Sudan ov't as asst. dir. of intelligence, Khartoum, 1924; publications, "Pan-Islam in Africa," "Cape to Cairo developments"; "Ruanda" (1919); "The Iabingi" (1919); "A Kinya-Ruanda Vocabulary" (1920); "Ethiopianum" (1921).

PHILLIPS, C. H., L.M.S.S.A. (Lond.).—empy. lieut., R.A.M.C., Jan., 1915 (General list); med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Dec., 1920.

PHILLIPS, HAROLD ERNEST.—B. 1877; clk., auditor, B. Honduras, Oct., 1892; 5th clk., treasy., customs and P.O. depts., June, 1893; 7th clk., Feb., 1894; 3rd clk., treasy. and cust., 16th May, 1897; 2nd clk., June, 1898; 2nd k., C.S.O., Sept., 1900; ag. dist. commr., Stannreek, 1905; ch. clk. and clk. of couns., Jan., 1906; priv. sec. to gov. Sir E. Swayne, 1909-10; gov. Collett, 1911-13; to ag. gov., Walter, 1916; ag. commr. of currency, 18th Feb., 1911; ag. treasy., collr. of cust., 1911-14 and 1917-20; ag. col. sec., 1920; Br. Honduras del. to Canada-W. Indies Confec., Ottawa, June, 1920; asst. col. sec., Apr., 1921; commr. and judge, Turks and Caicos Is., May, 1923.

PHILLIPS, TREVOR STANLEY, B.A.—Ed., Llandovery Coll., and Jesus Coll., Oxford; jnr. supt., educn. dept. N. Nigeria, 5th Sept., 1914; attached, Nigeria Regt., 1917-18.

PHILLIPSON, SYDNEY.—B. 1892; on mily. serv., May, 1915; cadet Ceylon civil serv., Nov., 1919; attached to Kandy Kach., Dec., 1919; ag. office asst. to gov't. agt., N.C. Prov., Apr., 1921; pol. mag., Matara, Sept., 1922.

PICKWORTHING, G. H.—Town mag., E.A.P., 1910; ag. 2nd puisne judge, 1915; 2nd puisne judge, 1917.

PICKWOAD, HOWELL.—Ed. at Bedford Mod. schl.; clk., atty.-gen.'s off., Br. Hond., Nov., 1896; 3rd cust. offr., 12th Aug., 1898; 4th clk., treasy. and cust., and clk. to commrs. of currency, 27th Dec., 1901; 2nd grade cust. and excise offr., Aug., 1903; col. branch of exchequer and audit dept., 21st Oct., 1904; asst. treas., E. Africa Prot., 26th June, 1905; dep. treas., Kenya, Jan., 1922; reor. gen., Mauritius, Oct., 1923.

PICKWOAD, HUGH FREDERICK.—B. 1878; commr. (4th div.), Bahamas, 1909; ditto (3rd div.), ditto (2nd div.), 11th Sept., 1923.

PIENAAR, ANDRIES GUSTAF ERLAND.—Clk. of ct., Lichtenburg, July, 1902; ag. pub. prosecutor, Feb., 1903; pub. prosecutor, June, 1903; ag. ass't res. mag., Feb., 1904; ch. clk. and ag. ass't res. mag., Nov., 1905; addnl. asst. res. mag., Krugersdorp, Sept., 1906; res. mag. and native commr., Waterberg, Nov., 1910; res. mag., Ermelo, Apr., 1912; senr. mag., Germiston, May, 1920; pub. serv. inspr., Sept., 1921; deptl. of just., 1924.

PIERIS, PAULUS EDWARD, Samarasinha Sriwardhana, M.A., Trin. Coll., Camb., 1886, L.L.M., D. Litt. (Cantab.)—Barrister-at-law, Inner Temple, 1896; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., 1896; asst. to gov't. agt., Colombo, 1898; pol. mag., Panadura, 1899; dist. judge, Ratnapura, 1899; asst. to gov't. agt., Galle, 1901; ag. dist. judge, Matara, Mar., 1903; office asst. to gov't. agt., Galle, June, 1903; asst. commr., St. Louis exhibn., Feb., 1904; dist. judge, Kegalle, Mar., 1905; ditto, Kalutara, Mar., 1906; ag. regiar.-gen., Dee., 1910; ag. dist. judge, Kurunegala, May, 1912; commr. of requests, Colombo, Nov., 1912; ag. dist. judge, Kandy, Nov., 1913; dist. judge, Galle, June, 1914; ditto, Jaffna, Dec., 1915; ag. dist. judge, Colombo, Mar., 1919; ditto, Kandy, Apr., 1920.

PIGGOTT, CHARLES FRANCIS LOVELL, M.A.—B. 1890; ed. Dean Close Schol. and Univ. Coll., Oxford; asst. sec., Tanganyika Territory, 1919-22; supt. educn., dept., N. Prov., Nigeria, 17th May, 1922.

PIGGOTT, SIR FRANCIS TAYLOR, KT. BACH. (1905)—Barrister-at-law; employed by F.O. on special service in 1887; legal adv. to prim. min., Japan, Nov., 1887; sec. to atty.-gen. Sir C. Russell (afterwards Lord Russell of Killowen) during Behring Sea arbitrn., 1893-4; proc.-gen., Mauritius, 1894; ag. ch. just., 1895 to 1897; ch. just., Hong Kong, 27th Apr., 1905; ret., 1912; recd. thanks of coun. of govt. for ser. in connection with planters' loans, 1902; author of "Nationality and Naturalization," "Exterritoriality," "Extradition," "Foreign Judgments and Jurisdiction," "Law of Tort" and "Imperial Statutes applicable to the Colonies."
PILBEAM, S. A.—B. 1899; entd. C.O., Jan., 1915; passed asst. clk.'s exam., July, 1916; on military service from 18th July, 1917, to 10th Mar., 1919; assigned to C.O. as asst. clk., Apr., 1919; cler. offr., 1st Jan., 1920.

PILLING, HENRY GUY.—B. 1886; ed. King's Schl., Ely, and Keble Coll., Oxford; M.A., 1911; cadet, Fiji, 1907; passed cadet, 1910; 2nd grade dist. commnr., 1914; mem., Indian Franchise Coman., 1920; ag. asst. col. sec., 1920; asst. col. sec., 1st Jan., 1921; ag. sec., W. Pacific high comm., 21st Mar., 1924.

PINHORN, R. H., M.A., O.B.E.—B. 1871; ed. Wolverhampton Schl. and Keble Coll., Oxford; 2nd cls. hon., mod. hist., 1896; Oxf. Univ. dipl. in educn., 1911; asst. mast., R. Masonic Schl., Buahy, 1896-1904; headmaster, Free Schl., Penang, 1904; J.P. for Penang; O.B.E. "for services to education," 1923.

PINK, HERBERT JOHN.—Paymr. lieut., R.N.R.; fellow, Royal Economic Soc.; fellow, Royal Statistical Soc.; ed. Portsmouth Coll.; asst. treas., Kenya, and in charge income tax dept., 1920-23; col. treas., St. Helena, 1923; J.F., St. Helena, Feb., 1924.

PIRIE, D. A.—B. 1886; clk. Burgher camps, Transvaal, 1902; treasy., 1904; prin. clk. treasy., Union of S. Africa, 1920; sec. mily. pensions bd., treasy., 1920.

PIRIE, J. H. H., M.B., Bac. Surg., M.D., M.R.C.P.—Med. offr., E.A.P., Aug., 1913.

PITOT, LEON EMILE.—B. 1866; govt. surr. and supt. of pub. wks., Seychelles, 11th Apr., 1889; govt. engrn. and architect, Mauritius, Apr., 1891; gen. man. of rlyws. and engineer, Mauritius, 14th Sept., 1896.

PITT, WALTER JAMES, B.A.—B. 1879; ed. Downing Coll., Cambridge (modern and medieval language trips); ent. Middle Temple, Jan., 1919; passed Bar final exam., Dec., 1920; headmr., Cape Coast Govt. Schl., 1910; inspr. of schls., 1912; prov. inspr. of schls., 1914; attd. to polit. serv., Gold Coast, 4th Aug., 1914; asst. dist. comm., 25th July, 1917; dist. comm., 1st Jan., 1921; ag. prov. comm., W. Prov., Ashanti, Feb.-Nov., 1920.

PLACE, C. GODFREY M., D.S.O. (1917), M.C. (1918), B.A., LL.B.—B. 1886; ed. St. Columba's Coll. and Dublin Univ. (modr. and silver medallist, legal and polit. science, gold medallist, coll. hist. soc.); called to Irish Bar, 1909; asst. examr. of titles, land regisy., 1910-14; served European War, E. Surrey Regt. (ment. in desps.); major, res. of offrs.; examr. of titles, land regisy. of Ireland, 1919; dist. mag., Uganda, 1921; asst. to atty.-gen., Dec., 1924.

PLANT, GEORGE FREDERIC.—B. 1877; ed. Manchester Gram. Schl. and Brasenose Coll. (scholar, 1896); 1st cl. class. mods., 1898; B.A., 1900; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., 1901; off. asst., Kurunegala, 1902; off. asst., Galle, 1904; pol. mag., Avissawella, 1905; dist. judge, Ratnapura, Apr., 1906; ditto, Matara, Dec., 1906; asst. gov't. agt., Kalutara, May, 1906; temporarily employed in C.O. London, May, 1918, to Dec., 1918; sec., overseas, settlement comte., Jan., 1919; permanently transferred to Home civ. serv., Sept., 1919.

PLATTS, W. A. F.—Asst. dist. comm., E.A.P., 15th Feb., 1907; dist. comm., Apr., 1913.

PLOWMAN, CLIFFORD HENRY FITZHERBERT, B.A. (class. tripes), 1911, F.R.G.S.—B. 1889; ed. at King's Schl., Ely, and Trin. Coll., Camb.; asst. dist. comm., E. Africa Prot., Mar., 1912; pol. offr., Turkana Exped., 1915 (A.G.S. Med. with clasp); ag. offr. in charge, Northern Frontier Dist., 1919-20; seconded to F.O. as H.R.Y. Vice-Consul, Harar, Abyssinia, 1920; H.R.Y. Consul on transfer Harar Consulate to C.O., 1921; transf., Somaliland; 2nd cls., star of Ethiopia has passed E. Africa law exam. and Swah. Boran and Galla languages.

PLOWMAN, HON. SIR GEORGE THOMAS E. BACH, (1923), C.M.G. (1906),—C.I.C., and shorthand writer, col. sec.'s office, Natal, 1890; 1st cls. ch. clk., 1894; sec. to civ. ser. bd.; asst. univ. sec., 1898; sec. to prime min., July, 1901; w. lands and works, Nov., 1901; mem., civ. ser. bd., 1901; sec. to prime min.; acctng. offr., rly. & harb., 1st July, 1905; prov. sec., Natal Prov., 1910; dep. admstr., Natal Prov., Aug., 1913, and from Aug., 1917; mem. prov. admin. comm., 1915; admstr., Natal, 1918.

PLUMER, FIELD-MARSHAL RT. HON. BAR. SIR HERBERT CHARLES ONSLOW PLUMER, G.C.B. (1918), G.C.M.G. (1916), G.C.V.O. (1917), G.M. (1924), A.D.C.—B. 1857; served in Suda expedtn., 1884, 4th cls. Medjidiye, operation: S. Africa, 1896; S. African War, 1899-1902; A.D.C. to King Edward VII., 1901-2; Q.M.: the forces, 1904-5; comdg. 6th divn., India, 1906-9, G.O.C.-in-C., Northern comm., 1911-14, comdg. 2nd Army, British expdt. France, 1915-17; G.O.C.-in-C., British force, Italy, 1917; gov't., Malta, 10th June, 1919; 1924; gen., 1918; A.D.C. Gen. to the King, 1921; York and Lancs. Regt., 1917; Grand Off. Legion of Honour; Grand Officer, So. M. Laz. (Italy); Grand Officer, Order of Leopold and Croix de Guerre (Belgium).

POLGLASE, HERBERT BAWDEN, A.C.A.—1883; acct., govt. monopolies dept., Singapore, Nov., 1909; asst. treas., July, 1914; asst. audr., external audit dept., F.M.S., Apr., 1918; asst. acct., P. and T. Dept., F.M.S., Jul.-Aug., 1917; ag. asst. acct., F.M.S.R., 1918-Apr., 1919; ag. senr. asst. audr., ex. dept., Singapore, Apr.-Nov., 1919; ag. senr. ex. audit dept., Penang, Jan., 1920; asst. treas., Penang, and ag. asst. audr., in addn., May; sp. duty, treasuries, Singapore and F.M.S., Dec., 1922; dep. acct., rly., Nov., 1922; ag. acct., F.M.S.R., Dec., 1923; ag. asst. audr., F.M.S., Sept., 1923; ag. audr.-gen., F.M.S., 1924.

POLLARD, ARNOLD.—B. 1893; col. dept., Feb., 1920; asst. audr., Tanganyika Territory, Apr., 1920.

POLLONAIS, CHARLES ADRIEN.—B. 1892; entered civ. serv., Trinidad, 27th Mar., 1901; asst. recr.-gen., 1st Apr., 1907; asst. treas., 1923; has acted as recr.-gen. and treas. on several occasions.

POMARE, HON. SIR MAUI, M.D., Chm. U.S.A., K.B.E. (1922), C.M.G. (1920)—B. 1877; educ. Boys' High Schl., Christchurch; govt. health offr. to Maoris, 1901; entd. New Zealand parlmt., 1911; mem. of exec. coun., representative race, 1912; also min. of Cook Isl. since 1916; min. of health, 1923.

POOLE, HENRY BRADISH.—Joined Bechuanaland Prot. pol., 1914; ag. sub-inspr., 1914; J.P., 1916; ag. asst. rec. mag., 1920; ag. mag., 1920; ag. regis. of brands and ag. ch. and regis., 1924.

POOLE, THOMAS STANLEY, M.A.—Paymr. judge, supreme ct., S. Australia, 1919; ag. just., 1925.

POOLEY, CHARLES EDWARD.—B. 1892; apptd. after compet. exam., cler. offr., C.O., 25th Oct., 1920.
POPE, FREDERICK SIDNEY.—B. 1869; educ. Wellington Boys' Coll., New Zealand; served in ovt. rly. dept., N. Zealand, 1868-1900; dept. agric., 1900-1909; sec. for agriculture, industries and commerce, 1909-1918; asst. director-gen. of agric., 1918.

POPE, SIR JOSEPH, K.C.M.G. (1912), C.V.O. (1908), C.M.G. (1901), I.S.O. (1906).—B. 1854; itered civ. ser. of Canada in 1878 as priv. sec. to min. of marine and fisheries priv. sec. to the late Sir John A. Macdonald, minister from 1882 till his death in 1891; asst. clk. of the Queen's Privy Coun. for Canada, 1889; under-sec. of state and dep. regisr.-gen. of Canada, 396; author of the Memoirs of Sir John A. Macdonald; Royal Tour in Canada, 1901, and other works; attached to the staff of the Br. agt. in the Behring Sea arbitration at Paris, 1893; gt. of Canadian govt., joint high comm., Quebec and Washington, 1898-99; put by ovt. to arrange Royal tour in Canada, 1901; assoc. sec. to Alaska boundary tribunal, London, 903; appd., in association with Mr. Bryce, t.M.'s plenipotentiary at the International Conference on pelagic sealing, 1911; recd. C.V.O. or services on the occasion of the Quebec tercentenary celebrations, 1908; holds 2nd cls. of Japanese Orders of the Sacred Treasure, and Grand Cordon of the Rising Sun; under-sec. of state for external affairs, 1909.

POPE, PERCY W. T.—B. 1856; ed. at Prince of Wales Coll., Charlottetown, P. E. I.; appd. Dominion auditor at Charlottetown, 1883; ass't sec.-gen., 1st Jan., 1887.

PORTELLI-CARBONE, ALFONSO, M.D. (Malta Univ., 1883).—L. M. (Rot. Hosp., Dub.), 1890; police physician for Zurrico, Sal, Creedi, and act. oph. phys. for Micabiba and Chiricop, and sanitary inspr. for the 6th country dist., Aug., 1884; dist. med. offr. for Valetta, Sept., 1886; is mem. of the Br. Med. Assoc. (Mediterranean branch), 1888; ell. Br. Gyneco. Soc., and mem. Intern. Med. 'ong., Berlin, 1890, and Rome, 1894 (obt. sc.).

POTTER, THOMAS IRWIN.—Ed. Queen's Royal Coll., Trinidad; ag. asst. clk., col. hosp., 18th Dec., 1882; clerical asst., Crown lands off., 10th pr., 1883; clk., survey dept. (in addition to former post), 1st Dec., 1884; ch. clk., Crown lands off., 16th Aug., 1897; ch. clk. and asst. inspr. of chls., 1st Nov., 1898; warden, La Brea and tropuche (owing to spec. knowledge of asphalt question); ch. offr. of customs, Brighton, La Brea, 1st Jan., 1899; harb.-master, Brighton harbour, La Brea, in addition to wardenship, 1st July, 1899; J.P. for county of St. Patrick; mem. of Royal society of arts, and dormant mem. of Royal society of Lond.; ag. sub. int., crown lands, 1st Sept., to 31st Oct., 1901, and from 10th Oct., 1905, to Jan., 1906; ag. harb.-mast., Colony, June to Dec., 1906; stip. justice, La Brea, and tropuche in conjunction with wardenship, 5th June, 1907; ag. harb.-mast., Colony, May to Nov., 908; ag. sub-intendant, Nov., 1908, to April, 1909; g. admnstr.-gen., 28th Apr., 1909; ag. offl. recvr. and adminstr.-gen., 1st Feb. to 13th Dec., 1910; g. regisr.-gen., 1st Apr. to 30th June, 1911; ag. regisr.-gen. (provisionally), 1st July, 1911; confirmed, 16th Aug., 1912; mem. of Port-of-Spain own board, 10th June, 1913; nominated mem. of Port-of-Spain city council, 31st Oct., 1914; inspr. of wardens, Jan., 1919.

POZZO, JOHN WILFRED.—Served in Bechuanaland Prot. pol., 1912-15; clk., 1915; ag. asst. res. ag., 1920; ag. res. mag., 1920 and 1922-23; passed civ. ser. lower law exam., 1919; passed 2nd grade Seawana exam., 1922.

POZZO, MOSES A.—Ed. S. Leone Gram. schl.; served in H.M.'s commissariat, S. Leone, June, 1853, till Jan., 1860; ag. 2nd clk., treas., July, 1865, to Jan., 1866; extra clk., Jan., 1866; house and land tax clk., Aug., 1869; 2nd clk., treas., after a compet. exam., Sept., 1870; census master, 1871; ch. clk. and cashier, 1877; ag. aud.-gen., Dec., 1886, to Feb., 1887; charity comm., 1889.

POU, WILLIAM OSCAR, M.D.Mich., M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (London).—B. 1875; C.M.O., Natal, 1901-02; regiar. and sen. res. med. offr., Seaman's Hosp., London; Schl of Trop. Med., 1904-06; health offr., Pahang, Apr., 1921.

POUGNET, EDOUARD DESBARBIERES, A.C.G.I., A.M.I.C.E.—Pub. wks. dept., Mauritius, Jan., 1888; asst. water authority, Moh., 1898; inspr. of water wks., July, 1903; govt. survr., Moh., 1911; supt. of pub. wks. and survr. of roads, St. Kitts, Apl., 1914; in service of French govt., in France during the war.

POULIER, REGINALD SYDNEY VERNON.—B. 1894; B.A., Lond.; cadet, Ceylon civ serv., local divn., Aug., 1919; attached to Galle Kach., Aug., 1919; pol. mag., Matale, Feb., 1922; ag. dist. judge, Tangalla, Mar., 1923; addnl. dist. judge, Mannar and Mullaitivu, Oct., 1924.

POUNTNEY, ARTHUR MEEK, C.M.G. (1923).—B. 1873; ed. Univ. Coll., Oxford; B.A.; cadet, F.M.S., 1896; ag. prot. of Chinese, Singapore, 1903; ag. prot. of Chinese, Perak, 1904; ag. offl. assignee, 1905; ag. prot. of Chinese, Selangor, 1906; ag. asst. prot. of Chinese, Penang, 1909; supt. of census, F.M.S., 1910; ag. prot. of Chinese, Selangor, 1912; treas., S. Settmts., 1st Feb., 1914; on sp. duty in connection with war tax, Jan., 1917; offg. collr.-gen., war tax, Mar., 1917; war services recog. by sec. of state, Nov., 1918; treas., Dec., 1918; custodian of enemy property in addition, Dec., 1918; pres., Straits mercantile marine service comm., May, 1919; finan. adviser to govt.s. of Straits Settmts. and F.M.S. in addition, 27th Oct., 1921.

POUSSETTE, HENRY RIVINGTON.—B. 1872; ed. Canada Pub. Sch., Upper Can. Coll., Royal Mily Coll., Kingston, and Sch. of Prac. Science, Toronto; capt., S. African Constab., 1901, and thereafter in same corps throughout S. African war dist. comdr., and pub. pros., S. Africa; inspr. serv., dept. of trade and commerce, Can.; as trade comnr., Durban, S. Africa, 1909; trade comnr., Buenos Aires, 1910; enlisted for active serv., 1914; returnd, Can., 1919; inspr., trade comnr. serv.; sp. trade comnr., India, 1919; dir., comm. intelligence serv., Ottawa, 1921; trade comnr., Trinidad, 1924.

POWELL, HENRY.—Student, Royal Gardens, Kew, June, 1888, to Apr., 1890; curator, Botanic Gardens, St. Vincent, May, 1890, to Nov., 1903; asst. to dir. of agric., E. Africa Prot., 7th Nov., 1903; ch. of economic plants div., Apr., 1907.

POWELL, HENRY A., D.C.L., K.C., M.A.—B. 1855; ed. Richibucto Gram. Schl., Mt. Allison Univ. (B.A., 1875; M.A., 1890; D.C.L., 1914); atty., 1879; called to New Brunswick bar, 1880; K.C. (of Aberdeen, 1894; K.C., New Brunswick, 1894; councillor, N.B. Barristers' Assc.; prof. law faculty, King's Coll., Windsor, N.S.; el. to N.B. legislature for Westmorland, 1890, 1891 and 1892; el. to H. of C. for Westmorland, 1895 and 1896; mem., Bd. of Regents, senator, and mem., exec. comtee, Mt. Allison Univ.; mem., International Law Assc., of Washington, D.C.; mem. of International Joint Coms.
POWER, GERALD, B.A.—B. 1891; ed. Denstone Coll., and Queen's Coll., Oxford; jnr. supt., educ. dept., N. Nigeria, 14th Jan., 1914.

POWERS, HON. CHARLES—Justice of the high ct., of Australia, 1913.

POWTER, JOHN—Traffic ast., Baro-Kano rly., N. Nigeria, Mar., 1911; ast. traffic supt., Nigeria rly., Apr., 1913; dist. traffic supt., 1920; gen. man., Trinidad govt. rly., Mar., 1922.

PRAIRIE, LT.-COL. SIR DAVID, KT. BACH. (1912); C.M.G. (1912); C.I.E. (1906); M.A., M.B., LL.D., F.R.S.E., F.L.S., F.R.S.—B. 1857; ed. Aberdeen gram. schl. and Univs. of Aberdeen and Edinburgh; demonstrator of anatomy, coll. of surgeons, Edin., 1882-3, and univ. of Aberdeen, 1883-84; entd. Indian med. serv., 1884; curator, Calcutta herbarium, 1887-1888; prof. of botany, med. coll., Calcutta, 1896-1905; director, botanical survey of India, and supt. of royal botanic garden, Calcutta, 1898-1905; trustee of the Indian Museum, 1898-1904; sec. bd. of scientific advice for India, 1903-1904; mem. of coun. of various scientific societies; director of royal botanic gardens, Kew, 1905; ret., 1922.

PRANKERD, HORACE ARTHUR.—B. 1883; ed. at Ipswich and Queen's Coll., Cambridge (scholar, 2nd class Tripos), B.A., 1905; ast. master, Loretto, to July, 1907; then 24 years at Lausanne and Freiburg-in-Baden Univ.; ast. sec., N. Nigeria, Oct., 1910; ast. res., 1911.

PRASAD, MURARI.—B. 1888; Cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Dec., 1912; attached to Galle Kachcheri, Jan., 1913; ag. pol. mag., Point Pedro, Sep., 1913; addtl. office ast. to gov't. ast., N.C. Prov., Aug., 1914; addtl. dist. judge, Anuradhapura, Aug., 1915; office ast. to gov't. ast., N.C. Prov., Dec., 1915; pol. mag., Chilaw, Apr., 1917; ditto, Panadure, Apr., 1919; office ast. to gov't. ast., N. Prov., Mar., 1920; dist. judge, Anuradhapura, May, 1921; pol. mag., Kalutara, May, 1922; ditto, Gampola, Mar., 1923; dist. judge, Tangalla, Oct., 1924.

PRATT, CHARLES E. J. BLYTH.—Ed. Trent Coll.; 2nd lieut., 4th batt. Sherwood Foresters Derbyshire regt., Jan., 1897; lieut., 4th batt. Prince of Wales North Stafford regt., May, 1888; instructor of musketry, Jan., 1890; lieut., Falmouth div. submarine miners, R.E., Apr., 1893; ast. inspr. Sierra Leone frontier pol., Aug., 1895; inspr., Apr., 1896; J.P. for S. Leone.

PRATT, CAPT. EDWARD.—Ed. at Shrewsbury; cadet, F.M.S., Oct., 1898; ag. ast. dist. offr., Raub, May, 1899; ag. collr. of land rev., Kuala Lumpur, Feb., 1901; passed cadet, May, 1902; ast. dist. offr., Lower Perak, Jan., 1903; ag. ast. dist. offr., Tanjong Malim, Sept., 1903; ag. dist. treas., Batu Gajah, Jan., 1904; ag. ast. dist. offr., Kuala Kangsar, Nov., 1904; ditto, Tanjong Malim, Dec., 1904; ditto, Kuala Lipis, Aug., 1907; ag. dist. offr., Temerloh, Oct., 1908; ag. mag., Taiping, Oct., 1910; ast. regsr., supreme ct., Kinta, May, 1911; ag. revenue auditor, Perak, 23rd Oct., 1912; ag. dist. offr., Krian, 7th July, 1913; offr. of cls. III, S. Stltmts., 21st Dec., 1914; joined army, Aug., 1916; addtl. R.A.S.C., "Syren" force, Dec., 1918; offr., cls. II, S. Stltmts., 1st Juno, 1919; demob., May, 1919; ag. 1st mag., Ipoh, May, 1920; ag. dep. pub. pros., F.M.S., Sept., 1920; ag. legal adviser and judge, Johor, Dec., 1920; dep. pub. pros., F.M.S., July, 1921; offg. dist. judge, Malacca, sept., 1922.

PRATT, F. G., A.M.I.C.E.; ast. engnr., Lagos govt. rlys., Mar., 1907; ast. engnr., P.W.D., Uganda, Sept., 1908; ditto, P.W.D., N. Nigeria, Dec., 1911; represented N. Nigeria; 3rd International Road Congress held in London in June, 1913; dir. of pub. wks., Nyassaland, 1917.

PRENDERGAST, HON. JAMES EMIL PERKIN—Ed. at Seminary of Quebec, and Laval Univ., Quebec; B.A., 1878; LL.B., 1881; returned to La Verendrye, Manitoba, Aug., 1886; again Dr., 1886; on formation of cabinet by Hon. Thom Greenway, Jan., 1889, was given portfolio of pres.; re-elected in said constituency; elected to Woodlands, 1888; judge of sup. ct., N.W.T., 1902; ditto Saskatchewan, 1907; puisne judge court of King's Bench of Manitoba, 1910.

PRENTICE, ARCHIBALD HEPBURN GARDINER—Ast. treas., Uganda, 1913; senr. ast. treas., Apr., 1919; ag. dep. treas., in 1919, 1920, 1921, and 1922; dep. treas., Tanganyika Terr., 22nd Sept., 1922; ag. treas., Dec., 1922 to Sept., 1923.

PRESCOTT, ARTHUR STANLEY.—Appd. to compet. exam., supplementary clk., supreme ct., Gibraltar, 1896; 3rd cls. clk., 1899; ast. treas. and deputy clk. of arraigns, 1911.

PRETTY, ERIC ERNEST FALK.—B. 1891; Harrow, and Demy of Magdalen Coll., Oxon; cadet, S. Stltmts., Nov., 1914; passed final exam. in Malay, Jan., 1916; ag. collr. of land rev., Johore Bahru, Sept., 1917; offr., cl. V.; S. Stltmts., Dec., 1917; 2nd lieut. and ast. m.; Johore Vol. Rifles, May, 1918; ag. ast. admn. Endau, Johore, June, 1920; supernumerary, cls. IV., Nov., 1921; ag. 2nd ast. sec. "E.", Feb., 1922; ag. p. te. sec. to O.A.G., 28th April.

PREVOST, EDWARD WILLIAM DE TREMAYEN.—B. 1882; ed. Wellington Coll., Berks; senr. in S. Africa as 2nd lieut., 3rd Royal Lancs regt., 1901-2 (Queen's medal with two clasps); wmg. offr. of constab., and supt. of civil police, N. Borneo, 1904-1911; passed higher exam. in Malay language; passed course of instruction at R.I.C. depot, Dublin; ast. ensign of pol., Gold Coast, Apr., 1912; passed lower standard exam. in Fanti language; comm. pol., Jan., 1915; dep. inspr.-gen. of pol., Feb., 1917; ag. inspr.-gen. of pol., Mar.-Oct., 1917; June-Oct., 1920, and Nov., 1921.

PRICE, CHARLES ROY.—B. 1893; ed. Walton Schol. and University Coll., London; 1st Lieut. (war), 1919; unattached list, Territorial Force, Jan. to Aug., 1915; Royal Garrison Artillery, 1915 to Dec., 1918; served in France, June to Sept., 1918; appd. under reconstruction scheme, ast. prin., C.O., 1st Mar., 1921.

PRICE, G. F.—Dist. acctnt., S. Africas prov. rlys., (construction), Natal, 1904-1907; ast. Baro-Kano rly., N. Nigeria, Feb. to July, 1907; acctnt., P.W.D., 1st Aug., 1908; ast. treas., Nigeria, Oct., 1910; ag. chief ast. treas., to Nov., 1912.

PRICE, HERBERT HENRY.—2nd clk. to sec. comsrs., Northern Div., Bech. Prot., 1910; clk., res. comrs.'s office, 1st May, 1912; passed Cape div. ser. lower law exam., 1910; ag. res. mag., 1911-12; registr. of brands, 1913; clk. and registr., 1921.

PRICE, STANLEY LEWIS, B.A.—B. 1891; Lampeter Coll., and Jesus Coll., Oxford; ast. supt., educn. dept., N. Nigeria, 26th Sept., 1919; attached, Nigeria Regt., 1917-18.

PRICE, HON. WILLIAM H., B.A., LL.B.—B. 1878; ed. pub. and high schls., Ont.; Oxford Hall Law Schl., Toronto Univ. (B.A., LL.B.); barrister; el. to Ont. legis., g.e., 1914; rad., 1919 and 1923; prov. treasurer in Fernand adminstr., 1923.
PRICE-JONES, Capt. William.—Served during Great War in France; awarded M.C., 1917; asst. dist. commr., Gold Coast, 27th Aug., 1919; dist. commr., 1st Apr., 1924.

PRICHARD, Herbert William, K.C. (1873—1873; ed. at Keble Coll., Oxford (open class scholar, 1892); called to the bar, Gray's Inn, Jan., 1902; practised in London, 1902-1910; stip. mag., riniditius, 19th Aug., 1910; puisne judge, lauritius, 19th Feb., 1915; 1st puisne judge, 9th Oct., 1916; ag. procureur and advoc.-gen., 9th Oct., 1916, to 2nd July, 1917; chrmn. of omen. on Royal College, 1916-1917; chrmn., agar sales comites., 1st Sept., 1918 to 31st Aug., 1919; ag. col. sec., 6th Sept. to 13th Dec., 1920 nd 2nd Feb. to 3rd Apr., 1921; ag. procureur nd advoc.-gen., 16th April, 1921; confirmed in pth., 20th Jan., 1922; ag. col. sec. from 16th aug., 1924.

PRINCE, Edward Ernest, F.R.S.C., &c.—b. 1868; ed. Modern Schl., Leeds, and St. Andrews, Camb., and Edin. Univ.; apptd. demonstr., zool., Edin. Univ., 1885; naturalist, cotch fishery; bd. laboratory, St. Ands.; prof. of pol. and comp. anat., Royal Infirmary Med. Coll., Glasgow, 1890; fishery expert, Irish Deep Sea Survey, 1893; vice-pres. Internat. Fisheries Congress, Washington, Paris, and St. Petersburg, 903-06-09; vice-pres., bd. sect., Brit. Assoc., 909; ditto, Royal Soc. of Canada, 1908; mem. f internat. relations coun., American fish. soc., 910; Canad. mem. of internat. fish. congress, tome, 1911; life mem. of British Science Guild; mem. of internat. fisheries coman.; repres. Canada, under Fisheries Treaty, 1908; chrmn. of many sherry comans.: lobster, 1898; Pacific salmon, 907; Bay of Fundy Shad, 1908; Manitoba sheries, 1909; Alberta and Sask. fisheries, 1910-911; chrmn. of bd. of Canada; comanr. of sheries for Canada, apptd. 1892.

PRIOR, A. C. Vincent.—B. 1881; ed. King's Coll., Cambridge; M.A., LL.B.; called to the bar, Inner Temple, 1908; atty.-gen., St. Vincent, th Jan., 1915; ag. ch. just., Jan. to June, 1915; atty.-gen., Leeward Is., 8th Apr., 1918; solr.-gen., Sierra Leone, 5th Sept., 1920; ag. atty.-gen., 921-22.

PRIOR, Wm. Burgess.—Mem. provisional N. torneo Assoc.; res. E. Coast dist. Br. N. Borneo, aug., 1891; prot. of coolies, E. Coast, 1894; mem. E. Coast coun., 1893; Br. consular agt., 1890; res. and mag., Gold Field dist., Feb., 1897.

PRITCHARD, Major C. G.—1st commn. R.A., 3rd Nov., 1891; promoted capt., 4th Dec., 1899; dj., Hong Kong volunteers, Jan. to July, 1901; omdt. and adj. (local major), 2nd Apr., 1902.

PRITCHETT, Cecil John Suckling, B.A. (Oxon.).—B. 1888; cadet, Ceylon civil serv., Dec., 912; attached to Jaffna Kachcheri, Jan., 1913; g. pol. mag., Trincomalee, July, 1913; ag. ast. stltmt. offr., Nov., 1913; office ast. to govt. gt., N. Prov., Nov., 1914; ast. collr. of customs and land survr., Jaffna, Nov., 1914; ag. ast. ort. agt., Mannar, Dec., 1915; office ast. to ort. agt., N. Prov., Feb., 1916; pol. mag., visawella, Oct., 1916; ditto, Panadure, Dec., 917; ditto, Chilaw, Apl., 1918; ag. ditto, Galle, ept., 1919; ast. land stltmt. offr., Nov., 1921; g. dist. judge, Anuradhapura, Feb., 1922.

PROBYN, Sir Leslie, K.C.M.G. (1909); M.G. (1903).—Ed. at Charterhouse, and in France and Germany, called to the bar, lid. Tem., 1884; joint author of "The Jurisdiction and Practice of the Mayor's Court," nd other law books; atty.-gen., Br. Honduras, 1893; atty.-gen. of Grenada, May, 1896; also ag. col. sec. in 1897-8; ag. admstr. on several occasions; gov. secretary, S. Nigeria, 12th Apr., 1901; gov., Sierra Leone, 4th July, 1904; gov., Barbados, 6th Nov., 1910; assumed govt., 13th Feb., 1911; gov., Jamaica, 31st May, 1918; assumed govt., 11th June, 1918; ret., 1924.

PROFSTING, Hon. W. B., C.M.G. (1918).—M.L.C., Tasmania; atty.-gen. and min. for rly., Apr., 1916.

PROUT, Sir W. T., Kt. Bach. (1924), C.M.G. (1905), M.B., C.M. (Edin.)—Asst. poor law med. offr., Mauritius, 1885; surg. supt., immigrant ship "Dundee," 1887; asst. col. surg., Gold Coast, 1888; dist. commr., Gold Coast, 1890; col. surg., Gambia, 1893; ag. chief surg., Gambia, 1893; med. offr. in charge of base hosp. during campaign against Foday Sila; col. surg., S. Leone, 1896; title altered to prin. med. offr., 1901; retired, 1906; fellow of roy. med. soc., Edin., and corrpdg. mem. of the epidemiological soc. of Lond.; lect., schl. of trop. med., Univ. of Liverpool; med. adviser to C.O.; mem. of advisory, med. and sanitary comtes. for Tropical Africa, C.O.; senr. med. adviser to C.O., 1924; author of article "Yaws" in "Diseases of Warm Climates" (Davidson); Fil. Voloulous (Archives de Parasitologie, May, 1901); "Filariasis in S. Leone" (Brit. Med. Journal, 1902); and other papers.

PRYDE, William.—B. 1880; ed. Royal High Schl., and Univ., Edinburgh; M.A., Edinburgh Univ. (1st cls. hons. in class.); Pitt Club schol. and Guthrie fellow, Edinburgh Univ.; cadet, F.M.S., 27th Nov., 1903; passed cadet, May, 1905; offr., cls. V, Oct., 1910; offr., cls. IV, July, 1915; offr., cls. III, July, 1918; offr., cls. II, Nov., 1920; barrister-at-law, Lincoln's Inn, Jan., 1923; mag. Kuala Lumpur, Mar., 1923; ag. dist. judge and 1st mag., Singapore, Sept., 1924.

PUCKRIDGE, Geoffrey Martin.—B. 1895; ed. Exeter Schl.; 2nd lieut., Devon Regt., T.F., Dec., 1913; capt., Dec., 1914; served in France with 6th West Yorks regt.; seconded to Royal Flying Corps, July, 1917; seconded to Inter Allied Aeronautical Coman. of Control, Germany, 1920; re-signed comman., Sept., 1921; asst. dist. commr., Gold Coast, 1921.

PUDSEY, Fawcett.—B. 1882; Assoc. M.I.M.E.; Assoc. M.I.C.E.; ed. Hymer's Coll., Hull, and Repton Schl.; apprentice with Messrs. Rose, Downs and Thompson, Ltd., Hull, 1900-1905; engineering asst., dock engrn.'s staff, N.E. Rly., 1905-1911; engaged on survey work, Catalonia, Spain, for the Pearson Engineering Corporation, New York, 1911; in charge of opening of the Hesle quarry and crushing plant of the British Portland Cement Manufacturers, Ltd., 1912-1914; asst. dir. of pub. wks., B. Guiana, 1914; ag. D.P.W., Feb., 1916.

PUGH, J.—Med. offr., E.A.P., Jan., 1910.

PUGHE, S. R.—B. 1877; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civil ser., and assigned to the C.O., Aug., 1897; promoted, with gratuity, Aug., 1904; conf. clk., Dec., 1907; minor staff clerk, 1911; staff clk., 1st grade, 1st Mar., 1916; staff offr., 1st Apr., 1922.

PUGSLEY, Hon. William, K.C., D.C.L.—B. 1860; educ. schl., Sussex, N.B., Univ. of New Brunswick, B.A. (1888), and Univ. of Lond., B.C.L., D.C.L.; called to the bar, N.B., 1872; reporter of the supreme ct., 1873-83; Q.C. by Dom. govt., 1891; elec. to legis., N.B., 1886; speaker, 1887; solr.-gen., 1890; resigned, 1892; re-entrd. legis., 1899; attorney-gen., 1900;
premier, 1907; sworn of the priv. council for Canada and min. of pub. wks., 1907; re-elec. to H. of C., Sept., 1911; resig. portfolio on defeat of Laurier govt., Oct., 1911; lieut.-gov. of New Brunswick, 1918-1923; commr. to investigate illegal warfare claims, 1923.

PURCELL, Sir Gilbert Kenhelm Treffry, K.T., B.A., (1916).—Ed. Exeter Coll., Oxford; R.A., 1888; M.A., 1893; called to bar, Lincolns Inn, Nov., 1890; mem. of western circ., also practised at cent. crim. ct.; apptd. asst. to atty.-gen. Leeward Ialda. (St. Kitts), Mar., 1898; official mem. of exec. and legis. couns. of the presidency of St. Christopher and Nevis; ag. atty.-gen. Leewards, Aug.-Oct., 1900; apptd. as 1st puisne judge, June, 1901; puisne judge, G. Coast, 11th June, 1901; chief justice, Sierra Leone, 1911.

PURCELL, Hubert Kennett.—B. 1884; ent. Crown Agents office, Oct., 1901; asst. cashier, July, 1914; head of pay dept., Dec., 1920; dep. head of pay and checking dept., Nov., 1921.

PURCELL, Victor William Williams Saunders.—B. 1896; ed. Bancroft's Schol. and Trinity Coll., Camb.; 2nd lieut., Yorks Regt., Nov., 1914; B.E.F., France, 1915-16; "1914-15" Star, twice wounded, prisoner of war; cadet, F.M.S., Apr., 1921; proceeded to Canton to study Chinese, Dec., 1921; offr., cl. V., July, 1923; passed cadet, July, 1924; inspr., Chinese schls., S.S., June, 1924.

PURDON, Andrew.—B. 1876; ed. at Ebury and Conway colls., N. Wales; cadet, H.M.S. "Conway"; sub-lieut., R.N.R., Apr., 1905; lieut., 1908; qualified at Whale Island and H.M.S. "Vernon"; asst. marine supt., N. Nigeria Marine, 11th Sept., 1909; whilst on leave took special course of instruction in hydrographical survey at R.N. coll., Greenwich, 1911.

PUTTICK, Leonard James.—B. 1885; ed. at High Schol. and Huguenot Coll., Wellington and S. African Coll., Cape Town; served in Anglo-Boer war, 1900-01; draughtsman, Swaziland, 1910; elk. of lands, 1916; ch. clk., 1919.

QUICK, Hon. Sir John, K.T., B.A. (1901); LL.D.—B. 1852; elec. to first H. of R., Commonwealth of Australia, 1901; re-elec. in 1903 and 1906; postmr.-gen., C. of A., June, 1909; retired from politics, 1913; now dep. judge, federal arbitration, etc.

RAK, James Stanley.—B. 1881; articled and conf. clk. to Sir W. R. Davies, K.T., when atty.-gen., Bahamas; called to the bar, Bahamas, Apr., 1904; called to the bar, Middle Temple, Jan., 1919; ag. coroner for the Is. of New Providence from 1904, confirmed in 1911; J.P., 1910; ag. atty.-gen. Jan., 1910; ag. stip. and circ. mag., 1910-11, and on other occasions; dist. commr., Belize, B. Honduras, 1914; offl. recr. in bankruptcy, offl. admstr. and J.P. for the col., 1914; regar.-gen., Nov., 1915, in conjunction with duties as dist. commr.; dir. of P.O.G. fund, 1916; custodian of enemy property, Sept., 1916; press censor during war; prte., B. Hond. Territorial Force; attd. to staff as mil. censor; atty.-gen., St. Vincent, Apr., 1919; cross of Chevalier of the Order of the Crown, Belgium, for relief services during war, May, 1919; ag. ch. just., St. Vincent, June to Oct., 1919; atty.-gen., St. Lucia, Sept., 1920; ag. ch. just., June, 1921 to Feb., 1922 and from Sept., 1922 to June, 1923; ch. just., St. Vincent, June, 1923.

RAFFLES, Major Stamford Cecil, O.B.E. (Mily.), 1919.—B. 1885; ed. All Saints Schol., Bloxham, Royal Naval Academy, Gosport, and in Germany; 2nd lieut., 4th Suffolk regt., 1907; lieut., 1903; transf., K.S.L.I., 1906; regt. comm., 1908; supt., chandu monopoly, Perak, 1913; seconded for mil. serv., Jan., 1915; lieut. 3rd R.W.F., Mar., 1915; capt., Sept., 1915; st. offr., 3rd cl., R.F.C., 1917; staff offr., 2nd cl., R.A.F., 1918; tempy. major, 1918; trans. unemployed list, R.A.F., Apr., 1919; resume duty as supt., chandu monopoly, Perak; supervisor, Kinta, Dec., 1919; ag. treas., Perak, May, 1920; supervisor, Selangor, Dec., 1920; dep. commr., trade w. outst., F.M.S., Jan., 1921.

RAINSFORD, R. F.—Asst. supt. of psh. E.A.P., Apr., 1914.

RALPH, Charles Hugh Davison, L.R.C.I. (Lond.), M.R.C.S. (Eng.), 1902, Cert. Lond. Trop. Med.—Surg., Muttaburra hosp., Queensland; W.A.M.S., 1903-20; read. thanks of S. (Yellow Fever epidemic); dist. med. in Cyprus, 1921; ag. ch. med. offr. on war occasions.

RALPHS, Edwin, F.R.G.S., F.C.S., F.L.S., M.R. San. Inst.—B. 1872; ed. St. Mark's Chelsea; 1st cl. in Queen's scholarship, inst. teachers exama. (education dept.), and in bishops' divinity exam.; honours in sci. South Kens.; asst. master (junior) Que. Coll., Hong Kong, 1898; senior grade N. Normal mast., 1906; ag. second master, 1904 to 1908 and 1909; 2nd mast. 1908; head mast. and mem. of advisory comte. Ed. Inst., 1909 and 1910, to 1911; hon. exam. chemistry to Hong Kong Coll. of Med., 1901-03; dir., Hong Kong Technical Inst., 1907; J.P., 1910; inspr. of English schls., asst. commr., St. John Ambulance Brigade, Hong Kong and China dist., 1915; seconded as hse Red Cross commr. in Siberia, 1918 to 1919; capt., 1919; ag. dir. of educn., 1918 and 1920; Order of St. John of Jerusalem, 1919; dir. of educn., and mem. of coun., etc., and mem. Hong Kong Univ., 1918 and 1919 to 1920; bd. of educn., 1920; examr. in educn., Hong Kong Univ., 1920-23.

RALSTON, James, M.A., Glasgow F.R.G.S.—B. 1890; asst. mast., educn., Hong Kong, 1914; on active serv., 1918; asst. mast., cls. II., 1920.

RAM, George Edward—Lieut., 4th batt. of Wales's North Staffordshire Regt.; served S. Africa, Oct., 1902, to July, 1903 (medals 3 clasps); ag. priv. sec. and A.D.C. to gov. Newfoundland, 9th Sept., 1903.

RAMANATHAN, Sir Ponnambarai P. Bach., C.M.G. (1889), K.C.—B. 1851; ed. the Acad., Colombo, and Prem. Coll. Mat. barr.-at-law, Inn. Tem.; advoc., sup. et. Com., 1873; mem. of the legis. coun., 1873; mem. of the law comm. appd. to report upon codes dealing with the laws of Ceylon; served also on the comm. appd. at instance to report upon the Thoroughfare Finance, 1881; obtained the introduction of savings bank in Ceylon, 1881-83; was one of select comte. of the legis. coun. appd. to report upon retrenching the public expenditure in island, 1882-83; a mem. of the coun. of legal aid, 1884; mem. of the Ceylon comm. of the Colonial Ind. Exhib., 1886; mem. of the Cent. Irrig. Co., 1888; and of the select comte. to report upon incidence of the grain taxes, 1889; mem. of comm. to inquire into the extension of the to the N. parts of the island, 1890; rep. of Ceylon, 1892; ag. atty.-gen., 1894.
906; elected M.L.C., Ceylon, 1911; re-elected, 1917; nominated mem. of reformed leg. coun., 1921; elec. mem., reformed leg. coun., 1924.

RANASINHA, ARTHUR GODWIN, B.A. (Lond.)—B. 1898; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Jan., 1921; ttd. to Kegalla Kach., Mar., 1921; attd., Jaffna Kach., Oct., 1922; pol. mag., Pt. Pedro, Mar., 1923; ditto, Balapitiya, Nov., 1923.

RANEY, HON. W. E.—B. 1861; was schlr. teacher for some years; also engaged in newspaper work; grad. in law at Osgoode Hall and took up practice in Toronto, 1892; has taken an active part in temperance and moral reform movements; petty-gen. in U.F.O. govt., Nov., 1919; re-el. 1923; resigned portfolio on defeat of U.F.O. admnstr., 1923.

RANFURLY, 5TH EARL OF (SIR UCHTER JOHN LARK KNOX, G.C.M.G.), Viscount Northland and Baron Welles of Dungannon, co. Tyrone, Ireland, Baron Ranfurly of Pharamalie, co. Renfrew, United Kingdom.—Born 1856; succeeded his brother 1875; ed. Trinity Coll., Cambridge; D.L. for co. Tyrone; Knight of Justice of the Order of St. John of Jerusalem; lord-in-waiting to the Queen, 1895-7; governor of New Zealand, 1897-1904.

RANKINE, RICHARD SIMS DONKIN, C.M.G. (9-19).—B. 1875; clk. treasury, Fiji, Feb., 1894; riv. sec. to Sir George O'Brien, Sept., 1897, to 1901; acted clk. to ex. coun. Sept., 1899, to Mar., 1900; apptd. act. native taxes, treasury, 1901; riv. sec. to Sir Henry Jackson, July, 1902; priv. sec. to Sir E. im Thurn, 10th Oct., 1904; conf. sec., 1st Jan., 1905; sec. to consul-gen. for W. Pacific; clk. of exec. coun.; ag. sec., W. Pacific high commr., June, 1905 to June, 1906, and from Nov., 1907, to 31st Dec., 1908; asst. col. sec. and asst. sovr.-gen., 1st Jan., 1909; revr.-gen. and commr. of stamps, pres. of marine bd., mem. exec. and legis. couns., 1910; ag. col. sec., Nov., 1913 to Nov., 1914; gov'r's dep., 5th to 14th June, 1914; commr. of currency, Dec., 1914; agt.-gen. of emigrn. (conjoint), Mar., 1915; ag. col. sec., Aug., 1915 to May, 1916; gov'r's deputy, Aug., 1915; dep. sec., 18th Sept., 1917, to 13th Jan., 1918, 16th June to 9th Oct., 1918, and from Dec., 1918 to July, 1919; on special mission to India as personal rep. of the gov'r in connection with emigrn. of Indians to Fiji, Oct., 1919 to June, 1920; ch. sec., Nyasaland Prot., July, 1920; ag. gov., Oct., 1921, to Feb., 1922; ch. gov., Apr., 1923 to Mar., 1924.

RANSOM, HERBERT CHARLES, O.B.E. (23rd, B.E. 1920).—B. 1881; entd. crown agt.'s off., May, 1901; asst. cashier, Mar., 1914; ag. head of opts. dept. and ast. sec., Jan., 1917; head of miscellaneous dept., Apr., 1919; dep. head, gen. dept., 14th Nov., 1921; sec., Dead Sea mineral sources comte., 1923.

RAPER, ALEXANDER VINCENT.—B. 1896; ed. Portsmouth Grammar Schl.; served with the R. Gurkha Regt., 1914-20; (France, Belgium, Egypt, India and Palestine); cadet, F.M.S., May, 1921; ttd. to dist. office, Lower Perak, in 1921 and 1922; ag. 2nd ast. dist. offr., Kuala Kangsar, Jan., 1922; passed cadet, Jan., 1923; ag. ast. dist. offr., Lower Perak, Aug., 1923.

RASANAYAGAM, CHELLAPPAH.—B. 1870; ptd. to cls. V., Ceylon civ. serv., Sept., 1923; tra. office ast., Jaffna Kach., Sept., 1923.

RASON, HON. SIR CORNWALTHE HECTOR, K.T. (1909).—B. 1859; ed. at Brighton, W. Aust., 1879; M.L.A. for S. Murchison, 1897-1901; ditto Guildford since 1901; min. of works, 1901; min. of works and rlys., 1902-4; prem. of W. Aust., 1906; pres. of Royal comm. on mining, 1908, and of Royal comm. on immigr., 1906; agt.-gen. in London for W. Aust., 1906-1909.

RATTRAY, ROBERT SUTHERLAND, M.B.E. (1918), F.R.G.S., F.R.A.I., barrister-at-law.—B. 1881; served in S. Africa, 1901-02 (Queen's med., five clasps); Togoland, 1914 (ment. in despatch); cust. dept., G. Coast, 5th Oct., 1907; ast. dist. commr., 1911; dist. commr., 1915; Togoland polit. admin., 1914-18; ag. senr. ast. col. sec., and clk. to leg. and exec. couns., May, 1920; author of "Hausa Folk Lore," "Ashanti Proverbs," "Chinyanja Folk Lore."

RAVEN, ROBERT McPHERSON.—B. 1872; ed. Victoria Coll., Jersey; ast. engr., Admiralty, 1895; dist. engr., Gold Coast rly. construction, 1898; dist. engr., Nigerian rly., 1904; chief engr., E. African mil. rlys., German E. Africa (occupied territory), 1917; temporary gen. man., 1918-1919; mem. of Nigerian Land Contingent, Aug., 1914 to Dec., 1917; major, Rly. Corps, E. African Expd. Force, Feb., 1918; ch. engr., Tanganyika Territory, rlys., 1st Oct., 1919; ag. gen. man. in 1920 and 1923.

RAWSON, WALTER EDWARD.—B. 1870; ed. New Plymouth High Schl., N.Z.; barrister and solr.; judge, native land ct. and native appellate ct., N.Z., 1906; pres., Maori land bd., 1910; native trustee and east coast trust commr., 1921.

RAYMAN, LAZARUS.—B. 1889; ed. Manchester Gram. Schl. (Lauson medallist) and Wadham Coll., Oxford (Hodz prize-man); cadet, F.M.S., 1913; Brit. adviser's office, Kodah; ast. dist. offr., Pekan, Pahang, 1914-16; ast. dist. offr., Bentong, Pahang, 1916-17; ast. dist. offr., Ulu Selangor, 1917; ag. rev. audr., Selangor, Negri Sembilan and Pahang, 1917-18; ast. dist. offr., Bentong, 1918-19; ast. dist. offr., Ulu Selangor, 1919-21; ag. dist. offr., Ulu Selangor, 1920-1; on sp. duty as collr. of stamp duty, Mar., 1922.

RAYNE, H. A.—Ast. dist. commr., E. Africa Prot., Dec., 1914; dist. commr., Somaliland, Apr., 1919.

READ, SIR HERBERT JAMES, K.C.M.G. (1918), C.B. (1914), C.M.G. (1907).—B. 1863; M.A. Brasenose Coll., Oxford; 1st class math. mods., and 1st class math. finals; clk., higher div., W.O., Feb., 1887; 2nd class clk., C.O., Jan., 1889; ast. priv. sec. to Mr. Chamberlain, Sept., 1896; priv. sec. to Mr. (afterwards Sir E.) Wingfield, Feb., 1898; Ist clk., Oct., 1898; principal clk., 1st Apr., 1906; British delegate at African liquor confce. at Brussels, 1899; one of the Brit. delegates on boundary comm. at Berlin for the settm. of Anglo-German frontier in E. Africa, 1906; one of the Brit. plenipotentiaries at African liquor confce. at Brussels, 1906; mem. of hon. man. comte. of sleeping sickness bureau, 1908; ehmn. of deptnl. comte. to enquire into W. African med. staff, 1909; visited E. Africa, 1911-12; ast. under-sec. of state, 10th March, 1916; regnr. of the Order of Saint Michael and Saint George; gov., Mauritius, 1st Sept., 1924.

READING, EDWARD BABER SEGRAVE.—Capt., S. African constab., 1901; staff offr., S.A.C., 1902; relieving mag., 1904; 2nd grade mag., Vredefort, 1904; 1st grade mag., Heilbronn, 1907; inspgr. mag. and inspr. of prisons, 1919; pub. serv. inspr., 1921.

REAKES, CHARLES JOHN, C.B.E. (1919), M.R.C.V.S., Eng., Doctor of Vet. Science, Univ. of Melbourne.—B. 1865; vet. offr., N.Z. dept. of
agr., 1897; asst. ch. vet., 1901; dir., live-stock divn., and dir. vet. services and remounts, N.Z. Defence Forces with rank of lieut.-col. (since col.), 1909; dir.-gen., agr. dept., 1918.

REAY, JAMES MCCABE.—B. 1875; ed. Dundalk, and Trinity Coll., Dublin; scholar, senr. moderator and B.A., 1898; barrister-at-law, King's Inn; advoc. and solr., sup. ct., F.M.S.; cadet, F.M.S., 1898; ag. treas. and S.P.T., Pahang, May, 1899; ag. asst. dist. offr., Ulu Langat, Feb., 1900; ag. dist. offr., Kuala Langat, Feb., 1901; ag. asst. dist. offr., Serendah, Mar., 1901; ag. dist. offr., B.
